The surah says:

﴿A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant.﴾

Disavowal (al-bara'ah), as we have said, is the severing of protection (al-'ismah), and protection is holding fast (al-istimsak). The Exalted says:

﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah has certainly been guided to a straight path.﴾ (Al 'Imran: 101)

And He also says: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of Allah.﴾ (Hud: 43)

So disavowal necessarily implies that there was a covenant and a holding fast to it. The disavowal came as a release from holding fast to this covenant, which the Messenger of Allah had made with them; they had been holding fast to the treaty, and then the divine command came to sever this treaty. The word "bara'ah" is found in the context of debt (al-dayn), and it is said: "So-and-so was freed (bari'a) from the debt." That is, the debt had been binding upon his neck, and when he settled and paid it, it is said: "He was freed from the debt." It is also said: "So-and-so was cured (bari'a) of the illness" when he recovered from it, meaning the illness had been holding onto him, then the hold between him and the illness was severed.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a covenant with the Quraysh and had made a covenant with the Jews, and these did not fulfil the covenants, so it was necessary for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to annul these covenants. If someone asks: why did he not annul these covenants from the beginning, and why was their annulment delayed until the ninth year after the Hijrah, even though Makkah had been conquered in the eighth year after the Hijrah?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) liberated the Ka'bah from the idols and paganism. After the state of Islam was firmly established, the liberation of the "makin" (the people who dwell beside the Sacred House) began. There had to be a purification that would place the believers on one side and the disbelievers, the People of the Book and the hypocrites on the other side, and this happened in the ninth year after the Hijrah, so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not perform the Hajj except while the place was liberated, the mosque was liberated and the people were liberated. Therefore the Exalted, through this verse, made clear to those who had covenants between them and Muhammad (ﷺ): "You are not worthy of security or of fulfilling covenants; therefore We have cut off these covenants." This severance was not by human will from Muhammad and his companions, but a severance by the command of Allah the Exalted. It is possible for people to know some things while other things remain hidden from them. But the Supreme World said: ﴿A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger﴾ (al-Tawbah: 1), and did not say "a disavowal from Allah and a disavowal from the Messenger," because it is one single disavowal, issuing from Allah, the Supreme Legislator, and conveyed by the Final Messenger. The disavowal is directed at the polytheists with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a covenant.

We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) had an alliance with the tribe of Khuza'ah, and there was an opposing tribe called the tribe of Bakr, allied with the Quraysh. The Quraysh aided the tribe of Bakr against the tribe of Khuza'ah. A poet of Khuza'ah, 'Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i, went to Madinah and recited the famous qasidah, of which these verses are part:

O Lord, I appeal to Muhammad, [by] the alliance of our father and his father, the ancient one.

You were a father to us and we were a child; then we became Muslims and did not withdraw a hand.

So help, may Allah guide you, with a mighty help, and call the servants of Allah that they may come with reinforcements.

Indeed the Quraysh have broken their promise to you and violated your firm covenant.

They attacked us by night at al-Watir while we were prostrate, and they killed us while we were bowing and prostrating.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that, he said: "You have been helped, O 'Amr ibn Salim, and I shall surely help you."

So the polytheists were the ones who first broke the covenant, and they became those to whom no trust could be given, because they do not respect any covenant or treaty. The word of the Exalted came down: ﴿A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾ (al-Tawbah).

The address here is to the Muslims, and the disavowal is from the polytheists.

The revelation that came after that was the saying of the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted One: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾ (9:2).

The address here is to the polytheists. Some have asked: how can it be that the address of the Truth in the first verse is to the Muslims, declaring disavowal from the polytheists, and then an address comes from Allah to the polytheists? Some scholars said: since the disavowal was issued by Allah, it is as if Allah, exalted is He, is saying to the believers, "Say to the polytheists: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾" (al-Tawbah: 2).

But we answer this by saying that a covenant is between two parties, and therefore there must be an address to those who broke it and an address to those whose covenant was broken. The address to those who broke it is expressed in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾ (al-Tawbah: 1).

His address to those whose covenant was broken is expressed in His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾ (al-Tawbah: 2).

Among the gentleness of this religion which the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted One revealed is that the Lord, glorified is He, grants a period of grace to those with whom the covenant was terminated. So He gave them a period of four months, so that it would not be said that Islam seized them unawares. Rather, He gave them four months; and whoever had a covenant longer than four months, the covenant will continue until its appointed term.

﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾ (al-Tawbah: 2).

The word "fa-sihu" (travel freely) gives a faithful assurance. "Saha" means to travel slowly. There is "saha al-shay'" and "sala al-shay'": when you say "sala al-ma'" (the water flowed), meaning it gushed and flowed, and you see it flowing. And if you say "saha al-samn" (the ghee melted), meaning it moved slowly, imperceptibly, until it became liquid. Why did the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted One say ﴿fa-sihu fi al-ard﴾ ("so travel freely in the land")?

The answer: the gentleness of Islam prevents it from seizing you unawares, and those with whom Islam terminated the covenant should travel while reassured and in security, and no one should attack them. The scholars paused over the determination of the four months. Some looked to the date of revelation: this verse was revealed in Shawwal; therefore the four months are: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram.

Other scholars said: the moment of revelation has no connection with the four months, and the four months begin from the moment of proclamation, that is, at the Hajj, because Allah, exalted is He, says:

﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the Day of the Greater Hajj﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3).

Accordingly, they run from the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah to the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir. Some scholars said: the revelation of this verse was in the year of al-nasi' (intercalation), in which the disbelievers would postpone and advance within the sacred months, and about which Allah, glorified is He, said:

﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and make it forbidden another year, in order to conform to the number of what Allah has forbidden﴾ (al-Tawbah: 37).

The Prophet (ﷺ) also added, in his sermon which Abu Bakrah narrated, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) addressed the people in his farewell pilgrimage and said: "Behold, time has revolved to its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive ones, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." (1) That is, the Prophet (ﷺ) reckoned from the beginning of creation until this time, and so he returned the matter to its proper footing and abolished al-nasi', which they used to establish in the days of polytheism to advance or postpone the sacred months. For when the sacred months came and they wanted to fight, they would postpone the sacred month so that they could continue the fighting. Therefore the Hajj in that year fell in the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah. And since the Hajj was in Dhu al-Qa'dah, the four months end on the tenth of Rabi' al-Awwal. It was said that the choice of four months came to accord with what Allah legislated in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred﴾ (al-Tawbah: 36), so that the number of months corresponds to the number of sacred months. But this time there are only three sacred months: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram, and the fourth month is Rajab, so how is it said "four"?

We say: the four sacred months which include Rajab are the permanently sacred months. As for the four months mentioned in this verse, they are four months of covenant which end when they end. But the four original sacred months remain forbidden forever. Allah, mighty and majestic, legislated the sacred months so that the blood of people might be made inviolate from people, for wars among the Arabs used to continue for many years without decisive victory. So Allah made the sacred months so that people would incline toward peace, reason would govern, and wars would end.

Here the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted One informs us that He has given the polytheists four months in which they may travel in safety. Why? Because the one who is weak against his opponent seizes any opportunity he can to exploit it and finish him off, and does not grant him four months, nor even four days. But the strong does not mind extending the term for his opponent, because he can bring him to account at any moment. Therefore the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted One says: ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾ (al-Tawbah: 2).

It is said "fulan a'jaza fulanan," meaning he made him weak and incapable. Therefore every "i'jaz" (inability to overcome) is an honour to the one who is rendered unable: for example, when the noble Qur'an came as a miracle (i'jaz) to the Arabs, that was an honour to them, because they were a nation of eloquence and rhetoric. Allah does not challenge the weak; He challenges the strong. The language of the Qur'an rendered the eloquent and the rhetorician incapable. When the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted One gives the polytheists this period, it was on certain terms. The Commander of the Hajj that year was our master Abu Bakr, and he was the one who would proclaim the disavowal. Its terms were: no polytheist may enter the Sacred Mosque, no polytheist may perform Hajj, no one may circumambulate the House naked, and none will enter Paradise except the believer. These are the terms.

But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with his prophetic acuity, knew that the Arabs would not accept the annulment of covenants and pacts except from their own people. So he sent our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib to announce the annulment of the covenants, because he knew that the disbelievers would say: "We do not accept the annulment of the covenant from Abu Bakr; rather it must be from one of the family of the one who annuls it."

When the Lord, glorified is He, said: ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾ (al-Tawbah: 2), He granted this long period, because whatever they do during this period, Allah prevails over His affair. Nothing escapes or is hidden from Him, glorified is He; and however much they try to find allies for themselves, they will be able to accomplish nothing against Allah. True, they are weak during this period, and true, the weak one's power against the strong may be lethal, because he knows his opportunity is single, and if he cannot overcome his opponent he will be finished; but Allah prevails over His affair. The Arab poet wished to express this and said:

"A weak one, when it hits an opportunity, kills; likewise is the power of the weak."

Because the weak seizes the opportunity to finish off his opponent, whereas the strong knows that he is able to overcome his opponent at any time. Then the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted One says:

﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾ (al-Tawbah: 2). Ikhza' is humiliation through disgrace and shame, and this happens only to one who was arrogant and haughty. That is, Allah is able to disgrace the disbelievers with disgrace and shame, however great their strength and arrogance.

1 Narrated by Imam Ahmad, and recorded by al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 9, verse 3:

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says after that:

﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and [so is] His Messenger. So if you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you will not cause Allah to fail [in punishing you]. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.﴾

Some people say: since Allah, the Exalted, has already said ﴿[This is] a declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger﴾ (al-Tawbah: 1),

why then does He, glorified and exalted, repeat ﴿that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and [so is] His Messenger﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3)?

We say: The disassociation (bara'ah) came as an announcement of the principle, and the proclamation (adhan) came to convey the disassociation. And "adhan" means an announcement that reaches all the people, exactly like the adhan for prayer; it is an announcement to the people that the time of prayer has come. And adhan is derived from "udhn" (ear), because when a person informs people of something, he must address them so that they hear his words with their ears. For this reason you find that the ear is the first means of perception: before you see, you hear, and before you speak, you must hear; if you do not hear the one who speaks, you cannot speak yourself. Therefore the Truth, majestic is His majesty, says:

﴿Deaf, dumb﴾ (al-Baqarah: 18): that is, they do not hear, and as long as they do not hear, they do not speak. Some may come and say: the means of information may depend on the eye, and a person reads from it. But whoever says this forgets that a person cannot read unless he has heard the sounds of the letters, and when it is said to him: this is alif, this is ba', this is ta', then he is learning. So every communication begins with the ear, and the ear is the first organ of perception to perform its task immediately upon a person's birth, for if you point your finger at the eyes of a child who is a few days old, he is not affected. This is because the eye does not begin to perform its task until some days later; but if you shout beside the child, he hears and is startled.

When Allah, glorified and exalted, speaks of the means of perception, He mentions hearing first, saying, majestic is His majesty: ﴿And He made for you hearing, sight and hearts﴾ (al-Nahl: 78), because the ear begins its work immediately, as we have said, while the eye does not begin its work until after four or five days. With the ear we receive many sounds at one time, but the field of vision is limited. When you do not want to see something, you turn your eyes away from it, but sounds reach your ear from every place without your being able to prevent them. Therefore hearing comes in the singular, while sights come in the plural, because this one sees something and that one sees something else. But with the ear you hear while asleep or awake, and sounds come to you and the perceived unites through hearing; it is the instrument of calling and of waking. Therefore when God spoke of the People of the Cave, He intended to put them to sleep for three hundred years and nine more, although the longest a person sleeps is a day or part of a day. He, glorified and exalted, said about them in this matter:

﴿So We struck over their ears in the cave for a number of years﴾ (al-Kahf: 11). The striking upon their ears was so that no loud sound from a person or an animal would wake them. And when they arose, they said: ﴿We have remained a day or part of a day﴾ (al-Kahf: 19), because a person customarily does not sleep longer than this period. This shows that when they awoke they were in the same state in which they had slept, nothing in them had changed, which indicates that Allah suspended the effect of time upon them. Had Allah not struck upon their ears, a sound of thunder, or wild animals, or other sounds would have woken them. Modern science has also established that a person who lies in bed for a long time due to illness is feared by doctors to develop bedsores, so the doctor is concerned for the patient not only about the illness but also about the effects of lying still upon the body. Allah draws our attention to this fact when He says:

﴿And We turn them to the right and to the left﴾ (al-Kahf: 18). And because the ear is the means of hearing, we find the Truth, glorified and exalted, saying: ﴿When the sky is split open, and it has listened to its Lord and it is obligated [to do so]﴾ (al-Inshiqaq: 1-2). This statement shows that the sky, upon hearing the command from Allah to split, responds immediately and obeys His command to split, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. And if the one who conveyed the proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to all people on the day of the pilgrimage was 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, then how is it said:

﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3)?

We say: Allah, the Exalted, informed His Messenger, and the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, informed 'Ali, and 'Ali is the one who said: "He proclaimed and conveyed," since Allah requested the conveying to the people, even though the disassociation was for the polytheists.

We say: the announcement was for all people, for the believer and the non-believer alike, so that all people would know their position: the believer knows that the covenant has been cut, and the non-believer knows that the covenant has been cut, so no one is seized unawares, and each person arranges his position in light of the proclamation issued by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, glorified and exalted, wished for the balance to be upheld in the hands of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; therefore He addresses not the believers alone, but the address is to the whole world, although it is the believers who will strive so that the movement of the earth may harmonize with the method of the heavens. From this both believer and unbeliever benefit, because all will profit from the justice, trustworthiness and integrity that the method establishes on earth.

For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted, draws our attention to the fact that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, came with the method to reform the whole universe, and He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you﴾ (al-Nisa: 105): that is, judging between all people is what is required of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, according to the method of the heavens.

As for His, glorified and exalted, saying:

﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3): this statement contains generality in place and generality in the one addressed, since on the day of pilgrimage all people gather in one place.

Some may ask: why is it called the greater pilgrimage? We say: because it is the only pilgrimage in which disbelievers and believers gathered together, and after that there was no pilgrimage for disbelievers or polytheists.

Some exegetes say: the phrase "the greater pilgrimage" came to distinguish between the lesser pilgrimage, which is the 'umrah, and the pilgrimage in which standing at 'Arafat takes place. We say: the 'umrah is not called the lesser pilgrimage.

It has been said that the day of the greater pilgrimage is the day of 'Arafah. But some scholars said: it is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), because in it there are many rites: stoning the jamarat, shortening the hair, and the tawaf al-ifadah; therefore the day of sacrifice was called the greater pilgrimage because of the abundance of its rites. It has also been said: it refers to all the days of the pilgrimage, and that they were called "the day of pilgrimage" according to the Arab manner of describing a single event by its appropriate time-frame. Did not the Truth, glorified and exalted, say: "the day of Hunayn"? Hunayn lasted for days, so the day is meant as a container for a great event, and thus all the days of the pilgrimage may be called "the day of the pilgrimage."

Or the proclamation was made by our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, on the day of 'Arafah, and whoever heard this announcement conveyed it to others. The noble verse says:

﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and [so is] His Messenger﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3).

This is therefore a proclamation from Allah to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, from His Messenger to 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, from 'Ali to the believers, and from the believers to those who had not heard: that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists. This was an announcement of severance, but Allah, in His mercy, never closes the door before His servants, and therefore He says:

﴿So if you repent, it is better for you﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3).

That is, He opened for them the door of repentance; if they repent, Allah pardons them, and if they do not repent, the decisive word is:

﴿But if you turn away, then know that you will not cause Allah to fail [in punishing you]. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3).

So the Truth, glorified and exalted, is capable over them and capable of bringing them, whatever they may be. The Prophet and those who convey from him must give the disbelievers tidings of a painful punishment. Tidings (bushra) is the announcement of a pleasant news, and warning (indhar) is the announcement of something evil. So is punishment a tiding or a warning? We say: the beauty of the style of the Noble Qur'an is that it gives the disbelievers tidings, so they expect pleasant news; then it gives them the bad news of the punishment awaiting them. Just as when you come to a person suffering from severe thirst, then bring him a cup of chilled water, and when he reaches it and nearly touches his lips, you pour it onto the ground, which is an increase in torment and an increase in grief; the soul expands first and then comes the contraction.

On this the poet says:

As a cloud flashed lightning over thirsty people,
then when they saw it, it dispersed and vanished.

Thus the sting is a double sting: a beginning of hope and an ending of despair, whereas in a warning there is only a single sting. Consider His saying, blessed and exalted:

﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved﴾ (al-Kahf: 29).

When you hear "they will be relieved," you expect deliverance, but the answer comes:

﴿They will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces﴾ (al-Kahf: 29).

Here the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿But if you turn away, then know that you will not cause Allah to fail [in punishing you]. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾ (al-Tawbah: 3). The punishment from Allah is described once as great, another time as humiliating, and a third time as painful, and the reason is that the description differs according to the people punished. Every wrongdoer, disobedient one and disbeliever will receive the punishment that suits him. There is a person who can bear punishment but cannot bear humiliation, and there is a person who can bear humiliation but cannot bear pain. So it is as if each one of the people will be given the punishment that wears him down: if only great punishment wears him down, it comes to him; if only humiliation wears him down, it comes to him; and if only pain wears him down, it comes to him.

Almighty Allah says:

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists, then they have not fallen short of you in anything, nor have they supported anyone against you. So complete for them their covenant until their term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous (al-muttaqin). (4)﴾

This is an exception, but it is an exception conditioned on those people having been trustworthy in the covenant and fulfilling it, and not having fallen short in any respect. That is, they did not block your trade, did not seize your livestock, did not steal your weapons, did not incite anyone against you, and did not support anyone against you. These were the Banu Damrah and the Banu Kinanah, and nothing happened from them against the believers, so the command came that the covenant should continue with them until its term. It may be said: an exception requires something excepted from. We say: the thing excepted from is the polytheists in the words of Almighty Allah: ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists, then they have not fallen short of you in anything, nor have they supported anyone against you﴾ (al-Tawbah: 4).

Al-Inqas (falling short, diminishing) means reducing the quantity, either in the persons themselves or in what pertains to the persons. Diminishing in the persons occurs through killing, and diminishing in what pertains to the persons occurs through confiscating trade or livestock and stealing weapons.

So there are two stages of diminishing here: a stage concerning the persons, namely by killing, and a stage concerning what follows the persons, which are the possessions owned. For this reason He said: "they have not fallen short of you in anything", that is, in any thing whatsoever, whether in persons, in sins, or in what pertains to persons. Likewise, they did not raid you or encourage anyone to any act against the Messenger.

﴿Nor have they supported anyone against you﴾ (al-Tawbah: 4).

Yuzahiru (to support, to back) means to assist, and all these words are derived from the root "dhahr" (back). It bears more than the hand does: a person cannot carry a sack of wheat in his hand, for instance, but he can carry it on his back.

For this reason the colloquial proverb says: "He who has a back is not beaten on his belly." So the back is for support.

And Almighty Allah says: ﴿Then We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, so they became dominant﴾ (al-Saff: 14).

That is, uppermost.

And when Almighty Allah related to us the account of some of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) plotting against him, He said: ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that are his supporters﴾ (al-Tahrim: 4).

Here, "zahir" in the noble verse means helper. The Almighty comes here to the locus of strength in a person, which is why it is said: "So-and-so supports my back," meaning he helps me with strength. "So-and-so overcame so-and-so" means he defeated him and surpassed him. And it is said: "He mounted his back," meaning he seized the locus of his strength.

For this reason we find that when Almighty Allah spoke in Surat al-Kahf about Dhul-Qarnayn, He mentioned some scenes and said:

﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand any speech. They said: "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land, so shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?" He said: "What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength; I will make between you and them a rampart."﴾ (al-Kahf: 93–95).

Here Allah draws our attention to a scientific fact that we did not know until modern times. A dam built entirely of solid material is exposed to collapse if a tremor comes that affects all its sides. But if there is a part of solid construction at the edge, a small part in the middle, and a third part, then a fourth, with a layer of earth fill separating each part, then the fill has breathing spaces so that it absorbs the shock. This is the same idea as the sponge with which we surround things we fear will break, to protect them. If the box were of wood, iron, or any solid material, the object placed in it would be shattered by a strong impact on the ground; but if we surround it with a sponge cushion, it absorbs the shocks. Dams that receive shocks in this way are called rubble dams (al-sadd al-rukami).

We turn to the words of Almighty Allah: ﴿So help me with strength﴾ (al-Kahf: 95). This shows us that the strong must help the weak with a help that does not leave them needing him again. For this reason it is said: "Do not give the hungry a fish, but teach him to fish, so that he may depend on himself afterward." This is true assistance. And for this reason we find that Dhul-Qarnayn refused to take payment for building the rampart, because it is the duty of the strong on earth, those possessing faith-energy, to prevent injustice without compensation until the balance of life is set right, since the weak may not have what he could pay the strong. If every strong person demanded a price for supporting the weak, the balance of the universe would be disrupted and people would become tyrannical. But the strong in our world want to oppress by their strength; therefore the balance of the universe in which we live is disrupted. Let us look at Allah's entrusting of Dhul-Qarnayn, and how Dhul-Qarnayn judged well among people, established justice among them, and how he watched over the wrongdoers. The Noble Qur'an related, on the tongue of Dhul-Qarnayn:

﴿He said: "As for one who wrongs, we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment. But as for one who believes and does righteous deeds, he will have a reward of the best."﴾ (al-Kahf: 87–88).

Thus Dhul-Qarnayn established justice, by punishing the wrongdoer and honouring the believer who does righteous deeds.

The words of Almighty Allah on the tongue of Dhul-Qarnayn, "help me" (a'inuni), show us how justice is managed in the universe. He whom Allah has given the means, if he wishes to help the weak, must make them partners with him in the work; he must not work while they watch, for they would become accustomed to idleness and the determination of each of them would be corrupted. But if he has them work with him, they will learn the work and master it, and their skill and strength in facing life will increase. For this reason Dhul-Qarnayn included the weak with him and said to them: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾ (al-Kahf: 96).

So he had them work with him and build, and this is the trust of the strong concerning the strength Allah has given him. Indeed, we find that he reached understanding with them, although Almighty Allah said of them: ﴿who can hardly understand any speech﴾ (al-Kahf: 93). How did he reach understanding with them? Perhaps he used sign language and devices so that they would grasp his intent. The Qur'an shows us their understanding of him when Allah related on their tongue: ﴿They said: "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land, so shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you make a barrier between us and them?"﴾ (al-Kahf: 94).

The building of the barrier was completed with the help of these weak people, and the construction of this barrier was such that it defied the aggressive power of both Gog and Magog. Each of them tried to climb over the barrier to overcome it, but it was beyond the capacity of each of them, so they could not breach it. The Lord, glorified and exalted, clarified this in His saying:

﴿So they were unable to scale it, nor were they able to pierce it.﴾ (al-Kahf: 97).

Thus the saying of Almighty Allah: ﴿Nor have they supported anyone against you, so complete for them their covenant until their term﴾ (al-Tawbah: 4): that is, they did not help or assist any of your enemies so that he would overcome you. His, glorified and exalted, permitting the completion of the term of the covenant means that this term was more than four months.

Thus He, glorified, gives us the majesty of His justice: He allowed those with whom the covenant was less than four months to take a respite of four months. Almighty Allah does not love the breaking of covenants, so He commanded the believers to give the polytheists with whom they had covenants the term of the covenant, even if it was more than four months, so that the believer learns to fulfil the covenant as long as the other party respects it. The extension of the term there, or the increase of the respite, stems from the strength and power of Almighty Allah, because all who are on earth cannot escape Allah; whether the term is long or short, it will not give the polytheists any advantage, for Allah can seize them at any time and in any place.

Almighty Allah concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous (al-muttaqin)﴾ (al-Tawbah: 4). The muttaqun (the righteous, the God-conscious) are those who place between themselves and anything that angers Allah a shield (wiqayah). As for some people's wonder at the saying of Almighty Allah, "Fear Allah" (ittaqu Allah), and His saying, "fear the Fire" (ittaqu al-nar), we say: the meaning of ﴿ittaqu Allah﴾ is: place between yourselves and the attributes of majesty (al-jabarut) of Allah a shield. Guard against the attributes of majesty in Allah so that His punishment does not reach you. Allah has attributes of majesty, among them al-Muntaqim, al-Jabbar, and al-Qahhar, and He has attributes of beauty, such as al-Rahim, al-Wahhab, al-Razzaq, and al-Fattah. So place between yourselves and the attributes of majesty in Allah a shield and protection for you against being exposed to the anger of Allah, Exalted. A person guards against the attributes of majesty in Allah by following His method and obeying Him in all that He has commanded, so that he may receive from the overflow of the attributes of beauty. And the saying of Almighty Allah: ﴿Fear the Fire﴾ means: place between yourselves and the Fire a shield, so that the Fire does not touch you.

Then the Almighty and Exalted says:

﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and seize them, and besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go on their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And "insalakha" means that the sacred months have ended and passed. The root "salakha" and "insalakha" all revolve around the removal of something that is attached to something else. You say "salakhat al-shah" (I skinned the sheep), meaning I removed the hide from the flesh, and the hide is attached to the flesh very tightly. It is as if Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to draw our attention to the fact that the sacred months are a time, and time is a container; people are contained within time and place. So it is as if the sacred months surround them as a protection from the believers, and when the sacred months pass, this protection is removed from them, having previously been attached to them. And "insilakh" has two uses: sometimes one says "yansalikh al-shay' 'an al-shay'" (a thing is stripped off from a thing), and sometimes "yansalikh al-shay' min al-shay'" (a thing is stripped from a thing). Therefore you find in the Noble Qur'an the saying of the Blessed and Exalted:

﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our verses, but he detached himself from them (fa-insalakha minha)﴾ (al-A'raf: 175)

This noble verse was revealed concerning Ibn Ba'ura', whom Allah had given knowledge, wisdom and the verses, but he neglected them and abandoned them. It is as if he was the one who stripped himself away by his own will, and they were not stripped from him; and thus he became the counterpart of the sheep, for we strip the hide of the sheep from the sheep.

And the Almighty and Exalted also says:

﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip the day from it (nuslakhu minhu al-nahar)﴾ (Ya Sin: 37)

So it is as if the night is like the slaughtered animal; then the day comes and strips the darkness from it, removing it from it and bringing light. It is as if the night is a black garment upon which a white garment, which is the day, comes; when the time of night arrives, the white garment is lifted, or the light is stripped from the darkness of the night, so that the world becomes filled with the darkness of night. It is as if light is what comes upon darkness and clothes it in whiteness; that is, light is what comes and goes, while darkness is present. When the light of the sun comes to it, it becomes day, and when it is stripped from it, it becomes night.

And what happens when the sacred months end? The Almighty and Exalted says: ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and seize them, and besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ (al-Tawbah: 5). So it is as if Allah, glorified and exalted, after giving the polytheists a respite of four months, and those who had a covenant more than that are left until the term of the covenant ends, after which the punishment for the polytheist is killing, and why? Because two religions cannot coexist in this place.

And someone may say: where then is freedom of religion? We say: there is a difference between an environment in which the Qur'an was revealed in the language of its people, and to a messenger from among themselves, whom they know well and know his history and past, and an environment that has its own rulings by virtue of the revelation. Those among whom the Qur'an was revealed and in whose land the message came through a messenger from among them, who was a trusted person whom they knew for his truthfulness and trustworthiness, and whom they entrusted with every precious and valuable thing they owned, and all of that was a prelude to the message; and the prelude was sufficient: if he said to them, "I am the Messenger of Allah," they would not have called him a liar, because if he had not lied to them throughout the forty years he lived among them, would he lie about Allah? One who does not lie about a creature, would he lie about Allah? This is speech that does not agree with reason and logic; therefore the Almighty and Exalted says: ﴿a messenger from among yourselves﴾ (al-Tawbah: 128), meaning: he is not a stranger to you; you know him well, to the extent that you used to entrust him with the most precious of what you own, and you called him "the Trustworthy" in all matters of worldly life. So how would the trustworthy become untruthful in your eyes? Moreover, the noble Qur'an, which is the miracle of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, came in your language and style, of the same kind as that in which you excelled, so it was a miracle for you; and Allah challenged you to produce a surah like it, and you were unable, though you are the kings of eloquence and rhetoric. So it is as if the miracle is from the trustworthiness and truthfulness of the Messenger, and the miracle of the Qur'an's eloquence and its challenge requires belief from you; therefore non-belief here is obstinacy which calls for a severe punishment.

If someone asks: where is freedom of religion, and where is the implementation of the saying of the Truthful and Exalted:

﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾ (al-Baqarah: 256).

We say: Yes, there is no compulsion in your believing in Allah and believing in His religion; but as long as you have believed, you must commit to what this belief requires. As for the consideration of the principle of religious adherence, you are free to believe in Allah or not to believe.

But if you believe, then it is necessary for us to demand that you commit. Then Allah, the Truthful and Exalted, willed that two religions should never coexist in the Arabian Peninsula.

But in any other place, such as Persia and Byzantium, they would not know the miraculous nature of the Noble Qur'an as a language, but they would hear that it contains lofty meanings and effective laws that organize life and elevate it.

As for those who know the Messenger and the eloquence of the miracle he brought, nothing will be accepted from them except that they embrace Islam, and it is not accepted from them that they remain in the land of the message without Islam; and if they wish to remain in polytheism, let them depart far from this land.

And there are those who say: Islam spread by the sword or by the jizyah. We say: Islam spread by example. As for the sword, it was a defense of the right to choose one's creed in the lands that Islam entered as conqueror, and the jizyah was in exchange for protection for those who wished to remain upon their religion.

And we find in our daily life someone who uses "There is no compulsion in religion" in other than its proper place: when a Muslim says to another, "Why do you not pray?", he responds with this saying: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾.

We say: "There is no compulsion in religion" concerns the very essence of religiosity, that is, the matter of your acknowledgment that you are a Muslim or otherwise. But as long as you have declared Islam and are counted among the Muslims, you must commit to what religion has obligated upon you, so you do not drink wine or commit adultery. Thus "There is no compulsion in religion" means there is no compulsion to choose Islam, but there must be care, on the part of those who have declared Islam, for the requirements of the religion.

So why were the Arabs compelled to Islam?

Two reasons have been stated for this: the first is that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was from among them; and the second is that the miracle came in their tongue.

The Almighty and Exalted continues: ﴿and seize them, and besiege them﴾ (al-Tawbah: 5).

If it is difficult for you to kill them, then take them as captives, as long as they have not defended themselves by fighting you and have not threatened your lives; here blood is preserved and they are benefited from as captives.

And if you fear their evils, then confine them in a supervised place. When they make any hostile movement, it will be easy for you to detect it and inflict punishment upon them. Here "al-hasr" means restricting movement while permitting them limited movement, such that they do not disappear from your sight.

Then the Exalted Master continues: ﴿and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ (al-Tawbah: 5).

That is, watch their movements until you are safe from their deception, and so that they do not connect with one another and form a bloc hostile to Islam. Watch their movements, watch their speech, and watch their actions; do not let them escape your oversight, and do what you can to be safe from their evils. But do not carry the surveillance into the domain of humiliating them, for "al-istidlal" (seeking evidence/inquiry) is not "al-istidhlal" (humiliation).

Someone may ask: why this difference in punishment, where there is killing, and there is confinement, and there is watching them on their roads and paths? We say: the punishment differs according to the degree of the polytheists' enmity toward Islam. There are the leaders of disbelief who fight this religion, call people to non-belief, incite fighting, killing and harming the Muslims, and never reform, and never cease their harm to the believers: for those, their recompense is killing.

And there are those who do not harm the Muslims but openly oppose the call; their status is lesser, so we take them as captives. And there are disbelievers who do nothing except that they are not believers; for these we monitor their movements so that the Muslims may be protected from their evil, and remain constantly prepared to confront them should they turn to harm and attack the Muslims and fight them.

Thus one uniform punishment will not be imposed on all, because they are not equal in their enmity to Islam: the leaders of disbelief have one ruling, and those whose enmity to Islam is less have another ruling. Then comes the mercy of Allah, the Exalted; for He, glorified and exalted, is merciful to His servants, and never despairs them of returning to Him, so He says: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go on their way; indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (al-Tawbah).

And Allah, glorified and exalted, opens the door of repentance before all His servants and never closes it. Therefore the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said, as narrated from him by Abu Hamza Anas ibn Malik, the servant of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ("Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than any one of you who has lost his camel in a desert wilderness...")(1)(2)

Meaning: you, while traveling in a barren desert far from any habitation, sat down to rest, with your camel on which is your water, food and all your means of life; then you became heedless of the camel, and it ran off wandering into the desert, and when you awoke you did not find it and did not know where it was; then suddenly, as you were walking without direction, you found the camel before you. How would your joy be? It is without doubt a very great joy, because you have found what saves you from destruction, and this joy fills the soul and overwhelms it completely. Likewise Allah rejoices at the repentance of His servants. Therefore the Almighty explains that if these disbelievers repent from their enmity toward the religion of Allah and His Messenger, and establish prayer and give zakah, then the Muslims should let them go and leave them free.

Here we find three conditions: first, repentance and return to faith; second, establishing prayer; then the third condition, giving zakah. All three must be performed together, because repentance from disbelief is entry into the fold of faith, and entry into the fold of faith requires the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; then establishing prayer, then giving zakah, then fasting Ramadan, then pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it.

If you look at the five pillars of Islam, you will find that a Muslim may perform some of them and not others: a poor Muslim who has only the necessities of life is excused from zakah and excused from pilgrimage, and a Muslim with chronic illness is excused from fasting, while the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah remains, which a Muslim need only say once in his life; and the pillar of establishing prayer never falls, neither in poverty nor in wealth, neither in health nor in sickness, because prayer is what distinguishes the Muslim from the non-Muslim, and it is the pillar of religion, since it is repeated five times every day. The sick person must pray according to his ability: if he cannot perform it standing, then sitting, and if he cannot perform it sitting, then lying down.

We know that every prayer includes all the pillars of Islam: in every prayer we testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; and every prayer includes zakah, because zakah is giving out part of one's wealth to the poor, and wealth comes from work, and work requires time, and prayer takes some of the time you could use for work, by which you earn wealth to pay zakah; so it is as if in praying you have given part of your wealth to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, because you took the time in which you could have worked and earned money for zakah; thus prayer contains the zakah of time.

Time is what we need in the movement of life to obtain wealth, so in prayer there is zakah. Next we come to fasting, and in fasting you are refraining from desire.

---
(1) Stumbled upon (or: lost) ..
(2) Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Thus, if the polytheists do not repent, do not establish prayer, and do not pay zakat, and the Muslims are unable to overpower them, what happens? It is incumbent upon the Muslims to try to implement what Allah, glorified and exalted, has commanded concerning them.

But what if one of the polytheists seeks protection from the Muslims?

Here the word of the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted, descends:

﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah, then convey him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.﴾ (6)

After Allah, glorified and exalted, explained the respite, which is the four months, or the period of the covenant if there is a covenant, and after He explained that the disbelievers who repent, establish prayer, give zakat, and combine faith with action, Allah, the Truth, forgives them what has passed from them, and He explained the greatness of Islam and the mercy with which this religion was sent down. He informs us that those disbelievers who did not repent and remained in their state, and whom we were unable to subject to any of the punishments that had been prescribed, then one of them came seeking protection from the believers, what should our conduct be toward him?

The ruling from Allah, may He be exalted, is that since he has sought your protection, grant him protection. When you have granted him protection, let him hear the words of Allah, and try to guide him to faith and to the straight path. If he believes, is convinced, and declares his Islam, he becomes one of the Muslims. If he does not hear the words of Allah and is not convinced, do not kill him, but convey him to his place of safety. That is, ask him where he has come from. If he tells you the name of the tribe to which he belongs, or specifies the place from which he came, then ensure that he will be safe until he reaches the place where he finds security. This is the final stage of the relationship between faith and disbelief, the stage of granting safe conduct and providing security to those who seek protection from the believers.

Allah, glorified and exalted, showed favor to His creatures on earth by sending to them His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and this occurred after a long period had passed since the sending of those messengers who preceded him. People had forgotten the methodology of heaven, and indeed the People of the Book had distorted what had been revealed to them of teachings.

It was necessary for heaven to intervene by sending the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, Muhammad (ﷺ), because the Truth, glorified and exalted, has placed in faith multiple safeguards. The first is within the self: when the self yearns for disobedience, the faithful conscience restrains it from that disobedience, and the person repents and returns to Allah, exalted is He, from his own self and by his faithful conscience. This is the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah). The existence of self-reproach within the self means that faith still exists within it, and this faith is what restrains desire, prevents the self from inclining toward disobedience, and returns its owner to the right path and the sound methodology.

Suppose a self became infatuated with violating the methodology and ceased to be a self-reproaching soul, and continued to commit sins until it became accustomed to sin, and the faithful restraint within it died. Then you find it has fallen in love, and we seek refuge in Allah, with violating the methodology, indeed it has become a soul that commands evil (al-nafs al-ammarah bi-l-su'). Here Allah transfers the faithful safeguard from the self to those around it among the servants of Allah. You find that those surrounding the self, from among the servants of Allah, you find those surrounding the one who commits sins restrain him from sin, and they take toward him the positions of faith: deterrence, boycott, and harshness, until he returns to his Lord and comes back to his right mind. This is a second stage of the stages of faith. But if society as a whole becomes corrupt and there is no longer a group that enjoins good and forbids evil, then heaven must intervene with a new message and a new messenger, supported by a miracle from heaven, to awaken people from this sleep which has encompassed individuals and communities.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and confronted this society in which disbelief had spread among individuals and groups, a clash was bound to occur between faith and the society of disbelief, because fierce hostility confronted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This confrontation with the Messenger came only from those who profit from corruption on earth. Those who profit from corruption are the chiefs who benefited from the loss of truth and the spread of falsehood. They took the rights of others, enslaved people, monopolized benefits and whatever was good for them, and denied that to the rest of Allah's servants.

Those who profit from corruption hate every reformer who comes to correct the balance of life's movement in the universe. Therefore they must stand against him, to defend their sovereignty, their interests, and their wealth, which they obtained through falsehood and injustice, and through their enslavement of people. At that time the Arabian Peninsula was composed of many tribes, and each tribe had its own law, which its shaykh established so that he might monopolize everything for himself.

This means there was no bond connecting these tribes, and no general law governing them. Each tribe had its own strength, its own might, and its own wars. Every individual in a tribe had to be a fighter carrying his weapon, ready for war at any time, because he was threatened at any moment by another tribe raiding him, except for one tribe, Quraysh. Quraysh had attained sovereignty; no one attacked them, their caravans were not raided, and no tribe in the north or the south could attack their trade, because all these tribes would one day come intending the pilgrimage to the Sacred House of Allah in Makkah. During the pilgrimage these tribes needed security from Quraysh. Therefore all the Arab tribes were keen to maintain their relationship with Quraysh, because the sovereignty over the Sacred House of Allah, which Allah had granted to Quraysh, was the guarantee. Allah, glorified and exalted, took upon Himself the protection of the Sacred House from any aggression, even when Abraha came with his elephants to demolish the Ka'bah; Allah made him and his army like chewed-up husks, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plot into misguidance? And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and He made them like eaten straw.﴾ (al-Fil, 1-5)

If you read the surah that comes directly after Surat al-Fil, you find that it says:

﴿For the accustomed security of Quraysh, their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer. So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.﴾ (Quraysh, 1-4)

It is as if preserving the Ka'bah from demolition was Allah's preservation of Quraysh's sovereignty. Therefore it was obligatory for Quraysh to receive the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with faith and gratitude, and to understand this blessing and appreciate it, instead of taking this obstinate stance toward Islam and waging this terrible war against it. But instead, the opposite happened: Quraysh, falsely imagining that Islam had come to threaten their sovereignty, rose up to fight it.

Given that this is the case, why were the calls to Islam not made at a distance from this sovereignty? Because the Truth willed that the cry of truth should sound within the tyranny of falsehood, and that Islam in its first days should confront the tyranny of all the chiefs of the Arabian Peninsula, so that Allah might test the hearts of the early Muslims. They are the ones who would later carry the call of Islam throughout the world. Thus no hypocrite or weak believer would embrace Islam; rather, those who embrace it are those in whose hearts there is true faith, and who bear every form of persecution and torture through the strength of their faith.

Allah, the Truth, blessed and exalted, willed that Islam should begin in Makkah, but He did not make victory for Islam come from Makkah. He willed, glorified and exalted, that the victory of Islam should come from Madinah. This is because if Quraysh had been victorious through the call of one of their own, they would have tried to absorb him in order to rule the world with him, and then it would be said: they are a people who were partisan toward one of their own so that sovereignty would remain theirs, and embracing Islam would be hypocrisy rather than true faith. Therefore Allah, glorified and exalted, made the victory of Islam come from Madinah, so that all people would know that partisanship toward Muhammad (ﷺ) did not create faith in the message of Muhammad, peace be upon him; rather, faith in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) is what created partisanship toward Muhammad, peace be upon him.

Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted, willed that there be a fierce confrontation between the bearers of faith and the chiefs of disbelief. This confrontation passed through several stages:

The first stage was the call to faith, the call to love, and the call to equality, and not repaying torture and killing with violence. This beginning did not please the chiefs of Quraysh; rather, it made them belittle the believers and go to extremes in harming and torturing them, believing that they would eliminate them. When they found the call growing stronger despite everything it faced of torture and brutality, they increased their persecution of the believers. Some of the believers emigrated to al-Habashah (Abyssinia), and they began seeking those who would protect them and seeking refuge with them. Allah, the Truth, blessed and exalted, willed this so that Islam would be entered only by those whose hearts were saturated with love for Islam and who disdained all hardships, persecution, killing and displacement; and these are the ones who would become trustworthy for the call. After that, disbelief remained upon its disbelief, and faith continued to draw some individuals to it quietly. The disbelievers tried to win over the believers by cunning after force, oppression and terror had failed. They said: "We worship your god for a period, and you worship our god for a period." So Allah, glorified and exalted, sent down a surah containing what is called in modern custom "the severing of relations." The Truth, may He be mighty and majestic, said:

﴿Say: O disbelievers! I do not worship what you worship, nor do you worship what I worship, nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾ (al-Kafirun, 1-6)

This was an announcement of a second stage characterized by there being no compromise and no middle ground between disbelief and faith, because if the believers were to accept worshipping their gods, that would be an acknowledgment from them that their gods were true; and if they accepted worshipping the One God while associating other gods with Him, that would be a dereliction, and that could never happen. The prohibition in this noble verse includes the present and the future. This is what is called in international politics the severing of relations. Indeed, the severing of international relations occurs due to a temporary cause; but the dispute between the early Muslims and the people of polytheism was not a conflict between human thought and other human thought. Rather the matter was a struggle between a methodology that heaven wants for the people of earth and the profiteers of corruption on earth. Therefore the severance had to be final, with no leniency, no compromise, and no middle ground between disbelief and faith. Thus the disbelievers' scheme to dissolve and waste the matter of religion failed, their cunning was lost, and the existence of faith remained strong and united in confronting the tyranny of the disbelievers after it had been threatened.

Then came the third stage, the stage of disbelief's acknowledgment of the strength of faith. The disbelievers had confronted the believers with oppression and torture, and the believers met this with patience and endurance, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emigrated to Madinah, and armed confrontation occurred between faith and disbelief at the Battle of Badr. The believers were victorious and acquired an entity that protected them. They were no longer the small, weak, humiliated and submissive group; they now had strength and capability, and although they did not yet have full control, they had become a force able to confront the disbelievers, or a force equal to them, capable of repelling attacks and meeting a blow with a blow.

When faith had this strength and capability to protect itself, and an equal standing and an entity vis-à-vis the disbelievers, this became the beginning of the stage that gave Islam the freedom to spread its call beyond the environs of Makkah, and the Muslims were secure as they spread their call from the attacks of the disbelievers and their persecution of them after the treaty of al-Hud[aybiyah]

Then the Truthful, exalted is He, returns to the matter of covenants, saying:

﴿How can there be a covenant with the polytheists in the sight of Allah and in the sight of His Messenger, except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram? So long as they remain upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the God-conscious (al-muttaqin).﴾

That is: you have tested covenants with the polytheists, and every time they have made a covenant with you they have broken it. They broke their covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah. Thus Allah, exalted is He, wants to draw our attention to the fact that we must not feel secure in the covenants of the polytheists, because they do not uphold a covenant but break it. Accordingly, the cause of breaking the covenant is that they did not remain upright in the covenant beforehand. It is the continuation of the covenant that would be the astonishing matter.

"Kayfa" (how) here is used to ask about a state. It is said: "Kayfa haluka?" (How is your condition?), and you reply: "Bi-khayr, al-hamdu lillah" (Well, praise be to God). So "kayfa" is used to ask about a condition, and the condition may be general, i.e., "How are you, and how is your family, your children, your livelihood, and so on?" Or it may be specific, as when you ask about a sick person, saying: "How is so-and-so?" and it is answered: "He has recovered, praise be to God." Or you ask about a needy person, saying: "How is his situation?" and it is answered: "God has relieved his distress." Or you ask about a son who left the house running away, and it is answered: "He has returned, praise be to God."

So "kayfa," if used without restriction, is general, and if restricted, is specific. However, it is sometimes used not to ask a question but to express wonder (ta'ajjub), either wonder at something ugly or wonder at something good. For example, one may be told: "How did so-and-so curse his father?" Here the wonder is at something ugly, because what happened is a repugnant thing that should not have happened. And one may say to a person who has invented an important invention: "How did you reach this invention?" This is wonder at something good. Wonder at ugliness is wonder of denunciation (ta'ajjub inkar), and wonder at goodness is wonder of approval (ta'ajjub istihsan), as when we say: "How did you build this mosque?" In this noble verse, the Exalted says:

﴿How can there be a covenant with the polytheists﴾ (al-Tawbah: 7). This is wonder that the polytheists should have anything called a covenant, since they know only breaking covenants; they do not hold to covenants nor respect them. So it is right to marvel that they should have a covenant, when in reality they have no covenant.

This wonder is for mockery and denunciation. For instance, if someone comes threatening you and you say to him: "Who are you to threaten me?", this is mockery and denunciation, because you do not know him, and you also mock that he should have the ability to carry out his threat against you. Sometimes it is a genuine question, as when you ask a person you do not know: "Who are you?" and he replies: "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." Sometimes the answer to "how" is by speech, and sometimes speech is of no use and it must be answered by action.

Read the saying of the Truthful, exalted is He:

﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead"﴾ (al-Baqarah: 260). Here "kayfa" carries the meaning of wonder of approval, because when you bring life into what has no life, this is a wondrous matter that calls for approval. The Exalted did not answer Abraham, peace be upon him, verbally, but answered with a practical experiment, and a dialogue took place between the Truthful, exalted is He, and His friend Abraham, peace be upon him. The Lord, exalted is He, asked him: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ (al-Baqarah: 260). Abraham, peace be upon him, replied: ﴿Yes [I have]﴾ (al-Baqarah: 260), meaning: "I have believed, O Lord." The Noble Qur'an added on the tongue of Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿but so that my heart may be at rest﴾ (al-Baqarah: 260).

Faith is the tranquility of the heart, so how does Abraham say "I have believed"? Is there not a contradiction in that? I say: Abraham was certain that Allah, exalted is He, created the whole universe, but he wanted to know the manner of giving life and how it happens. Then the Truthful, exalted is He, did not answer him with speech but showed him a practical experiment, saying:

﴿Take four birds and make them incline toward you﴾ (al-Baqarah: 260). That is: you must choose four birds, gather them to you, and make sure of their form, so that when they die and are brought back to life, you will be certain that they are the very same birds.

﴿Then place on every hill of them a portion; then call them, and they will come to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise﴾ (al-Baqarah: 260). That is: cut these birds yourself, place a piece on every hill, and then call them; you will come to them, walking (sa'yan), meaning on foot, so that it cannot be said that they came from another place, but the very same birds will come to you walking. So if Allah, exalted is He, gives a creature the power that when he calls the dead, it comes to him alive, how much more is the power of Allah, mighty and majestic?

Thus the saying of the Truthful, exalted is He: ﴿How can there be a covenant with the polytheists﴾ (al-Tawbah: 7) is an interrogation of denunciation and wonder that the polytheists have no covenant; rather they have rebelled and become habituated to always breaking covenants. Then the Truthful, exalted is He, says:

﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram. So long as they remain upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the God-conscious﴾ (al-Tawbah: 7). That is: Allah, exalted and mighty, while informing the believers that these disbelievers have no covenant, does not demand that the believers confront the polytheists with the same treatment; rather the Exalted commands the believers to keep the covenant as long as the disbelievers keep it, until the disbelievers begin to break it, and then He obliges the believers to respond with a similar breach. This is what His saying, exalted is He, explains: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the God-conscious﴾ (al-Tawbah: 7). The muttaqi (God-conscious) is one who obeys Allah in what He commands and what He forbids, and places between himself and the attributes of majesty of Allah a shield. So the foundation of taqwa is that the believer does not break a covenant, whether with a believer or with a disbeliever; it is the disbeliever who begins the breach, and it is incumbent upon the believer to honor covenant and promise.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 9, verse 8:

The Blessed and Exalted Truth says after that:

﴿How [can there be a covenant with them], when if they gain the upper hand over you they observe regarding you neither ties of kinship nor pact? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

We observe here that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, did not say "how can the polytheists have a covenant," but was content with "how" (kayfa), because their treachery had become well known. The first "how" was a question about a matter that had already passed.

The questioning here makes clear to us that they will always break covenants, as they did in the past. It is as if the One who informs of the past also informs of the future and knows what will come from them. The Lord, glorified and exalted, continues His words: ﴿and if they gain the upper hand over you﴾ (al-Tawbah: 7).

The meaning of "yuzhirū" (they gain the upper hand) is that they gain power over you. If they gain power over the believers, they do not observe regarding them any ties of kinship (illah) or any pact (dhimmah). The verb "yarqubu" comes from "raqīb" (the watcher who observes things). So "lā yarqubūn" means they do not respect or heed, that is, if they gained power over the believers they would not heed any pact, covenant or agreement, but would consider everything permissible. This is a report from the Truth, glorified and exalted, of the hatred against the believers that lies in the souls of these unbelievers.

We note that the word "yarqubūn" is different from "yanẓurūn" (they look), and from "yubṣirūn" (they see), and it is also different from "yalmaḥūn" (they glance) and "yarmuqūn" (they gaze), although all of them express the meaning of seeing with the eye. But "yarqub" means to contemplate and scrutinise with attention so that no movement escapes one. Therefore when we say that so-and-so "yurāqib" so-and-so, it means that no movement of his escapes him, as he watches every movement that issues from him. As for "naẓara," it means to see with all of one's eyes; "lamaḥa" means to see with the corner of the eye; and "ramaqa" means to see from above. The words of the Exalted: "lā yarqubū fīkum illan wa lā dhimmah" mean: they do not respect a covenant regarding you, and nothing restrains any one of them from doing anything, however ugly it may be. An example: a strong man raises his hand to strike a small child who cannot bear his blow. Here someone seizes his hand and asks him to respect that the child is small and cannot bear the blow, and that he is the son of so-and-so, his relative, and that they are neighbours. He pays no heed to all of this, but falls upon the child, beating him.

The Exalted's words "illan" originally mean a gleam, that is, a glitter, and "illan" also means a loud sound. Gleam and loud sound attract the sensory means of perception, which are the ear and the eye. When a person makes a covenant, that covenant becomes a clear matter before him that catches his eyes as a shining thing catches them, and catches his ear as a loud sound catches it. A covenant or speech is called "illan" because it is known through the eye and the ear.

This is the linguistic meaning. But the technical meaning of the word "illan" is kinship (or bond of obligation), namely that you tie a thing as though you were forcing it not to adhere to another thing; for this reason the flaying of a sheep's skin is called "ghaṣb" (usurpation), because the flesh clings to the skin, and taking property is called "ghaṣb," because the owner holds fast to his property as a living sheep holds fast to its skin. When "ghaṣb" is used in jurisprudence, it does not refer to the linguistic meaning, which is gleam and loud sound. The scholars have more than one view on this meaning, and each of them took a sample from the root "ʾ-l-l" (illan), whose origin is gleaming: "alla... yuallu... allan," meaning "lamaʿa... yalmaʿu... lamʿan." "Al-ʾall" is also a loud sound. Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "illan" means kinship, because kinship is a cause of mercy; you find it grievous to betray a relative, since kinship needs no covenant. It has been said that "illan" means covenant.

Our master al-Ḥasan said: "illan" means neighbourhood and what it necessitates of rights. Qatadah said: "illan" means alliance and confederation. Abu ʿUmayrah said: "illan" means oath or swearing.

All these meanings draw our attention to the existence of a kind of mercy, such that cruelty or the unleashing of passion does not take possession of a person. A person should set for himself someone who says to him: "Calm down, he is your neighbour, or he is from a people between whom and those with whom you have a covenant there is a bond of kinship." For what keeps a person from inclining to evil and from spreading it at the moment when a matter provokes him is the consideration of all the circumstances. Thus dialogue intervenes. Yet there may exist kinship, covenant, oath or neighbourhood that prevents striking with cruelty; that is, "illan" is the matter that prevents responding harshly to something that may have been done in error. The meaning also includes disregard of kinship, neighbourhood, covenant or oath: when a strong man gains power over a small child, he regards none of these things.

The Truth wants us to know that when the polytheists gain power over the believers, they respect neither kinship, nor covenant, nor alliance, nor neighbourhood, nor oath, nor anything at all. So how can the polytheists have a covenant? If they gain power over the believers they respect nothing of them at all.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted, adds His words: ﴿nor dhimmah﴾ (al-Tawbah: 8). "Dhimmah" is the fulfilment of a trust for which there is no receipt or witnesses. If one person borrows an amount from another and writes a receipt for that amount, this receipt is the guarantor of repayment; likewise, if there are witnesses, their testimony secures the right for its owner. But if there is no receipt and no witnesses, the matter is left to the conscience (dhimmah) of the borrower: if this debtor wishes, he acknowledges the loan, and if he wishes, he denies it. There is another dhimmah, which is between you and yourself. An example: you may pledge yourself to give someone a sum of money every month; this is a matter with no written covenant or witnesses, but it is left to your conscience: if you wish you do it, and if you wish you do not. What is in the dhimmah, then, is something which, if you do not do it, you will be exposed. For example: you decide within yourself to help a family; this is a matter subject to your will, so no covenant compels you to it, nor kinship, nor neighbourhood; nothing but your conscience. Therefore you observe fulfilment of what you promised yourself, in order to preserve your reputation and how others see you. Likewise, when you take a debt with no receipt from you or witnesses against you, but you are careful to repay it because it is in your dhimmah.

﴿How [can there be a covenant with them], when if they gain the upper hand over you they observe regarding you neither ties of kinship nor pact? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ (al-Tawbah).

Thus we know that "kayfa" here expresses amazement that the polytheists should now or in the future have a covenant, because they make a trade of breaking covenants; and if they gain power over the believers, they will mutilate them most horribly without regard for any consideration. Someone may say: they are with us at their best, with cheerful faces, good reception and so on; how, then, if they gain power over us, will they turn into merciless beasts? We say: Allah, glorified and exalted, knows what appears and what is hidden, and He knows what passes through the thoughts of the believers, so He answered them, so that these matters would not remain suspended within their souls. Therefore He, glorified and exalted, responds to this thought: ﴿They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is, Allah, mighty and majestic, warns the believers and urges them not to believe the appearance they see before them of the polytheists, because it is not the reality but deception and hypocrisy. They speak fair words and meet you with cheerful faces and soft speech, but their hearts are full of hatred against you, O Muslims, so that when they gain power over you their true feelings appear, of intense hatred and enmity, and they observe regarding you neither ties of kinship nor pact. So when Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿They satisfy you with their mouths﴾ (al-Tawbah: 8).

So the believers must accept what the Truth has brought and discover that sweet tongues and good reception are nothing but deception from these enemies. By this disclosure He, glorified be He, gives us immunity against being deceived by what we see on their faces; this is merely a matter of reception, which represents neither past nor present. When the Glorified decides a future matter, He informs His servants the believers of it. Therefore we find Him responding in the same style to these thoughts. An example: in His words, glorified and exalted: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Ḥarām after this, their year﴾ (al-Tawbah: 28). The message here is a prohibition against the polytheists entering al-Masjid al-Ḥarām or approaching it. It is natural that thoughts arise here in the souls of a number of believers who profit from the polytheists during the pilgrimage seasons, because they are a people who live on the economy of the Hajj, where they sell goods to these people to earn their livelihood for the year. If the polytheists are prevented from the Hajj or from approaching al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, then from where will the provision they obtain from selling to them come? The believers must ask: from where shall we eat? We bring our merchandise and wait all season for the Hajj; if the number of pilgrims falls, to whom shall we sell?
