Allah, glorified and exalted, answers these thoughts with His words: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ (al-Tawbah: 28). That is: do not fear poverty, for Allah knows what will happen; Allah is the Rich, with Him are the keys of all things, and He will enrich you from His bounty and open for you the door of provision, giving you in return and more. Thus Allah, glorified and exalted, answers the thoughts that pass through the soul of the believer at the time of the Qur'an's revelation, so that the hearts and souls of the believers may be at peace, and so the Mighty and Majestic says:

﴿They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ (al-Tawbah). In this utterance is a reply to the thoughts that passed through the souls of the believers, who saw the polytheists receiving them with soft words and faces full of cheer; so the Truth, glorified and exalted, made clear to them: do not be deceived, for what is in the hearts is the opposite of what is on the faces.

As for His words, exalted is He: "and most of them are defiantly disobedient" (al-Tawbah: 8), it shows that they are far from the method. Fisq (defiant disobedience) is going out of obedience. Does the unbeliever or hypocrite have obedience?

We say: if you look at these people you will find them going outside even the method they chose for themselves; they do not keep to the method of falsehood that they adopt. So they are defiantly disobedient even in the method to which they belong. If they are like this with the method of falsehood, how then with the method of truth?

His words, "and most of them are defiantly disobedient," show that there may be a committed minority; this is a beautiful Qur'anic caution. It also answers the question that may come to mind: these are unbelievers, and there is no sin after unbelief; how then can it be said that they are defiantly disobedient, that is, rebellious or outside obedience, while they are not believers at all?

We say: they are outside even the methods of unbelief that they chose for themselves, which is why Allah, glorified and exalted, describes their state when He says:

﴿They have exchanged the signs of Allah for a small price and averted [people] from His way. Evil is what they have been doing.﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 9, verse 9:

Thus God, Mighty and Majestic, shows us the reversal of standards among them. What is purchase (shira')? Purchase is: obtaining a commodity in exchange for a price. So if you say, "I bought a watch," for example, you are the buyer as long as you are paying the price, and the one who takes the price is the seller. And here the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿They have purchased with the signs of God a small price﴾ (al-Tawbah: 9).

It should therefore have been that they were the ones who paid the price, because the buyer is the one who pays the price. But here the matter has been reversed. God, glory be to Him, made the price to be what they buy, although the price is what is paid. Thus the matter contradicts the reality of buying and selling. What we must also note is that the price equals the commodity. You take the commodity and give the seller a price equal to it, because the price of everything must be proportionate to it. If you buy something simple, you pay a simple price for it, and if you buy something precious, you pay a high price for it.

All of this is noticed even in deeds. You may be among those who wish to provoke others, and you may find someone who provokes another. One asks one of his followers to revile so-and-so and gives him ten pounds. If he wants the follower to strike his opponent, he says: "Strike and I will give you fifty." And if he wants the follower to kill his opponent, he gives him thousands of pounds. Often those who have no faith say: every conscience can be melted down with gold. But what differs in value is the amount that melts any conscience. There is one whose conscience melts for a riyal, another whose conscience melts for twenty or thirty, and there is one whose conscience melts for millions.

God, Mighty and Majestic, draws our attention to the fact that these disbelievers have turned faith into a commodity that is bought and sold. They have sold their faith, and instead of receiving in return what equals faith, and faith is more precious than all the treasures of this world, they sold their faith for a small price. That is, they did not even appreciate the value of faith, so they sold it cheaply. How did they sell faith for a cheap price?

We say, for example: whoever takes a bribe does so wanting to bend the scale of truth. Whoever changes the scale of truth makes people doubt justice, and when people doubt justice they lose their sense of security, because every wronged person hopes that his matter will be brought before the judiciary so that it will vindicate him, or that his matter will be raised to the official so that he will give him his right. When people sense that the truth has been lost, as a result that there has come to be a price for faith.

If this takes place, the balances become disordered, and in this case the whole society is corrupted. It is as if they sold the corruption of the whole society for a very small price.

Furthermore, God, Mighty and Majestic, wants to draw our attention to the Reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and how the believers will abide forever in Paradise and enjoy what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, while these disbelievers will enter the Fire. Thus they will have sold their faith for a cheap price, whatever wealth they obtain, because the wealth of the whole world does not equal a single day in Paradise, since the world is limited by time, and its enjoyments are restricted and few. It is as if they sold eternal bliss for a temporary pleasure that may last only a few days or years. Then the disbelievers will know that the price they received is very small compared to what they lost. Would that they had made faith a price they pay to obtain a little enjoyment in this world! But they added to that that they barred from the way of God.

For this reason God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿They have purchased with the signs of God a small price, and so they have barred from His way﴾ (al-Tawbah: 9).

Barring (sadd) occurs when there is a call presented with its proofs, and people are prevented from listening to it, because you know that if they heard it they would embrace it and be convinced by it. For this reason we find, for example, that when the Qur'an was revealed, and the Arabs were a nation of eloquence and clear expression, the disbelievers knew that if people heard the Qur'an they would sense its miraculous nature, its eloquence and its sweetness, and would believe in it. Therefore God, Mighty and Majestic, says on their tongues in the Qur'an: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, that perhaps you may prevail﴾ (Fussilat: 26).

Because the disbelievers know that if people listened to the Qur'an they would believe in it, they forbid them from listening. And if anyone recited the Qur'an, they would urge one another to make noise over it so that no one would understand anything. This is a testimony from the disbelievers that if the ears received the Qur'an, they would believe. Noise-making is a kind of barring from the way of God. There was another kind of barring from the way of God: they would prevent people from listening to the call of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because they knew that the sweetness of the call would make whoever listened to the Messenger's call believe in it. Therefore they would bar people from the speech of God, Exalted, and from listening to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and they used to say to the pilgrims: Do not believe the man who says he is a prophet. This is a testimony from them that if the ears received the Qur'an, hearts would be drawn to faith. It is a testimony against them and not in their favour, because they were certain that the pilgrims' hearing the call of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would turn them away from disbelief. For this reason they feared that people would be influenced by this religion, which is the religion of truth, and believe in it, and this is what led them to bar them from it.

Then God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾ (al-Tawbah: 9). Sa'a means evil (qabuh), and it is not only evil now, but it is evil at present and the punishment for it will be greatly intensified in the future.

God's saying, ﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾ (al-Tawbah: 9), shows us the precision of the Noble Qur'an in that their wrongdoing is not a single deed but multiple deeds: speech and action, meaning that they bar people through speech and prevent them by using force at times. By God's use of the word "ya'malun" (do/work), He draws our attention to the fact that their deeds are not only force and not only action, for there is speech and there is action, and both are deeds: speech is the deed of the tongue, and action is the deed of the limbs. Had God said, "evil is what they used to do," we would say they did, and not that they said. And had He said, "evil is what they used to say," we would say they said but did not do. God, Glory be to Him, has made clear to us that speech and action are both deeds, and He, Glory be to Him, said:

﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ (al-Saff: 2)

to show us that there is a difference between speech and action: speech's instrument is the tongue, and action's instrument is the rest of the limbs. The meaning of His saying, ﴿Indeed, they used to do evil﴾, is: their speech and their action were evil.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 9, verse 10:

The Lord, glorified and exalted be He, continues, saying:

﴿They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship or covenant. It is those who are the transgressors.﴾ (9:10):

Whoever does not observe a tie of kinship or covenant regarding others, he is only wronging them. So if there is between me and you a kinship, or a covenant, or faith, and you do not respect that, then you have transgressed against my rights over you. And even if you limit your transgression to the rights of others, you have also transgressed against yourself, because you have given it little enjoyment in this world, and you will burn in the Fire in the Hereafter. Thus you have wronged yourself. For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, says:

﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾ (3:135).

And He, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ (16:118).

Does not the one who commits an immorality wrong himself? Yes, he wrongs himself in the Hereafter, after having given it a desire in this world; that is, he takes a quick enjoyment in exchange for a deferred punishment. But the one who wrongs himself most severely and clearly is the one who commits a sin without taking any enjoyment in this world, so that he has taken neither the enjoyment of this world nor that of the Hereafter, like the one who volunteers to give false testimony. He takes punishment in the Hereafter and has taken no enjoyment in this world.

Someone may say: this verse is repetitive, because God, the Exalted, said previously:

﴿How [can there be a covenant] when, if they gain the upper hand over you, they do not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or covenant?﴾ (9:8).

We say: the subject differs. In the eighth verse of Surat al-Tawba, the Truth makes clear that if they gain power over the believers, they will not observe kinship, neighbourly protection, or alliance, even if they show the opposite. As for the verse about which we are reflecting, they wrong themselves and sell their faith for a small price, and there is a difference between wronging others and wronging oneself.

In their barring from the way of God, the Exalted, and their aggression against the believers, they gained no worldly benefit; rather, they fought faith and fought religion, so they took on sin and gained nothing. It is as though they do not observe any tie of kinship or covenant even regarding themselves. For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, described them as "those who are the transgressors," because, without anyone having attacked them, they volunteered to commit aggression against the religion of God, against His Messenger (ﷺ), and against the believers, and then they committed aggression against themselves.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 11:

And after that comes the mercy of Allah, to show us how Allah the Exalted is merciful to His servants and His creation. For Allah the Exalted tells us that, however they have acted, if they repent, Allah accepts their repentance. Therefore the Truthful, Majestic One says:

﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾ (9:11):

This noble verse confirms for us that Islam wipes out what came before it (yajubbu ma qablahu), and that the door of repentance is always open to the polytheists and disbelievers, whatever their sins. This is the mercy of Allah the Exalted. We notice that Allah the Exalted said, "fa-in tabu" (if they repent) and did not say "idha tabu" (when they repent). For if He had said "idha tabu," their repentance would be affirmed. But His saying "fa-in tabu" carries uncertainty, because what they did contrary to faith is much, and what we hope from them is little. Yet repentance requires that the penitent, after it, actually undertake his faithful duty. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah﴾ (al-Tawbah: 11).

So the faithful duty after repentance is, by the testimony that "there is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Naturally, one must begin the prayer, because it combines all the pillars of Islam, and it is a daily act, not something required of a person once like the Hajj, nor like fasting, whose period is one month of the year. So for repentance to be confirmed, the penitent must perform the prayer at its time every day; it is the daily act that is not postponed or delayed from its time. The prayer is often mentioned together with zakah in the verses of the Noble Qur'an, because zakah is a sacrifice of wealth, wealth results from work, and work results from time, and prayer is a sacrifice of time. So, as we have said, prayer contains a kind of zakah.

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾ (al-Tawbah).

We must notice in the detail here the stages of faith that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has shown us: the first stage is bearing persecution and patience; the second stage is that there is no compromise between faith and disbelief. This settled the attempt of the disbelievers to blur the matter of faith by saying, "We worship your god for a period, and you worship our god for a period." This was a process completely rejected now, in the future, and until the Hour. Then came the stage of treaties, then the breaking of covenants, then the grace period of the four sacred months given to the disbelievers. All these are regulated matters, and the Arab nation did not know regulations.

So all these regulations came from heaven. Legislation among nations takes long stages, and no human law is born sound and complete; rather every law is enacted and then defects appear in its application, so it is amended, developed and interpreted, and it needs the masters of law who spend their whole lives on amendments and details. So how would this Arab nation, illiterate, which had no share of knowledge or culture, arrange all these regulations?

We say: it did not arrange them; rather their Lord arranged them for them, the One who encompasses all things in knowledge. So all these stages through which faith passed were accompanied by regulations sent down from heaven, explaining to the believers what they must do.

﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion﴾ (al-Tawbah: 11).

We ordinarily know brotherhood by lineage: this is my brother from my father and mother, or this is my brother from the father only, or from the mother only. Concerning this Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the brothers of Joseph came﴾ (Yusuf: 58). This is brotherhood of lineage. We know that the root "akh" comes once to express brotherhood of lineage, and comes once as "ikhwan" to express brotherhood in creed and doctrine. Allah the Exalted willed to raise faith to the rank of lineage, so He said: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ (al-Hujurat: 10).

This shows us that, since they have entered with us into the enclosure of faith, they have over us the right of lineage-brotherhood in what exists of affection, mercy, bonds, protecting one another always, love and harmony, and all that we know of the rights of brotherhood by lineage.

But we notice here that Allah the Exalted said: ﴿then they are your brothers in religion﴾ (al-Tawbah: 11), and did not say "your brothers." Why?

We say: it is not reasonable that they come out of all the sins they were in by repentance and at that very moment become brothers; rather that happens when their faith deepens and the truth of their repentance is established, then they become brothers.

Then the Truthful, Majestic One says: ﴿And We detail the verses for a people who know﴾ (al-Tawbah: 11). How can there be detailing for those who know? And if they know, why detailing?

We say: the meaning here is that Allah the Exalted details the verses for those who want to know the true knowledge that comes from Allah, because this knowledge has a great effect on the future of faith. Therefore non-Muslims who seriously study the Islamic religion in search of true knowledge end up declaring their Islam, because, being people of knowledge, talent and ambition in their fields, and the desire for knowledge having overcome them, and wanting to study the method of Islam objectively, you find them declaring Islam, because they look at the true view of the religion they study, and they take Islam from its faithful source, which is the Noble Qur'an and the Prophetic Sunnah, and do not take Islam from those attributed to Islam, that is, from Muslims. For among Muslims there may be a sinner, a thief, a bribe-taker, a liar, a hypocrite. If they took Islam from Muslims, they would say: what is this? Sin, theft, lying, bribery and hypocrisy?!

I always say to whoever has not studied Islam from the people of other lands: do not look at those attributed to Islam, but look at Islam in its essence and method: (the Qur'an and the Sunnah). Did it prohibit bribery, theft, lying and hypocrisy and make a punishment for them, or not? Yes, it prohibited them.

So these acts that you found in a number of Muslims and denounced are in no way from Islam. But if you go to Islam to know it from its scholarly sources, isolated from those attributed to it, you will arrive at faith.

Therefore, if the Muslims who deviate from the method knew what they do to Islam and how they harm it, they would know they are doing something grave, because Islam is a method and conduct, not merely a theoretical method; it is a practical method applied in life. Thus, if the Noble Qur'an represents the rules of the method, the biography of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ represents the practical applied method of Islam. And the Truthful, Majestic One says:

﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day﴾ (al-Ahzab: 21).

When a Muslim applies the method of Islam, he draws the attention of the non-Muslim to this religion and makes him love it,(1) and when he does what Islam does not accept, he repels the non-Muslim from the religion. Therefore the Truthful, Majestic One says:

﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do﴾ (al-Saff: 2-3), because your action, when it differs from the religion you call to and believe in, turns into an argument against the religion. The non-Muslim says: I saw the Muslim cheat, I saw him steal, I saw his hand reach to what is forbidden. So every deviant from the religion carries an axe with which he demolishes the religion, and bears the burden of his deed and the burden of those who took him as a model.(2)

We have said: when we look at diplomatic representation in the Islamic world, we find seventy-two Islamic states having embassies in most countries of the world, and I wonder: how many of the members of these embassies adhere to the Islamic appearance? Very few. And how many of the Islamic communities in foreign countries adhere to the teachings of the religion? Very few. Had they all adhered to the teachings of Islam, the states of the world would have known that this religion has a strength and a immunity that protects it. And that this immunity is what prevented the deviant material civilization from affecting them, and it would have been a strong attraction for the peoples of the world to study this religion. But you find them melting and rushing toward the material civilization of the countries in which they live, which makes the peoples of those countries say: if their religion were strong, they would have held to it, and not rushed after our civilization.

And if we study the history of Islam, we find that it did not spread by fighting or by the sword; it spread by the good example. Here the Truthful, Majestic One says:

﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know﴾ (al-Tawbah: 11): i.e., We make them clear to a people who seek the true knowledge that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has shown in His method. Therefore we find, for example, that when a nation arrives at a new discovery, the people of knowledge in Islam know that it is not a new discovery, because Islam mentioned it a long time ago.

For instance, in the law in Germany, they reached an article of law they called "abuse of right": you have rights, but you may misuse them. The German state began moving toward enacting laws aimed at preventing abuse of rights, and composing commentaries on these laws and applying them, and so on. A Muslim lawyer from Beni Suef went to Germany to obtain a doctorate, and became acquainted with this matter. He was attending a lecture given by a law professor on the theory of "abuse of right," so the Muslim lawyer stood up and said to him: you say you are the author of this theory? He said: yes. The lawyer said: this theory came in the method of Islam fourteen centuries ago. The German professor became greatly confused, and brought the orientalists to debate this Muslim lawyer, and they brought books of the Prophetic biography. The lawyer presented to the orientalists a story from the biography of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which says: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting when a Companion came complaining that another Companion had a palm tree in his house; the house belonged to the complaining Companion, and the palm tree belonged to another Companion, who had got into the habit of coming to it often to trim it, pollinate it and check on it, and it had become, as the popular proverb says, "Juha's nail," so the modesty of the household of the Companion who owned the house was put in distress. He went to complain to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger summoned the owner of the palm tree and explained to him, in meaning: "Either you give the palm tree to the owner of the house, or you sell it to him for money, or you cut it down."(3)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained to him that the palm tree was his right, but he had misused the right by going to its place often, for reasons and without reasons, which exposed the household of the house-owner to hardship.(4) This act was the living example of abuse of right. And it was a matter of the trust of knowledge that the German law professor should amend his lecture and say: I thought I had brought something new, but Islam preceded me to it fourteen centuries ago. And indeed the amendment was made. And the German scholar acknowledged that Islam had preceded him in the theory of "abuse of right" by one thousand four hundred years.

Therefore you find that the attribute of illiteracy in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in his nation(5) was a testimony of excellence, because

1 From Abdullah ibn Amr that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the likeness of the believer is like the bee: it eats good, produces good, and when it lands it does not break or spoil anything." Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/199).
2 From Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls to guidance has a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything of their rewards; and whoever calls to misguidance bears a sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything of their sins." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (2674), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/397), al-Tirmidhi (2674) and Ibn Majah (206). al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih hadith.
3 From Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "A certain man has a palm cluster in my garden, and it has harmed me and burdened me, the place of his cluster." So the Prophet ﷺ sent for him and said: "Sell me your cluster that is in the garden of so-and-so." He said: "No." He said: "Give it to me." He said: "No." He said: "Then sell it to me for a cluster in Paradise." He said: "No." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have not seen anyone more stingy than you, except one who is stingy with greeting." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/338), al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/20) and al-Bazzar (2000) in Kashf al-Astar. al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (3/127): "In it is Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, about whom there is discussion, but he has been declared trustworthy."
4 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also taught us the etiquette of not looking into the private matters of Muslims. From Sahl ibn Sa'd who said: A man looked through a hole in the door of the Prophet's room while the Prophet ﷺ had a comb with which he was scratching his head, and he said: "If I knew you were looking, I would have stabbed you in the eye with it. Permission was only prescribed because of the sight." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6241) and Muslim (2156).
5 Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ (al-A'raf: 157). Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: "al-Ummi" is attributed to the unlettered nation which is in its original state of birth; it has not learned writing nor reading. So said Ibn al-'Arabi. Ibn Abbas said: your Prophet ﷺ was unlettered, not writing, not reading, and not calculating. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾ (al-'Ankabut: 48).

Then the Almighty, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and revile your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief—indeed, they have no oaths—so that they may desist.﴾ (9:12)

"And if they break their oaths": that is, they did not honour the terms of the covenants. Almighty God here gives us the justification for fighting the disbelievers after all the stages in which they waged war against faith. They broke the covenants, and they did not stop there but also reviled the religion. That is, they found fault with the religion in a vile manner. When it is said that so-and-so "reviled" (ṭaʿana) so-and-so, he must have gone beyond mere insult to something far greater. Here the Truth, glorified and exalted, commands us either to fight them or to have them declare faith. This is a right of the Muslims, for they had previously offered every avenue of goodwill, but the leaders of disbelief rejected them.

As for the words of the Almighty, ﴿fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, the meaning is that killing comes first for the leaders of the disbelievers who incite their followers to fight the religion of God. The followers are not the root; rather, it is the leaders of disbelief, for they are the ones who plan, execute and incite.¹

They are, as is said in the modern age, war criminals. All knowledge recognises that a war ends when the war criminals are eliminated, because these are the ones who devise the plans, direct the battles and lead people to the fields of combat, exactly like the leaders of disbelief. These are the ones who dared to attack the methods of the Noble Qur'an, who prevented the tribes that came for pilgrimage from listening to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and who fought the religion by every means, through enticement and incitement, threat and warning.

The strange thing is that you see people who justify for you the killing of war criminals while denouncing the killing of the leaders of disbelief. The Almighty says: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant﴾ (al-Tawbah: 12).

And the Almighty, Mighty and Majestic, says in the same verse: ﴿indeed, they have no oaths﴾ (al-Tawbah: 12). Here the orientalists and those who lean towards them in their hearts and are counted among us by their forms and outward appearances will come and say: there is a contradiction. God says ﴿if they break their oaths﴾, thus affirming that they have oaths, and then says ﴿they have no oaths﴾. How can oaths be affirmed for them and then negated of them? Negation and affirmation cannot be combined in describing one and the same person. We say: they cannot be combined for someone who thinks superficially or takes matters at their face value. But whoever knows the intended meanings of expressions knows that the negation and affirmation of a thing in the Noble Qur'an means that the aspect is distinct. God, glorified and exalted, says to His Messenger (ﷺ) at the Battle of Badr: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾ (al-Anfal: 17).

His words ﴿you did not throw﴾ are a negation of throwing from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and ﴿when you threw﴾ is an affirmation of throwing. The negation and affirmation of a thing come in a single verse, and the agent and the act are the same. In the terminology of rhetoric this is called "distinction of aspect" (infikak al-jihah), meaning that each aspect demands a meaning different from the other aspect, just as one says: so-and-so lives higher than I do. This is a correct statement, yet at the same time he lives lower in relation to someone above him; he is high and low at once, high with respect to those beneath him and low with respect to those above him.

Or we may say, as another example: so-and-so is a father and a son. Here there appears to be an apparent contradiction, namely that he is a father to his son and a son to his father. He is a father from the aspect of the son and a son from the aspect of his father, and there is no conflict. This is what we call the distinction of aspect.

Therefore there is not the slightest contradiction between the negation of throwing from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and its affirmation of him, because the Messenger of God took a handful of pebbles and threw them at the army of the disbelievers.² This is what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did, being a human being, but the power of God, glorified and exalted, carried these pebbles and delivered them to every soldier of the disbelieving army. And in the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted: ﴿But most people do not know. They know an outward appearance of the life of this world﴾ (al-Rum: 6–7). They said: God negated knowledge and affirmed it for the same persons. We say: No, He negated true knowledge and affirmed for them the outward appearance of knowledge, and this is entirely different. Here the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And if they break their oaths﴾ (al-Tawbah: 12).

The verse affirms that they have oaths, and at the end of the verse it negates oaths from them, saying: ﴿indeed, they have no oaths﴾ (al-Tawbah: 12).

We say: the benefit of oaths or covenants is that they be kept, and whoever does not keep his oath or covenant has no oath, because his oath, that is his covenant, has no value, being devoid of fulfilment. When a liar swears, we say: this one has no oath. These people's oaths did not attain the sanctity of oaths, so it is as if they have no oaths. It is like a son for whom an examination is approaching and whom you force to study; you sit watching him, and he turns the pages of the book but understands nothing. If you try to reckon the outcome of his study, you find nothing, so you say: he studied and did not study. This is a negation and an affirmation of the act with no contradiction between them, because the aspect is distinct.

The negation of oaths at the end of the verse means that they have no fidelity, and as long as they have no fidelity, their oaths have no value. As for His words, exalted is He:

﴿So fight the leaders of disbelief—indeed, they have no oaths—so that they may desist﴾ (al-Tawbah: 12). This is a command to fight them, not to kill them, so the meaning is: fight them. If they are not killed, the fighting may make them desist from their enmity to the religion, because when they see some of their number slain, and they are weaker than the confrontation, the intensity of their opposition to Islam will lessen, and the obstinacy in the matter of religion will end.

¹ The Almighty says in Surat Saba': ﴿And those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: Rather, the plotting of night and day, when you commanded us to disbelieve in God and to set up rivals to Him﴾ (Saba': 33).

Then Gabriel said to him: "Take a handful of dust and throw it in their faces." So he took a handful of dust and threw it in their faces, and there was not one of the polytheists who did not have dust from that handful in his eyes, nostrils and mouth, and they turned their backs in flight. Related by Abu Nu'aym (p. 404) and al-Bayhaqi (3/29), both in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa, and mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (2/294).

Then the Truthful, blessed and exalted, says after that:

﴿Will you not fight against a people who broke their oaths, and resolved to expel the Messenger, and they began (the hostility) against you the first time? Do you fear them? Then Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers.﴾ (9:13)

In this noble verse, the Exalted Lord urges jihad and fighting against the leaders of disbelief, and not leaving them to prosper in their war against the religion, preventing people from faith and barring them from the path of Allah. "Alā" (ألا) is called a particle of tahdīd (urging, exhortation), like our saying: "Will you not go to so-and-so?" It is an encouragement to act, because tahdīd is a type of request. His words ﴿broke their oaths﴾ mean they violated their covenants. His words ﴿and resolved to expel the Messenger﴾ mean: they were the ones who began the enmity and the attempt to expel the Messenger ﷺ from Makkah. ﴿Resolved﴾ (هَمُّوا) means they firmly intended to act. His words ﴿and they began (the hostility) against you the first time﴾ mean: they were the ones who began the enmity against the Muslims and the barring from Islam, from the very first moment that the master of creation, Muhammad ﷺ, began calling to it. Al-bada' (البدء) is the first action, and "al-marrah" (المرة) is an act that is not repeated; for if it is repeated we say ﴿marratayn﴾ (twice), as in the words of the Truthful, the Exalted: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾ (al-Baqarah: 229).

So it was they who began the first act with enmity. Islam, as we know, faced two powers in two different stages of the da'wah (call to Islam): the power of the polytheists of Quraysh, and the power of the Jews. As for Quraysh, they resolved to expel the Messenger ﷺ from Makkah. Someone may say: "But it was the believers who began the fighting at Badr." I say: The Muslims did not go out to Badr to fight; rather they went for the caravan, to compensate for their wealth that they had left in Makkah. But the disbelievers said: "We will not return until we uproot Muhammad and those with him," and they came out in full force to fight at Badr.(1)

Thus, despite the safety of the caravan through a stratagem of Abu Sufyan(2), it was Quraysh who wanted to fight, so they gathered soldiers and horsemen to fight the Muslims.

The Jews did likewise: they broke their oaths and resolved to expel the Messenger from Madinah. Just as the polytheists tried to expel him from Makkah, there was a covenant between him ﷺ and the Jews, and this covenant was among the first acts of the Messenger of Allah in Madinah. Did the Jews keep these covenants? No. They pledged not to aid an enemy against him, but they broke their oaths and violated the covenant, aiding Quraysh against the Muslims.

Likewise did Banu al-Nadir: they intended to assassinate the Messenger ﷺ by dropping a rock upon him. Moreover, the Jews persisted in the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), aiding Quraysh against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and agreed with them to let them enter through their land in Madinah to ambush the Messenger of Allah and the army of the Muslims from behind.

Thus the words of the Truthful, the Exalted, ﴿and they began (the hostility) against you the first time﴾ have more than one aspect: their breaking of covenants and their beginning of the fighting oblige you to fight them, so that you may be safe from their evil.

﴿Will you not fight against a people who broke their oaths, and resolved to expel the Messenger, and they began (the hostility) against you the first time﴾ (al-Tawbah: 13). His words ﴿Will you not fight﴾ are an urging to fight, meaning: what prevents you from fighting them, unless you are fearful of them? Therefore the Blessed and Exalted says:

﴿Do you fear them? Then Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers﴾ (al-Tawbah: 13). Here the Truthful, the Exalted, draws the attention of the believers to the fact that if they are faced with two states—fear of people and their harm—then what is more deserving of fear is the one who is stronger, greater and more enduring in punishment. Since, if you compare the power of these people with the power of Allah, Allah is certainly more deserving of fear. And if you are faced with two choices, you proceed with the lesser of two harms; so how can believers fear what may befall them at the hands of the disbelievers, and not fear what befalls them from Allah?

Allah the Exalted made clear that there is no fear of the disbelievers in another verse of the same surah, His saying:

﴿Say: Do you await for us but one of the two best things? And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him, or at our hands. So await; indeed we are with you awaiting.﴾ (al-Tawbah: 52)

Thus the Truthful, the Exalted, removed fear from the souls of the believers: what harm can the soldiers of disbelief do to you? Either you are martyred and enter Paradise, or you achieve victory. His words ﴿Do you fear them?﴾ are a rhetorical question of denunciation, meaning: it would never be right for you to fear them and be afraid of them; for if they were stronger than you and overcame you, you would attain martyrdom; and if they were weaker than you and you overcame them, you would attain victory. Both are beautiful matters, beloved to the souls of the believers and to their feet in the positions of battle and combat.

Then the Truthful, the Exalted, brings the final judgment, saying:

﴿Then Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers﴾ (al-Tawbah: 13). That is: review your faith. If you are believers in Allah, you are eager for martyrdom. If you are believers in Allah the Almighty, the Powerful, the Subduer, you know Allah, His power and His might, and these cannot be compared with human strength. Either you will defeat them and have the joy of victory, or martyrdom and attaining Paradise; both outcomes are good. As for what befalls the disbelievers, it is confined to two matters: either Allah afflicts them with a punishment from Himself...

Thus, in any battle in which faith meets disbelief, the winning side is found to be the believers, whether they are martyred or victorious. The loser in any case is the disbelievers, for they will either be punished at the hands of the believers, or a punishment from Allah will come to them in this world or in the Hereafter. Thus Allah has set the measures that remove fear from the souls of the believers in their fighting against the disbelievers, so do not turn your backs to them in any battle, for however great the material power of the disbelievers, the might of the Truthful, the Exalted, is greater. The Lord, Glorified, says:

﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah﴾ (al-Baqarah: 249).

Thus no reckoning is made of the difference in material strength; this fear has no place in the hearts of believers on the side of faith, because Allah is with those who believed.

(1) Ibn Hisham's Sirah (2/247) reports that Damdam ibn 'Amr was calling out to Quraysh, shouting in the bottom of the valley while standing on his camel, which had had its nose slit (i.e., its nose was cut), with his saddle turned around and his shirt torn, saying: "O assembly of Quraysh, the caravan, the caravan! Your wealth is with Abu Sufyan; Muhammad and his companions have intercepted it, and I do not think you will catch it. Help, help!"
(2) Abu Sufyan changed his route to Makkah with the Quraysh caravan, taking the coastal road and leaving Badr, and went on quickly. Ibn Ishaq said: When Abu Sufyan saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent to Quraysh: "You only went out to protect your caravan, your men and your wealth; Allah has saved them, so return." But they did not listen to him. See Ibn Hisham's Sirah (2/257-258).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 14:

Then Allah, glory be to Him, reinforces His exhortation to the believers to fight, saying:

﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands, and disgrace them, and give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people (14).﴾

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Fight﴾ in the previous verse was an exhortation to the believers to fight, and ﴿fight them﴾ here is an incitement and encouragement to fight, and a command of faith to the believers to fight the disbelievers. Then the Lord, glory be to Him, in this verse gives the wisdom behind the command to fight, saying: ﴿Allah will punish them by your hands﴾. We may ask: if Allah wishes to punish them, why does He not bring a sign from Himself that compels them to punishment?

We say: if the believers had been victorious through a cosmic event other than fighting, the disbelievers would have said: a cosmic event is what gave them victory. The Truth, glory be to Him, wills that these disbelievers be defeated at the hands of the believers, because the disbelievers are materialists who believe only in the material matter; had they been believers in Allah the matter would have ended. But Allah, glory be to Him, wants to show the disbelievers the might of the believers, so that their hearts are filled with awe and fear of the believers, and they reckon a thousand reckonings for them, so that their souls do not urge them to dare against the faith and the religion, or to belittle the believers.

One may say: here the Truth commands, saying: ﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands﴾.

In another verse He says:

﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ (al-Anfal: 33).

How then does Allah affirm punishment and negate it? We say: the two verses were revealed concerning the disbelievers. And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands﴾. Had He said: fight them, you will punish them by your hands, the meaning would have differed; but the two verses affirm one punishment and negate the other. We say: the direction is distinct. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ means: Allah does not send down upon them a punishment from heaven as long as you are among them. This is made clear in His saying:

﴿And when they said: O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment (32). And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness (33).﴾ (al-Anfal).

The disbelievers had previously asked for a punishment from the sky to descend upon them if the Qur'an were the truth; so the Truth, glory be to Him, responded that He would not punish them as long as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them, because He sent him as a mercy to the worlds. But the non-intervention of heaven with punishment after the sending of the Messenger of Allah with the message does not mean that punishment has ended for the disbelievers. He, glory be to Him, entrusted the believers with supporting His method and His religion, and He is with them. Yet punishment is carried out through earthly means, and there is no contradiction. For punishment from heaven may be a total annihilation of all disbelievers, young and old, such as the flood drowning them, or the Cry seizing them and destroying them to the last one, or a furious, violent wind destroying them, or the quake freezing them; in all these cases not one of the disbelievers remains. But human fighting does not eliminate the disbelievers entirely, for Islam forbids us to fight women and children (1), and those who have not fought us (2).

Thus punishment after the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is not a punishment of extermination and annihilation as it was among the earlier nations. We know that Allah, the Truth, glory be to Him, punished earlier nations by those means, so it was the duty of the messenger among the earlier prophets, before the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), to convey the message, and if his people did not believe in his message, heaven would intervene against them with the earlier kinds of punishment. But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, commanded Muhammad (ﷺ) and his nation after him to call to the religion of Allah, and to discipline whoever opposes faith and enters into enmity with the believers; so among them some flee or fall into captivity, and the woman and the child are left without punishment.

﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands, and disgrace them﴾ (al-Tawbah: 14).

What is the difference between punishment and disgrace? We say: one may find a person who has pride and endurance, and even if punishment befalls him he bears it and does not show fear, dread or weakness, and his self-pride prevents him from groaning. For such a person there is another kind of punishment, which is disgrace, and disgrace is harder on the soul than punishment, for its meaning is exposure. For example, a man may have prestige in the neighbourhood where he lives, like the champion of the quarter; then a young man comes and enters into a brawl with him in front of people and throws him to the ground. This throwing does not punish him or hurt him, but it disgraces him and exposes him before people, so that he cannot raise his head among people again; disgrace here is more painful to his soul than punishment. Allah, glory be to Him, does not only want the disbelievers punished by the hands of the believers, but He wants them to be exposed too, so that they cannot raise their heads. The Truth, glory be to Him, brought a third outcome of this fighting, saying: ﴿and give you victory over them﴾ (al-Tawbah: 14).

Accordingly, when the believers fight the disbelievers, punishment, disgrace and defeat befall the disbelievers. So ﴿Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ is one stage, ﴿and disgrace them﴾ is a second stage, ﴿and give you victory over them﴾ is a third stage; then comes the fourth stage:

﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people (14)﴾ (al-Tawbah), meaning: the victory that the believers will achieve, by the help of Allah, in their fighting with the disbelievers will heal the breasts of the believers whom the disbelievers oppressed and transgressed against; this victory is like a cure for the ailment that filled the breasts of those believers, and removes the rage of their hearts, that is, it expels the anger and agitation confined in the breasts. So the fighting of the believers against the disbelievers achieves not only punishment and disgrace for the disbelievers and victory for the believers over them, but also treats the hearts of the believers that were filled with pain and anger from the disbelievers' earlier aggression against them and their attempts to humiliate them and seize their rights. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and remove the rage of their hearts; and Allah turns in mercy to whom He wills; and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise (15).﴾

Thus those who broke the covenant and cooperated against the helpers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) see Allah's vengeance upon them, so the breasts of the believers are healed and the rage departs from them. Healing, as we know, is from an ailment, and medicine is necessary for healing; so Allah's vengeance is a healing for the breasts of the believers against the Quraysh disbelievers who aided the Banu Bakr against the Banu Khuza'ah, allies of our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So He punishes them by your hands, gives you victory over them, and disgraces them, glory be to Him.

1 This is established by the noble Sunnah. On the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: "A woman was found killed in one of the campaigns of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the killing of women and children." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3015-3014) and Muslim (1744).

2 He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being kind to them and dealing justly with them. Indeed, Allah loves those who deal justly (8).﴾ (al-Mumtahanah: 8).
Al-Qurtubi said in his commentary on it: "This verse is a concession from Allah regarding maintaining relations with those who have not been hostile to the believers and have not fought them," and he mentioned the views of those who held that it is abrogated by the verse ﴿then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. Then he said: "Most of the people of interpretation said: it is muhkam (not abrogated). They argued that Asma' bint Abi Bakr asked the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Should I maintain ties with my mother when she comes to me as a polytheist?' He said: 'Yes.'" Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 9, verse 15:

We perceive that He, glorified and exalted be He, despite His punishing them and intensifying the disgrace upon them, nevertheless opens a door to repentance. This is a matter that none can bring about except a Lord who is All-Wise, because all are servants of His, both believers and disbelievers; He is their Creator, and He is jealous of His handiwork. After the punishment and disgrace become severe upon them, and the hearts of the believing people are healed by this, He then opens the door of repentance. Through this He grants the believers the strength of faithful magnanimity, so they should not bear arrogance toward these people if they come repentant and believing. Thus He, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿And Allah accepts repentance from whom He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise (15)﴾. That is: He, glorified be He, knows all the requirements of the rulings, and for every matter with Him there is a wisdom. Fighting was willed by Allah, mighty and majestic, so that by it He may crush their arrogance, and repentance has its wisdom in preventing the disbelievers from persisting in evil; for the legislation of repentance is a mercy from the Real, glorified and exalted be He, toward His creation. Had Allah not legislated repentance, every one who commits sin would say: "As long as there is no repentance, and as long as my destiny is the Fire, I will take from this world what I can." Thus he would persist in wrongdoing and increase corruption and the causing of corruption, because he sees that his fate is one so long as there is no repentance. But the legislation of repentance prevents the wrongdoer from persisting in his injustice, and by this Allah protects society from his evils, and places in his soul the hope of Allah's acceptance of his repentance and the desire that He forgive him; so he turns to righteous deeds, perhaps he will expiate what he committed of sins and transgressions. In this there is protection for people and prevention of the spread of injustice and corruption.

So fighting has a wisdom, punishment has a wisdom, disgrace has a wisdom, and repentance has a wisdom. And He, glorified and exalted be He, when He punishes, He punishes out of wisdom, and when He accepts repentance, He accepts it out of wisdom.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 16:

Then the Truth, Mighty and Majestic is He, says, after that:

﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone, when Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive [in His way] and have not taken other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers as intimates? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

As soon as you hear "am" (or), know that it is an "idrabiyyah" (a particle of transition or rejection of the preceding statement), meaning: Allah, glorified is He, would not leave you until He knows, with knowledge of actuality, which of you has faith that qualifies him for striving in the way of Allah. So if you think that Allah will leave you without trial and without testing and purifying you(1), then you must turn away from that and understand what stands in contrast to it.

Thus trial is a necessity for those whom Allah, the Exalted, wills to bear the burden of the call, so that they may confront the fierceness of corruption and decadence. Therefore Allah refines those who believe until each one of them stands in the position of belonging to Allah, sacrificing in the way of Allah. And whenever the Truth, Mighty and Majestic, says concerning something the word ﴿wa-lamma ya'lam﴾ (and when Allah has not yet known), this does not mean that He has not known and will know. No. He, glorified is He, knows everything from eternity, but eternal knowledge is not a proof against mankind. I always give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest comparison: we find the dean of one of the colleges sometimes announcing a scholarly prize that he wants to give to the outstanding students. The teacher who supervises the students' achievement says to him: "So-and-so is the first, and he deserves the prize." The dean says: "But I want you to hold an examination, so that it may be a proof against those who are not outstanding." This is the knowledge of practical actuality that the Truth, Mighty and Majestic, intended through trial. He, glorified and exalted is He, knows everything from eternity, but actual knowledge is a proof against those who oppose.

﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone﴾ (al-Tawbah: 16): that is, without trial or purification. And His saying, exalted is He:

﴿wa-lamma ya'lami Allah﴾ (al-Tawbah: 16).

"Wa-lamma" is for negation, and its like is our saying "lamma ya'ti" (he has not yet come), meaning that the coming has not been realized until now. "Lamma" differs from "lam". "Lam" does not indicate the expectation that what follows will be established; what comes after it will never be realized. But "lamma" indicates the expectation that what follows will be established, meaning that what follows has not been realized up to the moment of its utterance, but it may be realized afterwards. If you say, "lamma yuthmir bustanuna" (our orchard has not yet borne fruit), meaning that the orchard you own has not borne fruit, but it may bear fruit afterwards. And He, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed." Say: "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾ (al-Hujurat: 14).

The meaning of the noble statement is that faith has not entered their hearts up to now, but it will enter afterwards, and this is good news for them. The Bedouins said, "We have believed," so Allah, the Exalted, clarified: "Rather, you have submitted, and faith has not entered your hearts," because faith is firm inner conviction of the heart, while Islam is submission to what the faith of the heart requires of conduct. That is, you have adopted the conduct of Islam, but it is a superficial conduct that has not come from the springs of the heart. The saying of the Truth here:

﴿wa-lamma ya'lami Allah alladhina jahadu minkum﴾ (al-Tawbah: 16) does not mean that His knowledge is connected to the time of speaking, for the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, is eternal and continuous, and He, glorified is He, is exempt from accidents.

Thus the knowledge intended here is the knowledge of actuality, which will be a proof against you, because if Allah, glorified and exalted, had not tested you, you would have said: "If You had commanded us, O Lord, to fight, we would have fought, and if You had commanded us to be patient in war, we would have been patient, and we would have been the greatest of strivers."

Therefore the trials came as a practical test. Among these trials is facing the enemy in war: whoever flees, his shortcoming in confrontation becomes evident, and whoever is not patient under trials recognizes the deficiency of his faith, and that becomes actual knowledge.

﴿wa-lamma ya'lami Allah alladhina jahadu minkum wa-lam yattakhidhu min duni Allah wa-la rasulihi wa-la al-mu'minina waliyjatan﴾ (al-Tawbah: 16).

Thus Allah, through actual knowledge, wills to distinguish between sincere striving and fleeing from it, and that there should be a clear believing conduct, showing that these people have not taken, besides Allah and His Messenger, any "waliyjah." The "waliyjah" is of the pattern "fa'ilah" in the sense of "fa'il," and "walijah" means "entering" (dakhilah).

﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ (al-Hajj: 61), that is, He makes the night enter upon the day and the day enter upon the night. The intended meaning of "waliyjah" is a thing that enters into something that is not of it. It is among the words that are used and in which the masculine and feminine singular, the dual, and the masculine and feminine plural are alike. You say: "imra'ah waliyjah," "rajul waliyjah," "imra'atan waliyjah," "rajulan waliyjah," "nisa' waliyjah," and "rijal waliyjah." Just as you say: "rajul 'adl," "imra'ah 'adl," "rajulan 'adl," "imra'atan 'adl," "rijal 'adl," and "nisa' 'adl," the form does not differ in all these cases.

The intended meaning of "waliyjah" here is the bitana of evil(2), who enters upon weak believers and penetrates their souls in order to spread the secrets of the believers and convey them to the disbelievers. For this reason, the Truth, Mighty and Majestic, willed to show us ﴿wa-lamma ya'lami Allah alladhina jahadu﴾, that is, that He, glorified and exalted, should know in actuality those who strove, and who did not take as bitanah of evil from among the disbelievers persons who enter into their affairs in a way that leads them to discover their secrets.

﴿wa-lam yattakhidhu min duni Allah wa-la rasulihi wa-la al-mu'minina waliyjatan﴾ (al-Tawbah: 16). So what is forbidden here is that believers take disbelievers as waliyjah, because such a disbeliever will take their secrets and spread them to their enemy, and thereby the believers are exposed to danger. The believer must make Allah, Mighty and Majestic, his waliyjah, and make the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, his waliyjah, and make the believers his waliyjah, and allow them to mingle with him, and they are trustworthy regarding what they know of inner matters. As for the enemies and adversaries among the disbelievers, they are not trustworthy with any of the believers' secrets. The Truth, glorified and exalted, concludes the noble verse with His saying:

﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ (al-Tawbah: 16). The meaning is: if you think that you mix with the disbelievers and give them the secrets of the believers and no one knows, then know that Allah, exalted is He, hears and sees, and that Allah is Acquainted, nothing hidden from Him. So do not deceive yourselves and think that if you conceal something from the eyes of creation, it may ever be hidden from Allah. Nothing is hidden from the eyes of the Creator, for if you were blinded to the decree of the earth, you will not be blinded to the decree of heaven(3).

1 Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? And We certainly tested those before them, so Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars﴾ (al-'Ankabut: 2-3). And Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers﴾ (Al 'Imran: 141). And "tamhis" is: testing and trial, and "tamhis" also means: sifting and purifying, and from it is the refining of gold, that is, testing it to know the good from the bad.

2 On the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "Allah did not send any prophet, nor appoint any caliph, except that he had two bitanahs: a bitanah that commands him to good and urges him to it, and a bitanah that commands him to evil and urges him to it, and the protected one is the one whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, protects." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7198), Ahmad (3/88-89), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/158).

3 On the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "You bring disputes before me, and perhaps some of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I judge for him according to what I hear from him. Whoever I give him a part of his brother's right, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire." Recorded by al-Bukhari (2680) and Muslim (1713).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 17:

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, moves us to another matter in His saying, mighty and majestic is He:

﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.﴾

It seems that this verse came as a justification (haythiyya) for the disavowal (bara'a) which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entrusted to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah ennoble his face, to proclaim it on the Day of the Greater Hajj(1). For bara'a means severance, and its meaning is that no polytheist should enter the mosque, nor circumambulate the House naked. Thus the disavowal from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, and from His Messenger toward the polytheists is a prohibition against them entering the Sacred Mosque. A number of the polytheists had made the Sacred Mosque a meeting place for themselves, sitting in it for evening conversation, trade and other things. They would also provide the pilgrims with a drink of raisin wine that had not fermented, along with the keepers of the House, and they would feed the visitors of the Sacred House of Allah.

All of this used to happen in Mecca at the hands of the disbelievers, but this came to an end with the disavowal which 'Ali ibn Abi Talib proclaimed on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom his Lord had inspired to do so. The polytheists no longer had any right to ﴿maintain the mosques of Allah﴾. The phrase has two meanings: the first is sitting in these mosques such that they are populated by their visitors; the second is preserving the building of the mosque, keeping it clean and repairing it. Allah has prohibited the polytheists from both kinds of maintenance(2). The discussion here concerns the Sacred Mosque, based on His saying, exalted is He:

﴿The polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this, their year.﴾ (al-Tawba: 28)

We say: the Sacred Mosque is the place toward which all the directions of people turn in every part of the earth when they establish prayer, because every place in which a Muslim prostrates is called a mosque. With the multiplicity of those who prostrate, the Sacred Mosque is considered mosques; or because the directions of prostration are multiplied in the Sacred Mosque. One person prostrates to the north of the Ka'ba, another to the south of the Ka'ba, and a third to the east of the Ka'ba. This is in the principal directions; and there are also the secondary directions: there are people who face northeast, people who face southeast, others who face southwest, and the multiplicity of secondary directions in facing the Ka'ba. Thus every direction faced is a mosque, and there are those in the parts of the earth who cannot see the Ka'ba who face toward it.

When you hear the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.﴾ (al-Tawba)

You notice that "kana" (it is/was) here comes in negated form, and from it we understand the meaning: it is not acceptable in the reckoning of reason, logic or religion that disbelievers approach the mosque, nor that a polytheist tend the mosque or safeguard it; for the mosque is for worship, and worship requires a worshipped one who is Allah, glorified and exalted is He, while the disbelievers associate partners with Allah. Therefore it is logical that they should have no connection with the mosques. Thus preventing them from the mosque, from establishing it, maintaining it and visiting it, is something logical, by their own testimony against themselves to disbelief, and this is the cause of their being prevented from approaching the mosques of Allah.

Testimony is either testimony by speech or testimony by state. As for testimony by speech, it is because they used to say to the Jew: "What religion are you upon?" and he would answer with his religion; likewise to the Christian. When the polytheist is asked, he acknowledges his polytheism(3); this is testimony by speech. As for testimony by state, it is that they prostrate to idols and worship them besides Allah.

How can a person be a polytheist and then we not say to him: "You have no relationship with the mosque; lift your hand from it." Islam has no need that a polytheist build a mosque for it, or that a disbeliever maintain a house of the houses of Allah, and Allah has no need that someone who does not believe in Him, glorified and exalted is He, visit His house.

Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿testifying against themselves to disbelief﴾ (al-Tawba: 16)

They forgot the first testimony in truth when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made them testify against themselves; for the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who says:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring, and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify." Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this." Or lest you should say: "Only our fathers associated partners with Allah before, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ (al-A'raf: 172-173)

They, then, at the moment of the first creation, acknowledged the oneness of Allah and covenanted with Allah, exalted is He, to that effect. But they disbelieved in that testimony, associated partners with Him, glorified and exalted is He, and placed idols in the Sacred House of Allah. They claimed falsehood and said:

﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in nearness.﴾ (al-Zumar: 3)

This is precisely association, and this is their testimony against themselves to disbelief.

﴿that they should maintain the mosques of Allah while testifying against themselves to disbelief﴾ (al-Tawba: 17)

The mosque, as we know, is the place where we prostrate, and every spot on earth is suitable for prostration for Muslims and counts as a mosque; this is among what Allah, exalted is He, singled out for the community of Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that no one before me was given: I was aided with awe over a distance of a month's journey; the earth was made for me a mosque and a means of purification, so whichever man of my community is overtaken by prayer, let him pray; spoils were made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and a prophet used to be sent to his own people specifically, while I was sent to all people generally(4)."

This hadith shows that among what Allah singled out for the Muhammadan community is that He made every part of the earth suitable for performing prayer in, and He also made the earth a means of purification; it suffices the Muslim to perform tayammum from the earth and pray upon it. But there is a difference between a place that is suitable for you to pray in and conduct the activity of your life, and a place designated for worship. The field in which you plant may be a place where you pray and plant; the factory may be a place where you pray and manufacture; likewise the school where you may study and also pray. All of these are mosques in the general sense, places of prostration to Allah, exalted is He. But the word "masjid," when used absolutely, refers to the bounded space of place removed from all the activities of life and specifically designated for prayer and prostration only. When you demarcate a place with a white line of lime, or enclose it with wire, and say: "This is a mosque," then no activity is practiced in it except prayer. This is the technical, legal mosque. Every house of Allah you build in any place is called a mosque. The qibla of the mosques spread across the earth is the Sacred Mosque; these are places demarcated for mosqueness, or for worship, or for prayer, and not for other movements of life. But the demarcation of the place was by the choice of men. Its qibla, the Sacred Mosque, which is the greatest congregational mosque, is by the choice of Allah, exalted is He, and the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who says:

﴿Indeed, the first House placed for mankind is that at Bakka, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾ (Al 'Imran: 96)

Since this Sacred House is by the choice of Allah and placed for people, we may ask: did people place it? No, rather something other than people placed it, because the definition of "people" is Adam and his descendants, and so it must be that it was placed before Adam. By the logic of the Noble Qur'an, the House existed before Adam. And if we go a little deeper, we find that this Sacred House is ﴿guidance for the worlds﴾, and among the worlds are the angels.

Thus we see that the saying of some people, that Abraham determined the place and foundations of the House, is a claim whose truth is not established, because the House is the place, not the one who dwells in it. The House is not the stone or the building, which is what we call the Ka'ba; the Ka'ba is "the one who dwells" (al-makin), while the House is the place in which the Ka'ba was set up. For when a torrent came and removed the Ka'ba, leveling it to flat ground, where would we pray? We pray toward the direction of the place. The flood carries away the one who dwells, but the place remains.

When Sayyidna Ibrahim, peace be upon him, came, the trace of the House was lost, and our Lord commanded him to raise the House. He did not tell him: "Determine the place"; rather He commanded him to build the third dimension, because every space has two dimensions, length and breadth, and if it is a circle it has a circumference, and if it is a triangle it has three sides. But height brings the thing into volume, and the Friend Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House, after the Master, glorified and exalted is He, had determined the place for him and shown it to him: ﴿And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House﴾ (al-Baqara: 127). So the House was designated before the raising, as evidenced by the fact that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, when speaking of the coming of Hagar and her son Isma'il, the infant, and Abraham, peace be upon him, settling them in this place, said: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, near Your sacred House﴾ (Ibrahim: 37). Abraham, peace be upon him, raised the foundations, and his son Isma'il helped him after he grew up and became strong; but at the time he settled him and his mother beside the House, he was a small infant. So the "House-ness" and the "place-ness" existed, but Abraham established the one who dwells, which is the third dimension, that is, height.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House﴾ (al-Hajj: 26), that is, We revealed and determined the place, in which Sayyidna Ibrahim would build with stones to make the House manifest. So the House, then, existed before.

We note that the mosques spread across the earth must have one direction, for one God, and the Truth determined this place as the qibla toward the Ka'ba. Some of the permissive ones try to invert the understanding of the Truth's saying: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾ (al-Baqara: 115).

They say: if we turn toward any place, we will find the Face of Allah, exalted is He. We say: the correct view is that the Face of Allah, exalted is He, is in all existence; but beware of understanding that Allah's determination of the Ka'ba to be our direction means that it is the Face of Allah. No, rather we are commanded to face it in prayer. And if you also look at the Muslims throughout the whole world, you will find that every Muslim on earth faces the Ka'ba in his prayer; and as long as the Ka'ba is a center to which we all turn, you will find someone facing it while it is to his east, another facing it while it is to his west, another while it is to his north, and another while it is to his south.

So ﴿wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾. Since we have come to know that the mosques are demarcated and designated for worship, it is not permissible for a polytheist to come to them, and we do not accept that a polytheist contribute to their repair or cleanliness, because Allah is free of need of that. And it is also incumbent upon us not to discuss our worldly affairs in a mosque. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There will come upon people a time when they sit in circles in their mosques, and their only concern is the world; Allah has no need of them, so do not sit with them(5)."

It is as though the love of the world outside the mosque were not enough for them, and they covet the minutes they allot to prayer, so they drag the world along with them into the mosque. I say to them: why do you not leave the affairs of the world during those minutes? Each one of you lives in all the world by the blessing of Allah. So let him give a portion of his time to Allah, the Lord of blessing.

Therefore we must know that we have designated a place for the worship of Allah, and we must accompany this spatial designation with a designation of the purpose for which a person enters the mosque, so that he turns toward Allah; for the mosque is specific to the worship of Allah. Although the whole earth is suitable for prayer, when you come to the mosque, bring with you the manners of worship. Emotion, interaction, movement and activity must all be for Allah, and...

1. On the authority of Abu Hurayra, who said: "Abu Bakr sent me on that pilgrimage among the callers to prayer, sending them on the Day of Sacrifice to proclaim in Mina that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year, and no one should circumambulate the House naked." Hamid said: then the Prophet (ﷺ) sent 'Ali ibn Abi Talib after him and commanded him to proclaim the disavowal. Abu Hurayra said: so he called out with us among the people of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice with the disavowal, that no polytheist should perform Hajj after this year, and no one should circumambulate the House naked. Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4656).
2. al-Qurtubi said in his commentary on the verse: "The scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse. It was said: it means they are not permitted to perform Hajj after it was proclaimed to them that they were prevented from the Sacred Mosque, and the affairs of the House, such as the custodianship (sidana), the providing of water (siqaya), and the provision of food (rifada), had been in the hands of the polytheists; so He made clear that they are not qualified for that, rather its people are the believers."
3. Said by al-Suddi. Transmitted by Ibn Kathir and al-Qurtubi in their commentaries on the verse.
4. Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (335) and Muslim (521).
5. Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/323) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him; he said: its chain is sound though they did not record it. al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 18:

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Only he who believes in God and the Last Day, establishes the prayer, gives the zakat, and fears none but God—it is they who may be among the guided.﴾

Faith (al-iman): it is belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree, both its good and its evil. The pinnacle of faith is the testimony that "there is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God." There was sensitivity among the people of Quraysh regarding this matter of the Messenger, that he was Muhammad son of 'Abdullah. Some of them said: the Qur'an is beautiful and splendid, so why did it come through the tongue of Muhammad? The objection of the disbelievers of Quraysh to the Messenger (ﷺ) was in these words, which the Qur'an relates about them:

﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?﴾ (az-Zukhruf: 31)

So the problem for them was not in the Qur'an itself, but in the person of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).(1)

The Almighty responds with His words:

﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾ (az-Zukhruf: 31).
