He said: "Return with your women and children to the heights of your homes; if the matter is in your favor, those behind you will join you; and if the matter goes against you, you will not disgrace your families and children." Malik said to him: "You have grown old, and your experience and your intellect have gone." And he insisted on his opinion. Then Malik ibn 'Awf began to array the army in the ravines and under the trees, so that the Muslims would not see them upon their arrival, and would advance without being alert to danger, and then the attack would come upon them from every side and every place.

When the Muslim army came, they did not notice the disbelievers hidden from sight. Then Malik ibn 'Awf gave the signal to begin the attack, and the disbelievers emerged from every place and struck the Muslims with a fierce assault. The narrator said: "By Allah, the Muslims did not remain before them except for the time it takes to milk a sheep," so that, because of the harshness of the battle, the ferocity of its fighting and the strength of the surprise, the Muslim army was routed in the first hours of the battle, and some of those who fled reached Makkah. Only nine remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the battlefield, among them al-'Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was holding the reins of the mount the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was riding; Sayyidna 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was carrying the banner; Sayyidna al-Fadl, who stood on the right of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); Sayyidna Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who stood on his left; and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, along with a number of Companions(4).

Here we ask: why did this defeat of the Muslims occur at the beginning of the battle? Because when they went out to war, they said: "We are a multitude; we will not be defeated through few." Thus they relied on the means and forgot the Causer, so Allah wished to punish them with a punishment that would humiliate them and exalt the rank of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw what had happened, he said to al-'Abbas, who had a loud voice: "Call out to the people." So al-'Abbas cried out loudly: "O assembly of the Ansar, O people of Surat al-Baqarah, O people of the Pledge of the Tree!" When the people heard al-'Abbas's call, they said: "Here we are, here we are!" Whoever said "Labbayk" was heard by those behind him, who said the same, until a large number of believers returned to the fighting. The war grew hot, its flames rose, and the battle intensified, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed and said: "Now the furnace (hamy al-waṭīs) has become hot," meaning the battle has intensified. Then he, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "I am the Prophet, there is no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib."

This hadith is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) by al-Bara' ibn 'Azib. It is related in the two Sahihs from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (may Allah be pleased with him) that a man said to him: "O Abu 'Umarah, did you flee from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Hunayn?" He said: "But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flee. The Hawazin were a people skilled in archery; when we met them and charged upon them, they were routed, and the people turned to the spoils, and they met us with arrows, and the people fled..."

1 Agreed upon: reported by al-Bukhari (946) and Muslim (1770) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.
2 Hunayn: a name for a place in Awtas, known by the name of a man called Hunayn ibn Qaniyah ibn Muhlail from the 'Amaliq, as in Mu'jam al-Bakri.
3 Thughā' al-shāh: the sound and clamour of sheep and goats.
4 See: Zad al-Ma'ad fi Hadi Khayr al-'Ibad (2/185-187).
5 Al-Awar: smoke and flame.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ (26)

Meaning: Allah, blessed and exalted, first sent down His tranquility (sakinah) upon His Messenger and upon the believers who stood firm with him. Then He sent it down upon the believers who had fled from the battle and then returned to fight again. As for His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And sent down hosts you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ (At-Tawbah: 26)

We have been told that the angels descended and strengthened the believers, cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers, and sent punishment upon them. Those who believed were the ones who witnessed this, because they described beings upon piebald (balaq) horses (1), and they had nothing like them.

When the Noble Qur'an tells us that the angels descended and that there were those who saw them (2), then it is incumbent upon us to take the stance of the believer, and to trust the speaker, who is truthful. Let him believe in what he has said and not seek to know the how. And if any of you stands before this matter, let him not stand in the stance of one who rejects its existence, but in the stance of one who does not know its modality; for the existence of a thing is entirely different from the comprehension of how it exists.

There are many things in the universe that exist and carry out their function, and we do not comprehend how they exist. Our not comprehending them does not mean that they do not exist. Every discovery that contemporary science has presented to us was already existing. But we did not previously comprehend how they existed. Earth's gravity was existing, but we did not perceive its existence or how it works. Likewise, electricity was present in the universe since the beginning of creation, but we did not perceive its existence until Allah, exalted is He, revealed its existence to us, and we used it. And microbes were existing in the universe performing their function, and we did not know them, until Allah revealed them to us, and we came to know how they exist and the manner of their existence. All of these things were existing in Allah's creation since Allah created the universe, but we did not perceive their existence. Our lack of knowledge will not diminish this existence in the slightest. Therefore, if you are told of something your intellect cannot grasp, do not deny its existence, for there are things we knew nothing about, then Allah, exalted is He, gave us knowledge and we found that they live by specific material laws. So: the existence of a thing is entirely different from the perception of that existence.

As for the saying of the Truthful, exalted is He: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see﴾, the phrase ﴿you did not see﴾ gives an excuse to everyone who did not see, and it suffices that Allah has said it, to make this a factual reality. The Almighty, exalted is He, says:

﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except He﴾ (Al-Muddaththir: 31).

When we were told that Allah has creatures called jinn, just as He has other creatures called angels, and that the jinn see us while we do not see them, some took the stance of disbelief. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us: "Indeed, Satan runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs" (3).

Some people denied this statement and asked: How can Satan enter a person's veins and run through them like blood?! When we advanced in experimental science and discovered microbes, and saw from their study that they penetrate the body and enter the blood in the veins, did anyone sense the microbe as it penetrates his body? Did anyone know of the microbe at the moment it entered the body? Of course not. But when it multiplies, reproduces, and its effect begins to appear on our bodies, we feel it. This indicates that the microbe is extremely fine, to a degree that the sensory hairs beneath the skin do not perceive it. And due to its extreme fineness, it penetrates these hairs or passes between them, and we know nothing of it, and it enters the blood and runs in veins governed by a law: that the square of the radius is distributed among the whole. An example of this is what happens in the distribution of water. We bring a main pipe with a radius of eight inches and bring it into a village; the discharge is 8×8, i.e., 64 square inches. When we come to distribute it to other branch pipes, we take from it a pipe with a radius of four inches, from it we take a pipe with a radius of two inches, and from it we take a pipe with a radius of one inch or half an inch. The point is that the squares of the radii of the branch pipes equal what the large pipe discharges.

So it is with the blood vessels: the blood runs in wide arteries, veins, and fine capillaries. But the fineness of the microbe's size enables it to penetrate these capillaries without any blood flowing out of them. When these arteries narrow, diseases arise that we hear about, from the accumulation of cholesterol or the occurrence of clots, and then medicine intervenes to widen the arteries, since they are the blood's pipes. There are also surgeries performed with laser beams or other modern discoveries, where these beams penetrate the skin between the capillaries, because they are fine beams that cut no capillary and spill no blood.

So: everything inside the body is measured by the will of Allah, exalted is He, and every microbe has an incubation period it spends inside the body without our sensing it. Then afterward its effect begins, the disease appears, and the processes of the microbe's reproduction in the blood and the white blood cells' resistance to it take a long time, while we neither sense nor perceive what is happening.

If the "microbe," which is of your own matter, i.e., something that has density and a specific volume, and which you cannot see except with a microscope, where we find it has a frightening form, reproduces and propagates, and has a life cycle, if this microbe is not sensed by you while it is inside your body, then what of Satan, who is created from a matter more transparent than the matter of the microbe? Could you sense him if he entered your body? No. And if a material thing has entered your body and you did not sense it, then what of the creature Allah created from matter more subtle and lighter than clay? Can he not enter and run through the son of Adam as the blood runs?!

So when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Satan runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs," do not be astonished or deny it because you do not sense him. Allah has given you, in the world of material things, what is denser in creation and enters your body without your sensing it.

So: science has established for us that there are existent things we do not see. And if, using modern electron microscopes, we examined every cell in the human body, we would see wonders: in the human skin that we consider smooth, we would see wells from which sweat emerges, and other extremely fine details that the eye does not perceive. So when Allah, glorified and exalted, tells us that there are angels who descend and fight, we believe. And the Truthful, blessed and exalted, has provided for our humanity what reassures it, saying: ﴿hosts you did not see﴾. If one says, "I saw them," and another says, "I saw nothing," we say: the saying of the Truth ﴿you did not see﴾ means you did not see them all together; some glimpsed them, and some did not see them.

As for the saying of the Truthful, exalted is He: ﴿and punished those who disbelieved﴾, that means by killing, by capture, or by seizing their wealth. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾, means that the defeat that befell them was a recompense for their disbelief. But some ask: Why did the punishment not descend and the defeat not occur from the very first moment of the battle? We say: Allah wanted to increase their punishment. For had He inflicted defeat upon them from the very first moment, it would have been lighter on their souls and less punishing. But He first gave them the joy of victory, so that the defeat would come more harsh and more grievous. The poet says:

As a cloud reaches a people parched with thirst,
But when they see it, it disperses and vanishes.

When a cloud passes over a people suffering from severe thirst, they dream that it will rain upon them, but the dream vanishes entirely, like the prisoner who suffers from intense thirst. He asks the jailer for a sip of water, and the jailer says: I will bring it to you. Indeed, the jailer goes and brings him a cup of chilled water, gives it to him, and the prisoner takes the cup in his hand, his soul filled with joy. Suddenly the jailer strikes his hand hard, and the cup falls to the ground, and the prisoner is struck with severe shock. This is among the most hideous methods of torture. Had the jailer refused to bring the cup of water from the outset, it would have been less painful for the prisoner. But after bringing the cup and placing it in his hand, then depriving him of it, this is more torturous. Thus Allah wanted to increase the torment of the disbelievers: He gave them first the preludes of victory and its sweetness, then the bitterness of defeat came after, to strip them of everything. Thus two calamities gathered upon them: the calamity of granting, and the calamity of taking away.

Then comes the glimpse of mercy with which Allah, glorified and exalted, envelops His creation, opening the door to every sinner to return to the path of faith, so that Allah accepts him. The Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, says:

﴿Then Allah relents after that to whomever He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (9:27)

This is the greatness of the Creator, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. He always keeps the door open for His servants, because He is the Creator of this universe. For everyone who disobeys, Allah opens before him the door of repentance. This is a logical matter, for the one who disbelieves and the one who disobeys do not harm Allah in the least; rather, they harm themselves and attempt to deviate from the laws of truth. When the disobedient person knows that he has no refuge except Allah, then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, opens for him the door of repentance.

After Allah, glorified and exalted, had shown us in this surah that Allah and His Messenger are free of obligation toward the polytheists, and had revealed their nature, that they have neither covenant nor pact, and after He clarified these matters with a doctrinal clarity in ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger﴾, and commanded us to terminate the treaties between us and them, so that whoever breaks the covenant, his covenant ends, and whoever keeps it, we keep the covenant with him until its term, then He commanded that the polytheists not approach the Sacred Mosque, and He cleansed any resentment or sin by opening the door of repentance.

Thereafter, Glorified is He moves from the treaty that ended with the disbelievers themselves to the disbelievers in their own persons, so He says, Blessed and Exalted is He:

﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ [9:28]

That is: it is not enough for the believers to cut off all their covenants with the polytheists; they must also disassociate themselves from the polytheists themselves, because they are unclean (najas). The najas is the filthy thing from which the soul recoils and shrinks. The polytheist may be acceptable in terms of outward form and dress, but this is only the mould, whereas when the Truth, Glorified is He, speaks, He speaks of meanings and of the inner reality. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not look at moulds but at hearts. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in the hadith narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "Indeed Allah does not look at your bodies nor at your forms, but He looks at your hearts."(1)

The form may be acceptable outwardly, yet the belief that exists in the hearts of those bodies is filthy and unclean, and He, Glorified is He, does not take by the outward appearance or by forms, but by values. When you look at values and at sound, true beliefs, you find that every belief reveals the nature of its substance. For example, when you are happy, it shows on your features, and whoever meets you will notice it and know that you are joyful; and if you are angry or suffering from distress, this too shows on your features.

So: the substance is affected by the affect of values, and as long as values are corrupt, the substance from which the body is formed becomes rebellious against its owner, because substance by its nature worships and glorifies Allah, and likewise the spirit by its nature worships and glorifies Allah, Exalted is He. Corruption arises only after the spirit is placed into the substance; then the soul (nafs) is formed from the two together, the substance and the spirit. If the soul prevails over the way of Allah, it becomes at rest (mutma'innah); if the soul wavers between obedience and disobedience, then either it obeys and becomes a self-reproaching soul (nafs lawwamah), or it disbelieves and takes the path of evil and becomes a soul that commands to evil (nafs ammarah bil-su'). But before the spirit is breathed into the substance, each of them glorifies Allah, Exalted is He, because everything in existence worships and glorifies. The soul in all its conduct is subdued to the will of its owner by subjection from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When death comes, human will ends and the human's control over his body falls away; indeed, this body will bear witness against its owner on the Day of Resurrection. A human in the life of this world lives with his will controlling his substance by the command of Allah: the hand may strike a person, or it may help another person who has fallen into hardship; the tongue of the Muslim testifies that there is no god but Allah, and the tongue of the disbeliever associates other gods with Allah.

So: a human's substance is subject to the will of its owner in the world of contingent things; but when he passes to the Hereafter, it has no influence over the substance, and the substance is freed from obedience to its owner in disobedience, rebels against him, and bears witness against its owner that he used it in disobedience.

The Truth, Glorified is He, says:

﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their sight and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do. And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who has made everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned."﴾ [41:20-21]

It is as though the limbs of a human say to him on the Day of Resurrection: "You exhausted me in the world and compelled me to do things I would never have done, because I am an obedient, glorifying servant of Allah, and what you ordered me to do departs from the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." I have already given the example of the battalion commander who issues wrong orders and the soldiers obey him; when they return to the supreme commander, they complain to him of what the battalion commander was forcing them to do. Likewise, the parts of the body bear witness against it before their Creator on the Day of Resurrection. If you are an obedient, glorifying servant, your limbs are with you; if you are otherwise, your limbs are against you. The tongue, for example, is by its essence obedient and glorifying; if you compel it to associate others with Allah, it is coerced in the world, and it becomes a witness against you on the Day of Resurrection.

The Truth, Glorified is He, will call out on that day, saying:

﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [40:16]

Here the Truth, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed the polytheists are unclean﴾, meaning that their corrupt belief becomes evident in their conduct. Glorified is He nurtures the meanings of faith in souls, that is, increases them. An example of this: we stone Iblis as one of the rites of the Hajj; we stone a piece of rock that we have symbolised as Satan, though we do not see Satan. We have set up a symbol for him and firmly established in our depths that Satan is our enemy and that we must stone him so as to keep away from his desires. Thus we have manifested these meanings in a sensory act, so as to make clear to the human soul that Satan is our enemy; and whenever Satan whispers to us about some matter, we stone him by making clear to ourselves the clear matters of faith, and so he flees from us. Each of us must remember that Satan will laugh at the disobedient and the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, and will say what the Truth, Glorified is He, has related on his tongue:

﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me.﴾ [14:22]

In this statement there is mockery of those who believed him, because authority is either the authority of compulsion, by which you bring a person something greater than himself and force him by strength to do a thing, or the authority of persuasion, by which you convince a person to do something. Satan has neither the authority of compulsion nor the authority of proof.

When the Truth, Glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, He makes clear to us that their uncleanness obliges us to prevent them from entering places that only a pure person enters. The Truth, Glorified is He, made moral uncleanness like material uncleanness, and therefore the scholars said: since the Truth has described them as unclean, there must be material uncleanness in them; hence when you draw near them you find an unpleasant smell, because they do not purify themselves from minor impurity and do not bathe from major impurity. When we went to Algeria after its liberation from France, we found no bathrooms in the houses, because one of the colonists would not go to the bath except once every twenty days, for example; so they placed the bathrooms far from the dwellings. But after Algeria was liberated, bathrooms appeared in the houses, because Islamic culture is built on purity, and it is incumbent on the Muslim that whenever a person enters the bath he purifies himself, and whenever he is in a state of major impurity he bathes.

Some have said: if I greet a polytheist whose hand is moist, I must wash my hand; if his hand is dry, it suffices for me to wipe my hand.(2) In this there is caution and emphasis on avoiding these polytheists. And if we avoid them in bodies and forms, should we not avoid them in hearts?

Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this noble verse in the ninth year after the Hijrah, the year in which the prohibition on polytheists approaching al-Masjid al-Haram and the disavowal of these polytheists was issued. The scholars asked: is what is prohibited and forbidden the polytheist's approach to al-Masjid al-Haram, or to the whole Haram? Imam al-Shafi'i specified the prohibition on the polytheists to their presence in al-Masjid al-Haram. With our respect for the ijtihad of Imam al-Shafi'i, we say: the Truth, Glorified is He, said ﴿fa-la yaqrabu﴾ and did not say "fa-la yadkhulu" (let them not enter). The prohibition of approaching means they should not be close to it, and the closest thing to al-Masjid al-Haram is the whole Haram; and had the intended meaning been the mosque alone, the Truth would have prohibited their entry into it by explicit text.(3)

Thus we see how a person can exert ijtihad and examine meanings to extract the true content. The Mawla, Glorified is He, continues His statement: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ In this noble statement there is a discourse about the unseen (al-ghayb). The unseen, as we have known, is what is hidden from you and from others. As for what is hidden from you but not from others, it is not unseen: if money is stolen from you, for example, you do not know who stole it, and the thief in this case is hidden from you, but he is not hidden from others; the thief knows himself, the one who planned the crime knows him, and whoever saw him and concealed it knows him. You also do not know where the stolen things are, but the thief knows the place where he hid them.

So: it is unseen to you but not unseen to others. This is the trick of charlatans and swindlers who enslave the jinn: as long as a thing is known and recognised by others, uncovering it is an easy matter. But there is an unseen that is hidden from you and from others, and this is what the Truth, Glorified is He, alone possesses, in His statement, Glorified is He:

﴿Knower of the unseen; He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to one whom He has approved of among messengers...﴾ [72:26-27]

But there is an unseen hidden from all people, which will not remain unseen until the end of time: for example, electricity was unseen and we discovered it; the splitting of the atom was unseen and we came to know it; the laws of gravity were unseen and then entered human knowledge and became known to him. This is not the unseen that Allah, Glorified is He, intends in His statement ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾; that unseen belongs to Himself alone. So do not say that so-and-so knows the unseen; rather say that he is one who has been taught some of the unseen. Unseen matters are either veiled by time or veiled by place. Buried remains, for example, express something past that has vanished, and in them are reports of earlier nations, and no one knows them; the veil of past time has covered them, until they are fully uncovered and Allah prepares for them someone who unravels their riddles.

As for Allah informing His Messenger of matters concerning the peoples of earlier times, which came in the noble Qur'an, this is a breaching of the veil of past time, as in His statement, Exalted is He:

﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, which of them would be guardian of Maryam; and you were not with them when they disputed.﴾ [3:44]

And He, Glorified is He, says:

﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Musa, and you were not among the witnesses. But We produced generations, and the life span lengthened over them; and you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were sending [messengers].﴾ [28:44-45]

His statement, Glorified is He, "and you were not" in other verses is evidence that Allah, Glorified is He, informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of what had been hidden in past time. As for what will happen in the future, it is veiled from you by the veil of future time; yet the noble Qur'an has breached the veil of the future in many verses, all beginning with the letter sin, and the letter sin is evidence that the thing has not yet happened. His statement, Exalted is He:

﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ [41:53]

is evidence that from future time Allah reveals to us His signs that exist in the earth. And His statement, Exalted is He:

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome, within several years.﴾ [30:1-4]

This is a breaching of the veil of the future, because the victory occurred nine years after the revelation of this verse. So: what happens in the future is veiled from you by future time; but there is something that happens in the present and which we do not know, and it is veiled from you by the veil of place: whatever happens in a place where you are not present, you do not know it. If you are sitting in Makkah, for example, you do not know what is happening in Madinah al-Munawwarah.

(1) Meaning: on the Day of Reckoning, the criterion is the look at your hearts, not your outward appearances, and this contains an exhortation to attend to the heart and purify it. The hadith was narrated by Imam Muslim (2564), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/285, 539), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4143); the wording is Muslim's.

(2) Al-Hasan al-Basri said: whoever shakes hands with a polytheist should perform wudu'. Cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3030). Ibn Kathir (2/346) said: "This noble verse indicates the uncleanness of the polytheist, as is reported in the authentic hadith: 'The believer is not unclean.' As for the uncleanness of his body, the majority agreed that it is not a matter of the substance and essence of the body, because Allah the Exalted made the food of the People of the Book lawful; some of the Zahiriyyah went to the view that their bodies are unclean. Ash'ath reported from al-Hasan: whoever shakes hands with them should perform wudu'." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

(3) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3031): "Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the verse is general regarding all polytheists and specific to al-Masjid al-Haram, and they are not prevented from entering other than it; so he permitted the entry of Jews and Christians into all mosques." Ibn al-Arabi said: "This is rigid adherence to the apparent meaning on his part, because the Mighty and Majestic's statement ﴿Indeed the polytheists are unclean﴾ is an indication of the cause, which is shirk and uncleanness."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 30:

Then he said after that:

﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their saying from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾ (30)

This claim touches upon the majesty of Allah, exalted is He. A person adopts a son for several reasons: either because he wishes his remembrance to remain in this world after he departs, whereas Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is everlasting in existence; or so that his son may help him when he grows old and weak, whereas Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is everlasting in strength; or so that he may inherit his wealth and what he possesses, whereas Allah, blessed and exalted is He, inherits the earth and whoever is upon it; or so that he may be a source of strength for him, whereas Allah, majestic in His majesty, is always Mighty. Thus, all the reasons that could lead to this claim are negated. And it is not conceivable that Allah, glorified is He, would send a Messenger to clarify for people the path of truth, only for him to tell the people: "He is the son of Allah." Therefore, they did not believe in Allah with complete faith.

The Blessed and Exalted Lord relates the saying of each of the Jews and the Christians: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾

Thus we find that they did not declare Allah free from such attributes, and they failed in true faith. We must know that those who said "Ezra is the son of Allah" were not all the Jews, but only a group of them, which made Ezra a son of Allah when they saw on his hands a blessing that Allah had bestowed upon him. They said: "This is a very great blessing; our Lord would not give it to an ordinary person, but He gave it to His son." That is because the Jews, after the time of our master Moses, peace be upon him, killed the prophets, and Allah punished them by lifting the Torah from the breasts of those who had memorized it. But a child was not pleased with the sight of the killing of the prophets, so he went out wandering in the desert, emigrating and fleeing. A person met him on the road and asked him: "Why are you wandering?" He said: "I went out seeking knowledge." That person was Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he taught him that Allah has a Torah, so he memorized it and became one of four who alone had memorized the Torah: Moses, Jesus, Uzair, and al-Yasa‘. Because books in ancient times were not written on thin paper like in our time, but were written on stones and palm leaves, the weight of the Torah was estimated at seventy camel loads. When Uzair returned having memorized the Torah, his people were amazed and said: "He must be the son of Allah, for Allah gave him the Torah and preferred him over all the people"(1). A group of Jews emerged who believed in this, among them Sallam ibn Mishkam, Shas ibn Qays, Malik ibn al-Sayf, and Nu‘man ibn Awfa. When Allah revealed His saying: ﴿And the Jews say, "Uzair is the son of Allah,"﴾, the contemporary Jews at the time of this revelation did not deny that matter nor did they refute it. It is as if there were among the Jews in Medina those who believed in this, for otherwise they would have objected to this saying. This is evidence that what the verse states is affirmed by some of them, or that they knew that a group among them had said this. Likewise, the Christians said about Jesus, peace be upon him, and so the saying of the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, came: ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾

The Truth continues: ﴿That is their saying﴾, clarifying for us, glorified is He, that prophethood for Allah came with a resemblance, which they should have paid attention to, and should have declared Allah free of it; because the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted describes His servants as servants of Allah, and all creation is the creation of Allah, exalted is He.

The Lord, glorified and exalted is He, who is the Creator and capable of everything, created all creation from nothingness, and He did not take a consort or a son. But the confusion among some of the followers of the Messiah came from the fact that he was brought into existence without a father. We say to them: If this matter came to you by this route, then it would have been more fitting for the same confusion to arise regarding the creation of Adam; for the utmost that is in the Messiah is that he came without a father, but Adam came without a father and without a mother. So which of them was more fitting to be a son of God?

For this reason the Noble Qur'an says: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam.﴾ The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, creates a thing—any thing—through causes, and all causes are created by Him; and a child among us—in the general run of people—comes from the union of a father and a mother. A thing brought about between two things has four logical forms: either it comes into being through the existence of two things, male and female; or it comes into being through the absence of both things, like Adam; or it comes into being through the existence of one of the two things, the male, like Eve, for Allah created her from Adam, in fulfilment of His saying: ﴿and created from it its mate﴾; or through the existence of one of the two things, the female, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was created from her without the presence of a male. And so that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, may teach us all that causes have no effect on creation, and that the Causer is capable of bringing into being without a father and mother as He brought Adam into being, and bringing into being from a father and mother as He brought the general run of people into being, and bringing into being from a mother without a father as He brought Jesus into being, and bringing into being without Adam as He brought Eve into being.

So then: the division is governed by the power and will of Allah, and no one has any part except the will of the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He. Causes are not in themselves the agents; rather the will of the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, is the agent. For this reason the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.﴾ (Ash-Shura)

That is: a male and a female may exist and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gives them no children; and this is the absolute power of Allah, exalted is He. So beware of saying that it is by causes; rather, glorified and exalted is He, bestows females upon whom He wills, bestows males upon whom He wills, combines males and females for whom He wills, and renders barren whom He wills. The reception of births by people differs: the Arabs loved begetting males, because they are strong, achieve strength, ride horses and fight enemies. They did not love girls, because scandals might come from them. For this reason the Blessed and Exalted Lord says:

﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female, his face darkens and he is filled with suppressed rage. He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given good news of. Should he keep it despite disgrace, or bury it in the dust? Surely, evil is what they judge.﴾ (An-Nahl)

Islam came to clarify that since you have no part in begetting and offspring, leave the matter to the One who grants children. The Blessed and Exalted Lord has called children "gifts" to remind you that begetting is something He, glorified is He, has given you without any compensation from you. So males are a gift, and females are also a gift. Do not prefer one gift over the other. I always say to the one who begets daughters, and goes with his wife to the doctors: If you received Allah's gift in females as you receive it in males, then the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted would reward you with a reward beyond what occurs to your mind; Allah would make every daughter of yours beloved in the eyes of a righteous man who would marry her. If they were ten daughters, they would bring ten husbands, who would treat the father and mother of each wife as a father and mother. Thus Allah provides for whoever is content with Allah's distribution in begetting, and the sons-in-law become more obedient than male sons. The one who is content with the gift of females, Allah makes clear to him: "You were content with My gift to you and you were not of the Arabs' custom of disliking females; therefore I give you, from your sons-in-law, sons whom you did not labour to raise, and who will be more tender and loyal than any sons you would beget yourself." Therefore, whenever you find a person who has been granted success in marrying off his daughters to men who guard their honour and treat the wife's family well, know that this father received the birth of a female with contentment, because she is Allah's gift. The Lord, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿and renders whom He wills barren﴾ (Ash-Shura: 50).

So then: barrenness too is a divine gift; for when a person receives barrenness with the pleasure of Allah, he finds in every man he sees a son of his own, because he has received the gift in withholding with contentment, just as one who receives females as he receives males. So then: since the matter is a gift from Allah, you must receive Allah's giving and His withholding with contentment.

Jesus, peace be upon him, came as an instance of the absolute power of the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, because the doctrinal and rational division is not completed except by Him, and it will not be repeated; for Adam was brought into being first, and those who came after Adam each came from two parents, and likewise Eve was brought into being before them. These are three forms that have existed in the universe, and the remaining forms are incomplete: that a human being should come from a mother without a father. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, completed this with Jesus, peace be upon him:

﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their saying with their mouths.﴾

The Truth's saying ﴿That﴾ refers to the saying that the Messiah is the son of Allah or Uzair is the son of Allah; and the Mighty and Majestic adds clarification: ﴿their saying with their mouths﴾. We ask: Is there a saying without mouths? Every saying is only by mouths; even the saying of the believers that Allah is One and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah is a saying by mouths. We say: there is a saying by the mouth only, without any meaning whatsoever, and there is also a saying by the mouth that has meaning, but it is not real, and is false.

Let us first know: what is speech? It is words by which every people expresses its purposes; as when you say to a child: "Sit," and the child must understand the meaning of sitting; and if you said it in Arabic to an English child, he would not understand its meaning.

So then: language is words by which every people expresses its purposes, and the purpose is a meaning agreed upon between speaker and listener, and both must know what the word refers to among objects. If the listener does not know the word the speaker uses, he understands nothing.

Thus we know that understanding between speaker and addressee requires that both be knowledgeable of the word; if a speaker says something the listener has no knowledge of, he does not understand. Formerly they used to give us the example of 'Alqama the grammarian, who was famous in grammar, vocabulary and language, and affected obscurity in his use of words, speaking only in the eloquent, rare language that people do not know. 'Alqama had a servant. Once 'Alqama fell ill and went to a doctor named "A'jaz" to complain to him of an ailment he had. 'Alqama said to the doctor: "I have eaten from the flesh of these jawazi, and I gorged upon a gorging which caused me a pain of the wabiya reaching to the nape of the neck, and it kept on troubling me until it mixed with the khalab, and from it I hoped for the sarasib." The doctor was not a specialist in language and had no dictionaries, so he stood astonished at 'Alqama's words and said to him: "Repeat to me what you said, for I did not understand." 'Alqama repeated what he had said with anger and reproach, because he had not understood his language. The doctor recognised 'Alqama's affectation and said to him: "Bring me pen and paper so I may write you the medicine," and he wrote for him: "Take a ḥurqa, a salqa and a rahraqa, wash it with māward and drink it with water, water." 'Alqama said: "Repeat it to me, for by God I did not understand anything." The doctor said: "May God curse the one of us who is less able to make his companion understand." 'Alqama realised that he was affected in language and used words that are not among the words circulating on people's tongues. Our teachers told us that only his servant, that is his attendant, corrected him in this. One night 'Alqama woke up and said: "O boy, have the 'atarif been struck with thunderbolt?" The boy did not understand, so he replied: "Zaqfeel." 'Alqama said to the boy: "And what is zaqfeel?" He said: "And you, have the 'atarif not been struck?" He said to him: "My son, did you mean the roosters have shouted?" He said: "And I meant they did not crow."

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ So then: speech is the utterance produced from the mouth, and this speech either has meaning or has no meaning. Like the word "zaqfeel" which the servant of 'Alqama said, this word has no existence in the language; it is speech by the tongue with no meaning. There may be speech that has meaning, yet it is words by the tongue without

Al-Sha'rawi, in his commentary on Surah 9, verse 31:

The Almighty says after that, concerning the People of the Book:

﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary. Yet they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no god but Him. Glorified is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ (9:31)

"Al-habr" (rabbi, scholar) is a title among the Jews, and it means the learned man. In the language it is said "hibr" or "habr," meaning a man who examines speech and weighs it with the manner of a scholar. Among the Christians, the "ruhban" (monks) are meant to be those who devote themselves to worship. So the habr is the scholar of the Jews, and the rahib is the worshipper of the Christians. The scholar of the Christian religion is called "qissis" (priest), and for this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿qissisin wa ruhban﴾ (5:82).

If we mean the scholar of the Christian religion, we say "qissis"; and if we mean the man of practice, that is, the worshipper, we say "rahib." The rahib is one who says that he has devoted himself to the worship of God beyond what God required of the same kind. We know that there is no monasticism (rahbaniyya) in Islam(1), but a person may draw near to God in whatever way he wishes, from the same kind of what God has required of him. If the Truth, mighty and majestic, has commanded the establishment of prayer five times a day, then the Muslim who desires to draw nearer to God may pray twice the number of prayers. And if the Truth, glory be to Him, has prescribed zakat at two and a half percent, the righteous servant may increase it by double or many times over. This is an increase of the same kind as what God has prescribed, plus more, and this in Islam means entering the station of ihsan (excellence)(2). Read, if you wish, the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good.﴾ (51:15-16)

That is, they had entered the station of ihsan, meaning they had risen above the station of faith. The Truth increases our knowledge of the station of ihsan when He says:

﴿They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness, and in their wealth there was a right for the one who asks and the deprived.﴾ (51:17-19)

He, glory be to Him, does not require of us in the obligations of religion that we sleep only a little of the night; rather, we pray the night prayer and sleep until dawn. But if one of us stands in prayer during the night and performs tahajjud, that is an increase beyond what God has obligated, yet it is of the same kind as what God has obligated. Likewise seeking forgiveness: whoever does it voluntarily, it is good for him. Likewise charity to someone other than the needy: here is an increase in giving beyond the zakat God prescribed, which was previously specified in the words of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right﴾ (70:24).

Monasticism was a desire on the part of some of them to enter the station of ihsan, but God did not prescribe it for them, because He is the One who created and knew from eternity the capacities of His creatures. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿But monasticism, they invented it; We did not prescribe it for them﴾ (57:27).

They, then, invented it seeking the pleasure of God and as an increase in worship, and there is no blame upon them in that; but it is contrary to human nature, so they did not observe monasticism with its proper observance. The Lord, glory be to Him, says here in the noble verse about which we are reflecting:

﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords﴾. Does that mean that they say to the rabbi or the monk, "Lord"? No, but their treatment of them was like the treatment of one who treats his lord; for Allah is the One who makes lawful and unlawful with "do" and "do not." So when these rabbis came and made lawful something God had made unlawful, or made unlawful something God had made lawful, they had in fact taken the attribute of divinity and ascribed it to them, because legislating what is lawful and unlawful is the authority of God. Hence, when Adi ibn Hatim entered upon our master, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found the Messenger, peace be upon him, seeing a gold or silver cross around the man's neck, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Remove this idol." And out of courtesy toward the Messenger, the man removed the cross. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, also said: "Indeed you take your rabbis and monks as lords." The man said: "We do not worship them." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: "Do you not obey them in what they forbid and permit?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is worship"(4).

﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary.﴾ And one may ask: what is the meaning of joining the Messiah with the lords, and with the rabbis and monks? The answer: one who makes lawful and unlawful, if he is not a messenger, is a human seeking worldly authority, and that does not befit a messenger; for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, came only to draw people to the worship of God through what God legislated, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was a messenger who did nothing but convey from God. But some erred in their assessment and thought he was the son of God. Therefore the Truth continues His statement:

﴿Yet they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no god but Him. Glorified is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ Thus the Truth mentions that the command issued from Him, glory be to Him, was only that the one God be worshipped by those who believe in the messages. And our Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:

﴿The best thing I and the prophets before me have said is: There is no god but Allah﴾(5).

When you look at "There is no god but Allah," you find the negation in "la" and the exception from negation and affirmation in "illa." This is the negation of divinity from other than God and its affirmation for Him alone. When we say "Allah is One," this includes only affirmation. Philosophers who possess eloquence and expression take from this matter "affirmation and negation," or "the positive and the negative," and they say: every meeting of a positive and a negative produces energy, and energy can be used for lighting or to run a machine; likewise faith-energy needs "a negative and a positive." The poet Iqbal says:

"Tawhid is affirmation and negation,
In both is resolve and vigor."

And God, glory be to Him, says, as an appendix to the noble verse: ﴿Glorified is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ When you hear the word ﴿Glorified﴾ (subhanahu), know that it is for tanzih (transcendence), so there is no essence like the essence of God, and no attribute like the attributes of God. God is rich and you are rich; but is your created richness like the eternal richness of God? You are living and God is living; but is your temporary life like His life? His life is essential, and your life is bestowed. He, glory be to Him, is living in His essence; therefore you must distinguish between His name "al-Hayy" (the Living) and His name "al-Muhyi" (the Giver of Life). He is living in His essence, and giver of life to others. Although the attribute belongs to God in essence, it does not extend to others: God is described by it and is not described by its opposite. You say "Living" and you do not say its counterpart; but if you say "Giver of life," you bring a counterpart and say "Causer of death." You say "Withholder and Extender," and "Merciful and Subduer."

Thus: the attribute of essence is one by which God is described and by whose opposite He is not described; but the attribute of action is one by which He is described and by its opposite, because it relates to others. So He, glory be to Him, is the giver of life to others and the causer of death to others, but He is living in His essence. Therefore the word ﴿Glorified﴾ means transcendence in essence, attributes, and actions. When an action comes from God, and a similar action comes from a human, we say: the action of God, mighty and majestic, is different from the action of humans, because God's action is without treatment(6), whereas human action is with treatment. That is, every portion of time takes a measure of the action; for example, when you move something from one place to another, you take time and duration according to your strength. But the action of God, mighty and majestic, requires no time, and His power, glory be to Him and exalted, is infinite:

Therefore, when our master, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "I was taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis," those who heard him said: "Do you claim that you went there in one night, when we travel to it for a month on the backs of camels?"(7) But none of them noticed that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say: "I went there by my own power," but said: "I was taken by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque." Therefore, the One who took him by night is the powerful, capable God, and God does not need time.

Thus: ﴿Glorified is He﴾ is the transcendence of God, glory be to Him, above anything that exists in humans. The power of God, glory be to Him, is not to be compared with the power of any human whatever; rather, the work is attributed to the power of its doer, and the more power, the more capacity, and God is the Most Powerful. His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Glorified is He above what they associate with Him﴾ is a declaration of God's transcendence, and you will not find a human saying to another, even among the disbelievers who obstinately oppose faith, that any of them says to another ﴿Glory be to You﴾, because transcendence is a matter specific to God, mighty and majestic.

People give names to their children; names are within human capacity. But you will not find an obstinate disbeliever, one who wars against the religion of God, naming his son "Allah." The believer does not dare this naming because he believes in God, and the disbeliever never dares it, by the power and subjugation of God. Therefore the word ﴿Glorified﴾ and the word "Allah" are two expressions specific to God alone, by the absolute power of God, glory be to Him.

Thus: God, by power and subjugation, has restrained the tongues of all humans from saying to anyone "Glory be to you," or from naming a son "Allah."

And God, mighty and majestic, says here: ﴿There is no god but He. Glorified is He above what they associate with Him﴾; and the stance of the polytheists and the People of the Book falls under this verse, because the divine method does not come except when corruption has spread. God, glory be to Him, wants from man, the vicegerent on earth, that he be righteous and a reformer, and the least degree of righteousness is that you leave the righteous thing and do not corrupt it; but if you can elevate it, that is best. If there is a well from which people drink, then righteousness is to leave the well and not fill it in; more righteous than that is to protect its walls with brick so that the dirt does not collapse and block it, and to try to make it easier for people to obtain water from the well; and more righteous still is to build a high tank from which pipes extend so that water reaches people in their homes without effort. This is reform, because by doing so you are taking up the causes of the Truth, who says about the distinction of thought, concerning Dhu al-Qarnayn:

﴿And We gave him of every thing a means. So he followed a means﴾ (18:84-85).

That is: God, glory be to Him, gave Dhu al-Qarnayn the means, and he, by his own effort, added other means. Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, wants man to reform on earth so that society may be happy with any reform on earth, and everyone benefits from it. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, gives choices in some matters and does not give them in others. Man has a choice in whether to pray or not, to give charity or not, to work or not, and so on, as far as we know. But the higher universe is governed by compulsion: the sun, the moon, the stars, the air, the water, and all of this have a precise order; neither the sun nor the moon nor the stars, nor anything else of the higher universe, is subject to human choice, or else the universe would be corrupted. Every compelled thing is sound by nature, and corruption occurs only in the thing in which man has choice, because choice may follow desire and the whims of the soul. Even compelled creatures such as the animals that God subjected to man do not bring evil; rather, their droppings are used to increase the fertility of the land. But the things that man has made have filled the atmosphere of the world with poisons and polluted the air; because the first are created by divine engineering, while the second are human, their maker knowing some things and being ignorant of others.

People may believe that some discoveries have solved the problems of the universe, and then years pass and they learn that these brought misery to humanity. Perhaps the pollution of the environment, which has lately begun to affect the life of the universe, draws our attention to this, until

Ibn Ishaq said: When he woke in the morning, he went to Quraysh and informed them of the report. Most people said: By God, this is a manifest matter.
