The word "imr" means a great, wondrous, and reprehensible matter.

Earlier we said that God, glory be to Him, struck a parable for the Truth and made for it two lights. The first light is sensory (hissi), and it belongs to material things. The second light is immaterial (ma'nawi), and it belongs to values. Just as sensory light guides a person along his path without his colliding with anything, because if a person collides with something smaller than himself he breaks it, and if the thing is larger than him it breaks him, so light plays its role in sensory matters. Likewise God has made a light for immaterial matters. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, said:

﴿Light upon light. God guides to His light whom He wills.﴾ (al-Nur: 35)

The corrupter (al-mufsid) dislikes that such a light should exist; rather, he wants to extinguish it. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says after that:

﴿They desire to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ (al-Tawbah: 32)

But can they extinguish the light of God? No. In sensory matters a person cannot extinguish the light, because there is a difference between the source of light and the instrument of illumination. A person can smash the glass casing that holds the light, but no one is able to extinguish the "illuminator" (al-munawwir), and the highest illuminator is God, and no one can put Him out.

﴿They desire to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God refuses﴾ means: God does not will anything ﴿except to perfect His light﴾. God, glory be to Him, sent the Messengers carrying the method of light, and He did not send the Messengers so that disbelief would prevail over them. For this reason He tells us: ﴿but God refuses﴾, that is, He does not will ﴿except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it﴾.

He, Glorified and Exalted is He, continues His saying:

﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾ (9:33)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came only with the principles that guide to the straight path; he came with the true religion. The word "dīn" (religion) has been used and applied to falsehood as well. Did not Allah, the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, command His Prophet (ﷺ) to say to the disbelievers and the polytheists of Makkah:

﴿To you your religion, and to me my religion.﴾ (109:6) (al-Kafirun)

Did they then have a religion? Yes, they had that which they followed, of beliefs they had devised and invented; but ﴿the religion of truth﴾ is that which came from heaven.

﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion.﴾ Let us note that Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, stated this to affirm that Islam came to prevail above every corrupt religion, and we know that there are many religions that came from falsehood. He, Glorified is He, says:

﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted.﴾ (23:71) (al-Mu'minun)

We pause at the saying of Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He: ﴿over all religion﴾. Had the corruption in the universe been of one kind, it would have said: that He may make it prevail over the existing corrupt religion. But there are many religions: among them Buddhism, the beliefs of the polytheists, the religions of the People of the Book, the Magians who worship fire or certain kinds of animals, and likewise the Sabians(1). Therefore Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, does not wish to make His religion, which is the religion of truth, prevail over just one religion of the existing false religions; rather He wishes to make it prevail over all of them, and to elevate it until the religion of Allah stands atop the backs of all these religions. Anything that comes upon the back of something becomes high and manifest.

Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, says:

﴿So they were not able to scale it [or: to get atop it].﴾ (18:97) (al-Kahf) That is, to come upon its back. All religions are in a position far lower than the Islamic religion. Some people ask: then how is there still disbelievers, Magians, Buddhists, Sabians and adherents of other religions such as Judaism and Christianity, whose religions still exist in the world and whose followers are many? We say: let us understand the meaning of the word "ʿilāʾ" (elevation). Elevation is the elevation of proofs, soundness and teachings. This means that the world opposed to Islam will be struck by cosmic and social issues, and will find no way out for them except by following what Islam has commanded, and they will take their legislation from Islam. In this case they are not taking the teachings of Islam as a religion, but they take them as a social necessity without which life cannot be set right. As for you as a Muslim, when you are zealous for the teachings of your religion, this is no testimony that you have believed; rather your conscience and the depth of your insight have driven you to believe in the true religion. But the strong testimony comes when the adversary who hates Islam and opposes it is compelled to take an issue from the issues of Islam in order to resolve his problems with it. Here is the strong testimony, which comes from the opponent of your religion or your enemy. The meaning of this is that he did not find in any other thought in the universe a solution to this issue, so he took it from Islam.

For example, if we say: Italy, in which is the Vatican, which controls the Christian beliefs in the entire Western world, and the Catholic Church in the Vatican used to fight divorce and attack Islam because it permits divorce; then the enormous problems that faced Italian society and other European societies compelled them to permit divorce, because they found no solution to the grave social problems except by that.

But did they permit it because Islam permitted it, or did they permit it because their social problems cannot be solved except by permitting divorce? When they take a solution to their issue from our religion and apply the solution as legislation, this is a strong testimony by which the soundness of Allah's religion is confirmed, and by which the saying of Allah, the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, is confirmed: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ By Allah, if the prevailing meant doctrinal dominance, in the sense that no other religions exist on earth but only one religion, which is Islam, He would not have said here: ﴿even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾, nor would He have said in another place in the Qur'an: ﴿even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾ This means that Allah, the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, has made among the opponents of Islam those who will have Islam prevail over other religions, not by prevalence of conviction and faith; no, rather they remain upon their religion, but their circumstances compel them to take solutions to their difficult issues from Islam. Another example from another issue is the issue of breastfeeding. Allah, the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, says:

﴿The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two full years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing.﴾ (2:233) Many campaigns arose in Europe and America against natural breastfeeding, and people were urged to use dried, chemically manufactured milk instead of mother's milk, which in their view was a more perfect system for nourishing the infant. Then afterward enormous harms appeared on the child's health and psychology from not being nursed by his mother. The whole world was compelled to return to natural breastfeeding, and with extraordinary enthusiasm. Did they do that in confirmation of the Noble Qur'an, or because they found that there is no solution to their problems except by returning to natural breastfeeding?

Likewise with wine: we now see a fierce war against wine in countries that had previously permitted it and expanded in it; but they waged this war against it only after science discovered its harms to the liver, the brain and human behavior. This is the meaning of ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, that is: He makes it dominant through proof, argument, truth and evidence over everything other than it. Therefore Allah, the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, says: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it.﴾ This religion has prevailed and dominated in confronting numerous issues that appeared in the societies of the polytheists and the disbelievers who dislike this religion and fight against it; and this is a prevalence not of faith but of acknowledgment, that is, in spite of them.

(1) al-Sabi'a: a people whose religion was composed between Judaism and Magianism. Al-Khalil said: they are a people whose religion resembles the religion of the Christians, except that their qibla is toward the south wind; they claim that they are upon the religion of Noah, peace be upon him. See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1/471), al-Milal wa'l-Nihal of al-Shahrastani (2/62), and Nash'at al-Fikr al-Falsafi fi'l-Islam by Dr. Ali Sami al-Nashshar (pp. 213ff.).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 34:

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, had made clear that the rabbis (al-Ahbar) and monks (al-Ruhban) do not believe in Allah with true faith, nor in the Last Day in its proper form, that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden and forbid what Allah has made lawful, and that their followers take them as lords besides Allah, here the Truthful Lord, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿O you who believe! Indeed, many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and hinder from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah – give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ (9:34)

After the Mighty and Majestic Lord had described to us what goes on within their souls, their deviation from the methodology of Allah, the immersion in love of this world and love of desires, and that they have "bought with the signs of Allah a small price" and distorted the teachings of heaven so that they might "devour the wealth of people unjustly," the question arises: Can wealth be eaten? Of course not. Rather, we buy with money the food that we eat. So why did the Truthful Lord, glorified and exalted be He, use the expression ﴿they devour the wealth of people﴾? Allah, glorified and exalted be He, intended by this to draw our attention to the fact that they do not take wealth in proportion to their need for food and drink, but rather they take more than their need, in order to hoard it.(1)

Therefore, in the same verse comes His saying, glorified and exalted be He, that they ﴿hinder from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah – give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ So they have devoured the wealth of people unjustly, in confirmation of His saying, glorified be He, ﴿they devour the wealth of people unjustly.﴾ This means that there is eating of people's wealth by right, in exchanges of benefit: the merchant takes your money in order to give you goods, and the merchant goes to buy goods with it, and so on. The law of precaution here is that there be rabbis and monks who are committed to preserving the teachings of the religion and who do not devour people's wealth unjustly. This is evident in the saying of the Truthful Lord, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly.﴾ He, Majestic in His majesty, did not say: "All the rabbis and monks devour the wealth of people unjustly," but rather He said ﴿Indeed, many of the rabbis and the monks﴾, because there may exist a limited number of rabbis and monks who are committed, and Allah does not wrong anyone. Therefore He expressed it as a possibility. For if Allah, glorified and exalted be He, had generalized, and among them there were some who were committed to the religion, this would mean that the Noble Qur'an had not covered all possibilities – and God forbid that this should be the case, because the Truthful Lord, in His Qur'an, safeguards all possibilities.

Thus: the seizure of people's wealth by some of these rabbis and monks is not by right, meaning they do not obtain only what suffices them, but by falsehood, that is, by more than they need. They take wealth in order to hinder with it from the way of Allah, and in their pursuit of worldly wealth they alter the methodology of Allah in line with their lust for money and with what achieves for them the abundance of wealth they acquire. For this reason the punishment comes in the same verse, when the Mighty and Majestic Lord says:

﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah – give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

Hoarding (al-kanz) is derived from fullness and gathering; for this reason it is said: "the sheep is muktanizah (plump)," meaning filled with flesh, and much flesh has gathered in it.

So: "yaknizun" means they gather. The words of the Truthful Lord, glorified and exalted be He, ﴿yaknizun al-dhahab wa'l-fiddah (hoard gold and silver)﴾: these two metals are the basis of the worldly economy. Economic dealing began with exchange, that is, one commodity for another, which is called the process of barter. When economic dealing advanced, currency was invented, which became the basis of dealing between people and states. And currency, from its beginning until now, rests upon gold and silver. Even when paper currency came into existence, it had to have a gold backing in order to acquire economic value, because paper currency has no value except through what covers it of gold and silver.

Among the miracles of the Noble Qur'an is that the Truthful Lord, when He speaks of gold and silver, which are two metals, makes them the basis of currency and trade. Other metals have been found that are more precious than gold and more precious than silver, such as diamond, for example. But the monetary foundation of the world still remains gold and silver. In proportion to the amount of gold reserve that covers paper currency, the value of any country's currency rises or falls. For example, in Egypt in the era of the British occupation, the circulating currency was eight million pounds, and our gold reserve was ten million pounds, so the surplus of gold was two million pounds; accordingly, the value of the Egyptian pound equalled one pound of gold plus two and a half piastres. What brings currency down to the bottom is that the gold reserve be small while the quantity of currency in circulation is large. Thus gold remains the proof and the basis of the world economy.

So: the Truthful Lord, in this noble verse, intended to draw our attention to the fact that gold and silver are the basis of dealing in directing the movement of the world's economy, and that this dealing requires the constant movement of money, because the function of money is to be used in the building of the earth. If you do not move your money, while being a believer, it decreases every year by 2.5%, which is the value of zakat. Therefore this money perishes within forty years. If the believer wishes to preserve his money, he must put it into the movement of life, to invest it and grow it, and not hoard it, lest zakat consume it; and zakat is a small proportion paid from the money. But if the owner of money circulates what he possesses in the movement of life, people will benefit from it even if he did not intend to benefit them. For the one who invests his money, for example, in building an apartment block has in mind only the profit he will realise for himself, yet people benefit from this money even though he did not intend their benefit. Whoever lays the foundation takes a wage; whoever brings the bricks takes its price; whoever brings cement is paid; whoever brings iron is paid; the factories that made the building materials are paid; the workers take their wages; in the factories of sanitary fittings, electrical cables and other things, and those who installed these items, they are paid. So a large number in society have benefited from the owner of the building, even though he did not intend to benefit them. Therefore the one who builds the building offers the society an economic service from which a number of people benefit, and likewise whoever establishes an investment project.

So: the Mighty and Majestic Lord does not want money to be stagnant, but wants it in motion, even if it is in the hands of unbelievers, because when it moves it benefits all people: sales and purchases take place, goods are produced, factories are built, manual labour is employed, and so on. But if each one of us hoards his money and does not invest it in the movement of life, goods will not be consumed, factories will stop, and people will be idle from work.

Just as Islam urges the investment of money, it also requires of us that money not go to people without work, so that they do not become accustomed to earning with idleness and not working.

For this reason it has been said: if wealth is abundant and there is no need for new projects, do not leave people unemployed; rather, you should order them to dig a well and then order them to fill it in, that is, to refill it. In this case the workers take the wage of digging and filling, so unemployment does not spread, and people do not become accustomed to eating without work, because this is the shortest path to the corruption of society.

So: the Truthful Lord wants money to move and not be hoarded; for this reason the Mighty and Majestic Lord said: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah – give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ Because by hoarding money they halt the movement of life that Allah, glorified be He, willed for His creation. You see the world now living in the peril of unemployment, because money does not move to build the universe; rather there are those who merely hoard.

Someone may say: but people now deal in paper currency, whereas Allah, glorified and exalted be He, mentioned gold and silver. We say: paper currency is not money in itself, but it was used to spare people from carrying large and heavy quantities of gold and silver, which they might not be able to carry. So it is a mechanism for facilitation, and it is referred to its value in gold. Thus those who hoard paper currency and do not spend it on what builds up the universe and brings about its development fall under this noble verse.(2)

But hoarding in this verse does not come only in the sense of gathering; it also means that they do not pay the right of Allah due on it. For this reason, wealth whose zakat has been paid is not counted as hoarding, because it diminishes by zakat year after year; whereas hoarded wealth is wealth whose zakat is not paid.

Whoever owns wealth, whatever its amount, and pays Allah's right in it, is not considered a hoarder of wealth.

Rather, hoarding in this case is what has not had Allah's right paid on it.(3)

And if we return to the text of the noble verse: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them﴾, we ask: why did Allah not say "and do not spend them both" (dual), although they are two metals? We say: the Truthful Lord used the plural form, because gold is used in many applications: one person owns a thousand dinars of gold, another owns a hundred dinars of gold, and a third has only a single gold dinar; and likewise with silver. And since plurality is present here, the form "yunfiquna-ha" must be used.

The noble verse did not say "and he who hoards," but said ﴿wa'lladhina yaknizun (and those who hoard)﴾. So the addressees are many: this one has gold, that one has gold, and a third has silver. Therefore the plural form must be used. The Noble Qur'an draws our attention to this matter in His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight (iqtatalu)﴾ (al-Hujurat: 9).

It did not say "iqtatala" (dual), because a group (ta'ifah) is the name of a collective made up of many individuals. When fighting comes, one group does not stand up holding a sword and fight the second; rather, every individual of the first group fights every individual of the second. So they are two groups at the time of peace, but at the time of war every member of the first group fights every member of the second. For this reason the Truthful Lord said ﴿iqtatalu (they fight)﴾, and did not say "iqtatala." As for the case of reconciliation, He, glorified and exalted be He, said ﴿fa-aslihu baynahuma (so make peace between them)﴾ (al-Hujurat: 9), and used here the dual, because when we make peace between two groups, we do not bring every individual of the first group and reconcile him with every individual of the second; rather we bring the leader of the first group and reconcile him with the leader of the second group, and peace is achieved. For this reason the dual is required here.

Likewise in His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ He did not say "and do not spend them both," but the Truthful Lord said ﴿wa-la yunfiquna-ha fi sabil Allah (and do not spend them in the way of Allah)﴾. Spending in the way of Allah includes many fields. In the way of Allah, movement takes place in society from which people benefit: when zakat is paid, people benefit from it; when the armies of the Muslims are equipped with it, people benefit from it. The theory of not hoarding money may have appeared recently in the world economy, but it has existed since the Noble Qur'an was revealed.

So if you spend and do not hoard, there is a boom in the market. Boom means the creation of work and means of livelihood, and the creation of the incentive that leads to advancement.

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of the verse (4/3049): "They used to take from the wealth of their followers taxes and obligations in the name of churches, temples and other things, making them believe that spending on them was from the Shari'ah and a means of drawing close to Allah, the Exalted. And during that they were withholding those funds, as Salman al-Farisi mentioned concerning the monk who extracted his hoard." Al-tazallaf (the seeking of nearness) means: drawing near.

2 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3049): "The origin of kanz in the language is gathering and collecting, and that is not restricted to gold and silver. Do you not see the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: 'Shall I not tell you of the best thing a man can hoard: a righteous woman'? That is, he holds it to himself and gathers it. Gold and silver were singled out for mention because they are things that are not seen (hidden), unlike other wealth. Al-Tabari said: kanz is everything gathered, one part upon another, whether in the belly of the earth or upon its surface." The hadith that al-Qurtubi mentioned here was recorded by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1664) and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (1/409) (2/333), and he graded it sahih, and al-Dhahabi affirmed it in the first place.

3 Ibn Umar said: whatever its zakat has been paid is not hoarding, even if it is beneath seven earths, and whatever its zakat has not been paid is hoarding, even if it is above the ground. Al-Qurtubi mentioned it in his tafsir and said: "Similar is what is narrated from Jabir, and it is the sound (view)."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 35:

We do not know that fire is only heated for metals. If what they hoarded were paper currency, how could it be heated upon? And if what they hoarded were metals, then they are suitable for branding their bodies with, but how would that be done with paper? We say: the Almighty, glorified and exalted is He, is able to make what is not heated become heated, or to transform them into gold and silver; and with them are branded various parts of their bodies. Branding (kayy) is that we bring a hot metal and press it against the skin, so that it burns it and leaves a mark.

When one of the Companions (sahabah) died in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ) and they searched his garments and found in them a dinar, the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "This is a branding from the Fire," because its owner had been eager to hoard it. Likewise, they found with another Companion two dinars that he had hoarded, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "These are two brandings."(1)

This was before zakat was legislated. As for when the owner of wealth has paid God's right in it, it is not considered hoarding. Otherwise, if we were to say that when a person leaves some wealth for his children, even if he has paid its zakat, this is considered hoarding, then we would have taken the verses of inheritance in the Noble Qur'an out of their meaning, because the verses of inheritance came to transmit what is in the possession of the deceased. Inherited wealth is presumed to have come by a lawful means and its owner has paid God's right in it, so it is not considered hoarding.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿So their foreheads and their sides and their backs will be branded with it﴾. Why did God single out these places for punishment? Because each of these limbs has a role in not spending wealth in the way of God. How? For example: you see that the face is the instrument of confrontation. When you see a poor man coming toward you to ask for charity, and you know he is poor and has come because of his dire need, if the first thing you do, so as not to pay God's right, is to turn your face away from him or frown, and anger appears on your face, then this poor man feels humiliation and abasement, because the rich man has left him and distanced himself from him. If turning the face does not help and the poor man continues advancing toward the wealthy man, then he turns away from him by presenting his side to him, so that he feels his displeasure. If the poor man continues standing beside him, he then gives him his back.

Thus, the three limbs may share in withholding spending in the way of God: the face, which he turned away, and then he gave him his back. These are the three limbs that share in withholding God's right from the poor, and therefore they must be punished, so the foreheads, the sides and the backs are branded.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾, meaning: this is what you withheld God's right from. If a person hoards much wealth, his punishment will be more severe than one who hoards little wealth, because the branding will cover a large area; but if the hoard is small, the branding will be small. Therefore the hoarder should not be deceived by the quantity he has hoarded, because his reckoning will be according to what he hoarded.

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾, meaning: your punishment in the Hereafter will be because of your hoarding of wealth. The wealth in which you rejoice by hoarding it in this world should have been the cause of your sorrow, because you are hoarding punishment for yourselves on the Day of Resurrection. However much the hoarding of wealth gives you of pride and delusion in the life of this world, it will be met in the Hereafter with punishment, each according to what he hoarded.

1) On the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: A man from the People of the Bench (Ahl al-Suffah) died, and a dinar was found in his garment. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A branding." Then another died, and two dinars were found in his garment, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two brandings." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/252-253). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/240): its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Shahr ibn Hawshab, who was declared trustworthy. And this hadith and similar ones were narrated by Ahmad from several Companions.

It may be said: What is a dinar or two, that one should be branded with them by the Fire? The answer: This was a man from the People of the Bench, that is, from the destitute poor who were constant in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ate from the charity of the Muslims, while he was hoarding gold, even a dinar, in the folds of his garments. It is as if he took the right of others and deprived the Muslim community of what he hoarded and of the fruit of his labour. Had he used this dinar to buy a mount and gathered firewood as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did with others, it would have been more beneficial for himself, his family and others; and for this reason he deserved the threat.

Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says after that:

﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion. So do not wrong yourselves therein. And fight against the polytheists all together as they fight against you all together. And know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾ (36)

Al-shahr (the month) is the cycle of the moon, as is well known. We know that the universe contains a sun, a moon and stars; these are the things visible to us. There are other planets far from us that could take a million suns into their interior. All of this gives you an idea of how vast the universe is. So do not think that this sun exists by its own essence; rather, it takes things from planets far higher than it, many of them. But what we see with our eyes is limited, and there is what we cannot see, because it is not visible to us. If you look at an electric lamp, the light of the lamp is not self-originated; rather, behind it are many devices that supply it with electricity: wires, cables and substations, then the power station that generates the electric current, then the factories that produced the machines that work in the power station. Thus, behind this small lamp there is a huge amount of work and various devices.

We see that the sun has ḍiyāʾ (radiance) and the moon has nūr (light). What is the difference between ḍiyāʾ and nūr?

Ḍiyāʾ: it has light and it has heat. Nūr: it has luminosity and it has no heat. For this reason they call the light of the moon "the cool light" (al-ḍawʾ al-ḥalīm); that is, when you sit in the moonlight you do not need a shade to protect you from it, but if you sit under the sunlight you need a shade to protect you from the intense heat of the sun.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, calls the sun a sirāj wahhāj (a blazing lamp), and the lamp has heat and has light. As for the moon, He called it munīr (illuminating), because the rays of the sun are reflected upon it and so it gives light. These two luminous bodies, the sun and the moon, Allah placed in them the measures of time. Time has many states that require different measures and calculations. The foundation of time is the day and the night; the foundation of the day is morning, noon, afternoon and sunset, and there is the true dawn (al-fajr al-ṣādiq), the false dawn (al-fajr al-kādhib), and sunrise. There are times when a thing and its shadow are equal, and times when the shadow is twice the length of the thing. The night contains darkness. After the day and night, in the measures of time, come the months, and after the months come the years.

So the measures of time need instruments by which they are measured, and you know the beginning of the day by the sunrise; thus the sun is the standard of the day. You know the beginning of the night by the sunset. Thus the sun gives us the beginning and end of night and day, but it does not give us anything about the months. If you look at the sun you do not know whether you are at the beginning of the month, its middle or its end. But when you look at the moon you know: at the beginning of the month the moon is a crescent (hilāl), in its middle it is full (badr), and at its end it is al-maḥāq(1). And the months with Allah are twelve months.

Thus we see that the Truthful, glorified and exalted, before He created man and made him a khalīfah (vicegerent) on earth, created for him a universe prepared with wisdom for his reception. He decreed the sustenance in the earth, made the sun and the moon, and sent down rain. Everything that sustains human life existed in the universe before man came to it. Man, whom Allah made a khalīfah on earth, has movement, and this is the events that occur from him, or occur in him, or occur upon him; and events require time and place, so Allah created time and place for them. Thus all of life is an interaction between the movement of the vicegerent man and time and place.

Just as Allah, glorified and exalted, prepared for man in His universe the foundations of his daily life, He sent down for him the values that preserve the moral dimension of his life, and by them the Truthful, glorified and exalted, intended that the movement of man should support one another and not contradict one another. The meaning of mutual support is that the movements of all people unite in producing what is beneficial, for greater reform on earth. But if human movements contradict one another, corruption appears on earth, because each one wants to demolish what the other has done.

In order for human movements in the universe to support one another, there must be one legislator — the supreme Legislator — who gives the laws of human movement to all people. If people turn away from the legislations of Allah, and begin to legislate for themselves, you find human laws following their desires, and each one tries to obtain privileges for himself and takes the rights of others; so life is corrupted. For this reason the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 71).

If the truth followed their desires, the universe would be subjected to human desires: this one wants, that one does not want. And the Truthful, glorified and exalted, wants in the universe a movement of peace, security and tranquility, and this is not accomplished except when every person adheres to the method of Allah; then there is lasting peace, comprehensive and all-encompassing: encompassing man's peace with himself, man's peace with the universe, and man's peace with Allah. But man, whom Allah created with choice and sent down for him a method with obligation, has the ability to obey this method or to disobey it. If man disobeys the method, he spreads corruption and oppression on earth.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, wanted to establish a guarantee for peace, which is that there exists a force that stands against corruption on earth. Therefore the Truth willed that war should have existence in this universe, so that wills may clash. As long as man has choice, and as long as there are those who disobey and those who obey, conflict must occur. As for matters in which man has no choice, they do not disturb the peace of the universe: a revolution will not occur, for example, so that the sun may rise, nor will a war break out so that rain may fall, because these matters proceed by the laws of compulsion that Allah willed for them, and they give their benefit to all. But corruption comes from people's deviation from the method of Allah. As long as there are guardians of the method among mankind, such that if a person deviates they strike his hand until he returns to the straight path(2), the tranquil and secure life remains. But if corruption spreads and there is no one in society who stands against it, the movements of life contradict one another, and people are exhausted in their lives and livelihoods.

And in order for peace to prevail in the universe, the Truthful, glorified and exalted, established in time and in place barriers against the tyranny of souls, perhaps they will awaken and return to the truth. So He placed in time sacred months in which fighting is forbidden, and peace prevails by the command of heaven. The Truth willed that this compulsory peace be an opportunity that makes these warring parties come to their senses and end their disputes. Likewise, Allah specified some places for the prohibition of fighting in them; so if people meet in these places, there is an opportunity to purify souls and end the dispute.

A man in his war with his fellow man is worn down by the fires and consequences of war: it exhausts him in blood, exhausts him in wealth and equipment, and weakness afflicts the man as a result of these exhaustions, whether he is victorious or defeated. Yet, before the dignity of his self in confronting his opponent, he wants to continue the war so that he does not appear before the opponent as having been humiliated.

So Allah, by His mercy toward His creation, made in time and in place that in which fighting is forbidden, so that it is not said that some tribe or group stopped fighting out of fear of its enemies, or because its enemies were the stronger; rather people will say: they stopped the war by a command from Allah.

By this, each of the warring parties keeps its dignity, so reconciliation becomes easy and lives and souls are saved.

Likewise, if one of the warring parties takes refuge in the place or places where Allah forbids fighting, he is secured in his person. In this there is a restraint on evil from continuing, and a protection of souls from humiliation, abasement and defeat before others. Therefore Allah willed to make clear to us: I am your Creator, and I am Merciful to you, and I will make for you a time in which fighting is forbidden, and I will make for you a place whoever enters it is safe. So take shelter behind that and refrain from fighting.

These are some of the mercy of Allah, by which Allah, glorified be He, gives people opportunities for life, and this is among the gifts of lordship (rubūbiyyah). The gift of lordship is from Allah to all His creation, the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient, and all the blessings of the universe are gifts of Allah's lordship.

The gifts of Allah, glorified be He, do not distinguish between believer and disbeliever. The earth, for example, does not give crops to the obedient while withholding them from the disobedient, and the sun does not shine and cast its warmth and heat upon the believer and not upon the disbeliever. Thus all the material blessings of the universe are gifts of the lordship of Allah, glorified and exalted, to His creation.

The causes, then, are for all people, and they may take the appropriate times for the movement of life as they wish, so they schedule their cultivation by any calendar, and they set their seasons according to what benefits them; and by this they determine their material interests, which are among the gifts of lordship. But Allah is the Lord who establishes (qayyim), and therefore there is a gift of divinity (ulūhiyyah) from Allah in the method with which He sent the messengers to people, and He made clear: I choose the time that I find suitable for lofty values and meanings, and I choose the places suitable for lofty values and meanings.

And the Truthful, glorified and exalted, willed through the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) to spread the selection of place and time for all time and place.

The months and times with Allah are twelve months. Since He said "with Allah" (ʿinda Allāh), there is an "with" other than Allah, and there is an "with" of people.

And Allah, glorified be He, made clear to His creatures: measure your times by your interests. This is what happens in the lived reality. You find someone who plants according to the Coptic calendar, in which the months of summer are fixed, and likewise the months of winter, spring and autumn, because the Coptic calendar is based on the solar calendar.

But the Truthful, glorified and exalted, wills for values specific times; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾ and Allah made clear: do not make the time of values like the times you make for your interests.

And Allah willed that values should pervade all time and not be confined to specific times. For this reason He chose times for prayer, for example: the dawn prayer has a time, the noon prayer has a time, the afternoon prayer has a time, the sunset prayer has a time, and the night prayer has a time. Yet although the times of prayer are defined, they encompass the whole of time: the prayer is performed, for example, in Aswan, and minutes later in Luxor, and minutes later in Cairo, and minutes later in Alexandria, then it moves on to the countries of Europe, and so on. It is as if it never stops at a specific period; rather it continues according to the differing times in the various countries. So the dawn prayer, for example, is before sunrise, and the sun rises every minute upon a different patch of the earth. It is as if the prayer is perpetual on the surface of the earth. Moreover, at the very time we pray the noon prayer, others may be praying the afternoon prayer in northern Europe, the sunset prayer in America, and the night prayer in Canada, for example; so it is as if prayer is performed at every time on the back of the earth, because the whole universe glorifies Allah.

Then we come next to Allah's choosing of the Day of Arafah standing, and the month of fasting, and other times. The month of Ramadan comes once in the summer, as it comes in winter, spring and autumn. Likewise the Hajj comes in the different seasons of the year. Thus the justice of Allah willed that the days preferred by Him be distributed over all time. The Truthful, glorified and exalted, made the unit of time the day, and the day consists of night and day; the unit of days is the month, and the unit of months is the year. He made the task of the sun to determine the day for us, and the task of the moon to determine the month for us: at the beginning of the month it is a crescent (hilāl),

(1) al-maḥāq: the end of the month when the crescent is effaced and not seen. It is that the moon hides for two nights, not seen at morning or evening. Ibn al-A'rabi said: it was called maḥāq because it rises with the sun and so the sun effaces it, and no one sees it. See Lisan al-'Arab (root m-ḥ-q).

(2) On the authority of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The likeness of one who stands upon the limits of Allah and one who falls into them is like a people who drew lots for a ship; some of them got its upper part and some its lower part. Those in its lower part, when they needed water, passed by those above them, and they said: 'If only we made a hole in our share and did not harm those above us.' So if they leave them and what they desire, all perish together; and if they take hold of their hands, they all are saved." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2686, 2493), Ahmad in his Musnad (4/268-270), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2173), who said: hasan sahih. See Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's commentary on this hadith in Fath al-Bari (5/295-296), where there is a very valuable discussion.

Then after that, God gives the ruling concerning those who alter the sacred months, or change them, by postponing one month or delaying it by one month. So He says:

﴿Indeed, the postponement (al-nasi') is an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year, to conform to the number of what God has made unlawful, and thereby make lawful what God has made unlawful. The evil of their deeds has been made appealing to them. And God does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ (9:37)

Al-nasi' means postponement (ta'khir). It is as if they, when they entered into fighting and a sacred month came, said: "We will shift it to a coming month," and they continued in their fighting. By doing so they had made lawful the month that was forbidden, and made a month that had no sanctity into a sacred month. Here God makes clear that this action is an increase in disbelief, because it introduces into the lawful what does not belong to it and introduces into the unlawful what does not belong to it. For disbelief is the absence of faith; so if you alter and change the method of faith, this is an increase in disbelief.

Then He says: ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year﴾. Here "yudallu" (is led astray) is in the passive voice. The meaning is that there is someone who misleads those who disbelieve, and this is the task of Satan. For there is a difference between going astray (dalal) and leading others astray (idlal). Going astray concerns the self and the soul, whereas leading astray extends to others. There is one who astray is not content with his own straying, but comes to others and misleads them and seduces them into sin by making it appear attractive to them. Therefore there is a punishment for going astray, and a greater punishment for leading astray. If a person is astray, he is in himself not a believer, meaning his straying has not gone beyond his own self and has not passed to another. But if he tries to tempt another to straying and sin, he has by that gone astray and led another astray. Some orientalists take this matter as a point of criticism against the Qur'an, without awareness or understanding, saying: The Qur'an says: ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ (35:18), and then in another verse it says: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾ (29:13).

So how can the Qur'an say that no one bears anything but his own burden, and then say that there are those who will bear their own burden and the burden of others?

We say to them: You have not understood the meaning. The first is the one who goes astray and commits sins but does not entice others to them; that is, he disobeyed God but did not go beyond the sin. The second has gone astray and led others astray; that is, he was not content with committing the sin but began to incite people to disobey God. And every time he enticed one person to sin, he bore the same burden as the one who committed the sin.

Here the Truth says: ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and unlawful another year﴾. Of course, the making lawful and making unlawful here arose from them because they thought this was in their interest; that is, they subjected the sacred months to their own desires and departed from God's purposes in His creation, on the day He created the heavens and the earth.

But why do they make it lawful one year and unlawful another? The answer comes from the Truth: ﴿to conform to the number of what God has made unlawful﴾. That is, to match the count of what God has made lawful, so that they may justify themselves and say to themselves: "We are not disobedient; if God wants four sacred months, then we have committed to that!" But God's legislation is not only in the number; it is also in what is counted. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has specified for us the sacred months.(1)

Umar ibn Luhayy, or Nu'aym ibn Tha'laba, were the first(2) to carry out this act of postponement. He made the month of Muharram lawful and made others unlawful.

Those who carried out this action knew that there were four sacred months, as shown by the fact that they made lawful and made unlawful. Had they not known them, they would neither have made lawful nor made unlawful. But they wanted to subject God's legislation to their whims. This is the purpose of making Muharram lawful and making another month unlawful: they wished thereby to subject God's purposes to the desires of their souls. For the sacred month has fixed sanctity, and it is a sacred month whether a person postpones it or does not postpone it; it is sacred by God's will, not by people's will. Therefore God has judged the postponement to be an increase in disbelief, because when you delay the sanctity of the month of Muharram to another month, you have done two things: you have made lawful a sacred month, which is disbelief, and you have made unlawful a lawful month, which is another disbelief. That is, an increase in disbelief. Then the Truth says: ﴿to conform to the number of what God has made unlawful﴾, and God has judged them to be disbelievers in that they made lawful what God had made unlawful.

Then the Truth says: ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made appealing to them﴾. Adornment (tazyin) is something incidental or added to the reality of a thing, which makes it acceptable to people. A woman, for example, has natural beauty, but she adorns herself by exaggerating the display of her charms so that she is more beautiful in the eyes of men; this is adornment. So adornment is a change in appearance, not in essence. There is adornment in many things; adornment in thought, for example, when there is readiness for battle and the commander comes and makes the entry into the battle appealing to the fighters, saying: "You will be victorious within hours, none of you will be harmed, and your enemy will flee." This is praiseworthy adornment.

Therefore the Truth wished to reveal to us the reality of the adornment they practised when they made lawful the sanctity of the sacred months, and God showed us that this kind of adornment is not praiseworthy, so He said: ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made appealing to them. And God does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ Since evil has been made appealing to them, this act has gone outside the realm of guidance and outside the scope of praiseworthy adornment into evil adornment. And since they have departed from God's guidance, God will not help them, for He does not help those who disbelieve, nor those who do wrong, nor those who transgress.

Thus He said: ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ That is, by their disbelief they have removed themselves from God's guidance. The Truth did not withhold guidance from them; rather they withheld it from themselves by disbelieving, removing themselves from the will of God's guidance for them. This applies to the guidance of assistance (hidayat al-ma'unah). We know that God has guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalalah) and guidance of assistance (hidayat al-ma'unah). The guidance of indication is for both the believer and the disbeliever: God indicates the method to all, shows them His signs, and the messengers convey the heavenly method which makes clear the path to God's pleasure and the path to His wrath and punishment.

Whoever believes in God enters into the will of the guidance of assistance, so God helps him in this world and gives him Paradise in the Hereafter. As for one who rejects the guidance of indication from God, God does not give him the guidance of assistance, because disbelief has preceded from the servant. Likewise injustice and transgression: he has prevented himself from the guidance of assistance by committing those sins.

Therefore God, glorified and exalted, says: {And God does not guide the disbelieving people (9:37)} {And God does not guide the wrongdoing people (9:19)} ﴿And God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ (9:108).

So: it is they who put forward disbelief, injustice and wickedness, and so they prevented themselves from the guidance of assistance, about which the Truth said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ (47:17).

(1) On the authority of Abu Bakra, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed time has returned to the form it had on the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three in succession: Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja, and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3197) and Muslim in his Sahih (1679).

(2) Scholars differed in determining who first postponed the months for the Arabs. That it was Amr ibn Luhayy is the view of Ibn Abbas. That it was Nu'aym ibn Tha'laba is the view of al-Kalbi. Ibn Ishaq said it was al-Qalammas, who is Hudhayfa ibn Abd, mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/357); see also the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (4/3064). Al-Qalammas linguistically means: the cunning man. See Lisan al-Arab.

Since God, glorified and exalted be He, had asked the believers to confront falsehood as a whole, just as falsehood gathers against them and fights them as a whole, He says, glorified be He:

﴿O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But the enjoyment of worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is but little.﴾ (9:38)

When you hear ﴿O you who have believed﴾, this is an address specific to those who have believed in Allah, because Allah does not impose obligations on one who has not believed in Him. There is no ruling among the rulings of Allah's method that imposes an obligation on a disbeliever or a non-believer. Rather, the rulings of the method are all directed to the believers. Therefore, whenever you hear ﴿O you who have believed﴾, know that Allah is addressing or commanding the one who has believed in Him, because you are the one who believed by your own choice and entered into faith by your own desire. The Exalted has not taken you to faith by compulsion; rather, you came to faith by your own choice. So Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says to you: since you have believed in Me as a God, Capable and Self-Subsisting, possessing the absolute attributes of perfection, then listen to Me regarding what I want for the movement of your life.

No one should reckon that he is able to enter into faith and yet not implement the method[(1)], and no one should reckon that he is able to harm Allah in anything. We have previously given the example of the sick person who chooses the most skillful of physicians, and no one forced him to go to him. The physician examined the patient, identified the illness, and wrote the prescription. But after the patient leaves the clinic, he holds the prescription and tears it up, or he buys the medicine and does not take it. Has he thereby punished the physician, or punished himself? The physician will not be affected, and nothing that this patient has done will harm him; rather, it is the patient himself whose illness will increase and who will lead himself to destruction. Likewise, if a human being does not follow the method of Allah, he places himself in harm's way and plunges himself into misery, because Allah, glorified be He, has set down this method, and in it is the cure for all of man's ailments. If a person acts by it, he is saved from the afflictions of this world; and if a society acts by it, misery will not appear in it, but rather it will be filled with prosperity and tranquility. And whoever does not act by it will not harm Allah in anything; rather, he obtains misery and destroys himself.

When Allah, glorified be He, addresses those who have believed, He clarifies: take from Me this obligation, for in it is the happiness of man in this world and the Hereafter. For this reason we find that the Exalted does not mention any of His commands with any obligation, or any of His prohibitions, except that it is preceded by His saying, glorified be He, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, such as His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you...﴾ (2:183) (Al-Baqarah)

And His saying, glorified be He:

﴿O you who have believed, retribution has been prescribed for you...﴾ (2:178) (Al-Baqarah).

These obligations did not come in the active form, so who is the one who prescribes? It is the Exalted. Also, it is a form in which the doer is not named, meaning that the prescribing came from many. We say: it is true that Allah, glorified be He, is the One who prescribed, so why did He not say: "O you who have believed, I have prescribed for you"? And why does He say: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you﴾? We say: because Allah, although He prescribed, did not prescribe them upon all His creatures, but prescribed them upon those who have believed in Him, and by your faith you have become bound by the elements of the obligation[(2)]. So it is as though Allah did not prescribe and then impose it on you; rather, your binding yourself occurs in the very moment you entered into faith by your own choice. Thus all these rulings have been prescribed for us by the choice of each of us. Whoever does not choose faith is not obligated to implement the rulings of faith, because they are not implemented except through the covenant of faith between us and the Exalted. He, glorified be He, has respected our entry into this covenant, so He did not attribute it only to His exalted Essence, but included also everyone who entered into faith.

Therefore, if anyone asks about the wisdom of obligation from Allah, we say to him: wisdom springs from the fact that He, glorified be He, is the One who imposed the obligation. Moreover, knowledge of wisdom is only possible from one who is equal to the one [being asked], so if the patient goes to the physician, and the physician writes him a prescription, and the patient keeps debating the physician about the medicine and its benefits, the physician rejects the debate and says to the patient: enter medical school, spend seven years there, obtain the academic degrees, then come and debate me.

So: you attach the obligation to the one obligated, even though the obligated human may err. But if we bring a group of physicians to examine a patient whose condition has baffled medicine, and they sit after the examination discussing among themselves, each of them accepts the other's debate, because he is equal to him in thought, culture, knowledge, and so on. But if you wish to ask about the wisdom of an obligation from Allah, you will not find anyone equal to Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and therefore the debate is rejected.

So: the one obligated must have a standing prior to the obligation, and the standing of the Truth is that you have believed in Him. For this reason I see that searching for the causes of obligation is something rejected in faith. If it is said: Allah prescribed fasting so that the rich feel the pain of hunger and so incline toward the poor, we say: No, otherwise fasting would drop from the poor, since he knows the pain of hunger well. And if it is said to us: fasting cures such-and-such diseases, we say: this is not correct, otherwise Allah would not have dropped the obligation of fasting from the sick in His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And whoever is sick or on a journey [prescribed] a number of other days...﴾ (2:184) (Al-Baqarah).

If Allah has permitted the sick to break the fast, how can a person come and say: the reason for prescribing fasting is the healing of diseases? Moreover, there are some illnesses in which fasting is not permitted.

So: we fast because Allah has prescribed fasting upon us, and since Allah has said it, the reason for implementation is that the command proceeds from Allah, glorified be He, and nothing else. If the wisdom of the obligation becomes apparent, it increases us in faith, just as the harm of pork to man has been established, because pork is full of microbes and germs which it eats along with filth. We do not abstain from eating pork for this reason; rather, we abstain from it because Allah has commanded us to. Even if this wisdom had not been revealed by medicine, it would not diminish our conviction in abstaining from pork, because we take the obligation from Allah, and not from any other source.

Let us return to our reflections on the noble verse: ﴿O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth﴾. We find that the phrase ﴿What is [the matter] with you﴾ (mā lakum) comes when we marvel at a state that does not accord with a state [expected]; as though the believers' fighting against the disbelievers were an expected matter demanded by the situation. This is because when the believers fight the disbelievers, they introduce a degree of certainty into people of uprightness; for if people of uprightness do not find someone who strikes the hands of the disbelievers, then some of them may deviate, whose souls entice them toward deviation. But if they find someone who strikes the hands of the disbelievers, then by this act he strengthens the faith of the believer, because he sees his enemy receiving punishment. For instance, you might say to a student: "What is the matter with you that you neglect your studying when the examination is near?" That is: it is supposed that when the examination draws near, the student must strive in studying. If the student neglects his work, we marvel at his behavior, because it does not accord with what ought to happen. Thus we denounce that such neglect should occur, just as we denounce and marvel at a patient who abandons the medicine while he is in pain.

Here the Exalted marvels at the believers' heaviness when they are called to fight, because the strength of faith always calls for a continuous readiness to fight. This readiness frightens the disbelievers and prevents their aggression and their contempt for the believers, first; and secondly, it enables the believers to respond and deter at any time. Thirdly, it gives some certainty to the believing society when it sees that there is someone who strikes the hands of the disbelievers if they belittle the community of faith and try to humiliate the believers.

So: in order that the believing society remain strong and secure, there must be a constant readiness to fight in the way of Allah and a desire for martyrdom. Here the Truth says: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah"﴾. It is as though continuous readiness to fight in the way of Allah is something that must exist by nature and by reason; so if this readiness weakens or diminishes, it becomes a matter for wonder, because the believers know that the society of disbelief is always lying in wait for them, and they must be in constant, continuous readiness for confrontation. The Truth denounces that the believers should be heavy or slack when called to fight in the way of Allah.

His saying, glorified be He: ﴿Go forth [infiru]﴾ derives from "nafra," which is departing toward a matter that stirs a person's settledness. When a person is sitting in his place, a matter may come that stirs him, so he rises to do what fits the stirring matter. For example, if you see a person about to fall into a well, this matter stirs you, so you set off from your place to pull him away. From the same root is "nufra" (aversion) that occurs between beloveds who live in constant affection, and then something happens between them that turns this affection into estrangement.

So: the word ﴿infiru﴾ indicates departing toward a stirring matter, which is the natural logic that ought to be; for the actions of the disbelievers stir the believers to confront them. The saying of the Truth ﴿infiru﴾ indicates continuous provocation from the disbelievers toward the believers. The Exalted says: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily﴾.

Heaviness (thaql) means that the mass of a thing exceeds the capacity of the one who carries it; if you say that this thing is heavy, it means that its weight, for example, is greater than the strength of your muscles, so you cannot carry it. But tathaqqul (adhering heavily) is failing to accord with the thing's natural constitution. As when you say: so-and-so is heavy, meaning his weight is huge and he cannot rise from his place except with difficulty, nor move except with hardship.

But tathaqqul means assuming hardship: that is, you have the capacity to act, but you pretend that you are unable, as when there is—for example—an object weighing a pound, and you claim that it is heavy for you and that you cannot carry it.

So: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿you adhere heavily to the earth﴾ means: you have assumed heaviness without reality; you have the capacity to fight, but you feign that you have no capacity.

Thus we know that the situation calls for departure to confront disbelief, because the method they have chosen for themselves and to which they have bound themselves achieves safety, security, and tranquility for them and for others. It is as though adhering to the earth has a counterpart: departure is in the way of Allah, and the counterpart is in the way of Satan or in the way of the desires of the soul.

The scholars have discussed the matters that make a person incline toward disobedience, which is the soul that whispers something to a person; a person inclines toward disobedience only through these two factors. What is the difference between the two, and how does a person recognize it? The scholars said: if the soul insists upon you to commit a specific act of disobedience, such that if you turn it away from it, it returns insisting upon you to perpetrate the disobedience in order to attain immediate pleasure, this is the insistence of the commanding soul (al-nafs al-ammara bi'l-su').

But Satan does not want that from you; he wants you to oppose the method of Allah in any form. If he fails to draw you to unlawful wealth, he adorns for you the desire for women; if he fails, he comes from the direction of wine. So: he wants you to be disobedient in any act of disobedience, while the soul wants you to be disobedient in the very act of disobedience that it craves. This is the difference.

Thus we know that there are two realities: a reality that calls the believers to fight the disbelievers who corrupt Allah's method on earth, and a reality that calls them to adhere heavily away from this fighting, either because of the love of this world in order to fulfill the desire of the soul, and

2 This is made clear by the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). On the authority of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal when he sent him to Yemen: "You are going to come to a people of the People of the Book. When you come to them, invite them to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. If they obey you in that, inform them that Allah has enjoined upon them five prayers in every day and night..." The hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1496) and Muslim (19).
