It has been used as evidence that disbelievers are not addressed with the subsidiary rulings, since they were called first only to faith, and then called to action."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 39:

Meaning: If you do not go out to fight, Allah will warn you of punishment. When the Truth gives a warning, what it warns of must certainly come to pass. So if you do not go forth out of fear of a punishment that is only presumed, namely hardship and fatigue, then what about the punishment that is certain, if you do not carry out Allah's command to go forth to fighting? When the comparison is between the hardship of travel and fighting and the intense heat, and the punishment of Allah, the believer will undoubtedly choose the hardship of war, whatever it may be; for every act is measured by the capacity of its doer. The presumed punishment of heat, the hardship of travel, and the severity of fighting cannot be compared with the punishment of Allah, because the punishment awaiting one who lags behind or flees from the march is greater than the hardship of answering the call to march, however exhausting it may be.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And He will replace you with another people﴾. So do not think that by your slowness and your lack of desire for fighting you will harm Allah in any way; for Allah is able to bring about a new creation, and He is capable of that. Therefore He says: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾. In another verse the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Here you are, those who are invited to spend in the way of Allah, but among you are those who are stingy. And whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself. And Allah is the Free of need, and you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be like you﴾ (Muhammad 38).

So do not think that, with whatever wealth or strength you have, you are able to obstruct the method of Allah through stinginess or failure; for He, glory be to Him, is able to replace you with a people other than you, who possess the zeal for fighting and sacrifice in the way of Allah, for He is the Irresistible above all creation.

His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾ is a justification (hay'iyya, i.e. a rationale) for the rulings that preceded it in His saying: ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all﴾. And if one of them supposes that this is merely theoretical speech, the Truth, glory be to Him, presents them with a practical example from the reality they witnessed and lived through, when the disbelievers of Quraysh gathered to kill him, and Allah gave him victory over them. So He, majestic is His majesty, says to him:

﴿If you do not support him, then Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two. When they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquillity upon him and supported him with hosts you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest; and the word of Allah is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ (40).

The orientalists paused at the Almighty's saying: ﴿Unless you aid him, Allah has already aided him﴾. And, as is their custom as skeptics of Islam, we find them exerting great effort in seeking out errors they imagine in the noble Qur'an. They say: "The awe and sanctity that the Qur'an holds for you Muslims, O Muslims, do not allow your minds the necessary boldness to examine its styles, so that you may discover the flaws in it. But if you look at the Qur'an as a book without any sanctity, you will find in it contradiction and discrepancy."

The orientalists devoted a large chapter to examining grammar in the noble Qur'an, and they came to the question of the conditional (al-shart) and its response (al-jawab). Whoever reads their criticism immediately recognizes a clear fact: their ignorance of the depth of the secrets of the Arabic language. They have taken only the surface of the Arabic language, and they possess no mastery of it or good understanding. They said: the conditional constructions in Arabic require that every condition have a response. If you say, "If Zayd comes to you, honor him," you find the honoring comes after Zayd's coming; and if you say, "If you study, you will succeed," success comes after the study. Therefore, the time of the response is later than the time of the condition.

They presented all these premises in order to cast doubt upon us regarding the Qur'an. We say to them: your statement about the condition and its response is correct, but understand the surplus. In the matter, we find that the response is a cause of the condition. For when you say, "If you study, you will succeed," the student, if he does not call to mind the benefits of success, will not study. Rather, the student must picture in his mind the benefits of success in order to be impelled to study. Therefore, the response is a motivating cause within the condition, but the condition is a cause of the response, yet an actual cause. Thus, imagining success first is the path to exerting effort to achieve success. In this way the aspect is distinct: this is a motivating cause, and that is an actual cause.

As for His saying: ﴿Unless you aid him﴾, it is a verb in the present tense, its time being the present time. But the Truth follows the present-tense verb with a past-tense verb: ﴿Allah has already aided him﴾. So is the condition in the present or future, and the response in the past? We say: the meaning is, "Unless you aid him, Allah will aid him," as proof that He has already aided him before that. This is not the response of the condition; rather, it is the evidence of the response. When the evidence of the response is in the past, it is more indicative of the certainty of the occurrence of the response. When Allah called them to go forth and they were sluggish, He made clear to them, glory be to Him: Do you think that your fighting is what will aid Muhammad and aid his call? No; for He, glory be to Him, is able to aid him, and the proof of that is that Allah had aided him before in many situations, the most important of which was the victory in the Hijrah. He aided him with one man, Abu Bakr, against the Quraysh and all the disbelievers of Makkah. Likewise, He aided him at Badr with hosts you did not see. Therefore, the precedence of Allah's victory for His Messenger is a past precedence, and accordingly it is not the response, but the evidence of the response.

In His saying: ﴿Unless you aid him, Allah has already aided him﴾, we see that Allah's victory for him has three times. The word ﴿idh﴾ (when) is repeated three times, for He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿When those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two; when they were in the cave; when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us"﴾. That is to say, we are before three times: the time of the expulsion, the time of the cave, and the time in which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾. Victory came in these three times: at the hour of the expulsion from Makkah, at the hour when our master the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the cave with Abu Bakr, and at the hour of his conversation with Abu Bakr.

A questioner may ask: Did the disbelievers expel the Messenger of Allah from Makkah, or was it Allah who expelled him? We say: the obstinacy of his people, their plotting against him, and their stubbornness before his call all compelled him to leave. But the Truth intended by this departure a goal other than what the disbelievers intended. They wanted to kill him, and when he left they thought his call would be suffocated by isolation from the people. So Allah expelled him so that the call might spread. He made clear to them, glory be to Him: You want to expel Muhammad through your obstinacy toward him, but I will not enable you to expel him in humiliation; I will expel him supported by the Helpers. They said: the Hijrah is the twin of the Prophethood (al-ba'thah). That is, the Muhammadan mission came together with the Hijrah. The evidence is that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was taken by the Mother of the Believers Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, to Waraqah ibn Nawfal, after what had happened to him in the cave of Hira, Waraqah said to him: "Would that I were alive when your people expel you." Waraqah ibn Nawfal said this to the Messenger of Allah before he was established in prophethood. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Will they expel me?" Waraqah ibn Nawfal said: "Yes; no man has come with the like of what you have brought except that he was opposed."(1)

Thus, the Hijrah was decreed along with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, being charged with the message. Why? Because he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the first to make the message of truth and monotheism heard in the ears of the chiefs of Quraysh. So the idea of the Hijrah was preceded by the Prophethood, because the mission (al-ba'thah) was the cry that resounded in the ears of the chiefs of Quraysh, and they were the chiefs of the Peninsula. Had he cried out in the ears of a people who were not among the chiefs of the Arabs, they would have said: he weakened a people and then cried out to them. But the cry of proclamation came into the ears of the chiefs of the entire Arabian Peninsula, so they set out to torment the Muslims in order to eliminate this call. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, willed not to aid him through Quraysh in Makkah, because Quraysh had become accustomed to lordship over the Arabs. If a messenger came to guide people in general to Islam, the one who had sent him among them would say: Quraysh has been partisan for him so that he may rule the world as they ruled the Arabian Peninsula. So the Truth, glory be to Him, willed to make clear to us: No. The first cry was in the ears of the chiefs of the Arabs, and the victory of Islam and the spread of the religion had to come not from this town alone but from another land, so that it would not be said: partisanship for Muhammad is what created faith in the message of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rather, faith in the message of Muhammad is what created partisanship for Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

It is noticed in the matter of the Hijrah that its verb is "hajara" (he migrated). This indicates to us that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not abandon Makkah (hajara), but rather emigrated (hajara in the form of mufa'alah). Mufa'alah is from two sides, as if his people had troubled him and he went out. The expulsion itself contains victory, because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out alone from his house, which was surrounded by strong young men from all the tribes of the Arabs, to strike him with a single blow, and he scattered dust over them so that their sight was covered, while Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was waiting for him outside.(2) As if the Almighty and Exalted wanted to establish for them that they would never reach Muhammad, neither by hidden plotting nor by open collaboration. This is a victory from Allah.

The Almighty continues: ﴿When they were in the cave﴾, and another victory is confirmed in the cave. For the tracker of footprints whom Quraysh employed, named Kurz ibn 'Alqamah from Khuza'ah, tracked the trail until he came to the cave and said: "These are the footprints of Muhammad, and he resembles what is in the Ka'bah," that is, he resembles the footprint of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Then he said: "These are the footprint of Abu Bakr, or the footprint of his son, and they did not go beyond this place." Trackers used to recognize the shape of the foot and its imprint on the ground. He added: "They did not go beyond this place, except that they must have ascended to heaven or entered into the depths of the earth." Despite this confirmation, they did not enter the cave, and none of them thought to turn over the rock or search for Muhammad and his companion, although this was the first thing that should have come to mind. For as long as the footprints had ended at the entrance of the cave, they should have searched inside it. But no one paid attention to that.

Then one of them came and began to urinate, so he faced his private part toward the cave. This is the reason for Abu Bakr's saying to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "If one of them looked beneath his feet, he would see us."

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said with the insight of prophethood: "If they had seen us, they would not have faced us with their private parts."(3) This is evidence that the Arab would be averse to having his private part exposed, or it is a dignity for Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that He not show him the private part of another. Let the reader take it as he takes it; in any case it is an inspired overflow to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, the Almighty caused the spider to weave its threads at the entrance of the cave, and caused the dove to build a nest in it with eggs, and caused Suraqah ibn Malik to say: "It is impossible that Muhammad and his companion entered the cave, for otherwise they would have broken the dove's nest and torn the spider's web."

We know that the frailest of houses is the house of the spider. The Almighty says:

﴿Indeed, the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if only they knew.﴾ (al-'Ankabut: 41).

The divine miracle appears here in that Allah, glory be to Him, barred a large group of strong fighters with the frailest of houses, which is the house of the spider, and the power of Allah was manifested in His making the spider's thread stronger than steel. Likewise, the Truth willed that the dove lay eggs, though it is the most fearful of birds, and if it is startled, it is startled. This is a victory. Then there is a third victory, psychological and personal: when Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "If one of them looked beneath his feet, he would see us," we find the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, respond with confidence in his Lord: "What do you think of two whom Allah is the third of?"(4)

This response does not fit Abu Bakr's question, for Abu Bakr feared that if they looked beneath their feet they would see those in the cave. The natural response would have been: "They will not see us." But the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wanted to draw our attention with a faith-filled notice to the higher necessity, so he said: "What do you think of two whom Allah is the third of?" Because, since the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr were in the companionship of Allah, and Allah is not perceived by sight, then whoever is in His companionship is not perceived by sight.

The word of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, whom Abu Bakr was accustomed to finding truthful in all that he said, becomes the proof of the truth of what he said. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said that he had been carried by night to Bayt al-Maqdis and ascended to heaven, Abu Bakr said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth."(5) So when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, says to Abu Bakr, as He relates, glory be to Him: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾, grief must depart from Abu Bakr. Yet our master Abu Bakr, when he entered the cave and found holes, feared that there might be snakes or serpents in them, so he began to tear his garment and stop up those holes with it, until nothing of the garment remained except what covers the private part, and he stopped the remaining holes with his hand and his heel.(6)

Thus, Abu Bakr wanted to ransom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with himself, for if something happened to Abu Bakr, he is a companion, but if harm befell the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the entire call would be destroyed. Thus Abu Bakr did not grieve out of weakness of faith, but he grieved out of fear for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he might be struck by harm.

Then the Almighty and Exalted says: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us. So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with hosts you did not see﴾. The scholars differed(7) regarding His saying, "upon him" (ʿalayhi): is the intended referent the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or is the intended referent Abu Bakr? And since tranquility was sent down, it must be that it descended upon a heart that had been struck by grief. But the scholars say: the pronouns in the verses refer to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Truth said: ﴿unless you aid him﴾, that is, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him; He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Allah has already aided him﴾, that is, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and He also says: ﴿when He expelled him﴾, that is, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. So all the pronouns in the verse refer to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Then comes the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him﴾. Therefore, the pronoun here must also refer to the Messenger

1 Agreed upon, from the hadith of ʿAʾishah. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3 and other places) and Muslim in his Sahih (160).

Rather, the intended meaning is that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out alone from his house at night and passed through the ranks of forty strong men who had drawn their swords to kill him if he came out of his house alone. He said: No, angels are shielding us with their wings. That man sat down and urinated facing the cave. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: If he were seeing us he would not have done this." Among its narrators is Yaʿqub ibn Humayd, whom Ibn Hibban and others declared reliable, while Abu Hatim and others declared him weak; the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih. In it is Musa ibn Mutayr, who is abandoned (matruk). See Fath al-Bari (7/11).

5 This hadith has been mentioned shortly before and we cited it there. And from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said regarding Abu Bakr: "Will you leave my companion for me? (twice) I said: O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, and you said: You lie, while Abu Bakr said: You speak the truth." Related by al-Bukhari (4640-3661) and Ibn Abi ʿAsim in al-Sunnah (2/576).

In the cave there was a hole in which were snakes and vipers, and Abu Bakr feared that something might come out of it and harm the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so he put his heel over it, and the snakes and vipers began striking and stinging him. Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 9, verse 41:

Then the Exalted says:

﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your persons in the way of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ (41)

Thus the Truth opens the door to reaching Him, so that they may rush to support the Messenger and dispel the fog from their minds. He opens for them the door to reaching Him because they are the creation of Allah and His dependants. He, glory be to Him, wants them all to be guided and to take part in supporting the call to Him.

Fighting in the way of Allah may appear to be hardship on the surface, but it grants the call spread and stability. When the Muslims stand up to support the call to Allah, in this standing there is forgiveness and repentance, and it is a mercy from Allah towards them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than any one of you who, having lost his camel in a barren wilderness, suddenly finds it again." (1)

And the Truth, the Exalted, says in a sacred hadith: "The heaven said: 'O my Lord, permit me to drop a piece of itself upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your bounty and withheld Your thanks.' The seas said: 'O Lord, permit me to drown the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your bounty and withheld Your thanks.' The earth said the like."

So what did the Truth, the Exalted, say? He said: "Leave Me with My servants. Had you created them, you would have shown them mercy. If they repent to Me, I am their beloved; and if they do not repent, I am their physician." (2) Thus we see Allah's mercy towards His creation.

After the Exalted rebuked the Muslims because they were not zealous for jihad, He opens before them the door of repentance, saying: ﴿Go forth﴾, that is: go out to fight. This is a command from Allah by which He awakens faith in the hearts of the Muslims; and at the same time He opens before them the door of repentance for their slackness in going out to fight in the expedition of Tabuk. For this reason He said ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. The word "nafrah" (going forth/mobilisation) means going out towards something that stirs one to it; the example is the estrangement between a person and a friend with whom he had affection, when some conduct or speech from this friend stirs one to depart from him, so the person recoils from him. The Exalted here commands: ﴿Go forth﴾, and what stirs one to go forth is the elevation of the religion of Allah and His word; and when you raise the word of Allah, the door to rising by it is opened for you, so He said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. "Khafif" (light) is the sound, healthy, strong one whom movement does not tire or burden. "Thaqil" (heavy) is the sick or the aged.

Allah desires from all of them that they hasten to fight, so that they may be saved from the painful punishment and attain His repentance and His pleasure.

But the healthy one who is light in movement can fight; so what does the sick person do? He does as our master Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab did, when he was sick and they said to him: "Allah has excused you from going out to battle," by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ (al-Fath: 17). He said: "By Allah, I will increase the numbers of the Muslims and guard their goods." (3) It is possible for the sick person to be distinguished by intelligence and soundness of mind, and he may be consulted on some matter. The sick person may be an example among his people: if he goes out to fight, his people are stirred and go out with him. The sick or weak person may also be an incentive for the strong to fight; when the strong see the sick going out to fight, they feel ashamed to remain behind.

The scholars differed in interpreting His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. Some said: this is a reference to the person's own self, for there is a light self and a heavy self in terms of weight, unable to move easily. Others said: a single individual may have both conditions. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Go forth﴾ is a command to the group, and ﴿light﴾ is the plural of "light" (khafif), and ﴿heavy﴾ is the plural of "heavy" (thaqil), and matching a plural with a plural requires distribution to the individuals.

The meaning is: each one of the Muslims should go forth, whether light or heavy. We have previously given the example when the teacher enters upon the students and says: "Take out your books"; the meaning of this command is that each student takes out his book. And if you say: "Mount your cars," it means that each one of you should mount his car.

So the verse means: let each one of you go forth, whether heavy or light.

But how can a person be heavy and light at the same time? We say: he is light, that is, possessed of energy for jihad, and heavy, that is, he will enter into hardship that makes the task heavy on himself. The Exalted says:

﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, and it is hateful to you﴾ (al-Baqarah: 216). Entering into what is disliked (4) in the way of Allah is a matter that raises the degrees of faith.

So: the verse bears more than one meaning. It carries the general meaning that some are light and heavy in themselves; or that fighting combines lightness in movement and heaviness in hardship; or that the one who owns a mount is the light one, because the mount removes hardship and speeds the journey, while the heavy one is the one who strives on foot, for he will bear the length of the distance. When the Exalted fills the hearts of the believers, He asks of them what He obligates them with, strongly; then His mercy appears and He lightens the obligation. Had the ruling come light at the beginning of legislation and then been raised, that matter would be hard on the soul; but when the ruling comes heavy and is then lightened, it is closer to the soul. The example is in the saying of the Exalted to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve﴾ (al-Anfal: 65).

Here the Truth gives a measure of the believer's capacity relative to the disbeliever. The twenty overcome two hundred, that is, the ratio is one of the believers to ten of the disbelievers. Therefore when this verse was revealed, each believer had to kill ten of the disbelievers. But the Exalted knew that this matter was severe upon the souls of the believers, that a single believer should face ten disbelievers, and that only the people of resolve could bear it. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Now Allah has lightened it for you, and He knows that there is weakness in you﴾ (al-Anfal: 66). And since there is weakness, the matter must be lightened for the believers when facing the disbelievers during fighting. The Exalted shifted the ratio from one to ten, to one to two, and He said:

﴿Now Allah has lightened it for you, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred of you steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand by Allah's permission, and Allah is with the steadfast﴾ (al-Anfal: 66).

Therefore: whoever flees from fighting two (men) has fled from the battle line; but if he flees from facing three, he is not counted as a fleeing man (5), because they exceed the ratio Allah has established. As for the Truth's saying in the verse we are reflecting upon, ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, it is a command that includes everyone despite their different conditions; that is, it carries a general command for all Muslims. (6) There is another statement in Surat al-Tawbah which exempts certain cases of believers who sincerely devoted their hearts to Allah. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no cause (for blame) against the good-doers; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (91). ﴿Nor (is there blame) upon those who came to you that you might provide them mounts; you said, "I cannot find anything to mount you on." They turned away with their eyes overflowing with tears from grief that they could not find anything to spend﴾ (92) (al-Tawbah). That is: there is no blame upon those whom the two noble verses mention for remaining behind from fighting. This was the exception to the general rule imposed upon every believer to fight in the way of Allah, and it is what the verse we are reflecting upon brings: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy, and strive with your wealth and your persons in the way of Allah.﴾ Wealth is what enables you to prepare weapons for war, and when the army goes out to fight it must be equipped with weapons, with vehicles, which in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were like horses, and also with provisions sufficient for the days of fighting. Therefore the Exalted mentions wealth first, then afterwards mentions persons and lives. Whoever possesses strength and wealth must strive with both; and whoever possesses only one of the two, strength or wealth, must strive with that. If he is weak, he must help with his wealth the strong who is capable of fighting, by providing for him weapons, horses, shields and other means of fighting.

Here the Exalted says: ﴿and strive﴾. "Jahada" (strive) and "qatala" (fight) are built on the pattern of mufa'alah (reciprocal action), meaning: if one of the disbelievers fights you, you must exert all your effort in fighting him. "Jahada" is like "shaaraka" (take part): would you say "Zayd shaarak" and stop, or say "Zayd shaarak 'Amr"? So there is mufa'alah.

But the Exalted says in another verse:

﴿O you who believe, be steadfast, outdo one another in steadfastness, stand guard, and fear Allah that you may prosper﴾ (Al 'Imran: 200).

This statement is a command to be patient in fighting. But suppose your enemy is as patient as you; here comes another command from the Exalted: ﴿Outdo (sabiru)﴾, that is, overcome him in patience by being more patient than he. Likewise ﴿strive (jahiduhum)﴾, that is, overcome them in jihad, by striving more than they.

Let us return to the Exalted's saying: ﴿and strive with your wealth and your persons in the way of Allah﴾. The way of Allah is the path leading to the goal which is the pleasure of Allah and Paradise. Then the Exalted says: ﴿That is better for you﴾. "Dhalika" is a demonstrative, pointing to the singular notion derived from His saying: ﴿strive with your wealth and your persons﴾. So "dha" refers to jihad with wealth and self, and ﴿lakum﴾ addresses the plural, since the Exalted addresses a group.

Some who do not understand the language say that ﴿dhalikum﴾ is one word, a demonstrative or an address; we say to them: no, rather it is two words: a demonstrative and an address. The demonstrative here refers to one thing, and the address is to a group. An example of this is also the saying of the Exalted on the tongue of the wife of the Governor in the story of Joseph, when the wife of the Governor gathered the women, brought Joseph out before them, and there was a group of women, and Joseph was there too:

﴿That is the one about whom you blamed me﴾ (Yusuf: 32).

"Dha" here refers to Joseph, and "lakunna" refers to the women addressed.

Another example is the saying of the Exalted:

﴿Those two are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ (al-Qasas: 32).

"Dhan" is a demonstrative for two, and they were two miracles of Moses, peace be upon him: the staff and the white hand; and the particle "ka" is for the addressee, who is Moses, peace be upon him.

So: the Truth's saying ﴿dhalikum﴾ in the verse we are reflecting upon consists of two words: the demonstrative for one and the address to a group.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is better﴾... about what good does He speak?

If you go forth and strive with your wealth and your persons, that is good, and it must be good relative to its opposite. Its opposite is sitting back from jihad with your wealth and your persons.

So: jihad is better than sitting back.

The word ﴿khayr﴾ is used in the language in two ways. The first usage is that it is meant as general good, as in His saying:

{Whoever does an atom's weight of good...}

1 Agreed upon; related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6309) and Muslim in his Sahih (2747), and the wording is al-Bukhari's. "Saqata 'ala ba'irihi" means he chanced upon it and came across it unintentionally, having lost it, and then found it; and "al-Fala" is the deadly desert.

2 Cited by al-Ghazali in Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din (4/52) as a saying of some of the early generations, and its wording: "No servant disobeys except that the place of the earth asks permission to swallow him up, and his roof from the sky asks permission to drop a piece upon him; and Allah the Exalted says to the earth and the sky: Hold off from My servant and give him respite, for you did not create him; had you created him you would have shown him mercy, and perhaps he will repent to Me and I will forgive him, and perhaps he will replace (his sin) with righteousness and I will change it for him into good deeds."

3 Al-Zuhri said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab went out to the raid though one of his eyes had gone. It was said to him: "You are ill." He said: "Allah has called the light and the heavy to go forth; if fighting is not possible for me, I will increase the numbers and guard the goods." Mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3076). "Takthir al-sawad" means increasing their numbers.

4 The scholars differed in interpreting this verse into ten opinions, mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3075), then he said: the correct meaning of the verse is that people were commanded as a whole, i.e., go forth, whether the movement is light for you or heavy.

5 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (1/952): "Jihad was only disliked because it involves spending wealth, leaving homeland and family, exposing the body to wounds and injuries, loss of limbs and loss of life; so their dislike was of that, not that they disliked the obligation of Allah."

6 From Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever flees from two has fled, and whoever flees from three has not fled." Related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11151) as marfu' through the route of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid from him. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/328): "its narrators are trustworthy." It was also related by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan (2538) as mawquf on Ibn 'Abbas through the route of Ibn Abi Najih from 'Ata' from him.

7 Al-Qurtubi (4/3077) said: "That is when jihad becomes obligatory by the enemy's conquest of a region of the regions, or by his descent upon the homeland. When that happens, it becomes obligatory on all the people of that abode to go forth and set out against him, light and heavy, young and old, each according to his capacity; whoever has a father, without his permission, and whoever has no father; and no one able to go out, whether a fighter or one who increases numbers, should stay behind."

8 It was said: the verse ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ is abrogated by these two verses. It was also said: its abrogating verse is His saying: ﴿Why should not a party from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware?﴾ (al-Tawbah: 122). Al-Qurtubi (4/3076) said: "The correct view is that it is not abrogated." I say: jihad varies according to the circumstances of the battle; some of it makes fighting obligatory on each individual, as we have explained, and then jihad is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn); and some of it does not make fighting obligatory, so it is a collective obligation (fard kifayah), which, if some undertake it, lifts it from the others; this is when the enemy is outside the borders and has not raided the lands or occupied them.

Then, after that, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, returns to those who are reluctant to join the jihad, in order to settle all the matters. So He, majestic in His majesty, says:

﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you. But the distance seemed long to them. They will swear by Allah, "If we had been able, we would have gone out with you." They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars.﴾ (42)

Al-ʿarad (transient worldly goods) is what stands opposed to al-jawhar (substance), and al-jawhar is that which is not subject to changes. Thus health is an ʿarad and sickness is an ʿarad, because both do not last. Therefore everything that changes is called an ʿarad that passes away. It is said: "The world is a present ʿarad (transient goods), from which the righteous and the wicked both eat."(1)

So the word of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Had it been a near gain﴾ means: had it been a matter of goods easy to obtain and appealing to the soul, without the hardship of travel and the sacrifice of wealth and life, they would have hastened to it. ﴿And a moderate journey﴾: al-qasid is the one who is moderate, who is in the middle. Some people go to excess in idleness, so they do not seek good from striving on the earth and from what Allah has created, and some people go to excess in the worldly motion, running like wild beasts in the wilderness, and get nothing except what Allah has apportioned to them. The temperaments of people vary between extravagance and stinginess, but the believer must be of the moderate community. The Truth says:

﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾ (al-Ma'ida: 66), because the believer is not seized by idleness so that he loses the good of this world, nor is he seized by extravagance so that he forgets faith. Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, makes clear to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that had there been a worldly benefit or a journey without hardship or fatigue, they would have followed you. They did not follow you, because there were no worldly spoils, since there was hardship: the journey to Tabuk, and fighting the Romans, who were a civilized power that equalled the Persian state, and this too was hardship. The year was one of difficulty and the heat was intense. Had the matter been easy and facilitated, they would have followed you.

He, glorified, continues: ﴿But the distance seemed long to them﴾, meaning the hardship was lengthy. Then He says: ﴿They will swear by Allah, "If we had been able, we would have gone out with you."﴾ So they did not follow you, because the matter was neither a near gain nor an easy journey, but a journey full of terrors and sacrifices of wealth and life. When you return from the fighting, they will swear to you that they would have gone out with you to fight had they been able.

The Truth said this before the time of the oath came, and this is one of the signs of prophethood, so that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would know the hypocrites from those of sincere faith. He, glorified and exalted, exposes the foolishness of the hypocrites; therefore He said: ﴿They will swear by Allah﴾. The use of the letter sin (sa) here means that they had not yet said it, but they would say it in the future; had they been alert to this, they would have refrained from swearing, and they would have said: "The Qur'an said 'they will swear'." But Allah blinded them, so they swore, and thus the opponents of Islam come to bear witness—despite their noses—to Islam. Another example of the same matter: when the qibla was changed from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Noble Ka'ba, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them from their qibla which they were upon?"﴾ (al-Baqara: 142).

His saying here, ﴿will say﴾, means that they had not yet said it; otherwise the letter sin would not have been used. This verse was revealed in a Qur'an that is recited and does not change or alter until the Day of Resurrection. Although they were able not to say that word, and had they done so they would have contributed to casting doubt on the credibility of the Qur'an and demolished the cause of religion that they wish to demolish, yet they said: ﴿What has turned them from their qibla﴾, and they came affirming and confirming the Qur'an.

In these days we find something strange: we find someone who says, "I follow only what has come in the Qur'an; as for the Sunna, I am not obliged to adhere to it." We say to whoever repeats this statement: How many rak'ahs are there in the dawn prayer, and in the noon, afternoon, sunset and night prayers? Someone will answer: the dawn prayer is two rak'ahs, the noon four, the afternoon four, the sunset three, and the night four. We say: From where did you get this? He says: From the Sunna.

We say: Then it is necessary to follow the Sunna so that you can pray, and you will not understand the practical application of many rulings except by following the Sunna.

The Truth, glorified is He, compels this one who wars against the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and calls to not adhering to it; He, glorified, compels him to acknowledge the necessity of following the Sunna. Thus the saying of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is confirmed:

"There will soon be a man reclining on his couch, to whom my hadith is related, and he will say: Between us and you is the Book of Allah. Whatever we find in it to be lawful, we deem lawful, and whatever is in it to be unlawful, we deem unlawful. But what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has forbidden is like what Allah has forbidden."(2)

They said that statement out of disparagement of the Book, but without realizing it they confirmed the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They did not possess intelligence, because intelligence that does not guide to faith is a form of foolishness and blindness of insight. Likewise was the condition of those who swore that they were unable to go out to fight; the word of Allah had preceded them: ﴿They will swear by Allah, "If we had been able, we would have gone out with you."﴾ and they came afterward and swore, to confirm the truth of the Qur'an. In their oath they claim inability to fight, although they have wealth and capability.

The Truth says of them: ﴿They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars.﴾ Since they swore falsely by Allah, they have put themselves into destruction; they did not suffice with abstaining from jihad, but they lied, and Allah exposed their lie.

(1) A very weak hadith, from Shaddad ibn Aws, traced to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. It was related by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya (1/264) and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (3/361), ed. Dar al-Fikr, in the biography of Abu Mahdi Sa'id ibn Sinan. al-Jawzajani said: "I fear that his hadiths are fabricated." al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith." See Mizan al-I'tidal (biography 3208). However, Abu Nu'aym related it as a statement of Shaddad from another route, which is more likely correct.

(2) Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/132), al-Tirmidhi (2664), Ibn Majah (12), and al-Daraqutni (4/286) in their Sunans, through al-Hasan ibn Jabir from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'di Karib. al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith from this route." The wording is that of al-Daraqutni.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 9, verse 43:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Allah has pardoned you. Why did you grant them permission before it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?﴾ (9:43):

The word ﴿ʿafā﴾ (pardoned) indicates that there was a trace that has been erased, just as a person walks in the sand, his feet leave a mark, then the wind comes and fills the area of that mark with sand and removes it. In religious usage, it denotes Allah, glorified and exalted, erasing the sins of His servants so that He does not punish them for them. Once a person has asked forgiveness for his sin and said: "I ask Allah forgiveness, the One besides whom there is no god, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I turn to Him in repentance"(1), no one should embarrass him after that, nor should anyone reproach him, for he has sought forgiveness from the One who owns the entire dominion, and He alone, glorified is He, possesses pardon and forgiveness(2). So let none of you involve himself in this matter, and a person should not embarrass a sinner so long as he has sought forgiveness from the One who holds the power to pardon. Whoever hears a person seeking forgiveness should say to him: "May Allah pardon you." No one knows whether Allah has pardoned him or not, so let him be helped by your prayer for him. As for one who reproaches a sinner, we say to him: "Mind your manners," for the sinner did not commit the sin against you, but he committed it against his Lord. If one who seeks forgiveness for his sin is not to be embarrassed before people, then how much more so the pardon of Allah, glorified is He, who alone is capable of pardoning.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, mentions the pardon granted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who gave them permission to stay behind from fighting. Then the Qur'an comes afterward to affirm that what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did, by permitting them to stay behind, was correct, saying in another place in the same surah:

﴿Had they gone out with you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:47).

Thus, had they gone out, they would have been a cause of defeat, not one of the causes of victory. The Truth affirmed the action of the Messenger, and he (ﷺ) is protected from error (al-ʿiṣmah).

Here we are before a pardon from the pardon of Allah, even though there was no sin to be pardoned; and here also is a permission from the Messenger to them to stay behind, and the Qur'an came down to affirm its correctness.

Some have understood the Truth's words ﴿Why did you grant them permission?﴾ as a rhetorical question of disapproval, as if the Truth were saying: "How could you grant them permission?"

Thus the Messenger was between two matters: between a pardon after which no sin is mentioned, and an interrogative that, according to some, implies disapproval.

We say: Allah, glorified and exalted, supported His Messenger (ﷺ) with His saying:

﴿Had they gone out with you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:47). It is as if the Messenger had been guided to the matter by his faithful nature (fiṭrah īmāniyyah), and the Qur'an pointed to that, to make clear to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is protected from error and his nature is sound. It was incumbent upon him to present rational explanation to people, because he is the exemplar, so that no one from among the common people later comes to issue a religious ruling and say: "I saw with my nature such-and-such." Rather, a person must make sure of what has come in the noble Qur'an and the Sunnah before issuing a ruling on any matter of religion.

For example: the matter was disputed among the Muslims concerning the ransom of the captives of Badr(3), and the Truth's word came down: ﴿Had there not been a prior decree from Allah, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾ (al-Anfal 8:68), and Allah confirmed the ruling of His Messenger and let it stand. Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was guided to the matter by his faithful nature, but this right is not permitted to anyone other than the protected one (maʿṣūm).

Allah, glorified is He, has also permitted seeking permission in His saying:

﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, grant permission to whom you wish among them﴾ (al-Nur 24:62).

The Truth, glorified and exalted, says here, in the verse about which we are reflecting: ﴿Allah has pardoned you. Why did you grant them permission until it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?﴾ Thus it becomes clear to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) granted them permission on the basis of preliminary considerations, investigation and his faithful nature, and he saw that permitting these laggards was a matter that agreed with the will of the Truth, glorified is He; for had they gone out with the army of the Muslims, they would have increased them in nothing but corruption(4), since there was no sincere intention in jihad. Therefore Allah discouraged them(5) and weakened their resolve so that they would not go out. The pardon here came in the form of the matter, since it was necessary to investigate before granting permission. So the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿until it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars﴾. That is: had the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not granted them permission, they would have been exposed; but his permission gave them a screen behind which to hide their hypocrisy, for they had resolved not to go out, and had they done so, their affair would have been exposed to all the Muslims. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) willed to conceal them(6).

(1) Narrated by Abu Dawud (1517) and al-Tirmidhi (3577) in their Sunan, from the hadith of Zayd, the freedman of the Prophet (ﷺ). al-Tirmidhi said: "A strange hadith which we do not know except through this route." al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib (2/269): "Its chain is good and continuous." It was also narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/118) from Ibn Mas'ud, and he declared it sound according to the condition of Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed.
(2) This is the affair of the Lord, the Forgiving, who says, glorified is He: ﴿And who forgives sins but Allah?﴾ (Al ʿImran 3:135). As for the affair of people, Allah has said of them: ﴿Say: "Even if you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would withhold them for fear of spending, and man is ever stingy"﴾ (al-Isra 17:100). So they, in addition to their pursuit of people's faults, if mercy were in their hands and they were charged with giving people some of it, they would withhold it.
(3) Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1763) and Ahmad in his Musnad (1/30–31) from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, in a long narration, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and ʿUmar: "What do you think of these captives?" Abu Bakr said: "O Prophet of Allah, they are our kinsmen and tribe. I think you should take a ransom from them, so that it becomes a strength for us against the disbelievers, and perhaps Allah will guide them to Islam." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What do you think, O son of al-Khattab?" He said: "I think you should let us establish ourselves and strike their necks... for these are the leaders of disbelief and its chieftains." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) acted upon the opinion of Abu Bakr and they took the ransom, but the revelation of Allah came down: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a heavy slaughter in the land. You desire the goods of this world, but Allah desires the Hereafter﴾ (al-Anfal 8:67).
(4) Al-khabal: corruption, slander, sowing discord and rumours (false reports).
(5) Al-tathbīṭ: discouraging, undermining, and weakening resolve to go out.
(6) Qatadah and ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: Two things the Prophet (ﷺ) did for which he was not commanded: his permitting a group of the hypocrites to stay behind from him, and he had no right to carry out anything by revelation; and his taking ransom from the captives, so Allah rebuked him.

Then the Truthful, Exalted One says:

﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to be excused from striving with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the God-conscious.﴾ (9:44)

He draws our attention, glory be to Him, to the fact that those who sought that permission to remain behind exposed themselves, for they asked for leave after the command had come from Allah: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. Every believer in Allah and the Last Day, in those circumstances, cannot possibly stay behind from striving in the cause of Allah. The true believer does not present excuses to stay behind, even if he has genuine excuses; rather, he will try to conceal them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that he may go out with him as a fighter, and indeed he hastens to jihad, even if Allah had granted him a concession not to fight.

This verse, therefore, carries a rebuke to those who asked for permission, and it carries more than that. The believer, when he is called to jihad with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and by command of Allah, does not think like an ordinary person; for a person, in ordinary matters, when something is asked of him, turns his mind and thought over: will he do it or will he not do it? But the believer, when he is called to jihad in the cause of Allah and alongside the Messenger of Allah, does not turn the answer over in his mind, and the word "no" never even crosses his thoughts; rather, he sets out on his way to jihad.

And how can the command to go out to fighting come from Allah, and then these people make the seeking of permission not to go out into a pretext?

Therefore, the mere asking for permission is evidence of the wavering of faith in their hearts, because each one of them in this situation has turned the matter over in his mind: will he go out to jihad or not go out? Then he decided to stay behind. What is strange is that these people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission not to go out, although the command to jihad came from Allah the Glorified and Exalted, and the matter did not need the Messenger to grant them permission to stay behind. But they were seeking an excuse to shelter behind.

An example from our daily lives: we find the people of the town mocking the miser who does not honour his guest yet claims that he will honour him. You find him calling his son and saying to him in front of the guest: "Go down to the market and look for a sheep for us to slaughter for the guest, and do not delay, for we are waiting for your return..." And as soon as the guest, out of courtesy, says: "No." You find the miser dismissing his son, and taking the guest's refusal as a reason for not honouring him, as if he wanted that, when in reality he never wanted it from the start.

We all know that a person does not ask permission to honour his guests. The example is Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when the angels came to him in the form of men, and he wished to honour them; he did not ask their permission to slaughter a calf for them, but brought it to them slaughtered and roasted(1). This is the conduct of one who truly wishes to honour the guest with a sacrifice. As for one who wants to seek an excuse, he adopts various methods in which he pretends to carry it out, while in reality he does not want to do it, just as a guest may be asked: "Will you drink coffee, or do you not like it?" or he is asked: "Do you want to have dinner, or would you like to sleep lightly?" or it is said: "Would you like to sleep with us, or sleep in the hotel, which is more comfortable for you?"

Since there are those who asked the Messenger: "Shall I go out with you to fight, or shall I stay behind?", this question indicates hesitation, and faith presupposes firm certainty, for hesitation means doubt, which is going and returning alternately, and it means that the one asking is undecided, since both sides of the judgement are equal for him.

Therefore, believers in Allah do not ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission when they are called to jihad, for the mere seeking of permission to go out to jihad does not befit a believer.

As for His saying, ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the God-conscious﴾: meaning, Allah knows what is in their hearts of piety. So if they deceive people, they will not be able to deceive Allah, for He is aware of what the hearts conceal.

(1) This is mentioned in His saying: ﴿So he did not delay to bring a roasted calf﴾ (Hud: 69), and He said: ﴿Then he turned quickly to his family and brought a fat calf﴾ (adh-Dhariyat: 26). "Labitha" (ما لبث): meaning he did not delay in bringing a calf roasted on hot stones without the fire touching it, and this is the meaning of "haneeth" (الحنيذ).

Then Allah sends down His judgment regarding these people, saying:

﴿Only those seek your permission who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt, so in their doubt they waver back and forth.﴾ (45)

Thus Allah issued His judgment concerning those who hastened to ask for permission. For as long as a person wavers between going out to jihad or not going out, this reveals the shaking of his faith, and this shaking means there is doubt in his soul about what Allah has prepared for him in the Hereafter. For he would have been certain within himself that he would enter Paradise without reckoning if he were martyred. He would not have hesitated for a single moment, nor turned the matter over in his head: should he go or not go? So long as Paradise is the goal, whatever path leads to it will be the path followed by the one in whose heart is the certainty of faith. The shorter the path, the more it gives joy to the believing person, because he wishes to move from the misery of this world to the bliss of the Hereafter, even if he lives in comfort in this world. He knows that this comfort is fleeting, and he does not want this fleeting comfort, but rather the lasting bliss that does not pass away.

The meaning of hesitation (tardud) and asking permission (istidhan) here is this: doubt (shakk) has entered the heart of the person. The meaning of doubt, as we know, is the presence in oneself of two equal matters, neither of which is preferred until one follows it. Speculative discourse (al-nasab al-kalamiyya) and rational propositions (al-qadaya al-'aqliyya) revolve around many things, so when you affirm a judgment there must be a reality that supports it, for if you affirm something that has no reality, this is ignorance (jahl). Ignorance, as we know, is to believe that something is a fact when it is other than that and has no reality. For example, if you say: "The earth is flat," and then people bring you a picture of the earth as a sphere, and you insist that it is flat, this is ignorance and obstinacy in it. There is a difference between the ignorant (jahil) and the unlettered (ummi). The unlettered person who did not know that the earth is spherical, and then came to know the true knowledge and affirmed it, will, once he knows the reality, accept it and believe in it. But the ignorant person believes in what contradicts reality. If you bring him the truth, he begins to argue about it, insisting on his opinion. That is why we find that the calamity of the whole world lies not in the unlettered but in the ignorant, because the unlettered person needs only one intellectual effort: you convey the information to him and he accepts it. As for the ignorant person, persuading him requires two efforts. The first effort: you must remove from his mind the mistaken information and illusions that do not exist in reality. The second effort: you must convince him of the truth.

If there is a reality in life that you can demonstrate, this is knowledge ('ilm). If you cannot demonstrate it, this is indoctrination (talqin). For example, when we teach a small child that Allah is One, at an age when he cannot yet intellectually be shown proof of this. You tell him: "Allah is One," and the child affirms it, and this is a真 established reality, yet he cannot demonstrate it. In this state he imitates his father, his mother, or whoever taught him these words, until his mind matures and he can demonstrate what he believed in childhood through indoctrination.

So, knowledge requires that you believe in a proposition for which there is evidence. But if you have not reached the stage of certainty, there are two propositions in your mind, not one. If neither proposition is preferred over the other, this is doubt (shakk). If you think one of them is preponderant, this is opinion (zann). If you take the preponderant proposition, this is delusion (wahm).

Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Only those seek your permission who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. Had certain faith in Allah and the Last Day settled in their hearts, and that their return is to Allah, glorified and exalted, and that they will be held accountable for what they have sent forward, and had they regarded their sacrifice of wealth and self as a small deed compared to the great reward awaiting them in the Hereafter, they would not have asked permission. But since doubt has entered their hearts, this means there is hesitation regarding the matter of meeting Allah on the Last Day. And since they doubt this matter, would they sacrifice their wealth and selves for nothing? Therefore the Almighty says of them: ﴿and their hearts are in doubt﴾.

So, doubt has its seat in the heart, and knowledge also has its seat in the heart, and both doubt and knowledge pass through the intellect, because it is the intellect that refines such matters after receiving sensory data and debating premises and conclusions. If the intellect refines these matters and settles upon faith, then faith becomes a certain and firmly established proposition in the heart, and it no longer rises again to the intellect to be debated anew. That is why they called it 'aqida (creed), meaning that you tie ('aqadtu) the thing so that it settles in its place and does not budge.

For example, if a child brings his hand near something burning and feels the sting of fire, he now knows that fire burns, and he does not try to repeat the same experiment, nor does he debate it in his mind saying: "The fire will not sting me this time." Rather, the matter settles in his mind, and moves from a sensory matter to a matter of creed that is not subject to experiment again and needs no proof.

Here the Almighty says: ﴿and their hearts are in doubt﴾, and in another verse He says: ﴿Allah has sealed their hearts﴾. The heart is the locus of matters that have passed the stage of rational reflection and have become firm propositions that the intellect no longer examines anew.

His words here, ﴿and their hearts are in doubt﴾, mean that faith has not reached among them the level where it no longer rises again to rational reflection: "Will he believe or not?" That is, they have not reached the rank of certainty, but remain in the stage of doubt, which returns matters from the heart to the intellect to be debated anew. Therefore the Almighty describes them with a precise description, saying: ﴿so in their doubt they waver back and forth﴾, meaning that their faith oscillates between the intellect and the heart: it descends to the heart, then rises to the intellect to be debated anew, then descends to the heart again, and so the matter keeps wavering between intellect and heart without settling in one place. Thus they are not certain about the Hereafter and what Allah has prepared for them there of reward, and they doubt meeting Allah on the Last Day. Allah, glorified and exalted, wishes to clarify the picture for us further, and says:

{And had they intended to go out, they would have prepared for it some preparation, but Allah disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said: "Sit with those who sit." (46)}

Therefore, their hesitation is evidence that they do not want to go out for jihad; for had they truly been resolved upon it, they would have prepared what war requires of provisions, mounts and weapons. But they never did any of this at all, because they lacked the sincere intention to strive in the way of God with their wealth and their selves.

One might say: was it not permissible for them to prepare everything for battle at the last moment? We say: No. The one who goes out to fight cannot prepare at the last moment. Rather, he must occupy himself with the preliminaries of war, of weapons, provisions, mounts and other things; and if he had not occupied himself with these matters some time before departure, and ensured that his weapons were fit for fighting and that the food he would carry with him was available, and so on, he would not have been able to go out as a fighter. So the matter is not one of the moment; rather, their failure to prepare for fighting was a revealing of the hidden leaven settled in their depths against going out. God, glory be to Him, has knowledge of their intentions and of what their breasts conceal, and He has requited them for what they hid within themselves. Therefore He says:

﴿But God was averse to their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said: "Sit with those who sit."﴾ God, exalted is He, has no need of any of His creation; the creation are those who are in constant need of Him, glory be to Him. Therefore He held these people back from going out, and He was averse to their going forth to fight. "Held them back" means He made them remain in their place, and did not accept from them that they prepare their equipment for fighting, out of His aversion that they should go out eagerly to fight. Aversion (al-kurh) is an emotional state (ʿamaliyya wijdāniyya), and restraining (al-tathbīt) is an impulsive act (ʿamaliyya nazʿiyya).

I always give this example—and God's is the highest similitude: you see a rose, and your eye perceives its beauty. If you reach out to pluck it, here the Sharʿ intervenes to say to you, "No," because this is an impulse toward what you do not possess. If you wish to obtain a rose like it, then either you buy it or you plant one like it. So the Sharʿ intervenes only in impulsive actions.

God's aversion to their impulse became manifest in their being held back, forsaken and turned away from action. He made the staying behind seem fair to them in their souls, so that they did not go out to fight alongside the Messenger of God (ﷺ). That was for a wisdom which the True One, glory be to Him, intended, and it coincided with what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had permitted in regard to staying behind. Here we note that the True One, glory be to Him, said: ﴿and it was said: "Sit with those who sit."﴾ And if the restraining was from God, it is as though He made clear to them: sit, by God's permission, through the divine will. And the Messenger of God (ﷺ) permitted them to sit and stay behind when he perceived their sluggishness; or the devils inspired them to sit. The True One says, glory be to Him:

﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy—devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with ornate speech as deception.﴾ (al-Anʿam: 112)

Thus we find that the word ﴿qīla﴾ ("it was said") is cast in the passive form, because it may be that there are several speakers: God, by His restraining of them, is as if He said to them, "Sit"; the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to them, "Sit"; and the devils, when they made sitting seem fair to them, were as if they said to them, "Sit." And their saying to one another, "Sit," made the sitting seem fair to them. Thus one word gave us several gifts.

And does one gift negate another gift? No; rather, all of them are gifts fitting the situation.

﴿But God was averse to their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said: "Sit with those who sit with you."﴾ The intended meaning of "those who sit" here is those upon whom jihad is not obligatory: women, children and the elderly. It is as though by not going out they had abandoned their manhood, which obliges them to jihad. This is a matter they should not have accepted for themselves. In another place in the same surah, the True One, glory be to Him, said:

﴿They were content to be with the women who stay behind, and a seal was set upon their hearts.﴾ (al-Tawbah: 87). Manhood required of them that they rise up for fighting, but they accepted for themselves the weakness of women and children. And the Arab poet denounced those of his tribe who were slack about fighting alongside him, when he wanted to provoke them, saying:

"I do not know, and I do not think I know, whether the people of Ḥiṣn are men or women."(1)
"Qawm" is applied to men without women.(2)

1. The verse is from a poem of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma.
2. This is reinforced by the Almighty's saying: ﴿O you who believe, let not one people scoff at another people, who may be better than them, nor women at women, who may be better than them﴾ (al-Ḥujurat: 11). Had women been included in "qawm," He would not have said "nor women at women."

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) explains to us the wisdom behind the discouragement (tathbit). If their staying behind came from a good source, then God's discouraging them is wise, and the Messenger's granting them permission not to go out is wise. But if the matter of their staying behind came from the whispering of Satan to them or the whispering of their own souls, then the whisperings of the devils and of their souls have served the cause of faith (in the sense of working against it), and they have helped the will of God, and this is the stupidity of disbelief. The whispering thus made attractive to these hypocrites the not going out to fight in the way of God, because if they had gone out, there would have happened from them what the Truth, glory be to Him, said about them:

﴿Had they gone out among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption, and they would have hastened between you, seeking [to cause] dissension among you, and among you are those who listen to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

Al-khabal (confusion) is a mental illness in which the balance of thought is disturbed. You say: "So-and-so is makhbul," meaning he judges matters without reason. So His saying, exalted is He, ﴿they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾ means that they would only have been a source of confusion of thoughts if they had gone out with you to fight, so that you could not make a sound decision. It is as if they were a spy upon you, opposed to you and not with you, and they might have been among the factors of defeat, which God did not want for you, and not among the factors of victory. So their not going out was a repelling of an evil that would have befallen you had they gone out with you. God willed their not going out in order to preserve the strength of the believers and their capacity for jihad.

As for His saying, ﴿and they would have hastened between you (la-awda'u khilalakum)﴾, it means that they would have caused division among the ranks of the believers, separating them, and would have infiltrated among them to spread corruption, because al-khilal is the gap between two things or two persons. One of them would enter among a group of believers and corrupt them, and another would corrupt another group, and so they would walk through the believers to divide them.

But the question arises: would they have gone out with them, or among them? They would have entered into the gaps between the believers to confuse their thoughts. We say: the prepositions (huruf al-jarr) may stand in for one another, and when you hear the word "fikum" (among you), know that it signifies the penetration of a container and what is contained. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, said in another place in the Qur'an, clarifying the container and the contained:

﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ (Ta-Ha 71).

Would Pharaoh have crucified the magicians inside the trunks or upon the trunks? Although the linguists have said that the prepositions stand in for one another, we do not accept this answer, for if we accept it in human speech, we cannot accept it in the speech of God, because "fi" has the meaning of enclosure, and "ʿala" has another meaning. Had the Truth, glory be to Him, said "la-usallibannakum ʿala judhu‛ al-nakhl" (upon the trunks of palm trees), its meaning would be that the crucifixion is upon the trunk, i.e., an ordinary crucifixion. But His saying, ﴿And I will crucify you in the trunks of palm trees﴾, means that the act of crucifixion would be carried out with such force that parts of the body of the crucified would enter into the thing crucified upon, i.e., Pharaoh's soldiers would have pressed upon the bodies of the magicians until they entered into the palm trunk, and these bodies and the palm trunks would become as if they were one piece. This is a picture of the harshness and force of the crucifixion.

But if we said "ʿala judhu‛ al-nakhl," the meaning would be lighter and the crucifixion less harsh. So it is as if the noble Qur'an has used what gives us precision of meaning, such that if one letter changes, the meaning is disturbed.

We find the Truth, glory be to Him, saying in another place of the noble Qur'an: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord...﴾ (Ali 'Imran 133). That is, our haste in righteous deeds leads us to forgiveness. Therefore, before we hasten to righteous deeds we were not in forgiveness, and when we hasten we arrive at it.

Then we find the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, also: ﴿Indeed they used to hasten in good deeds...﴾ (al-Anbiya' 90).

He did not say "yusari'una ila al-khayrat" (hasten to the good deeds), because their deed is now good, and they will hasten in it, i.e., they will increase it. Therefore: if you hasten to something, it is as if it was not in your mind, but you hastened to good first and then you increase in doing good.

If we reflect on the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, ﴿and they would have hastened between you (la-awda'u khilalakum)﴾, we find that "awda'a" means to proceed at a degree between slowness and speed. It is said: "awda'at al-dabbah," i.e., the animal walked at a pace that was neither slow nor fast at the same time. And if you looked at the condition of these hypocrites, had they gone out with the believers to fight, you would have seen them making corruption attractive to them and working so that the minds of the fighters would be struck with confusion, and you would find that this matter requires both slowness at the beginning and speed in movement. They would need slowness, because they would be whispering into the ears of the believers, adorning falsehood, and this requires slowness; then each of them would move to a second believer to do the same operation, and he must hasten to be beside the other believer. So the movement here requires slowness in the whispering and speed in moving from one believer to another.

And this is the most precise description applicable to what would have happened.

But what was the aim of these hypocrites in placing confusion in the minds of the believers and dividing them into groups? The aim was to undermine their unity and strength. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿seeking [to cause] dissension among you (yabghunakumu al-fitnah)﴾, i.e., they seek for you dissension. For the wicked person, when he sees good being done by another, finds the faith-related qualities within his depths striking him with a kind of self-contempt, so he tries to diminish the one who does good by mocking what he does or ridiculing him. This is most evident in gatherings of wine-drinking, when those present feel great guilt; if there is among them a person who does not drink wine, you find them trying to entice him in every way so that he commits the same sin, and if he refuses, they begin to taunt him, ridicule him, mock him, and claim that he will never reach the level of men, and other methods of mockery. Likewise you find the liar trying to push people into lying, the thief enticing people to steal, and the bribe-taker trying to spread bribery among all his colleagues; if he finds an upright person among those who practice these kinds of evil conduct, they persecute him and mock him. An example: when a person stands to pray among a number of those who neglect prayer, you find them trying to mock him: one says to him, "Take me on your wing," and another says to him mockingly, "May God make us partake of your blessings." The Noble Qur'an clarifies this matter to give us faith-based immunity, saying:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as overseers over them. So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, observing. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ (al-Mutaffifin 29–36).

These verses give us a picture of what happens when corruption spreads across the earth. Those who mocked the believers laugh laughs that will certainly pass away, sooner or later, followed by punishment in the Hereafter; as for the people of faith, they fear God in this world, so God rewards them in the Hereafter, and they laugh a lasting, everlasting laugh.

So His saying, exalted is He, ﴿they seek for you dissension (yabghunakumu al-fitnah)﴾, means that from the excess of their hatred towards you and your faith, they try to tempt you in your religion until you descend to their level, exactly like the patterns of behaviour we explained earlier.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, explains that the faithful front would not be secure from what these hypocrites would have done. It is true that they did not go out with the believers, but there were among the believers those who would listen to them. The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿And among you are those who listen to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ One says "sami'tu lahu" (I listened to him), meaning my ear heard what he said, and "sami'tu min fulan" (I listened from so-and-so), meaning for the benefit of another person; i.e., whoever listens to them or listens to your news, he conveys it to them.

So the lam (la-) comes with both meanings: among the believers there would have been those who listened to these hypocrites, which would cause confusion in their thinking, and among these confusers of thoughts would be spies for them who convey the news of the believers to them and work for their account; and there would be among the believers those who would first listen to them, and once they were struck with confusion, they would begin to convey the news of the believers to them. Thus the "lam" came as a link between "sami'at lahu" or "sami'at min ghayrihi li-salihihi." God, glory be to Him, clarifies this matter further in the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be a advocate for the treacherous (lil-khа'inin khasiman)﴾ (al-Nisa' 105). The superficial thinker says: this is a warning against disputing with the treacherous, out of fear that one may not be able to overcome them, or that they may increase in their sin because of this dispute. We say: you have not understood the meaning; the clear meaning is: do not be an advocate for the interest of the treacherous, i.e., do not litigate on behalf of the treacherous or defend them.

And His saying, ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾: because the one who would have listened and the ones for whose benefit he would have listened are both wrongdoers, and Allah is Knowing of them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 48:

Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, they sought to cause fitnah (discord) before, and they turned matters over against you until the truth came and the command of Allah prevailed, while they were averse.﴾ (9:48)

Almighty Allah wants to remind the believers of the past events that the hypocrites and the disbelievers carried out against Islam and the Muslims: plots against Islam, attempts to sow discord among the Muslims, and conspiracies against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).
