His saying, glorified is He, ﴿they sought fitnah before﴾ is evidence of those past events (1). As for His saying, ﴿and they turned matters over against you﴾: taqlib (turning over) means making the bottom of a thing its top and its top its bottom, so that nothing of it remains hidden. We see this manifest in the market. When you go to the fruit seller, you find the best of what is there carefully selected on top, but when you buy from him he fills your bag with the inferior type that he hid at the bottom of the basket. Thus he brings you what is at the bottom, or the bad thing whose defect is uncovered, and what you would never buy had you seen it, he places before you (2).

This is how the hypocrites act when they turn the matter over in its various aspects until they find what gives the greatest harm to the believers without themselves being struck by anything. A clear example: when Quraysh conspired against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they brought a young man from every tribe to strike him with one blow, so that his blood would be lost among the tribes.

But Almighty Allah comes to all these trials and makes them work for the benefit of the believers. Therefore He, majestic is His majesty, says: ﴿until the truth came and the command of Allah prevailed, while they were averse.﴾ So the conspiracy against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the attempt to kill him led to his emigration (hijrah) from Makkah and his departure from it, which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made a means of manifesting the truth and spreading Islam. For Allah does not send a messenger and then forsake him; since He has sent a messenger, He must support him (3). So rest yourselves, and do not seek fitnah, for the fitnah that you devised has turned against you and led to abundant good for the believers.

On this the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And certainly did Our word precede for Our servants the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant.﴾ (37:171-173)

His saying, ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant﴾ is a cosmic and doctrinal principle. If you see a people of believers engage in fighting a people of disbelievers and they are defeated, know that they are not truly among the soldiers of Allah, and that a condition of being soldiers of Allah has been violated. Therefore we must first hold ourselves accountable.

For example, at the Battle of Uhud, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked the archers not to leave their positions, but they disobeyed him (4), a condition of being soldiers of Allah was broken, namely obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ). What would have happened to Islam had those archers disobeyed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and yet been victorious? Had that happened, the commands of the Messenger, peace be upon him, would have become insignificant to the believers. And on the day of Hunayn, when the believers thought they would be victorious by their numbers rather than by their faith, the result was that they were struck with a harsh defeat at the start of the battle, so that it would be a lesson of faith for them. Therefore, when you see faith defeated before disbelief, know that a condition of the soldiery of faith has been broken. Read the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He:

{And how many a prophet fought, and with him fought many religious scholars. And they did not weaken for what afflicted them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken or submit. And Allah loves the patient. And their words were only that they said, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, and make firm our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people."} (3:146-147)

So: the first thing these fighters did was recognize that sins could bring defeat upon them, so they sought forgiveness from Allah, repented to Him, fought, and Allah granted them victory. And if it happens that the believers are not victorious, this means that there is a flaw in their faith, for Allah does not leave a Qur'anic promise to be contradicted by a cosmic event.

1. See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/361). As for al-Qurtubi, he said in his commentary on the verse (4/3083): "That is: they had sought corruption and mischief before their affair became apparent, and before the revelation came down with what they would do." Ibn Jarir said: it refers to twelve men of the hypocrites who stood at the Thaniyyat al-Wada' on the night of al-'Aqabah to assassinate the Prophet (ﷺ)..
2. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade this. He passed by a heap of food and inserted his hand into it, and his fingers touched something moist. He said: "What is this, O owner of the food?" He said: "It was struck by rain, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Why did you not put it on top of the food so that people could see it? Whoever cheats is not of me." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (102), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/242), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1315), from Abu Hurayrah. al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih hadith..
3. In this regard Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ (Ghafir: 51)..
4. From al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "We met the polytheists that day, and the Prophet (ﷺ) seated him, and he appointed over them 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr and said: Do not leave, and if you see us gaining the upper hand over them, do not leave, and if you see them gaining the upper hand over us, do not come to our aid." But they disobeyed him (ﷺ), and seventy of the Muslims fell as martyrs. The hadith is related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4043) and Ahmad in his Musnad (4/294).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 49:

The Blessed and Exalted Lord says:

{Among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial." Have they not already fallen into trial? And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers.} (49)

These are the ones who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to refrain from going out to jihad. Among them is one who said this statement: "Do not put me to trial by refusing to grant me permission." But what is the subject of the trial? Is it punishment, or evil, or polytheism and disbelief, God forbid? All of that, and other things besides, may be meant by the trial. The saying {Grant me leave and do not put me to trial} apparently takes the form of a command, but it is not a command. For when a command comes from the lower to the higher, it is not called a command; rather it is a supplication (du'a') or a hope (raja'). If it comes from an equal, it is called "musawalah" (a request between equals). But if it comes from the higher to the lower, this is what is called a command (amr). All of them are a request for an action.

Al-Jadd ibn Qays, who was from the Ansar, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial, for if the Messenger of Allah does not grant him leave, he will fall into the trial of opposing the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." (1)

It was said: this Ansari was not strong in war and its hardships. It was also said: he had a strong attachment to loving women, and he had heard of the beauty of the daughters of the Romans, and feared he would be tempted by them, especially since the battle would take place on Roman land, and it was expected that the fighters would capture captives from the daughters of the Romans.

The saying of the Exalted: {Grant me leave and do not put me to trial} actually caused him to fall into trial. Therefore the word of the Truth came: {Have they not already fallen into trial?} This Ansari was corpulent, and complained of his inability to travel a long distance and of the heat, so the response came: "If you flee from the heat and the cold, then the Fire is more deserving of being fled from," and therefore the Blessed and Exalted Lord said: {And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers.}

In another verse, He, glorified be He, says:

{Say, "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they would understand."} (81, at-Tawbah)

So: the blaze of Hell is more severe and fiercer in heat than the fire of battle (3), and the heat of this world, however intense, is far less than the fire of the Hereafter, which encompasses the disbelievers.

(1) See: Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 94) and Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/362). Al-Jadd ibn Qays was among the nobles of the Banu Salamah...
(2) Al-jald: strength, vigor, and steadfastness in fighting.
(3) This is the saying of the Glorified: {Those who were left behind rejoiced in their staying behind, contrary to the Messenger of Allah, and disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah, and said, "Do not go forth in this heat." Say, "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they would understand."} (at-Tawbah: 81)...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 50:

﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them; and if a misfortune strikes you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution before," and they turn away while they are rejoicing.﴾ (9:50)

The discussion of the hypocrites continues. After Allah, the Exalted, explained how the hypocrites tried to escape from the war for various reasons and excuses, He wished to make the picture clearer by showing the hatred that the hearts of the hypocrites conceal toward the believers. Here He says:

﴿If good befalls you﴾, and what is meant by good here is victory in war. Victory in war, from the viewpoint of the hypocrites, is confined to the believers obtaining spoils of war, and this is something that distresses and grieves the hypocrites, because the primary concern of the hypocrites is this world, and they want to obtain the greatest share of it. Since they did not go out to fight and sought invalid excuses to escape the war, they grieve when the believers are victorious, because then they will have no right to the spoils. In this case they say: "If only we had been with them, we would have obtained the spoils and taken a share of them." As for when the tide turns against the Muslims and they are defeated in battle, this is an evil for every believer, but the hypocrites consider the defeat of the people of faith to be good, and they will say to one another: "We were more prudent in judgment and took precaution in the matter, and we did not go out with them, so we were saved from what befell them." Misfortune in war takes the form of: lives, men, wealth, and equipment, in addition to the bitterness of defeat. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them; and if a misfortune strikes you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution before," and they turn away while they are rejoicing.﴾ It is as if they had taken precaution before the fighting began, so they did not go out, and as hypocrites they may rejoice if a calamity or misfortune strikes the Muslims, which here is defeat in war. And they will say: ﴿We had already taken our precaution before﴾, meaning they took precaution and did not go out to fight, whereas Muhammad and his companions and army did not take precaution. Then they turn their backs to conceal their joy.

When the Truth says: ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them﴾, it shows us that any victory for faith grieves the hypocrites within their souls, and this statement becomes a Qur'an that is recited and worshipped by, and that they hear with their ears. By Allah, if the good that the believers attain did not grieve them, would it not have been a reason for them to say: "We did not rejoice and we did not grieve"?

By Allah, when the Qur'an suddenly surprises them by uncovering the secrets of their souls, would that not be a call to their guidance?

Muhammad (ﷺ) knew the unseen that was in their hearts and exposed their inner thoughts and secrets after Allah had informed him of that. Although they concealed hypocrisy in their hearts and awaited an affliction to befall Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, the Truth, the Exalted, responds to them:

﴿Say, "Nothing will strike us except what Allah has decreed for us; He is our protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely."﴾ (9:51)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 9, verse 51:

﴿Say: Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed for us.﴾ The discussion here concerns what befalls a person, that is, what happens to him. If something comes to a person that brings good, it is a good deed (ḥasanah) for him; and if what comes from it is evil, it is viewed as a bad outcome (sayyi'ah). Thus, affliction (iṣābah) is the meeting of an event with an aim: if the aim is achieved and brings good, it is a ḥasanah, and if it brings evil, it is a sayyi'ah. Afflictions are of two kinds: an affliction in which there is an opponent (gharīm), and an affliction in which there is no opponent. If someone strikes me, for example, he becomes my opponent, and resentment (ḥafīzah) and rage (ghayẓ) toward him arise in my heart, and I desire to retaliate against him and avenge myself on him. But if I fall ill, for example, who is my opponent in the illness? No one.

So afflictions are of two kinds: one in which I have an opponent, and one in which I have no opponent. In the first kind, where I have an opponent, my heart fills with spite, and the Mighty and Majestic urges us not to harbour spite and to pardon such an opponent. He says:

﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon people—and Allah loves the good-doers﴾ (Āl ʿImrān 3:134).

Here there are three stages: the first is restraining anger (kaẓm al-ghayẓ), the second is pardon (ʿafw), and the third is to do good (iḥsān), so that you ascend to the station of those whom Allah loves, namely the good-doers (al-muḥsinīn).

Likewise the Truth says: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ (al-Shūrā 42:43). That is: whoever bears patiently what has befallen him and forgives his opponent and enemy. Patience and forgiveness are among the matters that require resolve and strength, until a person is brought to pardon and to abandon revenge.

As for afflictions in which a person has no opponent, these do not require that effort of the soul, but only patience, since a person has no recourse in them. The Truth, glorified and exalted, says regarding this kind of affliction:

﴿And be patient over what befalls you; indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ (Luqmān 31:17). The determination required here is less, and therefore the emphatic lām (lām al-tawkīd) used in His saying ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ (al-Shūrā 42:43) was not used here.

We must also pay attention to the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted, concerning human feelings, when He said: ﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon people—and Allah loves the good-doers﴾ (Āl ʿImrān 3:134).

This noble verse represents the stages of what happens within the soul. What is required first is that a person restrain his anger, meaning that anger exists in the heart and renews itself whenever a person sees his opponent before him; a person needs to restrain his anger each time he sees him. Then the believer rises in his faithful emotional response, and pardon comes. This is a second stage, namely that anger leaves the heart and pardon takes its place.

Then comes the third stage: ﴿and Allah loves the good-doers﴾, meaning that this is a kind of good which Allah loves and rewards, namely that you do good to the one who wronged you, and thus you attain the love of Allah. This is among the perfections of faith, because all of the servants are the dependants (ʿiyāl) of Allah. Let the example for yourself be—and to Allah belongs the highest example—suppose you entered the house and found that one of your children had struck the other. With whom is your heart, while you are the master of the house? It must be with the one who was struck. Therefore you pat his shoulder and reconcile with him, and perhaps you give him money or buy him something to please him; that is, you do good to him.

And since we are the dependants of Allah, if one servant dares against another and wrongs him, then Allah stands on the side of the wronged. So whoever wrongs you, Allah places Himself at your side. Should you not, in such a case, deserve to return that greeting with good toward him?

The wrongdoing child sees his wronged brother having benefited from his father's kindness, and the wronged son may obtain something he desires, while the wrongdoer in this situation wishes that he himself had been the one attacked, so as to obtain some of the good.

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, the Truth instructs us, when afflictions come, to answer the disbelievers and say:

﴿Say: Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed for us.﴾ Thus all matters are referred back to the wisdom of the Creator of the universe and the Manager of its affairs. Something may happen to me that I dislike, yet in reality it is for my benefit. If my father strikes me because I neglected my lessons, is that punishment or is it for my benefit? If you look to the future and to the success you will achieve in life if you study, then this punishment is for your benefit and not against you. Likewise we must take the events Allah brings about in His dominion in relation to the believers: if they are defeated in a battle, the Truth, glorified and exalted, wishes to draw their attention to the good within their religion, and to the fact that they must know that victory has causes which they did not take up; for this reason they were defeated.

And to Allah belongs the highest example: we find the teacher—when he takes the notebooks from the pupils to correct their mistakes—punishes the one who erred among them, and in this there is training for the pupils.

So: if you see an affliction that has befallen us and you suppose that it harms us, know that we trust in the One who brought it about, and that He brought it about for a disciplinary wisdom for us, and that everything decreed for us, not against us, is decreed by Him, the Truth, glorified and exalted, who said: ﴿Certainly I will prevail, I and My messengers…﴾ (al-Mujādilah 58:21).

So: we know by our faith that everything that afflicts us from Allah is good, and that there are events that occur for discipline, refinement and training, so that we walk upon the correct method and do not depart from it. A person only trains one he loves; as for one he does not love, he does not concern himself with training him. How then about the love of the Creator for us? If a father enters the house and finds in its courtyard a number of children playing cards, with his own son among them, he becomes angry at the son; but if he enters and finds the neighbours' children playing cards, he may not even pay attention to them. So when afflictions befall the Muslims that the hypocrites and disbelievers regard as a calamity and rejoice in, this is from their foolishness, because everything Allah decrees is for the benefit of those who believe in Him, whether as discipline, or as reward, or as elevation in life. Therefore it is good (khayr),[2] and from here came the noble verse: ﴿Say: Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed for us.﴾ And what Allah decrees for the believers is indeed for their benefit.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted, further affirms the meaning, saying, glorified is He: ﴿He is our Protector (mawlānā)﴾. Since the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who manages the affairs of the believers and is their helper, the supreme Protector does not harm one who has taken Him as ally. Then the explanation comes complete in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, because the God in whom you believe is capable and wise. So if matters befall you, examine them: if they are the result of your own actions, then you must blame yourself; but if they are among the things Allah brings upon you, then you must understand that they happen for a wisdom.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, may give the disbeliever the means of his livelihood, but He gives the believer the means of his life, both material and moral. With this understanding we know that if something befalls us that we dislike, this does not mean that Allah has abandoned us; rather He wishes to discipline us or to draw our attention to something, for if He did not discipline us or draw our attention, He would indeed have abandoned us.

And when the believer errs, the Truth, glorified and exalted, draws his attention to his error, and in this case the believer knows that Allah has not left him; therefore let no one say: "Allah has abandoned us," for this is weakness of faith and consequently weakness of reliance (tawakkul). Rather say: when Allah disciplines you, He does not abandon you; so at the moment an affliction comes, know that He is still your Protector. And since your Protector holds you accountable for any error and corrects it for you, trust in Him, glorified is He, and rely upon Him.

By way of example: suppose a person relied on you in some matter, and then you erred in that matter; he must come to alert you to what you erred in and suggest to you a means of correcting the error, and in this case you will find yourself filled with trust in this person. So what of Allah, glorified and exalted, when we rely upon Him and He corrects for us every matter?

But beware lest you transfer reliance from the hearts to the limbs. Therefore it is said: "The limbs work and the heart relies." You plough the land, place the seeds in it and water it; this is the work of the limbs, which you must perform. After that you rely upon Allah and hope for an abundant harvest that the crop will produce, so that no blight or weather phenomenon, such as heavy rain or a fierce wind, comes and ruins all that you have done. After perfecting your knowledge, your supplication to Allah, glorified and exalted, comes that He preserve for you the product of your work.

As for those who do not work with their limbs and yet declare that they rely upon Allah, we say to them: you are liars; for reliance is not the work of the limbs but the work of the hearts. The limbs work and the hearts rely.

But upon whom do we rely? When you rely upon the Living One who does not die, your work will not be lost; but if you rely upon a human being like yourself, even if he is powerful, his strength may turn into weakness, he may come to hate you or humiliate you, or a calamity may befall him and he may die.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, instructs His Messenger to answer those who rejoice at the afflictions of the Muslims, to reveal to them that their joy at the calamity is the joy of fools. Then comes His saying, the Truth:

﴿Say: Do you await for us except one of the two best outcomes, while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Himself or at our hands? So wait; indeed, we are waiting with you.﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:52)

[1] Ḥafīzah: anger and rancour.
[2] From Ṣuhayb al-Rūmī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Indeed all of his affairs are good, and this is so for no one except the believer: if prosperity reaches him, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if adversity reaches him, he is patient, and that is good for him." Recorded by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (2999), Aḥmad in his Musnad (4/332–333), al-Dārimī in his Sunan (2/318), and Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-Awliyā' (1/154).

Al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi)

Commentary on Surah al-Tawbah (9), verse 52

Subhanahu wa ta'ala (Glorified and Exalted is He) addresses with this verse those who grieve when good befalls the believers and rejoice when a calamity strikes them. So the Words of the Truth come to make clear that everything that befalls the believers is for their benefit. Therefore He said: ﴿Nothing will ever happen to us except what Allah has decreed for us﴾. He, glorified is He, did not decree matters against us but for us, and "for us" (lana) denotes ownership: whether as discipline, or as an expiation for sins, or as a turning toward the truth after the deviation of falsehood, and all of that is for our good.

Then He, after that, said: ﴿So wait﴾, meaning: be patient, wait, and watch for your end. As for your end, it is the continuation of punishment in this world and in the Hereafter. The causes of punishment are gathered for you in this world, while the causes of good are withheld from you in the Hereafter. The result of our waiting for you is that we see evil befalling you, and your waiting for us makes you see good coming toward us. Thus the outcome of the comparison will be in our favor.

After Allah has made this clear, a question may occur to the mind of the believer: Does no good deed proceed from these peoples? And does no least good come to them? We know that the Truth, subhanahu wa ta'ala, always rewards even the least good.

We say: The Truth wished to explain decisively the matter of the supreme treachery, which is disbelief, and Allah forbid. He made clear that every disbeliever in Allah, no good deed of his is accepted, because disbelief nullifies any deed. And even if his deeds contain benefit that serves people, the Truth rewards him materially in this world, but for him in the Hereafter there is nothing but the Fire(1). He says:

﴿Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiant people﴾ [9:53].

(1) On the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong a believer in a good deed: he is given for it in this world, and is recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for the good deeds he did for Allah in this world, until when he comes to the Hereafter, he has no good deed for which he is recompensed." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2808) and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/123, 125, 283).

Therefore, the condition for God's acceptance of any deed is that it come after faith in God. As for doing a deed while God is not in your mind, then take your reward from those you had in mind while you were doing it.

For this reason God has struck a parable about the deeds of those who disbelieve, in His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, but he finds God with him, and He pays him in full his account. And God is swift in reckoning.﴾ (An-Nur: 39), and God gives us another parable in His saying, Exalted is He:

{The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the far-reaching error.} (Ibrahim: 18).

And the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, says:

{Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter.} (Ash-Shura: 20).

This explains to us what some scholars found difficult to understand in the saying of the Truth:

{So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.} (Az-Zalzalah: 7-8).

Some scholars asked: Does God repay these disbelievers in the Hereafter or in this world? The matter was obscure to them because the verse is general. We say: The Truth gives the reward in this world to those who work for this world, and He gives in the Hereafter to those who work for this world and the Hereafter while God is in their hearts. Therefore, those who skilfully take the created causes, while attributing lordship to the One who grants it, succeed in their lives. Those who advance worldly in cultivating land, selecting seeds and tending them, God gives them the reward of their work in this world, and He does not diminish any of it. But the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, also says:

{And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.} (Al-Furqan: 23).

This saying clarifies the reward of the Hereafter. Therefore the good that a non-believer does is not rewarded in the Hereafter, because he did it while God was not in his mind. How can he expect a reward from One in whom he did not believe?

God, Glorified is He, rewards those who believe in Him and act for His sake. But whoever disbelieves in God, all his deeds are nullified. This is a natural matter, because as long as you did good while God was not in your mind, do not expect a reward from Him. If you work for humanity, humanity will give you [its regard]; if you work for society, society will give you what it gives: they will make statues for you, name squares and streets after you, establish institutions in your name, and immortality in this world will be realised for you. That is your reward. But if you are a believer in God, hoping for His reward, you will come on the Day of Resurrection to find God's hand extended to you with the good you had sent forward.

The Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, says here: {Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly.} "Taw'" (willingly) is the act you undertake by your own will without being compelled. So how would you not be recompensed for a good deed you did by your own will?

We must distinguish between "ṭaw'" and "ṭā'i'" (obedient), and likewise between this and an act you perform when another compels you and forces you to do it. All acts are either voluntary and by will, or by compulsion. Had the Truth said "spend in obedience" (ṭā'atan), He would not have said {it will not be accepted from you}, because obedience means the submission of a worshipper to the will of the One worshipped. But His saying here, {ṭaw'an}, reveals that what they spend is a matter of their own choice. This was the state of the hypocrites: some of them offered their children for jihad, and some offered part of their wealth; they did this obeying themselves and hiding behind such acts so that their hypocrisy would not be exposed. One of them would advance to the first row of the prayer in the mosque, doing so by his own will, out of fear of his hypocrisy being exposed, not out of obedience to God. So obedience to God is the obedience of a worshipper to the One worshipped; as for such acts when they stem from the self's own choice, they are for display and not for worship.

{Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly.} Is this a command to spend? Or does God want them actually to spend, especially since He will not accept it from them? No, this is not a command to spend; rather it is a threat and a warning. Just as you say to a person, "Be patient," which is not a command to patience but a threat, meaning: "Be patient, and you will see great terror from me." This is like His saying: {Be patient or be not patient...} (At-Tur: 16).

And His saying: {Do what you will...} (Fussilat: 40), meaning: whether you are patient or not, that will not change anything of the recompense you will meet; the matter is the same. Had His saying {Do what you will} been a command, then everyone who did disobedience would be included in obedience, because God commanded him to do what he wills. But this is a command of threat, meaning: do what you will, for you will return to God and He will call you to account for what you have done, and you will not be able to escape from God, Glorified is He.

His saying, {Spend}, is therefore a command of threat, because spending willingly or unwillingly will not benefit you.

The word {unwillingly} (karhan) occurs in the Qur'an in more than one surah: it is in Surat Al 'Imran, Surat An-Nisa', Surat At-Tawbah, Surat Al-Ahqaf, Surat Ar-Ra'd and Surat Fussilat, mentioned as {karhan} with a fatha on the kaf, and some have read it with a damma on the kaf. Some said: "karhan" with fatha and "kurhan" with damma have one meaning. We say to them: No, the meaning is not one. For example, the saying of the Truth, Glorified and Exalted: {His mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship...} (Al-Ahqaf: 15). The "kurh" here is neither for the carrying nor for the delivery, but for the hardship that the pregnant woman suffers during her pregnancy and at birth. No one compelled her to this pregnancy. But some say: pregnancy happens and a woman has no means to choose to conceive or to give birth; no woman says to herself, "I will conceive tonight," because conception happens without her knowing it, through the union of man and woman. A woman cannot choose the hour of conception or the hour of delivery, nor can she say, "I will give birth today" or "I will not give birth today." All of this happens by compulsion, without her choice. Therefore we say to those who claim that "karhan" with fatha and "kurhan" with damma have one meaning: No, because "kurh" with damma is what a person does not want because there is hardship in it, while "karh" with fatha is what involves compulsion from another. Thus "karhan" with fatha differs in meaning from "kurhan" with damma.(2)

The Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, says: {Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will not be accepted from you}, meaning: God will not accept from you what you spend. But what is the difference? The hypocrites used to pay zakat and the Messenger accepted it from them, but he did not accept it as a matter of courtesy, peace be upon him. Every deed is presented and then goes to the Supreme Watcher, the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He. But it happened that one of them, Tha'labah, asked the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, to pray for him to be made rich. When he prayed for him and God gave him abundant provision, he withheld from zakat and tried to evade paying it;(3) then the noble verses were revealed:

{And among them are those who made a covenant with God: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and surely be among the righteous." But when He gave them of His bounty, they withheld with it and turned away, averse. So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke what they promised God and because they used to lie.} (At-Tawbah: 75-77).

When these verses were revealed, Tha'labah came to give zakat to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, but he did not accept it from him. When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, died, Tha'labah came to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, but he did not accept it from him. After Abu Bakr, he came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, but he did not accept it from him. Tha'labah died in the time of Uthman.(4) This is the non-acceptance.

But there were among the hypocrites, in the time of the Messenger, peace be upon him, those who paid zakat and it was accepted from them, yet God did not accept it from them. So every deed may be accepted from its doer, but God, Glorified and Exalted is He, may accept it or may not accept it. Thus the meaning of the verse is: God will not accept from these hypocrites their spending in good, even if it was accepted from them in evil.

Then the Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, gives us the reason for this, saying:

{Indeed, you were a defiantly disobedient people.} As we have said: the word "fasiq" (defiantly disobedient) is derived from "fasaqat al-ruṭabah," meaning the skin separated from the fruit. The shell of the date is created to protect the fruit. We know that the meanings in the legal obligations have been drawn from sensible matters; for this reason you find that religion is a fence that prevents a person from going beyond God's limits and protects him from sin, and when a person separates himself from religion he becomes like a fruit that has separated from its covering.

Whoever drinks wine, commits crimes or fornication is punished for the sin; but if a person is a hypocrite, far from faith in God, his obedience is not accepted. Suppose a person believes in God but is weak before some sin; here we say: one thing does not cancel another, and he has the reward of his faith and the punishment of his sin.

1. From 'Aishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, Ibn Ju'dan used to join the ties of kinship and feed the poor in the Jahiliyyah; would that benefit him?" He said: "It will not benefit him, for he never said one day: 'My Lord, forgive my sin on the Day of Judgement.'" Reported by Muslim in his Sahih (214) and Ahmad in his Musnad (6/93, 120). It was also reported by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/305) by another route from 'Aishah, and he said: "Its isnad is sound, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi affirmed it.
2. Al-Farra' went to this view; he said: "al-kurh is what you compel yourself to, and al-karh is what another compels you to." Transmitted by Ibn Manzur in Lisan al-Arab.
3. Tha'labah ibn Hatib al-Ansari came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of God, pray to God that He grant me wealth." He, peace be upon him, said: "Woe to you, O Tha'labah! Little that you thank for is better than much that you cannot bear." Tha'labah said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, if you pray to God to grant me wealth, I will surely give every person with a right his right." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "O God, grant Tha'labah wealth." The matter gradually progressed until he abandoned the prayer and Friday prayer, then withheld zakat and said: "This is nothing but a poll-tax." After the verse of at-Tawbah (75) was revealed, Tha'labah came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, hoping he would accept his charity, and he said: "God has forbidden me to accept your charity." So Tha'labah began throwing dust on his head. A lengthy report, recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7873) from the hadith of Abu Umamah. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/32): "In it is 'Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani, who is abandoned." See also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi (p. 145).
4. When Uthman became caliph, Tha'labah came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, did not accept it, nor did Abu Bakr nor Umar, and I should accept it?!" So Uthman did not accept it. See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi (145, 146).

Therefore: the "fisq" (transgression, ungodliness) in this noble verse is not departure from obedience in general. Rather, it is a special kind of transgression, because there is a limited transgression, which is that a person departs from mere obligation. But the great transgression is that a person disbelieves in God. For this reason the following noble verse came:

﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, and they do not come to the prayer except while lazy, and they do not spend except while unwilling.﴾

Therefore: transgression is of two kinds: general transgression and specific transgression. Some may say: if you commit a sin, then your prayer and your zakat are sinful; your prayer and your zakat and all your acts of worship do not benefit you.

We say: No. As long as the summit is sound — belief in God and belief in the Messenger (ﷺ) and affirmation of the method — then for every act of worship there is its reward, and for every sin its punishment, because the Truth (al-Haqq), glorified is He, is absolute justice and mercy, and He cannot place all evils in the scale of a human being. Whoever has a good quality will receive its prize and reward, and whoever has an evil quality will receive its punishment.

His saying, the Truth, here: ﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger﴾. This noble statement is the justification (haythiyya) for the judgment that their contributions are not accepted, and in this is a specification of the generality of transgression, which is disbelief, not in the particular sense of transgression. The Truth specified three things that prevented their acceptance: disbelief in God and His Messenger, which is the disbelief of the summit; then their standing for prayer while lazy; then spending with reluctance.

The prevention is understood as a reaction (radd al-fi'l) to what diminishes the act or contradicts it. It is as if a person wants to stand and you make him sit, meaning you have turned the intention to stand back into sitting, which contradicts it; or a person tries to strike another and you block his hand, thereby having prevented the other from being attacked. Thus prevention sometimes applies to the agent and sometimes to the object. When you prevent Zayd from striking, you have prevented the agent; when you prevent the striking from him, you have prevented the object. The whole philosophy of life rests on prevention, which is summed up in action and reaction; you find this in the human being, in time and in place.

If you examine this matter in the human being, you find that his life rests on breathing, food and drink. Breathing is the thing a human cannot patiently stop; if you do not take in the inhalation, your life ends, and if you hold back the exhalation, your life ends. If you prevent air from entering the lungs, the person dies, and if you prevent air from leaving the lungs, the person also dies.

The movement of the whole world is built on action and what opposes it. If a person tries to strike another and you seize his hand, and you tell him: his sons or brothers or family will come and strike you, then he refrains from the act out of fear of the reaction. The whole world cannot live in peace unless there is fear of reaction(1); the strong confronts the strong, and everyone fears the reaction to his aggression against the other. But if the strong confronts the weak, you find the strong destroying the weak.

So too with the whole world: the cosmos is either still or moving. In the moving cosmos you find balanced forces living in peace out of fear of reaction. Likewise in the still world: the towering building derives its stability and stillness from the fact that the wind does not come from one direction but from many directions, which makes the pressure balanced on all sides of the building. But if you empty the air from one side and let it blow from another side, the building would collapse, just as when you empty air from a sealed vessel it shatters.

His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger﴾ does not mean that their tongues did not utter the testimony. No; the hypocrites did testify verbally, but there is a difference between the utterance of the tongue and the affirmation of the heart. Faith has its locus in the heart, and the hypocrites combined a tongue that testifies with a heart that denies. So the Messenger gave them the right of the testimony of the tongue: he did not confront them, did not take them captive, did not kill them, and gave them the same material rights equal to those of the believers, all out of respect for the word "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God" which they uttered. And because their inner state is ugly, the Truth recompenses them according to what is within them, so that they do not take a reward for what they do outwardly while denying it inwardly. Thus dealing with them was logical and appropriate. As long as they showed the outward, God gave them outward rights; and because they did not give a good inward state, God did not give them of His unseen reward or of His unseen paradise, and He punished them with His fire.

We come to the second reason in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and they do not come to the prayer except while lazy﴾. Laziness is slackness in performing a duty. So they pray for show; if they are among the believers and the call to prayer is made, they stand up heavily. If they are where the believers do not see them, they do not perform the prayer. Thus their conduct is full of duplicity and contradiction.

The third reason: ﴿and they do not spend except while unwilling﴾. Spending is giving away from what you have of the surplus that God has granted you, whether that be wealth, action, standing or strength. This is what achieves balance in society, because every society has many circumstances: you find the strong and the weak, the rich and the poor, the knowledgeable and the ignorant, the healthy and the sick. If every person moved in his life only according to his need, the weak, the sick, the incapable and the poor would perish. Rather, every person must work according to his capacity, not according to his need, and must take from the product of his work according to his need and that of his dependents. You take your need from the fruit of your capacity, then you extend to others from God's bounty upon you, especially to those who cannot move in life. The healthy gives the sick from his strength what helps him to live; the wealthy gives the poor from his wealth what helps him to live; the one able to live gives to the one unable. This is the interdependent (mutakaful) society.

Such conduct is for the benefit of all, because the rich today may be poor tomorrow, and the strong today may be weak tomorrow. If a person feels that he lives in an interdependent society, he will not fear events and changes. This is the true insurance for the capable and the wealthy, in which every person feels solidarity and mutual support. The poor is not preoccupied with fear of changing events; if he dies, his dependents will not go hungry; if the wealthy becomes poor, he will find support; if the healthy falls sick, he will find treatment.

Therefore: spending is a necessity for the soundness of society. We find that the market is described as "nafiqa" (brisk, in demand), and in it all goods are sold and bought. Whoever wants to sell, sells; whoever wants to buy, buys; so movement in it is balanced. When you go to the market to sell or to buy, you either take money in exchange for what you sold, or you pay money as the price of what you bought. In earlier times a person bartered one commodity for another. After the invention of money, a person began to buy goods with a price, and whoever spends his money and offers it to God, the Truth gives him every good. God, glorified is He, willed for the hypocrites inward punishment in this world and the punishment visible to all in the Hereafter, and He explained to them that their spending, willingly or unwillingly, will not bring them any good.

But whoever looks at the hypocrites may find that they enjoy wealth and children. The person looking at them does not notice that wealth and children are the instruments of their punishment. Someone may say: God has said:

﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life...﴾ (18:46).

We say to whoever says this: complete the verse:

﴿But the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope﴾ (18:46).

And the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial...﴾ (64:15).

(1) In this regard the Lord of Might, glorified is He, says: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you terrify the enemy of God and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know; God knows them﴾ (8:60).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 55:

Allah addresses the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and within this address is an address to all Muslims. Here the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the worldly life, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.﴾

Beware lest you see any one of these, to whom Allah has given wealth and children, and then say: "How can their punishment be in this world when they possess wealth and children?" Such admiration means approving of wealth and children and assuming that in them lies all good. But if you look deeply at wealth and children, and at all the trappings of this world, you will find that they do not deserve admiration. Beware of being deceived by something that may be taken away, and which may become the cause of your punishment. Wealth and children may cause a person to fix his attention on the blessing and distract him from the Bestower. If a person does not turn his attention to the Bestower, he does not remember Him, and if he does not remember Allah, he neglects His guidance.

Wealth and children in this worldly life may be the causes of a person fearing the loss of this world. If you do not have faith in what is with Allah in the Hereafter, you may fear the loss of wealth and children. Whoever does not believe in the Last Day, for him the world is his whole lifetime; if it escapes him, that is a calamity for him, and if he escapes it, that is a calamity upon him. But if a person believes in Allah and the Last Day, he would say: "If the world escapes me, I have with Allah something better than it." The Truth, glorified is He, wishes to protect those who believe in Him from the trial of blessing that distracts from the Bestower, so He says:

﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you.﴾ The noble verse shows us that wealth alone has an allure, and children alone have an allure. Whoever has wealth is impressed by what he has, and whoever has no wealth but has children is impressed by them too. When the two are combined, the admiration becomes greater and more comprehensive. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants us to understand that the combination of wealth and children must not stir admiration in our souls. Indeed, the context of the verse warns us against being impressed by one who has wealth alone, or one who has children alone. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, repeated the word: ﴿lā﴾ ("not"), saying: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you.﴾

He, glorified is He, has made us understand that when He provides a disbeliever or a hypocrite with wealth and children, that is not an elevation of his station; rather it is to punish him with them in this world and the Hereafter. So He says: ﴿Allah only intends to punish them thereby﴾. The lam in "liyu'adhdhibahum" ("to punish them") is what is called the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). It means that we may perform an act for a specific purpose, but its outcome may be something entirely different from what we intended, and may even be the opposite of what we intended.

When we read the Qur'an, we find the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief... (8)﴾ (al-Qasas).

Did the family of Pharaoh pick up Moses, peace be upon him, so that he would become an enemy to them? Or so that he would be a comfort to their eyes?

They picked him up so that he would be a comfort to their eyes, but what happened was the opposite of what they intended at the moment of picking him up. Instead of Moses becoming a comfort to their eyes, he became an enemy to Pharaoh, and was even the cause of the end of his kingdom. Thus this is the lam of consequence.

Allah, glorified is He, gave some disbelievers wealth and children, and this in its outward appearance is an elevation in this world; but instead of using this blessing to draw near to Allah, they were distracted by it from faith in Allah, and the matter reached the point that the Truth caused them to enter punishment. The Truth did not intend punishment for them, but by their conduct and their trial by wealth and children they deserved to enter punishment. Illegitimate action in increasing wealth or in pleasing children is what brought them to punishment.

﴿Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the worldly life﴾. The first forms of punishment: those blessings distract them from the Bestower, and keep them far from the way of Allah, so that they become in enmity with the believers who follow the way of Allah, and they fear to declare this enmity. Therefore, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent someone to summon one of the hypocrites or Jews, they would tremble and ask (1): "Has the Messenger discovered our matter, or has Allah revealed to him some of our secrets?" They were in fear that their affair would be exposed, so that the Muslims would treat them as polytheists and expel them.

Second: they feared that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, would enter into war; for since they had declared faith, they were obligated to spend wealth and to send their sons who had reached fighting age with the army of the Muslims. They would say among themselves: "Why should we spend wealth and sacrifice our sons in the cause of something we do not believe in?" With those feelings they differ from the feelings of the believers, who answer the call of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) out of desire for Paradise or victory. This is a form of punishment.

Another form of punishment: when these hypocrites go out on one of the military expeditions, they fear for themselves death, harm by capture, or the taking of women as captives, so they live in psychological torment throughout the journey to the expedition and during the war.

A third form of punishment: a person who gathers wealth from both unlawful and lawful sources, not caring where the wealth came from but only that it comes. The one who earns lawfully moves openly in life, while the one who earns unlawfully is a thief who fears being exposed before people, and lives in painful, constant torment, fearing that a day will come when Allah uncovers his cover and people learn that he took bribes, or embezzled, or forged and falsified, or did something that debases him in people's eyes or exposes him to punishment, such as having trafficked in narcotics or in people's honor, or in other things. His fear of his affair being exposed makes him live in constant torment and continuous conflict.

If we want to know the difference between the lawful and the unlawful, let us give this example: if something in your neighbour's house pleases you and you ask him for it, and he gives it to you, you do not fear that people will know what happened. But if something in your neighbour's house pleases you and you want to steal it, you do not come in the daytime or in front of people; rather you come at night and take care that no one sees you. You do not enter through the apartment door, but keep circling and planning to find an opening by which to enter without anyone seeing you. You make a plan for the theft, and you enter the house on tiptoe, trembling. If while carrying out the plan you hear the sound of footsteps, you are alarmed and run to hide, take the thing, and are anxious to conceal it, and if anyone sees it with you, you are disturbed. All of this is torment that everyone who gathers unlawful wealth goes through. Therefore, gathering unlawful wealth is torment.

Whoever raises his children on unlawful wealth, Allah does not bless him in them. Either one of them grows up as a torment to his father in his upbringing, failing his examinations, and squandering the money in spending without awareness; the more you give him, the more he needs. Such a son does not obey his father, and the greatest torment comes when one of this man's sons grows up a sincere believer in Allah, and refuses to eat or wear from his father's wealth, or to question him about where this wealth came from, and hears from him what he dislikes, and constantly rebels against him.

In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu 'Amir was an enemy of Allah and His Messenger. His son Handhalah (2) was a believer. When Abu 'Amir saw his son, his heart boiled with rage. When the call to fight was made, Handhalah heard the call to jihad after he had been startled from enjoying his wife (3), and he did not wait to perform the ritual bath from major impurity, but hastened to war with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and was martyred in the battle. But how did the Companions learn the story of Handhalah, though this matter is a secret between a man and his wife that no one knows? The believers learned the news of Handhalah when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by the illuminations of Allah, saw that the angels were descending from the sky and washing Handhalah. Since the martyr is not washed (4), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew that this was not a washing for martyrdom, but a washing so that the martyr would not meet Allah while in a state of major impurity. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw what had happened to Handhalah, and when he returned to Madinah he sent for Handhalah's wife and asked her: "What happened at the time Handhalah went out to the battle?" She said: "When he heard the call to fighting, he went out without washing (5)." Reflect on how the angels descended to wash a martyr who was the son of an enemy of Allah and His Messenger, and how this must have been a rage in the father's heart.

Another story: Sayyidina 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy. His father 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy was the leader of the hypocrites in Madinah, and he is the one who withdrew on the day of Uhud with a third of the fighters from the battle (6). 'Abdullah heard that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were asking him for permission to kill his father Ibn Ubayy. Look at the faith: the son went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you are ordering the killing of my father, then order me to kill him, so that I do not meet his killer among the Muslims while there is rancour against him in my heart (7)." When the father hears that his son asks to be his killer, is that not torment in his heart? Thus we see that wealth and children, which were meant to be a blessing, become a calamity. Is this not torment in the world?

But those who do not believe do not turn their attention to the Giver of blessing, nor to the reward that awaits them in the Hereafter, nor do they heed the wisdom of creation, which affirms that man is the vicegerent of Allah on earth, and that Allah has prepared the earth with all that is in it of capabilities and good things to be in the service of this vicegerent. That is: he has been given a complete world of everything, prepared for him beyond his capacities and powers.

Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says in a sacred hadith: "I created things for your sake, and I created you for My sake, so do not occupy yourself with what is yours from what you are for."

That is: do not busy yourself with the blessing so as to neglect the Bestower. Just as a person enters a great banquet, finds the table prepared with every kind of food, and the host is standing, yet he neither greets him nor salutes him, but goes straight to the food, so people feel that this man is ungrateful for the generosity of the hospitality. Whereas another man enters, greets the host of the banquet, thanks him for his generosity and praises him. The first was occupied with the blessing; the second, his occupation with the blessing did not make him forget to thank the one who prepared it for him.

Another example: health is among the most precious blessings. As for illness, it is the harshest thing a person can suffer, because health is what allows a person to enjoy the blessings of life, while illness deprives him of these blessings. Therefore, when a person falls ill, Allah compensates him: instead of being in the company of the blessing, he is in the company of the Bestower, who is Allah, glorified is He. Therefore He says in a sacred hadith:

"My servant so-and-so fell ill, and you did not visit him." He says: "O Lord, how can I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He says: "Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him? (8)"

Tell me, by Allah: does any sick person feel constricted when he knows that health was a blessing from Allah and has parted from him, while illness has brought him into the company of the Bestower, who is Allah, glorified and exalted? No. Rather that eases the severity of the illness, and his intimacy with Allah lightens his pains. But you unfortunately find a person who is not logical with himself: the world was created for the sake of man, and man was created to worship Allah, yet you find him not attentive to what he was created for, but attentive to the things that were created for him. It would have been logical for him to be occupied with what he was created for.

If we take as an example man's relation to time, we find that time is either present, past, or future. If we want to go to the limitless, we say: time is present, eternal, and everlasting. The eternal (al-azali) is that which is ancient without beginning; the everlasting (al-abad) is the future without end; and the present is what we live in.

The existence you see before you was created by the Truth, glorified is He, the Necessarily Existent (wajib al-wujud), and by the word "Be!" came every "contingent existence" (mumkin al-wujud); because every existence that needs an originator is a contingent existence, and non-existence will come to it. As for the existence that does not need an originator, it is an existence that does not end; that is, the Necessarily Existent is the existence of Allah alone, glorified is He, and...

1 The Exalted said: ﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah may be sent down about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say: "Mock, for Allah will bring out what you fear."﴾ (al-Tawbah: 64). Mujahid said: they say the saying among themselves, then they say: "Perhaps Allah will not disclose our secret." Al-Hasan said: the Muslims used to call this surah "al-Haffarah" (the Digger), because it dug up what was in the hearts of the hypocrites and brought it out. See Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/366) and al-Qurtubi (4/3121).
2 He is Handhalah ibn al-Rahib, 'Abd 'Amr ibn Sayfi al-Awsi, and the kunya of his father was Abu 'Amir. Handhalah was among the People of the Suffah.
3 It is mentioned in al-Hakim's Mustadrak (2/204) that this was his first night with his wife, and he left a child in her womb who was born in the year 4 AH, named 'Abdullah, who became one of the notable Successors and their brave men. The people of Madinah appointed him over their affairs, and he fought the army of Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah fiercely until he was killed in the year 63 AH. See al-A'lam of al-Zirikli (4/99).
4 From Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said about the martyrs of Uhud: "I am a witness over these on the Day of Resurrection." And he ordered them to be buried in their blood, and they were not washed, nor was the funeral prayer performed over them... Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1343), Abu Dawud (3138), al-Tirmidhi (1036), Ibn Majah (1514) and al-Nasa'i (4/62) in their Sunan. Ahmad also narrated in his Musnad from Jabir (3/299): "Do not wash them, for every wound or every blood will emit musk on the Day of Resurrection," and the funeral prayer was not performed over them.
5 Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in Hilyat al-Awliya' (1/357), al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3/204) who declared it sahih, and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/247) and al-Bayhaqi in his al-Sunan al-Kubra (4/15), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your companion, meaning Handhalah, the angels have washed him; ask his family about his condition." His wife was asked and she said: "He went out while in a state of major impurity when he heard the caller's cry." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For that reason the angels washed him."
6 Ibn Ishaq said: when they reached al-Shawt, between Madinah and Uhud, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul withdrew from him with a third of the people and said: "He obeyed them and disobeyed me" (meaning Muhammad, ﷺ), "we do not know why we should kill ourselves here, O people." So he returned with those of his people who followed him from the hypocrites and doubters. See Ibn Hisham's Sirat al-Nabi (3/8).
7 Cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir of the verse ﴿They say, "If we return to Madinah, the more honourable will surely expel therefrom the more humble"﴾ (al-Munafiqun: 8), with similar wording, attributing it to Ibn Ishaq.
8 Muslim narrated in his Sahih (2569) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me.' He says: 'O Lord, how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds?' He says: 'Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him?'" The hadith.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are afraid.﴾

Why did Allah bring this verse after warning us not to be impressed by the wealth and children of the hypocrites? Because these things are not a blessing for them but a punishment upon them. Allah, glorified and exalted, wanted to rouse us against the hypocrites and make us wary of them with the utmost caution, and He sets for us the example of the oath. A person does not usually utter an oath except after a suspicion of denial. If you bring a person a report and he believes you, you are not obliged to swear to him.

But if he denies it, you swear to remove the suspicion of denial from him. Therefore, when you first relate the report you do not swear; if your listener denies it, you swear.

But why do the hypocrites swear without any prior denial?

They hear the Qur'an descending from the heavens filled with anger against them, and they feel in the depths of their hearts that every Muslim harbors doubt about their conduct. So their speech begins with an oath, so that the believers may believe them (1). The believers, however, have been granted by Allah an immunity of faith in their hearts, so they do not believe what the hypocrites say, so that they may take their precaution and be safe from the harm that these hypocrites plot. For this reason Allah, glorified and exalted, warned the believers against believing the words of the hypocrites, even if they swear.

Had Allah not granted the believers this immunity of faith, they would have believed the hypocrites' words out of the sanctity of the oath. And by what did the hypocrites swear? They swore that they are of the believers, while in reality, in outward legislative practice, they act as the believers act, but their hearts contain no certainty or sincerity.

And since they are without certainty and sincerity, why do they swear? We say: this is the self-contradiction (tanaqud al-dhat), and you find that the believer is not self-contradictory, because he is a believer in his heart, a believer in his essence, and a believer in his limbs, and there are no faculties in him that contradict one another. The disbelieber too is not self-contradictory, because he openly declares that he does not believe in Allah or His Messenger, so there is no contradiction between his outward and his inner state. It is true that he has one faculty, but it is corrupt; yet there is no contradiction in him between what he outwardly does and what is in his heart.

As for the hypocrite, his faculties contradict one another. He says with his tongue: "I am a believer, and I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." But his heart contradicts what he says, so he does not testify to the oneness of Divinity for Allah, nor does he affirm the message of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted, says in Surat al-Munafiqun:

{When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are surely the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are surely His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are surely liars (1)} (al-Munafiqun).

How does the Truth, glorified and exalted, say "Indeed the hypocrites are surely liars," when they testified to what Allah testified, namely that Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the Messenger of Allah? We say: the Truth wanted to expose them, for they testified only with their tongues, while their hearts denied it. Allah exposed what was in their hearts and made clear that their tongues lie, because they do not convey the truth of what is in their hearts.

Thus, the hypocrite lives in self-contradiction, and he is worse than the disbeliever, because the disbeliever openly declares his enmity toward the religion; he is a manifest enemy, so you take your precaution against him. As for the hypocrite, he pretends to faith, so you feel secure with him, and his harm is greater and his capacity for treachery is more severe. For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted, said:

{Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire.... (145)} (al-Nisa').

We know that self-contradiction is what wearies the whole world, and al-Mutanabbi explains this matter and shows how it is the most exhausting thing in existence, saying:

"Among the miseries of the world for the free man is that he sees an enemy whom he must befriend, from whose friendship there is no escape."

This is the contradiction of faculties when you find an enemy of yours, and circumstances compel you to be his friend. And in this another poet says:

"We spent the night together in blame, while our state, from fear, is the state of those gathered in praise."

And a third poet, wishing to depict the contradiction in society that makes people extol one whom they detest, says:

"Our humiliation from the contradiction of our selves is enough for us; when will words be true with tongues of fear?"

So the hypocrites swear with their tongues that they are of the believers, and they are so in outward legislative practice, but in their reality they are not of you; in their hearts they are not of you.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, completes the picture with His saying:

﴿And they swear that they are surely of you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are afraid.﴾ The word "farq" means fear, that is, they are in constant alarm, fearing that their affair will be exposed, so that the community of Islam will isolate them and fight them as it fights the disbelievers, drive them out, seize their wealth, and take captive their women and children. Therefore, fear is what made them swear falsely and out of dread of their affair being exposed; and for this reason the Truth said to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concerning them:

﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have recognized them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech... (30)﴾ (Muhammad).

In this statement there is a call to scrutinize what the people of hypocrisy say, even if their speech appears beautiful upon their tongues (2).

1 On this the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and have averted [people] from the way of Allah; indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ (al-Munafiqun: 2). Junnah: meaning a protection.

2 On this the Exalted says concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ (al-Munafiqun: 4). Al-Kalbi said: the intended ones are Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Jadd ibn Qays and Mu'tib ibn Qushayr; they had fine bodies, appearance and eloquence. As for the "tone of speech" mentioned in the verse of Surat Muhammad, meaning: you will know them, O Muhammad, in the sense, import, and implication of the words, which is not apparent.

Then the Truth, exalted is He, says:

﴿If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn towards it, rushing headlong.﴾

Al-Malja’ (refuge) is that to which one resorts to protect oneself from harm, such as fortresses; and likewise al-maghara (cave), which is a cavern in the mountain. Al-mudkhal (place of entry) is something resembling a tunnel beneath the earth, which one enters with difficulty and twisting. So there are three kinds of refuge to which they would flee if they found them during the battle, because they say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. They wish to go to a far-off place in order to revile Islam away from the Muslims, in the midst of the hardship of fighting, and they cannot do that in front of the Muslims; therefore you find them in a state of searching for a place where no one can hear them.

﴿If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn towards it while rushing headlong.﴾ The discourse, then, is about the hypocrites whose characteristics the Truth has mentioned, their covenants which they broke, their oaths of falsehood, and the inner contradiction each of them lives with, a contradiction that bequeaths wretchedness, because each one of them shows something other than what he conceals and fears that his condition will be exposed. So he remains agitated, because what is within him contradicts the reality of his life.

This state is the opposite of the state of the believer, who lives a harmonious life, because what is in his heart is what his tongue expresses, in addition to his harmony through faith with the universe in which he lives. Likewise, the state of the hypocrite differs from the state of the disbeliever: the disbeliever has openly declared the disbelief that is in his heart with his tongue. As for the hypocrite, he has a heart that disbelieves and a tongue that utters faith falsely. Therefore he is in constant weariness, fearing that his condition will be revealed, or that the believers will come to know what is in his heart, because he harbours hatred for the method of God even though he openly professes love.

When a person is compelled to praise one who opposes him and to feign love for him, this conduct represents a terrible psychological burden that he carries on his back. Thus we see that the hypocrites exhaust themselves before they exhaust society, just like the miserly man who pretends to be generous: each time he spends a piastre to confirm this pretence, that piastre slaughters him inwardly and causes him terrible pain. For a person to be at peace with the world, he must first be at peace with himself and in harmony with himself.

Hence we find the hypocrites, when they want to pour out what is in their breasts, seclude themselves with one another, far from the eyes and ears of the Muslims, to display the hatred, rancour and aversion to this religion that is in their souls. They seek a refuge in which they will be safe, or a cave in the mountain far from people so that no one hears them, or a place of entry, which is the narrow spot one can enter only with difficulty. They seek, then, a place where they will be hidden from the hearing and sight of the believers, so that they may release the hatred locked in their breasts. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn towards it, rushing headlong.﴾ "Wallaw" means they set off towards it, their haste to reach the place occupying them from anything else. "Yajmahun" (rushing headlong): jimah is when you lose control over the horse you are riding, so you cannot restrain its charge or direct it; it then bolts swiftly. When this is said of a human being, it means setting off quickly toward the place he intends, which no one can prevent; and if anyone confronts him, he pushes them away so that he may dash off swiftly.

The verse here gives us an exact picture of the state of the hypocrites in any battle. At the mere beginning of fighting, you find them not turning towards war, nor towards close combat with the enemy (1), nor seeking martyrdom; rather, at this very moment when the fighting begins, they search for a safe place to flee to, or a cave in which to hide, or an opening in the earth into which they squeeze with difficulty to shield themselves from combat. When the battle ends, they come out to join the ranks of the Muslims, for they do not truly believe. How could they fight in the cause of a religion they do not believe in? Therefore, you would find them in Medina, when a call to jihad was made, the first to try to flee, and they would go to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking exemption from the battle, and one of them would say: ﴿Grant me leave and do not tempt me...﴾ (al-Tawba, 49).

(1) Munazala: the combat of horsemen while mounted on their steeds, without dismounting to the ground.
(2) He was Jadd ibn Qays, and his case has already been discussed in the commentary on the aforementioned verse.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 58:

Regarding the alms (sadaqah), they try to cast doubt on the distribution of alms and how it is carried out. The Almighty says about them: ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are satisfied; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry.﴾ (58)

When they sit together with one another, you find them trying to disparage the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with the aim of harming him and defaming him, and the Almighty says about them:

﴿And among them are those who abuse the Prophet and say, "He is all ear." Say, "An ear of good for you, who believes in Allah and believes the believers and is a mercy to those of you who have believed. And those who abuse the Messenger of Allah will have a painful punishment."﴾ (61) (At-Tawbah).

These are some of the attributes of the hypocrites, by which Allah exposes them by revealing them to the believers. The Almighty has brought us further disclosure of their vices and disgraceful conduct. So He said about them:

﴿Among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are satisfied; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry.﴾ (58) (At-Tawbah). We all also read the saying of Allah the Almighty:

﴿Woe to every scorer and mocker (1).﴾ (Al-Humazah). So what is al-hamz and what is al-lumaz? "Al-hamz" is one who finds fault with others in a hidden way and mocks them secretly, and this happens by a gesture of his eye or by any movement of his limbs. An example of this: when there is a group of people sitting, and one of them tries to disparage one of those present in secret, winking with the corner of his eye at another person, or whispering with the tongue into a person's ear, or by any other means. The important thing is that the fault is pointed out in a hidden manner that most of those present do not notice.

As for "al-lumaz", they are those who find fault with others in their presence. There is the strong one who exposes faults boldly and openly, and he is the lammaz (one who finds fault openly); and as for the weak one, he finds fault secretly, and he is the hammaz (one who finds fault secretly). And lumazah is applied to one who finds fault a great deal in people.

And hummazah lummazah is from the intensive pattern "fu'alah" (fa'alah), which indicates the frequency of doing a thing. So you say "fulan akulah" (with a damma on the alif), meaning: he eats a lot. And "fulan dahkah" (with a damma on the dad), meaning: he laughs a lot.
