As for the saying of the Truth about the abiding of the hypocrites in the Fire: ﴿it is sufficient for them﴾, meaning it suffices them—as when there is a wicked person and you want to discipline him, you say: "This is enough for him," meaning this suffices him, to achieve the required discipline. Likewise the Fire: He, glorified and exalted is He, wishes to draw our attention to the fact that it suffices them, that is, what they will suffer therein of pain and punishment is quite sufficient to requite them for the evil deeds they committed.

Then the Truth says: ﴿And Allah has cursed them﴾, meaning He has expelled them from His mercy and from His obedience, so no repentance or return is accepted from them, because the place of repentance is this world. As for what follows death and the Hereafter, there is no place therein for repentance or turning back from disobedience, because the time for that has ended. Therefore the punishment for whoever did not repent in this world is a lasting punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿And for them is a lasting punishment﴾. The Truth has described the punishment of Hell once as a painful punishment, once as a humiliating punishment, and once as a lasting punishment, wishing us to know that all kinds of punishment will befall the people of Hell. If a person is proud and possesses dignity that bears severe pain without showing what he suffers, the punishment will not be only painful but also humiliating; humiliation is the pain of the soul. If he is proud and stubborn, he is dragged upon his face and humiliated. Some people may bear physical pain but cannot bear humiliation, which inflicts a psychological torment greater than the physical; a leader of a people may be insulted before his followers, or a father humiliated before his children, and this is more painful to his soul than being beaten.

The saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿a lasting punishment﴾ means a constant punishment. If it is painful, the pain remains at its intensity and is never reduced; if it is humiliating, the humiliation continues and never ceases. In both cases it is a punishment in which there is permanence and continuance.

1 Abiding in Paradise forever is mentioned in 8 places in the Noble Qur'an (al-Nisa': 122, 57; al-Ma'idah: 119; al-Tawbah: 100, 72; al-Taghabun: 9; al-Talaq: 11; al-Bayyinah: 8).

2 Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2/460): "This is what many of the scholars, ancient and modern, hold regarding the interpretation of this noble verse." Imam Abu Yahya al-Ansari added a beautiful meaning in his book "Fath al-Rahman bi-Kashf ma Yaltabis fi al-Qur'an," p. 195, saying: "It is an exception from the eternity of the punishment of the people of the Fire and from the eternity of the bliss of the people of Paradise, because the people of the Fire do not abide forever in punishment alone, but are punished with the zamhareer (bitter cold) and with other kinds of punishment, and with what is more severe than that, which is the wrath of Allah upon them; and the people of Paradise do not abide forever in bliss alone, but are blessed with the good pleasure (of Allah), and with gazing upon His Noble Face, and other things."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 9, verse 69:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, addresses the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and says, majestic and exalted is He, to those who depart from His method:

﴿Like those before you, who were mightier than you in strength and greater in wealth and children. They enjoyed their share, so you enjoyed your share, as those before you enjoyed their share, and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged. Those are whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers.﴾ (9:69)

Here He reminds them, glory be to Him, of the processions of disbelief that accompanied the earlier messengers. Those processions included hypocrites and disbelievers, and when He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, sends a messenger, He supports him against the enemies of the method of good.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, wants us to remember what happened to the earlier nations, who were stronger than, and had more wealth and children than, those disbelievers and hypocrites who confronted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Let us recite the saying of the Truth, majestic is His majesty:

{By the dawn, and by ten nights, and by the even and the odd, and by the night when it passes. Is there in that an oath for one of intellect? Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the land, and Thamud who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh, owner of the stakes, who transgressed in the lands and caused much corruption therein? So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment. Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation.} (al-Fajr 89:1–14)

We witness "Iram of the pillars," which the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, described with His saying: "the like of which was not created in the lands." But the Qur'an has confirmed for us that it reached a level of civilization that no one else reached. Some people may ask: where is "Iram of the pillars" among today's civilizations? We say: Allah has secrets in His creation which He has given to some of His creatures and has not given to anyone until now.

If we look at the Pharaohs, for example, we find that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, described them in the Qur'an with His saying: "Pharaoh, owner of the stakes." The pyramids are stakes, and the obelisks are stakes, and the sciences of the Pharaonic civilization still remain hidden from mankind until now. There are among the manifestations of this civilization things we are still unable to explain, such as the secret of mummification and the building of the pyramids. These huge stone blocks were raised and held together without any fixing materials, and modern science is still unable, until today, to build a pyramid in the same way as the ancient Egyptians did without using any fixing materials. Yet these Pharaohs could not dominate the universe despite their strength and their civilization. Rather, God seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, and the sands came and buried their civilization. Then God willed for us to uncover a small part of it, and behold, this small part dazzled the whole world. And behold, the whole world comes to witness the civilization of the Pharaohs and marvels at this art and this advancement in knowledge. If this is the civilization of the family of Pharaoh, then what about the civilization of "Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the lands"?

Thus we know that part of the civilization of "Iram of the pillars" is still hidden until now, and no one knows anything about it, buried in the depths of the earth. Perhaps Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, has preserved it to uncover it in a future time in which people's distance from religion increases, because man, the more he advances in civilization, the further he moves from faith, due to his feeling that he is empowered in the universe and in control of it. At that time perhaps the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, will reveal the civilization of "Iram of the pillars." We say to him: it is in the valley of al-Ahqaf(1), and a single gust of wind in this valley can conceal an entire caravan. That is, if a wind blows, the sand does not cover the road alone, but covers the whole caravan. How many sandstorms have blown over the place that "Iram of the pillars" inhabited and hidden their civilization? There must then be excavations at a very great depth to find that civilization, because we know and see that all archaeological discoveries require digging, since sand accumulates over antiquities. Indeed, we see old houses in villages; one must descend a step or two to enter them through the door, because natural factors, paving, and other things raise the level of the ground. If this is the work of ordinary winds over a short time, what about hurricanes over long ages?

And if you travel and close the windows of your home tightly, and return after one month, you find the furniture covered with a layer of dust; if you are absent a year, you find a thick quantity of dust. This is for a house tightly closed; what about a civilization exposed to all these natural phenomena, covered every month with a new thick layer of dust?

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: "they were mightier than you in strength." That is, their civilization was greater than ours, because the more advanced a civilization, the stronger the nation; and whenever a people falls behind civilizationally, it becomes weak.

So: those before us were more civilized and had more wealth and children. And someone may ask: how could they have had many children when the world increases in number every year, and how could there be abundant wealth when we are discovering the treasures of the earth generation after generation? We say: do not take "abundance" as numerical abundance, but take it in proportion. For if you bring a hundred people and place them in a room, they are called "many." But if you take each one of them and place him in a place far from the others, the number becomes small. And the world in the past was inhabited in limited places, as evidenced by the fact that we discovered continents and places that no one knew.

So: abundance here is relative to the space, and in their space in which they lived they were many; and in wealth, it was in their hands with their limited number, they were more wealthy than you with your large number; that is, the share of the individual was greater, and likewise the children.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, says: "they enjoyed their share (fa-istamtaʿū bi-khalāqihim)." Al-khalāq (خلاق) is the portion or lot that reaches a person from any blessing. He, glory be to Him, says:

{Among the people is one who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he has no share (khalāq) in the Hereafter.} (al-Baqarah 2:200)

That is: he has no share in the Hereafter of the blessings of God. Those who worked for this world alone and did not have God in mind, the justice of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, refuses to waste the result of their work on them, and therefore He gives it to them in this world. But whoever works with God in mind, God gives him from this world and fulfills his reward in the Hereafter.

Therefore we find some believers asking: how can the disbelievers be better off than the believers in material civilization, and why do the disbelievers take from the good things of the earth what suffices them and more, to the point that in some countries they throw the surplus into the sea, while we find Muslims living in a limited material civilization and importing what they eat?

Let us remember the clear truth which I always repeat to every Muslim: beware that there should be lost to you that there is "the giving of the Lord" and "the giving of the Deity." The giving of the Lord is for everyone, because the Lord is the One who created and nurtured, and supplied us with sustenance, and He, glory be to Him, is not the Lord of the believer only, but the Lord of the believer and the disbeliever. Therefore, whoever, believer or disbeliever, takes the means, God gives him; the earth gives abundant produce to whoever cultivates it well, selects its seeds and tends it, without distinguishing between believer and disbeliever; and the universe gives its treasures to whoever searches for them and strives, with no difference between believer and disbeliever. This is the giving of lordship.

As for the giving of deity, God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, has singled it out for His believing servants who follow His method. This is the giving of worship, by which a person is recompensed in the Hereafter. Whoever receives this giving is the happy one: he receives the giving of lordship, so he exploits the means of life and God gives him the good of this world; and he receives the giving of deity by making his life conform to the method of God, so God gives him bliss in the Hereafter.

The means in this world do not distinguish between believer and disbeliever: the sun shines on the believer and the disbeliever, and the rain falls on the obedient and the disobedient, because this is the giving of lordship. Whoever uses it well is given, regardless of obedience or disobedience.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, says:

{And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.} (al-Furqan 25:23)

Why? Because you worked for this world alone... and you were working so that it would be said that you are an inventor or a discoverer... or to obtain wealth or medals... or influence and status in this world, but you were not working with God in mind.

And some people come and say to you: is the one who discovered a cure for a microbe that was destroying mankind, or who discovered electricity, or discovered something that made all humanity happy, would he be a disbeliever and be punished in the Fire?

We say to him: yes, because he did this without having God in mind... Rather he did it with the acquisition of glory or wealth or influence on earth in mind. Therefore God gave him what he worked for, so he had enormous wealth and a history studied in schools, and they gave him medals and named streets and squares after him.

Since he worked for this world, God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, gives him his reward in this world. But the one who worked with God in mind takes from this world through the means, yet he takes in the Hereafter directly from the Causer. Man has advanced in civilization, so that now in some advanced countries you press a button that gives you coffee or tea, and another gives you food... We say: all this is the enjoyment of means. Before you press this button, there were people who prepared the coffee or food for you, and the machine delivered it to you.

But however much man advances in technology, there will never come a day when you think of a thing and find it before you... whereas in Paradise, as soon as a thing occurs to your mind, you find it before you(2), because the giving of this world is the giving of means, and the giving of the Hereafter is the giving of the Causer.

So God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, gave us choice and means in this world, but in the Hereafter He brings to you without work, differing in its taste and fragrance from this world.

So: whoever works with only means in mind is given in this world, and whoever works with the Creator of means in mind is given in both lives. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, said:

{And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, but he finds God with him...} (al-Nur 24:39)

Like the mirage that you walk towards imagining it is water, but when you reach it you find nothing, so is the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection: he is surprised that God exists, the God whom he did not believe in, and he asks God for reward, and it is said to him: your reward is from the one for whom you worked.

And since you did not work for God, there is no reward for you in the Hereafter, because it is God who recompenses in the Hereafter.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: {so enjoy your share, as you enjoyed your share, as those before you enjoyed their share.} That is: they took their share of this world, but in the Hereafter they have no share, because the share in the Hereafter comes with "do" and "do not do." If you do both, you rise. The proof is that the civilization of the Muslims lasted a thousand years when they took the means and did not forget the Causer... rather they guarded the means with the values of the Causer in "do" and "do not do," and so they possessed the world for a thousand years. No civilization has lasted such a period. And even if civilization has vanished from the nations of Islam politically, their religion remains in their souls, and no civilization has lived its principles after the civilization has vanished except Islam. It remains a guiding beacon, despite the political weakness of the Muslims.

And the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: {so enjoy, and you enjoyed your share, as those before you enjoyed their share} means: take your share of this world through means, but remember that enjoyment is limited by a time that man does not own, because the lifespan of the individual in this world is by the length of his life in it, not by the lifespan of the world itself, because the world belongs to you and to whoever comes after you. Your lifetime in it has limits whose length you do not know. Is it a month, or a year, or ten years, or a hundred years? So: your life in this world is conjectural and timed, and your work for the means of this world is limited in duration by the measure of your life in this world.

Suppose your life is long and you become among the long-lived, it will surely end.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: {as those before you enjoyed...}

1 al-Ahqaf: a vast desert on the outskirts of the land of Yemen where they used to dwell. Al-Ahqaf in language: what is bent and elongated of sand dunes.

2 This is reported in a hadith from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed you look at the bird in Paradise and you desire it, and it falls before you roasted." Narrated by al-Bazzar (3532 – Kashf al-Astar). In its chain is Hamid ibn 'Ata' al-A'raj. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/414): weak. But al-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan (2/137): abandoned (matruk). So the hadith is weak.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 70:

﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them: the people of Noah, and ʿAd, and Thamud, and the people of Abraham, and the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. It was not Allah who wronged them, but they used to wrong themselves.﴾ (70)

After the Exalted Truth mentioned in the previous verse the general matter in His saying: ﴿as those before you enjoyed their share, so you have enjoyed your share﴾, in this verse He came with the news and the individuals, namely the messengers and those who opposed them, saying: ﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them﴾. Here, when He says ﴿Has there not come to them﴾, there is the interrogative hamza and the negative lam. The hamza negates this negation, meaning: the news of these people has indeed come to them. When a negation is negated in a matter, the intended meaning is the affirmation of the matter. You only ask a rebuking question when you are confident that the answer from the one you ask is "yes". So when you say to a person: "You abandoned me in my ordeal," he replies: "Did I not visit you on such-and-such a day? Did I not give you such-and-such? Did I not do such-and-such with your son?" He is confident that you cannot deny any of this, because it is established with real certainty.

We notice here that the Truth addressed them in the third person, saying ﴿Has there not come to them﴾, and did not say "Has there not come to you", so that He addresses them tenderly and then speaks of them a second time as though they were absent. This is also a further expression of the earnest concern of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in their absence, for he (ﷺ) was keen on their guidance.

﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them﴾. Naba' (news) is important information. We do not call every piece of information "naba'"; we call only important information "naba'". The root of naba' is from nubuwwah (prophethood), and prophethood is clear and manifest, not obscured. Therefore, every important, manifest thing that has occurred is called naba'. In this regard the Exalted Truth says: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news, about which they are in disagreement﴾ (al-Naba'). There is no news greater than the news of the Resurrection.

The Truth has presented the first matter, in which the address was direct, as a general matter, and presented the second, in which He spoke of them in the third person, as a particular matter.

Then the Truth specified the meaning of ﴿those before them﴾: they are the people of Noah, whom Allah drowned by the flood. Whenever the people of Noah passed by him while he was building the ark, they mocked him. In response to those who mocked Noah, the Exalted Truth says: ﴿If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock﴾ (Hud, 38). That is, you who mock Noah (peace be upon him) are ignorant of the unseen, but Allah informed Noah and his people of what would happen. Therefore the real mockery belongs to those who rejected faith and did not act upon what Allah had prepared for them.

Then the Truth mentioned after that ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, who are the people of Shuʿayb, and the overturned cities, that is, the people of Lot. The meaning of al-mu'tafikah is al-munqalib (the overturned). Allah made its high part its low part. The Truth says: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down. Then covered them what covered﴾ (al-Najm, 53-54). That is: they were high, and He brought them down to the abyss. Ifk is turning away from the truth, as they said to Abraham: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful﴾ (al-Ahqaf, 22). That is, to turn us away from them.

What is the story of these prophets and their peoples? The Exalted Truth says:

﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. It was not Allah who wronged them, but they used to wrong themselves.﴾ That is, the messages of heaven came to the people of Noah, the people of Abraham and others, and the message did not come to them merely as a method, but there came to them miracles that establish the truthfulness of the messengers' communication from their Lord. So they have no argument for turning away from the method of heaven or for denying it, because every method is supported by a miracle that establishes the messenger's truthfulness in his message. These messengers followed one another among mankind to guide them to the method of heaven and to clarify for them the path of truth. The multiplicity of messages was at the beginning of creation, because the world was isolated from one another, to the extent that peoples lived on the earth at one time in scattered places, and none of them knew anything of the others. But the world is now connected to itself, so that when an event occurs in one place, we see it by means of satellites within seconds, and perhaps at the same moment it happens, if the event was prearranged. The world saw the first man descend upon the surface of the moon at the very moment he descended.

When the world lived in isolation, each environment had its own kind of disobedience and corruption, so the messenger would come to fight this kind of disobedience and corruption present in a specific environment, and this kind would not exist in another environment.

But after the world became unified, diseases became unified: a disease appears in America, for example, and after a very short time it appears in Europe or in Egypt. Therefore it was necessary that one messenger come, because the diseases had become one, and the matter required a unified treatment. Hence the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a message for all times and all places.

When He says ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, the bayyinat (clear proofs) are that which makes clear to you what the truth is. The miracles that accompanied the heavenly messages made clear and confirmed that the messenger conveys from his Lord, and the miracle was entirely clear so that every people could see it in a way that allowed them to comprehend it. Therefore every messenger came with a sign on which all agreed to be a miracle. You may bring something wondrous, but people do not agree that it is a miracle. When the magic lantern was invented, some people said: it is something wondrous; and some said: it is an optical deception. But the miracles of the messengers must be comprehended by all levels of minds: the learned and the one who has never read a letter in his life are both able to grasp them, because the religion is a religion of natural disposition (fitrah), addressing the greatest minds and most knowledgeable, just as it addresses the mind of the Bedouin who spends his whole life in the desert, knows nothing, has not lived in a civilization, and has studied no science.

Thus, miracles must be clear to all levels, so that no one has an excuse. Therefore the Exalted Truth says: ﴿It was not Allah who wronged them﴾. This is evidence that Allah, the Exalted, holds them accountable according to the measure of their comprehension of the miracle, as though every mind understood and became certain that there was a miracle. Those who received the miracle with disbelief wronged themselves, because after they comprehended the miracle and verified that it was a breach of the laws of the cosmos which none could bring except Allah, the Exalted, nevertheless they rejected faith.

The Truth says of them: ﴿It was not Allah who wronged them, but they used to wrong themselves.﴾ Wronging is that you take a right and transfer it to falsehood. But rights differ: which right is it that you transfer to falsehood? It is the right of the Supreme Being, which must be believed in and worshipped.

And how does a person wrong himself? A person wrongs himself when the self adorns for him a desire so that he commits it, seeking immediate pleasure and depriving himself of lasting bliss. And there is one who wrongs himself by wronging another, such as the false witness (1): one who supports the owner of falsehood against the owner of truth. Whoever bears false witness falls even in the eyes of the one for whom he testified. If he comes to testify before him in a case, he is not accepted and is looked upon with contempt. Whoever asks a person to give false testimony should be struck, because he wants to make him fall in the eyes of people and in the eyes of the one for whom he testified; for when the false witness helps a person against his opponent, everyone looks upon such a witness with contempt.

1. On the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" (three times). They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to parents"—and he was reclining, so he sat up and said—"Beware, and false speech." He kept repeating it until we said: "Would that he had remained silent." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2654) and Muslim (87).

The Almighty then says:

﴿The believing men and the believing women are protectors of one another; they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, they establish prayer and give zakah, and they obey Allah and His Messenger. Those — Allah will have mercy on them. Indeed, Allah is Almighty and Wise.﴾ (9:71)

This verse came after an earlier verse describing the hypocrites, in His saying: ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another...﴾ (9:67).

So it was fitting that the believers, men and women, be set against them, and this is the relation of opposites (munasabat al-did bi al-did), because comparing an opposite to its opposite makes both matters appear together. An example is the words of the poet when he praises:

"The face is like the dawn, and the poetry is like the dark night, black;
Two opposites that have gathered beauty, and the opposite reveals the beauty of its opposite."

After the Almighty had mentioned the disgraceful acts and faults of the hypocrites, and their unreliability in what they swear and their breaking of what they pledge, He willed to create a contrast between them and the believing men and women. But this contrast differs in one thing, for He, glory be to Him, said of the hypocrites:

﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another﴾ and when He spoke of the believers He said:

﴿The believing men and the believing women are protectors of one another﴾. So the hypocrites were described by the Truth as ﴿of one another﴾, meaning that they are all alike, and their conduct is based on imitation and following, so they imitate one another. And since they have founded their belief on evil, they are all evil, and there is none among them who advises them toward good or who turns them back from hypocrisy; rather, they proceed in the current of evil to its furthest extent.

As for the believer, his belief is built on conviction and on good. If evil is found in a believer, his fellow believers, his protectors, keep him away from evil and away from the path of good, because the human soul has many changes, and not every believer follows, in complete commitment, the method of God in everything. Rather, there is a point of weakness in every human soul. If weakness is found in a believer, his protectors among the believers show him his point of weakness, make him see it, and advise him, and he returns from his point of weakness. The believer also alerts and makes others see. Thus we find that in the believing society, each one turns the other back from his point of weakness, and each method advises and admonishes the other, so that the faith of the group may be complete, and whoever falls short in something finds one near him who fills the gap in his conduct.

As for the hypocrites, the Truth describes them as ﴿of one another﴾, meaning that they are all of one kind, so they do not forbid one another from any wrong they commit, and there is no advisor among them.

The saying of the Almighty and Exalted: ﴿The believing men and the believing women are protectors of one another﴾ does not specify to us who is the protector (al-mawla) and who is the protected (al-mawla), so every believer is both a protector and one protected, because wilaya (protection) is derived from "yalihi," meaning he became near, and its opposite is "'adahu," meaning he became distant from him, his believing brother, in the matter in which he is weak.

So if I am weak in some matter, my believing brother supports me in it. And as long as my believing brother supports me in some matter, if he himself becomes weak in something, I support him in it, and we interact and complete one another, and each of us becomes a protector and one protected.

For this reason the Almighty says:

﴿By time. Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ (103:1–3)

Had it said "wa-sau" (advise) it would have meant there are people who advise and people who are advised, but the Truth said "wa-tawasau" (they advise one another), and its meaning is that every believer must advise his believing brother. So if I have a point of weakness, you advise me and say: turn away from this and do not do it, for you are a believer. And if you have a point of weakness, I say to you: do not do this, for you are a believer.

Therefore each of us is both one who advises and one who is advised. Likewise, protection: you are my protector, meaning near to me, supporting me in my weakness, and I am your protector, meaning near to you, supporting you in your weakness, because we are people of changing conditions, and each of us has a point of weakness that differs from the other's point of weakness. Protection is also in the truth: I may incline toward falsehood in some point, and my believing brother says: turn back. And he may incline toward falsehood, and I say to him: turn back. In this way faith is completed. For this reason you find the word "wilaya" in the sense of nearness and support in the saying of the Almighty about Himself:

﴿There, protection belongs to Allah, the Truth...﴾ (18:44), meaning that true support belongs to Allah, because we live in a world of changing conditions. You may seek support from me, and then my strength has gone, or my wealth has been spent, or my authority has ended. But the Almighty and Exalted is alone always strong, always rich, who changes and is not changed, and when Allah supports you, this is true lasting support, not the support of changing things.

And we find the Almighty says:

﴿Unquestionably, the allies of Allah – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ (10:62), meaning that the Almighty made the allies of Allah...

Likewise, He, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Allah is the protector of those who have believed﴾ (2:257).

So the Almighty is sometimes the one who protects, and sometimes the one who is protected. If you take Allah as your protector by obedience, He takes you as His protected by His support. He, exalted, says:

﴿If you support Allah, He will support you and plant your feet firmly﴾ (47:7), meaning: if you draw near to Allah by obeying Him and supporting His method, He will draw near to you in your crises, support you, and make your feet firm.

So protection in its origin is nearness and mutual support, and as long as there is mutual support, there must be a point of weakness in one believer and a point of strength in another. But who will always be in weakness, or always in strength? No one.

So each one supports, and each one is supported.

And since the Almighty said "protectors of one another" without specifying which one, every one is fit to be a supporter and one supported.

But the meaning becomes clear when you read the saying of the Almighty:

﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not revealed upon a man of great importance from the two cities?"﴾ (43:31).

So the disbelievers acknowledged the truth of the Qur'an and its inimitability, but they do not believe, because the Qur'an was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it would not be revealed upon one of the leaders of Quraysh. So Allah, glory be to Him, responded to them:

﴿Is it they who would distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world and raised some of them above others in rank that some may take others in service...﴾ (43:32).

The Almighty willed to make some of you masters and some slaves, and to make some of you rich and some poor, and that is in matters of this world. If you wish to divide matters of religion, then first divide your livelihoods, for the Almighty is the One who divided them among you, and your life in this world follows the laws of causes, and it is easier for you to divide than to come and divide the mercy of Allah, which belongs to Allah alone, glory be to Him.

We notice in the saying of the Almighty: ﴿and raised some of them above others﴾ that one part is raised and another part is raised over. Since the word "some" is indefinite, each of us is both raised and raised over. No one among mankind is raised above all, such that he alone is a complete collection of gifts. Rather, each of us excels in one respect and not in another, so that interdependence in the universe is one of necessity for life and not a matter of favour. For this reason, when a believing person is raised over someone in some matter, he must ask himself: in which things am I raised, and in which things are people better than me?

We say to him: you excel at a particular work, and therefore you are raised in it, but in the rest of things you know nothing, so you are raised over. Thus: what I do not do well is raised over me, and in what I do well I am raised over people. Therefore you find that each person in God's creation is raised at one time and raised over at another. This is the meaning of ﴿and raised some of them above others﴾.

But the calamity is that we look at rank only from one field: this one is rich and that one poor, but we do not look at health, knowledge, children, the righteousness of a wife, blessing in life, and many other angles. And some of us, if he attains a high grade in one angle, may receive zero in another. The total of each person in the end equals the total of any other person, and there is no superiority except through piety. So if you see someone surpassing you in something, beware of envying him, but ask yourself in what field you surpass others, and you will find other fields and angles in which you are better than others.

So each of us is raised and raised over, and we must understand that every person of talent benefits society by his talent, and perhaps his benefit to society is greater than his benefit to himself. Look, for example, at the carpenter: you find him skilled at making doors and windows for people, but for himself he does not perfect them. Why? Because the door he makes for himself is the only door for which he does not charge a fee.

We have given the example of the right hand and the left hand: with most people, the right hand performs tasks easily, while the left does them slowly and clumsily. If you want to trim your fingernails, for instance, you hold the scissors in your right hand and trim the nails of the right hand.

Thus we see that no one enjoys complete talents; rather, he masters one thing and not others, but the total of each person's talents equals the total of any other person's talents.

The divine justice intervenes here: for example, we find the rich man who eats bread of fine white flour, and then a time comes when he can eat only black or coarse flour. And you find one who indulges in food, for whom a time must come when doctors forbid him food, because he has taken from it more than his right. And his health lies in being deprived. The Almighty has established a cosmic order in which all lend support to one another, so that all may be bound together. You need me in what I master, and I need you in what you master. Thus people support one another and a sound society is formed.

For this reason it is said: people are well as long as they differ, for if they did not differ and all became possessors of one talent or one occupation, the universe would be corrupted. Suppose we were all judges, for example: who would treat the patient? Who would dig the earth? Who would carry the bricks? Who would clean the road? If we were alike in talent, wealth, or work, we would not find anyone to do these tasks, for if we were all doctors or engineers or pharmacists or judges or legislators, we could not survive. Rather, we must differ, so that I need you and you need me. Thereby society holds together, and the interests of the universe are served through need, not through favour among people.

The Almighty describes the believers as: ﴿they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾. So if a believer commits a wrong, his brother comes and forbids him from it. And if he does not do a right, his believing brother comes and enjoins him to do it. Each of us forbids wrong, and is forbidden from wrong.

You cannot enjoin what is right while doing its opposite, or while being far from it. It is impossible for a cup of wine to be in your hand and then ask another person with a cup of wine to smash the cup in his hand. Therefore it is impossible to forbid wrong while you are committing it, and the one who enjoins right must be far from it.(1) So every believer is one who enjoins and one who is enjoined to do right, and one who forbids wrong.

The Truth adds a further description of the believers: ﴿they establish prayer and give zakah﴾. Establishing prayer is the declaration of loyalty to the Supreme Creator, the One who has endless permanence. The believers are protectors of one another, but who is the protector of them all? It is Allah, glory be to Him, and we must all be bound to the method of the Supreme Protector, of whom none of us can dispense. When Allah, glory be to Him, described the believers as protectors of one another, He said to us: ﴿If you support Allah, He will support you...﴾ (47:7).

So we must all turn toward the Great Protector.(2) He, glory be to Him, is above our causes and above our strength, and He is the one who supports us if the protection of believing individuals for one another becomes weak, so we turn to the Great Protector. And since protection belongs to the Truth, we must perpetuate our loyalty to Him, glory be to Him. And the perpetuation of loyalty is achieved only through prayer. And when you hear the muezzin say: "Allahu akbar..."

1. On the authority of Usama ibn Zayd, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and thrown into the Fire, and his intestines will spill out, and he will go round with them as a donkey turns around a millstone. The people of the Fire will gather around him and say: O so-and-so, what is wrong with you? Did you not used to enjoin right and forbid wrong? He will say: Yes, I used to enjoin right but would not do it, and forbid wrong but would do it." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3267) and Muslim (2989). Aqtab al-batn: its intestines.

2. Al-Wali (the Protector): one of the names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who is the Owner of all things and the One who disposes of them. Ibn al-Athir said: it seems that wilaya indicates management and the power to act.

Following the verse, there comes a promise to the believing men and women of reward and bliss in the Hereafter. Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. And approval from Allah is greater. That is the great achievement.﴾ (72)

Al-wa'd (promise) is good news of benefit that will come at its appointed time after the speech. Al-wa'id (threat) is a warning of harm that will come after the speech.

The promise encourages the listener to exert his effort and work, until the good that was promised him is realized. The threat gives the listener the opportunity to refrain from what angers Allah, so that he does not incur the punishment of Allah.

However, we notice that the Truthful, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women﴾ and then mentioned the punishment awaiting them. After that He said:

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women﴾ and then described the bliss awaiting them. Although the common usage in the language is that al-wa'd is for good and al-wa'id is for evil, it would have been appropriate by human convention for the Truthful, glorified and exalted, to say: ﴿Allah has threatened (awʿada) the hypocrite men﴾, because what follows is punishment, fire and evil; and to say of the believers: "Allah has promised (waʿada)", because what follows is paradise, bliss and good.

But the style came contrary to human convention: He used the word "waʿada", which is always said for good, in His speech about both the hypocrites and the believers. Using waʿada for the believing men and women conforms to human logic, because it is a promise of good. But regarding the hypocrites, the Truthful, glorified and exalted, used the word "waʿada" in place of "awʿada".

The one speaking here is the Truthful, glorified and exalted, so do not measure the speech of Allah by the speech of humans, for humans in their speech miss details, but these are not missed or hidden from Allah. Humans vary in performance and its methods, but the Truth has one method.

So why did He, glorified and exalted, use "waʿada" instead of "awʿada"? We say: after the Truthful, glorified and exalted, had made the hypocrite men and women known, and then spoke of their recompense if they persisted in their hypocrisy, that was a warning, so that they would not persist in hypocrisy out of fear of the punishment awaiting them, so that they would desist from hypocrisy and turn to the good of faith.

Thus, when the Truthful, glorified and exalted, warned them with the threat, He gave them counsel, just as you say to one who neglects his lessons: "You will fail if you neglect your lessons." Thus you have served his eagerness to study, and you have brought him by the threat to avoid the matter he was threatened with. Therefore the Truthful, glorified and exalted, said:

﴿There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and copper, and you will not be defended. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (Ar-Rahman, 35–36)

Is the flame of fire a favor, so that the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" That is, which of the blessings of your Lord do you deny? We say: Yes, it is a favor, because when the Truthful, glorified and exalted, makes clear to you that if you oppose this you will go to the Fire, He has offered you admonition and counsel, and admonition and counsel are a favor, because it makes you avoid the path of the Fire and choose the path of Paradise.

Thus, when Allah warns the hypocrite men and women of the destiny awaiting them, this is good and a favor, because if they take heed and desist from hypocrisy for faith, they save themselves from the punishment of the Fire, and in this is abundant good. Therefore the Truthful, glorified and exalted, used the word "waʿada" and did not use "awʿada", and the word would be expressing the meaning that Allah intended.

Here the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women﴾. The promise, as we said, is good news of future benefit, and the threat is a warning of future evil. The promise and the threat are the balance of existence in this world and the Hereafter, because if you promise good to one who adheres to the method of Allah, people all come to desire to reach good by following the method; and if you threaten them with evil if they oppose the method of Allah, people shrink from opposition and disobedience out of fear of punishment and avoid evil. If your promise to the people of good is fulfilled with good, and your threat to the people of evil is fulfilled with evil, the balance of life is set straight.

So we say to one who studies: "You will succeed. If you perfect your study, you will obtain the total that qualifies you to enter the faculty you choose; and if you neglect your lessons, you will fail, be expelled from education, and your future will be lost." Here there is a promise and a threat. If you fulfil what you promised and fulfil what you threatened, the balance of life is set straight. But if you come to a person who has not studied and you make him pass and give him the highest grades, contrary to your threat to him, you are demolishing a cosmic principle upon which the interests of all creation depend. And if you promise one who gets 90% that he will enter the faculty of medicine, then you break your promise, and one who got 70% enters the faculty of medicine while the one who got 90% is excluded because of the intrusion of whims, you have also transgressed against the movement of all life, corrupting the principle of serious work in the movement of life. And everyone who does not have the capacity to carry out what he promised or threatened, his words have no weight in the movement of life.

Yet if the promise and the threat come from the Truthful, glorified and exalted, it differs from the logic of humans, for we are people of changing circumstances: we may promise good that we cannot carry out, or threaten punishment and then weaken because of particular conditions, and so we are not able to carry it out. Therefore, for the movement of life to be set straight, the promise and the threat must come from the One who is always able, always strong, always existent, possessor of the supreme word, so that there is nothing that could prevent Him from fulfilling His promise or carrying out His threat. When you read Surah al-Masad, you find the Truthful, glorified and exalted, saying in it:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. He will burn in a fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of fiber.﴾ (Al-Masad)

In this noble surah, Allah, glorified and exalted, has ruled that Abu Lahab and his wife will die as disbelievers and will enter the Fire. But many who were disbelievers at the time this surah was revealed, such as Khalid ibn al-Walid, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, 'Amr ibn al-'As(1) and others, believed, their Islam was good, and they struggled in the way of Allah. So why did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rule that Abu Lahab and his wife would not believe, just as 'Amr believed, and just as Ikrimah believed, and just as Khalid ibn al-Walid and others believed? We say: this is not the ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but the ruling of the Truthful, glorified and exalted, and when Allah rules, beware of doubting this ruling, for there is no god but Allah, and He is over all things competent.

For this reason this surah came, and after it in the noble Mushaf, in Surah al-Ikhlas: ﴿Say, He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ (Al-Ikhlas)

And since Allah is One, His command is executed even in the matters of choice in life. So when Allah says: ﴿There is no changer of His words﴾. And when He promises good, it will certainly come to pass, and when He threatens evil, it will certainly occur.

Thus, for the balance of life to be set straight, the promise and the threat had to come from the Truthful, glorified and exalted, so that we might be certain that it will happen, for no one shares Allah's dominion, there is no powerful one but Allah, no victor but Allah, for He is Allah, the One.

Sometimes the Truthful, glorified and exalted, brings an established cosmic law. When you plough your land well, irrigate it and place the seeds in it, the harvest comes to you in abundance. If you neglect the land and leave it without ploughing, planting or seeds, it gives you nothing.

Thus the cosmic law here gives a promise to the one who strives in cultivating his land with an abundant harvest, and gives a threat to one who does not turn to cultivating his land that he will not obtain a single fruit from it. Were the matter otherwise, and we found one who ploughed, irrigated and did not obtain fruit, while one who did not plant and did nothing was given abundant fruit by the land, the standards in the universe would be reversed, and we would find no one cultivating his land.

Thus, for the law of life to be set straight, either the promise and the threat come from one capable of execution who does not weaken or change, or they come by a cosmic law that we see before us every day, and what contradicts it does not occur. The one who strives succeeds, and the one who does not study fails. A cosmic law. If you are true to reality, the balance of life is upright. But if you are not true to reality and the whims intrude to make the one who does not study pass and the one who studies fail, the movement of fruitful, successful life is disrupted.

Thus the balance of promise and threat is the wheel of the movement of life. If this balance is disturbed and the promise comes in place of the threat, i.e., the one who does not work is rewarded and the one who works is punished, the universe is corrupted. Why? Because every person loves benefit for himself, and in this neither believer, rebel nor disbeliever differs; but the rebel and the disbeliever love themselves with a foolish love, so they achieve for themselves a little benefit of limited duration, at the cost of continuous punishment of unlimited duration. As for the believer, he is a person distinguished by intelligence and far-sightedness, so he has deprived himself of immediate pleasure for a limited time, in order to achieve for himself a greater pleasure in a time that has no end.

We have struck an example—and to Allah belongs the highest example—saying: Suppose there are two brothers: one wakes early from sleep, prays, eats breakfast, takes his books and goes to school; he will listen well to the teachers and return home to study his lessons. The other remains asleep, enjoying sleep, and rises at mid-morning, goes out to loiter in the streets, and whenever his soul desires any pleasure, he achieves it regardless of the method of Allah and the values of life.

Both brothers love themselves, but the first loved himself and gave it the bearable hardship of the years of study, so that it would give him comfort, position and wealth for the rest of his life. As for the second brother, he also loved himself and gave it immediate pleasure, but he lost his whole future, and so he is no longer of any worth in society.

Thus each of us loves himself, but the measures of love differ. Some of us take the sound measure and bear a small hardship to gain eternal bliss, and some of us give himself a passing pleasure to lose lasting bliss.

Remarkably, you find that this is the law of the worldly life: you will not find a person who rested in his life unless he exerted himself in his early years to reach rest for the rest of his life, and you will not find a failed person, a burden on society, unless he took his share of life at its beginning in order to suffer for the rest of his life.

For this reason it is always said: no one takes his share of life twice. The one who toils at the beginning of his life rests for the rest of it, and the one who rests at the beginning of his life toils for the rest of it. The common proverb says: "Whoever wrongs his youth, i.e., wastes it on what is of no benefit, his old age wrongs him." Those in charge of the matter must urge those who face life with the promise and the threat until the matter of their lives is set right, and they must not postpone the promise until the fruit ripens, nor the threat until evil occurs and falls. Every guardian, in any place, must watch the movement of those facing life among his children or those under his care, encouraging and promising the diligent, and not waiting until he succeeds; rather, the promise must come so that the striving may be completed. And the threat must come before the son fails or wastes his life, so we do not wait until a person is corrupted and then threaten him, for the promise and the threat are what weigh the movement of life.

But if we see in some society that the one who works receives nothing, and the one who does not work receives everything, we know that the standards of work have been disturbed, and that troubles have begun in society, because the one who works, when he finds that work does not bring him to anything, directs the movement of his life away from his work, spending all his effort on hypocrisy, flattery, distorting facts and pleasing the one who holds the authority. The result is society's loss of the value of work, so society becomes a society without productive work, and becomes skilled in hypocrisy, showing off and the loss of truth.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, has made clear the measure of the movement of life in the promise and the threat, so do not give an incentive except to one who deserves it, and no reward to the diligent. But if you scatter incentives on the hypocrites, and on those who achieve your personal aims for you, such as one who serves you in your house or settles your affairs for you—

1 Khalid ibn al-Walid embraced Islam in the seventh year after the Hijrah, after the Battle of Khaybar. As for Ikrimah, he embraced Islam in the year of the conquest of Makkah, in 8 AH. As for 'Amr ibn al-'As, he embraced Islam before the conquest, in Safar of 8 AH. See: al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah by Ibn Hajar (2/98), (4/258), (5/2).

Therefore, after Allah has mentioned Paradise and what is in it, and what makes the soul long for Paradise, He now reminds us of what we must do to serve His method (and to Allah belongs the highest similitude). It is like when you tell your son: "When you graduate as a doctor, you will have a large clinic, then a hospital," and you raise him with what awaits him of great future, and remind him of the necessity of diligently studying until he reaches what he hopes for. In this way you have made him love the goal he will reach, and then you move on to make him love the means that will lead him to this goal.

Here the Almighty says:

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾. Almighty Allah honours and exalts His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so He did not call him by his name. Rather He said: ﴿O Prophet﴾ (1), and in other places He calls him: ﴿O Messenger﴾.

As for the Almighty's address to the rest of the Prophets, it is like His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise..." (35)﴾ (Al-Baqarah)

And His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿It was said, "O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings..." (48)﴾ (Hud)

And the Almighty called Ibrahim:

{O Ibrahim (104), you have fulfilled the dream... (105)} (As-Saffat)

And the Almighty called Musa:

﴿O Musa (11), indeed I am your Lord...(12)﴾ (Taha)

And the Almighty addressed our master Isa:

﴿O Isa, son of Maryam, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?..." (116)﴾ (Al-Ma'idah)

So every Messenger was called by Almighty Allah by his name, except the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for He called him: ﴿O Prophet﴾ and ﴿O Messenger﴾, honouring the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and elevating his station with his Lord.

Here Almighty Allah asks His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites (2).

We know that heaven does not intervene to send a Messenger except when society has become corrupt in a general way. We know that the human soul has been created with a love of goodness; if its desire does not govern it, it does good and loves it, but if its desire governs it, the good is hidden from it, and desire opens for the soul the doors of evil. A person may follow his desire in some matter, then awaken, and his soul blames him for what he did. This is the self-reproaching soul (an-nafs al-lawwamah), which blames its owner for evil and drives him toward good. But there is a soul in which the faculties of goodness cease, so it does evil and feels no remorse for it; then the soul advances in evil until it becomes one that commands evil (ammarah bi's-su'), and it refuses to be content with doing evil, but commands people to it and makes it attractive to them. Thus the stages of the human soul are many: there is the soul that is at peace with the method of Allah and obeys it. This is the soul at rest (an-nafs al-mutma'innah), of which the Almighty says:

{O soul at rest (28), return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing (28), so enter among My servants (29), and enter My Paradise (30)} (Al-Fajr).

When you find the soul at rest and the self-reproaching soul, know that society is in good condition, for the soul at rest obeys and commands obedience, and the self-reproaching soul blames its owner for evil. Every believer has a point of weakness; when a believer weakens, his brother who believes hastens to blame him for his weakness and to correct his course, because points of weakness differ. You find that society is upright whenever there is someone who draws attention to what is wrong and forbids it, and these are the ones of whom the Almighty says:

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience (3)﴾ (Al-Asr)

But when the souls all rust, and there is no longer anyone who commands good and forbids evil, but you find someone who forbids good and commands evil, then Almighty Allah must intervene to restore truth to its place in the world.

So the Lord of Might does not intervene while there are souls at peace that apply the method of Allah and command obedience to it, or self-reproaching souls, whether within the human soul itself or in society, that call the sinner to account. But when corruption spreads through society, and there is no longer anyone who forbids evil and commands good, and the people of goodness in it become unable to do anything, the Messengers come to restore the method of truth to organise the life of society.

When the Messenger comes, he knows that he was sent only after evil had spread through the universe, and that the people of corruption are the majority, and they are the holders of influence and authority, profiting from the corruption and deviation that have spread through society. If these people hear the cry of truth, they will not stand by as spectators, but will fight everyone who carries the method of truth to them. The Messenger must stand firm before them and strive against them.

"Jahada" (to strive) is of the pattern "faa'ala," like "shaaraka" (to participate): you participate with someone (shaarakta fulanan), and like "qaatala" (to fight): you fight someone (qaatala fulanan). So there must be a mutual contest between the Messenger and those who followed him, and between disbelief and corruption in society.

The Messenger and the believers who follow his method must prepare to bear harm from those who do not believe in the method, because the disbelievers profit from corruption; in order for this profit to continue, the disbelievers must stand against the bearers of the method of truth and oppose them, so that they may secure for themselves the continuation of the privileges that falsehood gives them. Almighty Allah alerts His Messenger to the reality of these disbelievers who profit from corruption, and that they will fight him. For this reason the Almighty did not say to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Unite with them," but He said: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, i.e., stand firm before them in the battle. Many verses came in which Allah commands His Messenger and the believers to be patient in striving, and striving requires confrontation, so He said: ﴿Be patient﴾.

But suppose my enemy is also patient in war; if I am patient and my enemy is patient, the two shoulders are equal. Therefore the Almighty says:

﴿Be patient and outdo one another in patience... (200)﴾ (Al 'Imran), i.e., if your enemy confronts you with patience, let your patience be stronger than his, so that you overcome him through patience and endurance. Stand firm in confronting them, with the believers in your message beside you, for the camp of faith must confront the camp of disbelief and hypocrisy. The disbeliever is one who denies faith in his heart and declares disbelief with his tongue; the hypocrite is one who disbelieves inwardly and declares faith outwardly. This is the one from whom we must be most cautious, because we do not recognise him and so we do not guard against his evil as we do against the disbeliever; the hypocrite may stab us from behind while we feel secure with him and at ease with him, so his stab is effective and painful.

Allah makes clear to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that the enmity he will face while proclaiming the method of Allah will come from two sources: from a disbeliever or from a hypocrite, i.e., one who openly disbelieves, or one who disbelieves in his heart and feigns faith with his tongue. As for the hypocrite, he is a difficult enemy, because he deceives us so we do not trust him, although hypocrisy in itself, with respect to the method of Allah, is a sign of the strength of this method, for only the strong are flattered in hypocrisy; the weak are flattered by no one.

For this reason there were no hypocrites during his presence, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Makkah before the Hijrah, because the Muslims were few, weak, tortured and persecuted. Nothing enticed anyone to feign with them, because there was no benefit from such hypocrisy; rather whoever sympathised with them would be exposed to torture and persecution. The hypocrite, in displaying what differs from what he conceals, seeks only his own personal interest.

The situation changed after the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Madinah, and the hypocrites appeared once Islam had become a state and a power. The hypocrite in this case declares his faith falsely, in order to benefit from the strength of the Muslims for his own advantage. Thus hypocrisy is a diseased trait in the hypocrite, but it is a sign of the strength of the believer whom he flatters.

We note that in this verse the Almighty mentioned the disbelievers before the hypocrites, and in other verses He mentioned the hypocrites first, and in other verses He mentioned the hypocrites before the disbelievers (3). The confrontation, as we know, first took place with the disbelievers. At the beginning of the call there was no such hypocritical category; there were only believers and disbelievers, and striving against the disbelievers came in stages, not in one stage. The first stage of striving was striving with argument, because the believers at the beginning were a small, weak group, possessing no strength with which to confront this great tide of disbelievers. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, presented the matters of faith with proof, to persuade the intellect, perhaps their minds would awaken and they would believe in the method of truth. He would ask them, for example, who created the heavens and the earth?

When the disbeliever considers this in his mind, he finds no one who claims, or could claim, that he created the heavens and the earth, so their answer can only be that the Creator is Allah, Exalted is He (4). Why? Because a person, in his make-up, may claim things that are not his, but he does not deny a thing that is his. The inventor of anything, or its maker, cannot deny that he made or invented it; rather he loves for the whole world to know that he invented or made it. For this reason you will not find anything beneficial to the universe, however trivial, without our knowing its history, where it came from, and who discovered or made it. An example is what we studied in school about the one who discovered electricity, and the one who made the electric lamp, and who developed it. Likewise the invention of the aeroplane; we know how the idea of flight arose with Abbas ibn Firnas, who tried to fly himself by means of large wings, and so the beginning was made.

Therefore, everything beneficial in the universe is known: who discovered it, made it, or invented it. If this is the case regarding limited human manufactures, what about the universe? When we ask: who brought the sun into being? Does its Creator not deserve that we know who He is, especially as we know who invented the electric lamp and brought it into our lives?

If we fill the world with talk about the inventor of the electric lamp, which lights a single room for a time, and large factories were established to produce this invention, do we not deserve to know who brought into being the sun that lights the whole earth at the same moment? This sun has been rising for millions of years and has never once gone out, and has never needed a spare part throughout this long life. It must have a maker whose power is commensurate with that wonder we see, whether in its light, or the qualities of this light, or in the precision of its making; it does not come late by a second nor early by a second. Its maker must have power commensurate with the greatness of this creation.

So if the Messenger comes and informs us that Allah is the One who created the sun, then either he is truthful, and we all accept that Allah is the Creator and Originator; or he is not truthful, and we say: then why has no one come forward to claim that he is the one who created it?

But the precision and miraculous nature of creation, which no single human power, nor several cooperating human powers, can attain, has settled the matter for Him, Exalted is He (5). Until someone comes who claims to have created the sun, and no one will come, the question of creation is settled for Allah, Exalted is He, and there is no contender.

The Messenger comes and says: the Creator of the earth, the sun, the heavens and the universe is the Almighty, Exalted is He, and no one has come forward to claim that he created any of this, which confirms the truth of the Messenger's claim, and confirms that the One who brought this universe into being is a power without limits and a might without bounds, and He is the most deserving of worship over these idols and gods that they claim.

The call then proceeds by reasoning, asking them who created them, in confirmation of the Almighty's saying:

﴿Were they created out of nothing, or are they the creators? (35)﴾ (At-Tur)

If the answer is: neither this nor that, then there must be a Creator and Originator for us. When the Messenger comes to us and informs us that the Creator of this universe and of us is Allah, we must believe him, because no one has claimed, or is able to claim, that he created this universe or created himself, just as if we had sat in a place, and after we left, we found a wallet, and the owner of the place came and asked...

3 Such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them﴾ (An-Nisa: 140), and His saying: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell﴾ (At-Tawbah: 68).
