He said: ﴿Ibrahim said, "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." And the one who disbelieved was confounded﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 258).

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives us another picture of the false oaths that the hypocrites used to swear, so He says, glorified is He:

﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they had indeed uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their submission (to Islam), and they plotted what they could not attain. And they resented only that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no protector or helper on earth.﴾ (74)

In this noble verse, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, clarifies for us the links of the hypocrites' false swearing: they swear that they did not say (it), and they make Allah a target for their oaths, even though they uttered the word of disbelief, disbelieving after they had declared Islam with their tongues, and their Islam is the Islam of a claimant.

Concerning this noble verse there is a story whose events took place during the expedition of Tabuk, in which the Muslims fought the Romans. It was the first fighting between the Muslims and non-Arabs. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for this expedition in an extremely hot period, and during this period each one preferred to sit in the al-akhyaf (small gardens), i.e., the small orchards, and they would sit under the palm trees and the trees in a moist atmosphere, and did not wish to rise from the shade.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for jihad in the way of Allah, and going to fight the Romans, the hypocrites sought false excuses so that they would not go out for jihad. The Qur'an kept descending concerning those who stayed behind from this expedition for two full months. A man named al-Jalas ibn Suwayd said: "By Allah, if what Muhammad says about those who stayed behind from fighting is true, then we are worse than donkeys." Here 'Amir ibn Qays al-Ansari said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has spoken the truth, and you are worse than donkeys. And you, O Jalas, are worse than a donkey." Here a number of hypocrites stood up to assassinate 'Amir ibn Qays al-Ansari, because al-Jalas ibn Suwayd was among the leaders of his people. 'Amir ibn Qays went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of what had happened, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Ibn Suwayd and asked him about the report, and he swore by Allah that everything 'Amir ibn Qays had said had not happened. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left him after he had sworn by Allah. Here 'Amir ibn Qays raised his hand to the sky and said: "O Allah, I ask You to send down upon Your servant and Your Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) the confirmation of the truthful and the refutation of the liar." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Amin" (ﷺ). They had not finished the supplication before the revelation descended with the words of the Truth, majestic is His majesty:

﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they had indeed uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their submission, and they plotted what they could not attain.﴾

Thus this noble verse settled the matter. It showed who was truthful and who was lying, regarding what 'Amir ibn Qays related and al-Jalas denied.

But the noble verse went beyond what was known of the incident to what had not reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and they plotted what they could not attain.﴾ That is because Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wished to make the hypocrites know that He informs His Prophet of what the hypocrites conceal from him. Had the verse been revealed only concerning the incident of the false oath, the hypocrites would have said: "Muhammad (peace be upon him) knew only what 'Amir said." But there were things 'Amir had not heard, and they had said them. The hypocrites had conspired against the life of the Prophet (ﷺ) and agreed to kill him at the 'Aqaba crossing. This 'Aqaba is a group of high rocks that block the path, and they would contrive to pass it sometimes through low tunnels and sometimes by climbing over them and then descending.

The hypocrites plotted to push the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the top of the rocks so he would fall into the valley, but Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who was walking behind the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), noticed the plot, so the hypocrites fled. Thus they did not attain what they wanted, just as they did not attain what they wanted when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came as an emigrant to Madinah, for they had been preparing to make 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy king over them, but the coming of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prevented them from that.

It was also said that they conspired to kill 'Amir ibn Qays, because he had informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of what al-Jalas ibn Suwayd had said, but they were not able to do so. As for the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿And they resented only that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty.﴾ "Resented" (nqmu) means: they disliked. And wealth, as we know, is not something to be disliked, but its mention here is evidence of the corruption of their nature and their lack of fairness in judgment, because the wealth and security that reached them is not a defect and does not produce resentment. Rather, it should naturally have produced love and devotion in faith.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, makes clear to them: What do you fault Muhammad for? What do you resent? Do you resent him when he has brought you honour and wealth?

Before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, they had disliked the Messenger's arrival in Madinah as poor people who owned nothing, but when they became hypocrites and entered Islam, they took from the spoils, and Allah enriched them. Indeed al-Jalas ibn Suwayd, when a boy of his was killed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him twelve thousand dirhams as blood-money. So wealth came to all through the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Is this something you dislike? Of course not. Rather it is evidence of the corruption of your natures and your lack of fairness in judgment. Since Allah, glorified is He, has enriched you through the coming of His Messenger, it was not proper for that to be faulted in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); rather it should have been praised, and you should have devoted yourselves to faith in him and to supporting him.

The words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿out of His bounty (min fadlihi)﴾ draw our attention to the style of the Qur'an. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah and His Messenger﴾, and the analogy of human speech would have been to say "Allah and His Messenger, out of their bounty," but He said ﴿out of His bounty﴾, because Allah is not coupled with anyone, even if it were Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah.

This is what happened when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a preacher delivering a sermon and saying: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been saved, and whoever disobeys both has perished." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Evil is the preacher of the people you are, for the preacher combined a dual form between Allah and His Messenger."

Here the preacher stopped and said: "Then what should I say, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has perished' (ﷺ), and do not say 'disobeys both'. Do not join anyone with Allah, and do not make anyone a dual with Allah." For this reason we find that the Noble Qur'an did not say "Allah and His Messenger enriched them out of their bounty", but said ﴿out of His bounty﴾, because bounty is one. If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has any bounty, it is from the bounty of Allah. In any case, no one is coupled with Allah, and for this reason we find in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿They swear to you by Allah to please you, but Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers.﴾ (62) (al-Tawba)

Here we also see that the Truth, glorified is He, used the singular form in the matter of being pleased, because the pleasure of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and the pleasure of His Messenger (ﷺ) are unified, since when the name of Allah comes, no one is coupled with Him.

After the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, exposed the hypocrites and clarified what was in their hearts, His mercy did not abandon them, for He, glorified and exalted is He, is merciful to His servants. Therefore He opened for them the door of repentance, saying: ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them﴾. The opening of the door of repentance is a mercy to the whole movement of life; for if Allah closed the door of repentance, everyone who committed a sin would have as his destiny punishment whatever he did, so he would certainly persist in sin and increase in wrongdoing, since there would be no difference between one sin and many sins. But when any person who errs knows that the door of repentance is open, he does not persist in wrongdoing. Moreover, the one who truly suffers from evils and sins is society as a whole: if a dangerous thief is found, for example, it is society that suffers from his thefts; and if a professional murderer is found, it is those members of society whom he kills who suffer from his crimes.

So, the opening of the door of repentance is a mercy to society, because it does not drive the criminal to persist in his crime. Looking at the noble verse, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, after making the truth manifest and showing the Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers things the hypocrites had been concealing, opened the door of repentance to the hypocrites. Then al-Jalas ibn Suwayd, leader of the hypocrites, said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has offered me repentance. By Allah, I did say what 'Amir said, and 'Amir is truthful in what he said about me." Al-Jalas repented and his Islam became good.

As for those to whom repentance is offered and who do not repent to Allah, He, glorified is He, said:

﴿But if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no protector or helper on earth.﴾ So the recompense of one who rejects repentance and does not acknowledge his error is a painful punishment, not only in the Hereafter but in this world and the Hereafter. The punishment of this world is either by killing or by disgrace, and the punishment of the Hereafter is in the lowest level of the Fire.

But the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿and they will have no protector or helper on earth﴾ might be misunderstood by some people as meaning that the punishment is in this world only. "Earth" here refers to the earth of this world, and there is another earth in the Hereafter, which is the earth of the Return, confirming His saying, exalted is He:

﴿On the day the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens...﴾ (48) (Ibrahim)

So the word ﴿earth﴾ gives us two images: in this world and in the Hereafter.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they will have no protector or helper on earth﴾ clarifies for us that the protector (wali) is the one close to you to whom you turn in times of hardship, and one turns in hardship only to one from whom he hopes for help, or to one who is of his own; and the helper (nasir) is the one from whom help is sought. A person may be among those far from you with whom you have no bond of allegiance (wilaya). So neither the close protector nor the distant stranger to whom you might turn for help can do anything for you; there is no escape from the punishment of Allah for one who disbelieves or is hypocritical.

1 Al-akhyaf in the language: places between the course of the torrent in the mountain and its rocks, where grasses grow. See Lisan al-'Arab (root: kh-y-f).
2 See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/371-373).
3 They were twelve men who died fighting Allah and His Messenger. From Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: "I was holding the halter of the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), leading it, while 'Ammar was driving it, until when we were at the 'Aqaba, suddenly I saw twelve riders who had confronted him there. I alerted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them, and he shouted at them, and they turned back fleeing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Did you recognize the people?' We said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah, they were masked, but we recognized the mounts.' He said: 'These are the hypocrites until the Day of Resurrection. Do you know what they intended?' We said: 'No.' He said: 'They intended to crowd the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the 'Aqaba so as to throw him down from it.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall we not send to their clans so that each people sends us the head of its companion?' He said: 'No, I dislike that the Arabs should say among themselves that Muhammad fought with a people, and when Allah made him prevail over them he turned on them to kill them.' Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (5/260, 261), and in it is 'an'anah of Ibn Ishaq.

5 From Adi ibn Hatim that a man gave a sermon in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided aright, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "(Evil is the preacher you are. Say: 'Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray.')" Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (870), Ahmad in his Musnad (4/256, 379), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1099).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 9, verse 75:

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, presents another image of the hypocrites, saying:

﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], "If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and surely be among the righteous."﴾

﴿And among them﴾, i.e., among the hypocrites whom Allah depicted in many images in this noble surah, when He said ﴿among them﴾, and ﴿among them﴾, and ﴿among them﴾, the narrations of the exegetes and the transmitters differed regarding the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾. Some of them said: it is Tha'labah ibn Hatib. Others said: it is Mu'attib ibn Qushayr. A third opinion said: it is al-Jadd ibn Qays. A fourth speaker said: it is Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. All these differing views are borne by the noble verse (1), because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], "If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and surely be among the righteous."﴾

The Truth did not say, "So when We gave them of Our bounty, they were stingy with it," in a way that applies to one specific case. Rather, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, brought it in the plural form, so He, glorified is He, said:

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it... (76)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

So there is a plural. And all the narrations may be correct in that the verse was revealed concerning several individuals. And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾. How then can the hypocrites have a covenant with Allah? We say: these hypocrites were treated according to the outward appearance of their tongues. They had declared their Islam, and each one of them would say, "I make a covenant with Allah to do such and such," just as one of them comes to the prayer and some of them are eager to be in the first row of worshippers. Did hypocrisy prevent him from praying outwardly? No one prevented him. Likewise, when he makes a covenant with Allah, he makes it with the outward part of his tongue.

The story of the verse (2) is that a poor man from the Ansar went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I am poor, mu'lik (i.e., extremely poor). So supplicate to Allah for me, O Messenger of Allah, that He may widen my livelihood." With the prophetic insight, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A little that you render its thanks is better than a lot that you cannot bear." He returned to him and said: "Ask Allah for me to widen [my livelihood]." So he supplicated for him, and Allah widened it upon him.

One may ask: how does the Messenger respond to and supplicate for a hypocrite? And if the Messenger supplicated to placate him and to win his heart, how does Allah answer His Messenger's request on behalf of a hypocrite?

We say: perhaps that was so, because the hypocrite wanted to test: is the Messenger of Allah truthful, such that if he supplicates to Allah, he is answered?

When the Messenger of Allah supplicated, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, willed to make this hypocrite know that: yes, he is the Messenger of Allah, and whoever he supplicates for, Allah answers him, and this is for the Prophet (ﷺ).

So when the Messenger of Allah supplicated for Tha'labah, or for al-Jadd ibn Qays, or for Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, Allah answered the supplication of His Messenger for them, and gave the one who asked for the supplication abundant wealth. They said: the wealth of Tha'labah multiplied, and his wealth in sheep multiplied until the valleys of Madinah could no longer contain them, so he fled with them to the valleys of the mountains and to the wide desert, and they filled it, and they preoccupied him from congregational prayer, and he came to prayer only on Friday. Then, when they increased to an excessive abundance, they preoccupied him also from the Friday prayer. In that is a proof of the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah's prophecy concerning him. So the whole matter came only as a confirmation of the Messenger's stance toward them, so as to expose their foolishness in that they had been hypocrites in Islam.

After that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked about him, and they said: "He is in the valleys; his wealth has preoccupied him." He said: "Woe to Tha'labah!" And he sent to him the collector of zakat (3), because Tha'labah had made a covenant with Allah and said: ﴿If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give charity﴾. So the collector of zakat went to him, and when he said to him, "Bring what Allah has enjoined upon you of charity from your wealth," he said: "Is it not the sister of the jizyah (4)?" And the collector reminded him: "You are the one who made the covenant, and among the terms of your covenant was that if you were given, you would give charity and be among the righteous, so why do you not fulfil the covenant?" Tha'labah replied to the collector of zakat: "Go away until I see my opinion."

So he had made a covenant with Allah, and supplicated to the Messenger of Allah, and Allah answered him, and his wealth increased. After that, Allah confirmed His Prophet in his saying: "A little that you render its half is better than a lot that you cannot bear." When the collector of zakat returned to the Messenger of Allah, [saying]: "Tha'labah refused." He (ﷺ) said: "Woe to Tha'labah!" When Tha'labah learned that a Qur'an had been revealed concerning him, he was greatly alarmed and hastened to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and offered him the zakat. The Messenger of Allah did not accept it from him, so he kept coming back to him seeking acceptance, but the Messenger of Allah did not accept it from him. By that, the Messenger (ﷺ) wished to establish that Allah and the poor of Allah are not in need of your wealth, O Tha'labah.

When the Messenger of Allah passed on to the Highest Companion, Tha'labah came with all the charities owed to him to Abu Bakr. [Abu Bakr refused:] It was not for the Messenger of Allah to refuse them and then for Abu Bakr to take them.

When Abu Bakr died, he came to Umar, and Umar said what Abu Bakr had said. Then he came to Uthman, but before he could reach him, he had perished in the time of Uthman.

﴿If He gives us from His bounty﴾: the word ﴿la-in﴾ [if, with the oath-particle] is an oath, and an oath is the form of a covenant. So it is as if he said: "I swear by Allah that if Allah gives me wealth, I will surely do such and such." We have understood that it is an oath from the presence of the lam in the answer to the oath, ﴿surely give charity﴾ [la-nassaddaqanna]. And "charity" (sadaqah) here is the obligatory charity, i.e., zakat. ﴿Surely be among the righteous﴾ [la-nakunanna min al-salihin], i.e., we will increase in voluntary acts, in manliness, in generosity, and in everything that indicates righteousness.

The Truth says concerning that:

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it, and turned away while they were averse (76).﴾

1 Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3134) mentioned these narrations and preferred that it was revealed concerning three of the hypocrites: Tha'labah ibn al-Harith, Jahd ibn Qays, and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr. As for it being Tha'labah ibn Hatib, al-Qurtubi rejected it, because he witnessed Badr. As for al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, he distinguished between the one who witnessed Badr and other than him. See al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah (biography 924).
2 The takhrij of this story was previously given at the tafsir of verse 53 of surah al-Tawbah.
3 This was when the verse was revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ (al-Tawbah: 103). Tha'labah here had made a covenant with Allah that if He provided him and gave him, he would surely give charity, and it had not yet been specified; when the verse ﴿Take from their wealth...﴾ (al-Tawbah: 103) was revealed and zakat was made obligatory, he refused to carry out what he had covenanted with Allah. This is similar to what the Lord of Honour related about the Children of Israel: ﴿When they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king that we may fight in the way of Allah." He said, "Would you perhaps refrain, if fighting was prescribed for you, from fighting?" They said, "And why would we not fight in the way of Allah while we have been expelled from our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them﴾ (al-Baqarah: 246)..
4 Jizyah: a sum of money imposed on those who enter the protection and covenant of the Muslims from the People of the Book. Islam imposed it upon them in return for the zakat imposed on Muslims, and in return for their defence and protection of the dhimmis in the Islamic lands where they reside. It is obligatory upon one who is: male, mature, and free, and it is not obligatory upon the needy and poor among the People of the Book. See: Fiqh al-Sunnah by Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq (3/112-117).

Divine giving is of two kinds: the giving of causes (ʿaṭāʾ al-asbāb) and the giving of grace (ʿaṭāʾ al-tafaḍḍul). The giving of causes is that a person, in whatever work he undertakes, finds that God gives him the fruit of his work, whether he is a believer or an unbeliever, obedient or disobedient, because the person has taken up the causes and perfected them. For this reason you find some who deny God living in abundance, because they handle causes well. And since they have handled causes well, and since they too are servants of God, and it is He, glory be to Him, who brought them into existence, He has guaranteed that the causes will respond to them and will not withhold from them. The sun shines on the believer and the unbeliever, on the obedient and the disobedient, and the rain falls on the earth. Likewise, everything on earth responds in its elements to what they sow or what they do. This, then, is the giving of causes.

But the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, conceals the giving of grace within the giving of causes, like one who walks along an unknown road and finds a treasure, or whose harvest is not struck by a wind or a storm that would diminish its yield. God blesses him in the sale of his produce and blesses him in his provision, so that his wealth is not spent on what is lost or wasted. All of this is called the giving of grace. The giving of causes is common to all people, whereas the giving of grace is specific to the friends of God (awliyāʾ Allāh) who have sincerely devoted their works to God in obedience and compliance.

The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty﴾ is evidence that the provision that came to them was not subject to causes alone, but exceeded what causes give, by a grace from God. The increase that occurred in Thaʿlabah's sheep was not an increase by causes alone; rather there was blessing in it, such that a single ewe brought forth more than one offspring, and the grass it grazed yielded a large quantity of milk.

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it﴾. What is stinginess? In the language there are names for withholding giving: there is bukhl (stinginess), shuḥḥ (niggardliness), and kazāza (tightfistedness), all of which are names for refraining from giving something. But the ranks of giving and stinginess differ. There is a person who gives only to one who asks him; that is one rank. And there is a person who does not give to everyone who asks, but gives to the one who asks with reasons that stir his compassion toward him, such as saying: "My son is sick," or "My house has burned down." The asker here does not merely ask, but comes with a cause for the request that stirs the emotions. And there is one who gives without being asked.

So there are three stages of giving: one gives to whoever he sees in such a state, presuming that his condition is pitiable without his being asked; this is a rank of nearness to God, by which God illuminates the insight of some people so that their hand becomes the hand of God toward God's creatures. Indeed, there are people who reproach themselves when a person comes and asks them for charity or assistance. Like the man who went and knocked on the door, and the householder came out to him and asked him what he wanted. The asker requested money from him, so the householder went in, took some money and gave it to the asker. His wife learned that he had come asking for money and had given it to him. But the husband who had given money went back weeping. She said to him: "What makes you weep, when you have answered his request?" He said: "What makes me weep is that I left him to ask me," meaning that he weeps because he did not possess the discernment that would enable him to perceive people's needs around him so as to give to the needy without their asking.

So: one gives upon a request, and that is a level; and there is one who gives without a request, indeed gives out of a surplus he has, meaning he possesses much and gives from it.

And a third gives half of what he has, sharing with him in what he owns, or gives the most of what he has according to what arises in his mind of the need of the person being given to.

So there are three stages: a man who gives without being asked, a man who gives upon a request containing stirring and provoking causes of emotion, and a man who gives merely upon being asked.

Who, then, is the stingy one? The most heinous degree of stinginess is that a man is stingy toward one who asks him with occasions that stir emotions, and yet his heart does not soften; this is the miser.

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away while they were refusing﴾. One of these did not merely withhold, but turned away from the one who asked him, like the one who turned away from the collector who came to take the alms, though it was incumbent upon him, for example, to seat the collector, offer him the due greeting, and then say: "We shall see our opinion," but he turned away and refused him.

Here the Truth brings the punishment of whoever follows this conduct, saying:

﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed God in what they had promised Him and because they used to lie﴾ (9:77).

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-Tawbah (9), verse 77:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So He caused them to follow it up with hypocrisy in their hearts﴾, i.e., He made the consequence of this conduct that hypocrisy was placed in their hearts, ﴿until the Day they meet Him﴾, i.e., until the Day of Resurrection. Since Allah has said this, its meaning is that whoever does such a deed, who is asked for charity and withholds it, stays stingy, turns away and refuses, this is an announcement from Allah that this person will never die upon faith. And none of these people died upon faith (ʿillat al-iymān, i.e., the ailment of faith, in the sense of having faith's ailment removed or being cured of it). This punishment came about because they broke with Allah what they had promised Him, so He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿because they broke their promise to Allah which they had made to Him﴾. Likewise, the punishment came upon them because they: ﴿used to lie﴾. So it is as if each one of them first broke the word of the covenant, and then lied a second time when he said: "Is it a sister of the jizyah?" – although he knows that zakat on wealth is one of the pillars of Islam.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 78:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

{Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private consultations, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen? (78)}

Knowledge here is intended to mean knowing a piece of information that was not known before. The words of the Truth, glorified is He, ﴿Do they not know﴾ contain the interrogative hamza (alif al-istifham), and "lam" is the negating particle, like the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? (1)﴾ (al-Fil).

We know that information conveyed between the speaker and the addressee has several forms. The first form: the speaker informs the addressee of what he has, and this is a "statement" (khabar). The second form: the speaker does not inform his addressee of the information directly, but makes the speaker himself state the information, like the words of one of the benefactors: "Did I not do good to you?" He was able to say "I did good to you," which would be a statement from his side, but he wants to give the statement strength, so he made the speech a question from the one questioned, as though he presented the matter in the form of a question within the form of a negation, confident that the addressee will find only one answer: "Yes, you did good to me."

Thus, a statement is either a bare statement free of negation, or a statement accompanied by negation, or a statement accompanied by interrogation. The strongest types of informing are the statement accompanied by negation, and that accompanied by interrogation, because a statement in the first form comes from the speaker, and a statement from the speaker is capable of being true or false. But interrogation requires an answer from the addressee, and the addressee answers only with what is in the speaker's own mind; and if the speaker knew that the addressee might deny it, he would not ask. Or one says to a person: "I am pleased with your protection," and this saying means that the speaker knows he will not be contradicted otherwise, and when he turns the speech over in his mind he will find only that what he hears is the truth.

﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private consultations⦆. What is the secret (sirr), and what is the private consultation (najwa)? The secret is what you conceal within yourself and do not disclose to anyone, so the secret is not what you confide to another, for that is the najwa. The root of najwa is distance. It is said: "So-and-so is at a najwa from such-and-such," meaning he is far from such-and-such. The root of najwa is also an elevated place on a mountain, as though the one raised on the mountain is distant from the level of the surface of the earth. When a person wishes to speak to someone with words that no one else hears, he asks his permission to withdraw from the rest of those sitting so that he may speak with him as he wishes, or he lowers his voice so that none hears it except the person he wishes to whisper a word to, and no one else hears it. For this reason they are called munajat (intimate conversation), and it is speech that the nearby person does not hear, because you have lowered your voice to a degree that is hidden from the one nearby, so it is as though he has become distant.

Thus, the secret is what you have kept within yourself, and the najwa is what you have confided to another in such a way that the one sitting with you does not know it.

As for those who prevented charity, they must have agreed upon that among themselves, and they must have spoken about this matter—the prevention of charity—after they became wealthy and had much wealth, and they rebelled against the logic of Islam, even though they were always eager to appear in their Islam in a manner that surpasses the true Muslims; so they were always in the front rows for prayer in order to conceal their hypocrisy.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, makes clear that they concealed within themselves a speech, this concealment within the self, when Allah informs of it, is a tearing away of the veil of both place and time together. Allah, glorified is He, informed His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of what took place in that concealment, just as He had previously torn away for him the veils of past time. This concerns matters he did not witness, did not hear from a teacher, and did not read in a book, since he was unlettered; so the Messenger of Allah reported more than one matter that he had not witnessed, heard, or read.

So: from where did he obtain that? Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, who knows the hidden things (khab'ah) of the heavens and the earth, informed him of it, and He also tore away for him the veil of future time, so he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, knew events before they occurred, and He informed him of them from the One who holds the forelock of time, the forelock of place, and the forelock of events. This is the tearing away of the veil of future time, and He, glorified is He, tore away for His Messenger the veil of place, so he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would inform them of something in their souls. Indeed, the Truth revealed to him:

﴿And they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say..." (8)﴾ (al-Mujadila). By Allah, when a man from among them heard what he had said within himself, the Messenger of Allah informed him of what he had said. So who was it that tore away the veil for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?

It is the One who knows the secret and what is more hidden that tore away the veil for the Messenger of Allah. There are no veils hidden from Allah, for the veils of the unseen exist only for human beings: a veil of the past, a veil of the future, a veil of place, and a veil of time.

﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private consultations, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?⦆ That is: the knowledge of Allah is not confined to knowing their affairs alone; rather, Allah knows their secret and their private consultations, because His attribute is self-subsistence (al-qayyumiyyah), and that He is the Knower of the unseen, He knows the unseen of this and the unseen of that and the unseen of that, and the emphasis comes from repeating "unseen" for every individual.

So: ﴿the Knower of the unseen⦆ means that He knows even what you tried to conceal and hide. He, glorified is He, said:

﴿"Indeed, if it be an atom's weight within a rock or in the heavens or on the earth, Allah will bring it forth..." (16)﴾ (Luqman).

So: the knowledge of the Truth, majestic is His majesty, is not absent from Him in anything.

1 The prohibition of private conversation between two to the exclusion of a third has been reported. On the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "If you are three, then two should not converse privately to the exclusion of their companion, for that would grieve him." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (2184), Ahmad in his Musnad (1/431), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2825), who said: it is a sahih hadith.

2 Al-khab' and al-khab': everything absent and hidden. The Most High says in Surah al-Naml: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth the hidden (al-khab') in the heavens and the earth﴾ (al-Naml, 25). Ibn Aslam said: it is what has been placed in them of provisions: rain from the sky and plants from the earth. (See: Ibn Kathir, 3/361.)

Then God, exalted is He, moves us to another image of the hypocrites and what they do to the believers. So He, majestic is His majesty, said:

{Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers regarding charity, and those who find nothing but their own effort, so they mock them. God mocks them, and theirs is a painful punishment} (9:79).

Al-lamz (faultfinding) means blame, but in a hidden way, such as by a gesture with the eye, the hand, the mouth, or other means. So there is a group of hypocrites who find fault with the volunteers (al-mutawwi'un) who collect zakat from the believers. Among these hypocrites are those who blame by speech, those who blame by action, and those who blame by gesture. The volunteers are those who give something extra of the same kind as what God has made obligatory.

For example, God has made five prayers obligatory, and there are those who pray five other prayers voluntarily. God has made zakat obligatory at two and a half percent, and there are those who give ten percent voluntarily. God has made fasting in the month of Ramadan obligatory, and there are those who fast beyond that every Monday and Thursday. This is what we call the believer entering the station of ihsan (excellence), by drawing near to God through what exceeds what God has imposed on you, and of the same kind as what God has imposed. If you perform what is obligatory, you have committed yourself to the method. A man asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the obligations of Islam, then said: "I will neither add nor subtract." The noble Messenger said: "He has succeeded, if he is truthful" (2).

Going beyond what God has made obligatory, and of the same kind as what He has made obligatory, has two aspects:

The first: the servant bears witness to his Lord's mercy, because He has not burdened him beyond what he can bear.

The second aspect: the act of obedience has lightened the burden on the believer, so he finds rest in it. Did not the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say about prayer: "Relieve us with it, O Bilal" (3)?

So the volunteer is one who adds to what God has made obligatory upon him, of the same kind as what God has made obligatory. These are the doers of good (al-muhsinun), about whom the Truth spoke in Surat al-Dhariyat:

{Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them; indeed, they were before that doers of good. They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness, and in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived} (51:15-19).

The method does not oblige me to sleep a little at night and spend the rest of it in prayer, and no one has obliged me to seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn (4). God, glorified is He, did not say in this verse that there is a specified right in wealth, because the believer here gives more than what has been made obligatory. When a believer volunteers and adds to what God has made obligatory, does he deserve to be blamed, censured, and held to account, or does he deserve to be honored and esteemed? But it is the distortion of the scales of the hypocrites in judging things. For this reason they regarded good deeds as a defect, just like the one who gives his wealth to the poor. We find someone who mocks him, saying: "He is a fool," while the mother of the believers (?) when she gives charity abundantly, he spreads the benefit of his wealth in society, and he is the most intelligent of them, because they spent their wealth on themselves and it perished, while he gave charity from it and it remained.

God, exalted is He, says:

﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers regarding charity﴾. This has an occasion of revelation. Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf migrated to Medina and left his wealth and everything he owned in Mecca. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) established brotherhood between the emigrants (muhajirun) and the helpers (ansar), so that each man of the Ansar had a man of the Muhajirun who would share his wealth with him.

When Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf came, his brother from the Ansar said to him: "I will share my wealth with you." He said: "May God bless you in your wealth. Show me the market." He went to the market, and God blessed his trade. He would divide his profit into two halves: half for charity and half for his family. Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, I have earned eight thousand dirhams. I lend four to God and keep four for my family." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "May God bless you in what you lent and in what you kept." When Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf died, they counted his wealth, and there was disagreement over its estimate. The heirs wanted to satisfy his fourth wife, whose name was Tumadir, by giving her eighty thousand dirhams. Since Tumadir was one of four wives, and the four wives inherit one eighth of the wealth, the value of the wealth was, at the very least, two million, five hundred and sixty dirhams. Abd al-Rahman used to trade only with his own wealth.

When news of what Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf had given in charity reached the hypocrites, they said: "Abd al-Rahman gave in charity only out of showing off and to be heard." And does showing off get seen by people, or does God alone know it? Asim ibn Adi came; he was the owner of an orchard that yielded much fruit, and he brought a hundred loads of dates and gave them in charity. The hypocrites said: "By God, Asim did this only to show off." A man called Abu Aqil al-Ansari came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, I spent my night working, and I earned two sa' of dates. I kept one sa' for my family and brought you the other sa' to give in charity." The hypocrites said: "He gives in charity a sa' of dates. God and His Messenger have no need of your sa', O Abu Aqil."

So they found fault with Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who gave much in charity, and said: "This is showing off." When Asim ibn Adi came, they said: "He is showing off by giving in charity half the fruit of his orchard." When one who owned only a sa' of dates came and gave it in charity, they said: "God and His Messenger have no need of your dates." They mocked the one who gave much and they mocked the one who gave little. Those who give in charity should have been praised, not mocked, because each of them gave according to his ability, and they gave from what God had given them, whether little or much (6).

Therefore, whoever mocks these believers must be blamed for the evil character displayed in responding to the believing conduct with mockery and derision. For this reason the reward of those who mock is that He mocks them and makes for them a painful punishment. Mockery is ridiculing a person's action. These hypocrites, when they mock the believers, their mockery does not go beyond their dissatisfaction with the one who did good, and with their mockery they could only inflict moral harm on the believers who give charity. But when God mocks, first, this is justice in recompense, because it is of the same kind as what they did. But is God's mockery, exalted is He, limited to dissatisfaction, or is there a punishment?

There is a punishment from God. And if the punishment varies with the power of the one who mocks, then there is a vast difference between God's power and human power. Those who mocked the believers when they gave in charity what little they had were confronted by God, exalted is He, who responded to them and to their mockery. God, the Blessed and Exalted, wants by this to give us a picture of how He defends the sincere believers in their faith. If we add to that that the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is the One who will punish the hypocrites, then the punishment will be painful and humiliating.

We said before: whoever wrongs another, that other responds to the wrong with a punishment according to his ability. But if he pardons him, we say to the wrongdoer: do not regard this pardon as being in your favor. On the contrary, it is exactly the opposite, because the one who pardons has left the judgment to God, and your punishment will not be by the power, strength, and capacity of the one who pardoned you, but he has left your punishment to God, and your punishment will be according to God's capacities.

So the one who takes revenge and responds to the one who wronged him takes according to his own strength. As for the one who pardons, he leaves it to God's capacities. There is a higher rank than that which God, exalted is He, has given to the wrongdoer and to the one who was attacked, because the Truth, exalted is He, is Lord of both. If a person wrongs you, you may respond, because the wrong is with your capacity; or you may pardon, and God will respond to him with His power and capacity.

And there is something better than that: that you feel that the one who wronged you has in reality done you good, even though he did not intend it. How? If you enter your house and find one of your sons has struck his brother and wronged him, with whom is your heart and compassion? Your heart is with the one who was attacked and wronged, so you try to please him, bring him a gift, give him some money, or other kinds of appeasement. It has been said: among the manners of Islam is that you do good to one who has wronged you, because he has presented a favor without intending it. For this reason, the Truth, exalted is He, asks you to pardon the one who wronged you. The Truth, exalted is He, says:

﴿so they mock them, and God mocks them﴾. When you hear an action from humans answered by an action from God, beware of understanding God's action the way you understand human action. When He says, exalted is He: ﴿And they plotted, and God plotted...﴾ (3:54), and when He says: ﴿They deceive God, and He is the One who deceives them...﴾ (4:142).

Here we find an action from God's doing, and we may see humans do the same act, but we Muslims take God's action as different from human action.

For example, if we come to God's saying: ﴿And they plotted, and God plotted.﴾ Makr (plotting) is overcoming an opponent by stratagem, by making him think you are doing him good while you are secretly intending him harm, as if you dig a large pit and cover it with some grass and flowers, then ask your opponent to come and fetch you a flower, so he falls into the pit and his bones are broken.

So you have plotted against him with hidden cunning. Plotting and scheming do not indicate strength; they indicate weakness, because the strong brave man openly confronts his enemy, since he is able to deal with his enemy. But the weak man uses trickery and plotting to ensnare his opponent. For this reason, the Truth, exalted is He, says about women: ﴿Indeed, the plotting of you women is great﴾ (12:28). And since their plotting is great, their weakness is great, because weakness is what drives to plotting. But the strong is not incapacitated by his opponent's request, and he says to him: "Go wherever you wish, and I will come to you when I want. There is no place where you can flee from me." Whereas the weak, when he gains power over his opponent, completely destroys him, because he knows it is an opportunity that will not recur.

For this reason the poet said:
"The weak, when he hits an opportunity, kills; likewise the opportunity of the weak."
But the strong one measures and pardons, because he knows he cannot bring his opponent whenever he wants.

The origin of makr is a tree whose branches are intertwined, as if braided, so that you cannot distinguish which branch a leaf you see sprouted from, and the matter becomes confused for you. Likewise makr confuses matters for you, so that you do not know where the truth lies. You plot according to the measure of your thinking and intellect, but when the Truth, exalted is He, repays you for your plotting, the requital is terrible, because your plotting is exposed before God, while you do not know anything of what God has prepared for you.

God, exalted is He, has granted victory to His Messenger (ﷺ) in open matters in battles, and He also granted him victory in every matter in which they plotted and schemed against him. For example, when the disbelievers stood at the door of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to kill him on the night of the Hijrah, his Lord revealed to him: "Go out and do not fear their plot." He went out (ﷺ) and found them asleep while he was standing; their eyes were open but they could not see. The Messenger (ﷺ) passed through their midst, took dust, and threw it on them, saying: "May the faces be disfigured" (7).

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) moved away from the place, they woke up again and wondered how he had escaped them. God, exalted is He, wanted them to know that they would not be able to harm the Messenger of God (ﷺ), neither by open battles nor by hidden plotting.

God's saying, exalted is He: ﴿so they mock them, and God mocks them﴾ shows you that God's mockery came as a requital for their mockery, and the mocker does not, in his action, go beyond finding fault with others. But God's mockery extends to punishment. For this reason the Truth, exalted is He, said: ﴿and theirs is a painful punishment﴾. This is the distinction of God's action from human action. Those who mocked the believers and found fault with what they did, the Truth mocks them on the Day of Resurrection before all His creation, and then adds to that a painful punishment.

We have already known that there is a painful punishment, a great punishment, and a humiliating punishment; all these are attributes of punishment. Punishment is pain, but there are those whom pain terrifies so that they scream, and there are those who try

My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him; and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely protect him. I do not hesitate about anything I do as I hesitate about the soul of the believer, who dislikes death, and I dislike to harm him." Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 80:

We know that the head of the hypocrites, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, was about to be crowned king over Madinah(¹). While preparations for the coronation festival were underway, they were taken by surprise by the arrival of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) as an emigrant from Madinah. This was one of the reasons for ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy's resentment toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for they had lost the kingship. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy had a son who had embraced Islam and whose Islam was sound; his name was also ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. Part of the good Islam of this son was that, when he learned that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was going to order the killing of his father, he went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because his father had said on one of the campaigns(²): ﴿If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it...(8)﴾ (al-Munafiqun).

By "the mightier," Ibn Ubayy meant the hypocrites in Madinah, and by "the meaner" he meant the Muslims, both the Emigrants and the Helpers. God, glorified and exalted, responded by confirming his statement that the mightier would expel the meaner, and He said: ﴿But might belongs to God, to His Messenger, and to the believers...(8)﴾ (al-Munafiqun). It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted, affirmed that the one who would expel the meaner from Madinah is indeed the mightier, but that might belongs to God, His Messenger and the believers. Therefore, the hypocrites will be expelled from Madinah, the believers will remain in it, and honour will be theirs.

When ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy learned that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was going to order the killing of his father ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, he went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, if you must order the killing of my father, then order me to kill him, for I fear that a believing brother will kill him and I will be driven to harm him, and I do not love to harm a believer(³)."

Thus we see the strength and truthfulness of faith. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) wished to honour that hypocrite for the sake of his son, so he did not order his killing. After that(⁴), the son said: "O Messenger of God, ask forgiveness for my father," that is, ask God to forgive him. Because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) knew that he had been sent as a mercy to the worlds, he asked forgiveness for ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. At that point the noble verse was revealed:

﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them, because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, and God does not guide the defiant people.(80)﴾

The scholars paused at this verse over a principle called mafhum al-mukhalafa (the implication of contrary meaning), because the Truth, glorified and exalted, fixed the number of times of unaccepted forgiveness-seeking at seventy. The Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, clarified that since the number of times of seeking forgiveness had been fixed at seventy, he would add a little beyond the seventy(⁵). Thus the noble Messenger gave precedence to the side of mercy and honour toward ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who had embraced Islam and whose Islam was sound.

Seven was always the final limit of number among the Arabs; when another number comes, it is considered an addition. The basis of counting is the repetition of one: one is the origin of number, one is added to it to make two, one is added to both to make three, and the addition continues until the number becomes seven. If we set aside one, since it is the origin, we find three even numbers: two, four and six, and three odd numbers: three, five and seven, and the number seven remains fixed for the singular, the dual and the plural.

For this reason, when they wished to go beyond seven, they would use the conjunction particle. We find the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted, in Surat al-Kahf:

﴿They will say, "They were three, their fourth being their dog," and they will say, "They were five, their sixth being their dog," guessing at the unseen; and they will say, "They were seven, and their eighth was their dog..."(22)﴾ (al-Kahf).

He did not say "their eighth being their dog," but used the conjunction particle, because the eighth belonged to a different category(⁶). When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard "seventy," he said: "We will add to the seventy," and thus he respected God's word and respected his honouring of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who had asked him to seek forgiveness for his father. Here some said: how could the Messenger of God (ﷺ) be unaware of the fact that he himself said: "I am the most eloquent of the Arabs, but I am from Quraysh(⁷)," that the number seventy is meant to indicate abundance, however great it may be? The ancient poet says:

"Treat us ill or treat us well, there is no blame," that is, do as you wish.

It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted, in His words ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times﴾ willed to bring the multiple of the final number, which is seventy, to settle the matter.

And the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted, came: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them...(6)﴾ (al-Munafiqun).

That is: however much you ask forgiveness, with whatever number, God will not forgive them.

We say: the matter here has two parts. The first part: that God forgives. The second part: the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) showing courtesy to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. He (ﷺ) knew that God would not forgive the hypocrites, and his seeking forgiveness was merely a courtesy to respect the son's request. Also, the Messenger's seeking forgiveness was merely a courtesy, because he knew that God would not forgive the hypocrites; for he (ﷺ) knew that his seeking forgiveness for a hypocrite would not be accepted by God. There is seeking forgiveness that results in forgiveness, and seeking forgiveness that results only in satisfying ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. But does the father not have his own individuality?

We say: history tells us that ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy received his share of this world, and the Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good deeds(30)﴾ (al-Kahf).

The reward for deeds is given to some in this world and to some in the Hereafter, in confirmation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter(20)﴾ (al-Shura).

The scholars of the biography (sira) have related to us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Abu Lahab's punishment is lightened on Monday." Abu Lahab was the one about whom the Truth, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. He will burn in a fire of blazing flame.(1-3)﴾ (al-Masad).

Why is Abu Lahab's punishment lightened on Monday? Because this is the day on which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was born, and Abu Lahab rejoiced at the birth of the noble Messenger, so he freed the slave-girl who had brought him the news of the Messenger's birth. From here, Abu Lahab's punishment is lightened on Monday as a recompense for his deed.

Likewise, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy had a position that counts in his favour at the event of al-Hudaybiyya, when the Muslims went out to perform the ʿumrah and the disbelievers prevented them from the Sacred House of God. It ended with the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya, which was the first treaty between faith and disbelief. Although the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions were turned back from the Sacred House of God, Abu Bakr perceived in the day of al-Hudaybiyya the gifts of God: the recognition by the disbelievers of Quraysh of Muhammad and of the Muslims, when they concluded a treaty between them and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and our noble Prophet was free to call to God in the Arabian Peninsula, and he was secure from Quraysh. Islam spread until Quraysh broke the covenant and the conquest of Makkah took place.

Returning to the story of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy on the day of al-Hudaybiyya: the disbelievers knew that there was something in his heart against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because the Messenger's coming had prevented ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy from being crowned king over Madinah. They also knew that he had embraced Islam only hypocritically, so they wished to create a breach in the hearts of the Muslims. They said: "Muhammad and his Companions will not enter, but we will permit ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and those with him to enter Makkah and perform the ʿumrah." But ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy refused and said: "For me in the Messenger of God there is a good example; I do not want us to go for the ʿumrah unless the Messenger of God (ﷺ) goes." This is a position for which he is to be praised.

He also had another position at the Battle of Badr, when al-ʿAbbas was taken prisoner by the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Al-ʿAbbas was tall, and his garments had been torn in the battle, and they could not find anyone tall like him except ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, so he gave them his shirt for al-ʿAbbas to wear, and the Messenger of God did not forget this for him.

For this reason the Messenger of God asked forgiveness for him, but the supreme judgment had come: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them.﴾ It is not enough merely that the Messenger of God seeks forgiveness, for there are things that erase sins: whoever sins must first come to the Messenger of God so that he may seek forgiveness from God, and then ask you to seek God's forgiveness for him, until he finds God Relenting and Merciful. Glorified is He who said:

{If they, when they have wronged themselves, had come to you and asked God's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found God Relenting and Merciful.(64)} (al-Nisa').

So the one who wants to repent and seek forgiveness, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) does not seek forgiveness for him unless the sinner first seeks forgiveness; they must first ask God's forgiveness for their sins, and then the Messenger asks forgiveness for them. The Messenger does not ask forgiveness for those who do not seek it. Thus we know that ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy did not grasp the manner of seeking forgiveness; he should have come to the Messenger of God in humility to seek God's forgiveness in his presence, not look for someone to request forgiveness on his behalf.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted, comes explaining the reason for the non-forgiveness, saying: ﴿That is because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, and God does not guide the defiant people.﴾ When the Truth, glorified and exalted, negates guidance from a person, this does not mean that the defiant person should say: "God did not guide me, so what should I do?" and place the whole matter upon God. Rather we ask the defiant person: why did He not guide you? Because you became defiant.

So, the non-guidance from God toward you was the cause of your taking the path of defiance and turning away from God's method. Hence the guidance meant in this verse is not guidance in the sense of pointing to the path of good, for the pointing to the path of good comes from God to believer and unbeliever alike; God's method, which is conveyed to all people, shows them the path of good and directs them to it. Rather the guidance intended here is the other guidance that the Truth gives to whoever enters the realm of faith, believes and does good deeds, and it is represented in the words of the Truth:

﴿And as for those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety.(17)﴾ (Muhammad).

So whoever walks the path of faith, God helps him in it. On the other hand we read the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted: ﴿Indeed God does not guide the wrongdoing people.(10)﴾ (al-Ahqaf).

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people.(37)﴾ (al-Tawba).

And also His noble saying: ﴿And God does not guide the defiant people.(5)﴾ (al-Saff).

We never say that these people are excused because God did not guide them, for He, glorified is He, has guided them all and pointed them to the path of good, but it is they who took the path of disbelief, wrongdoing and defiance.

And read, if you wish, the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them.(17)﴾ (Fussilat).

Then what did they do with their guidance: ﴿So they preferred blindness over guidance.﴾ That is, the Truth, glorified and exalted, made clear to Thamud the path of good, but they chose error.

So, the guidance of pointing is for all, and the guidance of assistance is for believers.

¹ Ibn Ishaq related in the Sira that the people of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy "had arranged a crown of beads for him so they could crown him and make him their king. Then God sent them His Messenger while they were in that state. When his people turned to Islam he became resentful, and he saw that the Messenger of God had replaced him as king. When he saw his people refusing anything but Islam, he entered it unwillingly, persisting in hypocrisy and resentment." Sirat Ibn Hisham (2/216).

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, gives us another picture of the hypocrites, saying:

﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their seats, against the Messenger of Allah, and disliked to strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah, and said: "Do not go forth in the heat." Say: "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood." (81)﴾

Al-farah (joy) is delight in an act by which the soul is gladdened. Al-mukhallafun (those left behind) are those whom their hypocrisy left behind, and whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left in Madinah when he set out for jihad, after they came to him with the false excuses they had offered. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left them behind because Allah, the Exalted, said:

﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would have added nothing to you but corruption (47)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

Whoever does not want to strive in the way of Allah, even if you take him with you by force, will be against you and not with you. He will spread lies among the believers, try to frighten them about war, and when fighting begins he is the first to flee from the battle, seeking a cave or a rock to hide behind. So he is not with you but against you, for he will not fight alongside you; rather he may well help your enemy against you. At the same time he harms the Muslims and tries to spread terror among them through false rumours.

Here Allah, the Exalted, shows the believing nature of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in that he permitted these people not to go out for jihad even though their excuse was false. Thus His saying: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their seats, against the Messenger of Allah﴾. Al-maq'ad (seat) is the place of sitting. Sitting (al-qu'ud) is a symbol of remaining in any place, while standing (al-qiyam) is a symbol of beginning to leave one place for another. Those who stayed behind sat and did not rise, out of desire to remain in their places.

He says: ﴿against the Messenger of Allah﴾. When we hear the word khilaf, we know its root is kh-a-l-f, khalafa khilafan and mukhalafa, just as you say qatala qitalan and muqatalah. It may be opposition in opinion, as when you say: "So-and-so is in khilaf with so-and-so", meaning each of them has his own opinion. Or it may be in movement, as when you get up to leave a place and your companion or someone with you opposes you by sitting, or you sit and he opposes you by walking away.

Opposition in terms of opinion is an inward act of the heart, while opposition in terms of movement involves the outward form or body. When they rejoiced in sitting after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers had risen for jihad, this is evidence that this sitting coincided with their desires, and they found ease in it. Thus they opposed the condition of faith, because the Qur'an has specified who may rightly stay behind from jihad, in the saying of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger (91)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

And His saying: ﴿nor upon those who came to you that you might provide them mounts, and you said, "I cannot find anything to mount you on" (92)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

That is, they came to you asking for mounts, and you told them that you did not have anything they could ride to reach the battlefield with you.[1] Allah has explained to us the condition of those who did not go out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for these excuses, saying of them: ﴿They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears, grieved that they could not find anything to spend (92)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

So those who stayed behind with genuine excuses are filled with sorrow, and their eyes overflow with tears, because they have been deprived of the reward of striving in the way of Allah.[2] As for those who rejoice at staying behind from jihad, they are hypocrites.

In His saying: ﴿against the Messenger of Allah﴾, we also find that the word khilaf is used in the sense of "after", meaning after the Messenger of Allah. As soon as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out on the expedition, they sat behind him and did not go. They remained with the weak, the sick, and those with genuine excuses; likewise those for whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could not find mounts. These are the ones who stayed behind. Allah then explains the reason for the hypocrites' staying behind, saying: ﴿and disliked to strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah﴾. That is, they disliked fighting and disliked jihad. And it would not have stopped there; rather they wanted to discourage the believers and make them dislike fighting in the way of Allah. ﴿And said: "Do not go forth in the heat."﴾ They were not content with their shameful stance, but set about inciting the believers not to fight. This expedition was the expedition of Tabuk, which took place in the days of intense heat. Madinah was full of the shade of its orchards and their fruit, while the road to the frontier with the Romans was long. So it was an expedition entirely of hardship.[3]

The hypocrites said to the believers: ﴿Do not go forth (la tanfiru)﴾. Al-nufur is aversion to the presence of something. It is said: "So-and-so is repelled by so-and-so," meaning he dislikes being in the same place with him. And it is said: "There is nufur between so-and-so and so-and-so," meaning they each dislike being in the same place. The one who goes out to war is, as it were, repelled from the place where he sits, going to the place of fighting. Fighting and sacrificing wealth and self in the way of Allah is dearer to him than sitting and rest.

So His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And said: "Do not go forth in the heat"﴾ means that they wished to give themselves an excuse for not going out to jihad, because the weather is hot and there is hardship in it. But they were foolish, for if they feared the heat and its hardship and sat in the shade and its comfort, they would have given themselves a pleasure of short duration in order to enter a hardship of long duration.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood."﴾ If they believed that by fleeing the heat they had escaped hardship, then the hardship of the Fire of Hell and abiding in it is far greater. A person who is given good news of things that will please him for a year or years, and then afterwards things come that will distress and torment him, will suffer pain in knowing what is coming and cannot enjoy the present, because a person always tries to endure in order to secure his future. That is why you find someone who works night and day and is happy; if you ask him how he bears this hardship, he says: "To secure my future." So how much more so is the case of a few years of pleasure spoiled by days or years to come full of evil and punishment, and what then of their abiding in the Fire?

But did they say "Do not go forth in the heat" in their thoughts without uttering it, or did they say it to one another secretly? And who told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what they said? We say: this may be what passed through their minds. Allah willed that they should know that He, the Exalted, knows what is in their souls. He willed to expose what is in their inner hearts, and perhaps this puts fear into their hearts, that He is aware of everything, so that they may believe out of fear of the punishment of the Fire.

A similar example is Allah's command when He wanted to prevent the polytheists from performing the pilgrimage to His Sacred House, saying: ﴿The polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs... (28)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

The polytheists, when they went for pilgrimage, revived the economy of Makkah, and goodness came to Makkah from every place in the season of pilgrimage. Indeed they used to say: "Beware of circumambulating the House in garments in which you have disobeyed Allah," as if piety filled their souls! The truth, however, is that they were far from piety, since they worshipped idols. They would say this so that the pilgrims would be compelled to take off their clothes and buy new garments to circumambulate in, and whoever had no money circumambulated naked.

So the pilgrimage was a flourishing economic season for the people of Makkah, through which they earned enough to sustain their livelihood throughout the year. When the declaration came from Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs﴾, the thought that arises in the human soul was: "How then shall we live?" This is the first thought that comes to mind, for it is a question about the means of life. And He who created them knows what passes through their thoughts. And if it was not spoken on their tongues, then the saying of Allah, the Exalted, came: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty... (28)﴾ (al-Tawbah).

So Allah, glorified and exalted, knew what passed through their thoughts, and He answered it before they uttered it.

Similarly is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood."﴾ Fiqh (understanding) is precise comprehension. When you know a thing superficially, you have known it, but when you know it with all its underlying implications, you have understood it (faqihtahu). If you go out for jihad in the heat, you may suffer fatigue; but if you sit back from jihad, your punishment will be greater and your suffering more severe.

So your knowledge of one thing, namely the heat you will face if you go out for jihad, must not make you forget what has escaped you, which is that a person's recoil from jihad leads him into a fire far hotter, in which he will abide forever. This means he did not understand it, for he knew one thing and was oblivious to many others.

From this Qur'anic logic, Imam Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, responded to the people when he called them to fight against the Kharijites, saying: "Now then, jihad is one of the gates of Paradise; whoever abandons it out of aversion will be clothed by Allah in the garment of humiliation, and will be overtaken by affliction, and will be bound to disgrace and the shame of degradation, and will be denied justice..."

Then he said: "If I tell you to march against them in winter, you say: 'This is a time of cold and harshness' (qarr wa sirr), i.e., severe cold. And if I tell you to march against them in summer, you say: 'Give us respite (anzirna), i.e., grant us time, until the heat passes from us.' So if you flee from heat and cold, then by Allah you are in the Fire. O likenesses of men and not men!"[4]

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood"﴾ means that they had rejoiced and been delighted that they did not strive in the heat, but they will regret that greatly, confirming His saying, the Exalted:

﴿So let them laugh a little, and let them weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn (82)﴾.

[1] The cause of the revelation of these verses will come when explaining verses 91 and 92 of Surat al-Tawbah.
[2] From Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You have left behind in Madinah men; you have not crossed a valley nor traversed a path but they shared the reward with you; sickness held them back." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1911), Ahmad in his Musnad (3/300), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2765).
[3] It is also called the expedition of hardship (al-'usrah), in the saying of Allah: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet and the emigrants and the helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾ (al-Tawbah: 117). Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2/396): Qatadah said: "They set out for Syria in the year of Tabuk in the blazing heat, and of the hardship that befell them, Allah knows; a severe hardship struck them, so much so that we are told two men would share a single date between them, and a group would pass one date among them, each sucking it and drinking water after it..." But the hypocrites had stayed behind from going out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the outset.
[4] From a sermon of Imam Ali when Sufyan ibn Awf al-Azdi raided al-Anbar, and the Muslims hesitated to fight them, he said: "Now then, jihad is one of the gates of Paradise; whoever abandons it out of aversion, Allah will clothe him in the garment of humiliation, overtake him with affliction, bind him to disgrace and the shame of degradation, and deny him fairness..." He then said: "When I order you to march against them in the days of heat, you say: 'The heat of summer is fierce; give us respite until the heat passes from us.' And when I order you to march in the cold, you say: 'Give us respite until the cold passes from us.' All this is flight from heat and cold. So if you flee from heat and cold, then by Allah you and the sword are the ones who flee. O likenesses of men and not men, O dreams of children and minds of curtained women!" See his full sermon in the book "Khutab Imam al-Bulaghah," edited by Adil Abu al-Mu'ati, published by al-Rawdah, Cairo.

Laughter and weeping are natural, innate reactions (infital gharizi fitri). Laughter occurs in a person when he encounters something that pleases him, or events in which he finds an incongruity he did not expect. Weeping is likewise an innate reaction to the onset of sorrow or grief, and it is the recollection of what saddens a person. Both are natural phenomena, meaning they arise from one human nature shared by all people, and neither depends on sex, colour or environment. There is no "Russian weeping" and "American weeping," or "Russian laughter" and "English laughter," or "Eastern laughter" and "Western laughter." Laughter and weeping are a uniform natural reaction, unaffected by environment, culture or sex. Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, alone ascribes them to Himself, for He is the One who gives life and the One who causes death. He alone makes one laugh, and He alone makes one weep, in confirmation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And that it is He who makes laughing and weeping (43). And that it is He who causes death and gives life (44). And that He created the pairs, the male and the female (45).﴾ (al-Najm)

Therefore laughter and weeping come without preliminaries. A person does not say to himself, "I will laugh now," and then laugh, nor does he say, "I will weep now," and then weep, because this is a natural reaction in which neither will nor choice plays a part. Sometimes, however, we resort to feigned laughter or feigned weeping, which is mere pretence without reality, and in which artificiality is evident. When a person tells you a foolish joke, which he meant to make you laugh, but you do not laugh, and at the same time you wish to be courteous to him, so you fake laughter, that is, you laugh artificially.
