﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (102)

The words of the Truthful One, ﴿And others﴾, are conjoined to His saying ﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who have become accustomed to hypocrisy﴾. So do they remain upon hypocrisy, or is there among them one who returns to his right mind, so that he finds his position shameful even before himself? For the first thing by which the hypocrite is humbled is that he is humbled before himself, because he committed hypocrisy and was unable to confront, and he regarded himself as less than the one he faces; so he despises himself. And it is inevitable that among them there is one who is disdainful of this position and desires to settle the matter: either he believes or he disbelieves. Then he prefers faith and frees himself from hypocrisy by confessing his sins.

Thus he becomes among those of whom the Truthful One says: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, meaning: among those who did not persist in hypocrisy (1), and acknowledged their sins. Acknowledgment is a kind of admission. Admission of sin is of various kinds: there is one who admits sin out of returning to sense, and another who admits sin in brazenness. Just as you say to someone: "Did you strike so-and-so?" and he says: "Yes, I struck him," which is his acknowledgment of his sin, and he may add: "And I will strike whoever defends him too." This is an acknowledgment that is marked by brazenness.

As for the one who acknowledges out of returning to sense, he admits that he committed the sin and seeks pardon for it, and this is the acknowledgment accepted by Allah. They ﴿acknowledged their sins﴾ as an acknowledgment of returning to sense, as evidenced by the fact that Allah said of them: ﴿They had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad﴾. Their righteous deed here is their admission of sin and their knowledge that the disgrace of this world is easier than the disgrace of the Hereafter; as for their bad deed, it is their staying behind from jihad and from spending.

This acknowledgment of theirs is the acknowledgment of returning to sense. The scholars differed: does this acknowledgment count as repentance or not?

We say: when the Truthful, Exalted One said ﴿They acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad﴾, and then His saying ﴿Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness (2). Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: it is a hope that He will turn to them in forgiveness. These are the preliminaries of repentance, not repentance itself. Its possessor feels remorse for what has passed and resolves not to return in the future, so one looks to see whether this was an act of opposition that deserves exposure, or a conformity to the method of Allah (3).

If the matter was conformity to the method of Allah, then repentance is hoped for them.

The word ﴿mixed﴾ conveys the meaning of joining two things that were separate. Joining two things or several things that were separate has two forms. The first form: that you bring them together while retaining their state of separateness, as when you bring together items that do not blend with one another, such as chickpeas, lupine seeds and fava beans, and mix some of them with others in one container, yet each one remains in its state of separation. You will not make a lupine seed enter a chickpea, and nothing one thing will form from them, for if that happened it would become a blend, not a mixture, just as you mix tea with milk, because once you combine them they become one thing, such that you cannot separate this from that.

So, when they mixed the righteous deed and the bad deed, they did not make the righteous deed and the bad deed into one blend. Rather the righteous deed remained righteous, and the corrupt deed remained corrupt.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾, the word ﴿perhaps (ʿasā)﴾ means hope (4), which is the inclination toward the occurrence of good. It is a kind of expectation of the occurrence of something beloved. Hope differs from wishing, for wishing is that you love something and wish that it existed, but it never comes, like the words of the poet:

Would that youth would return one day, so I could tell it what old age has done.

He wished that his youth would return, and this is evidence that the period of youth is beloved, but that does not happen. So, the manifestation of a beloved thing has two kinds: one that is attainable, and one that is not. That which is attainable is called (hope), and that which is not attainable we call (wishing), like the words of the poet: Would that the stars would draw near to me so I could string them into necklaces of praise for you, though nothing I have is enough for you.

The poet wishes for that to happen, but it will not happen. As for hope, it is an expectation that can happen, and hope has stations and stages with respect to the human soul. When you hope for something for someone, you say: "Perhaps so-and-so will grant you such-and-such." Here you are the one hoping, there is one for whom you hope, who is the one you address, and one from whom you hope, who is the giver; these are three elements.

But do you have authority over the one who grants? No. But if you say: "Perhaps I will grant you such-and-such," then you are hoping that someone else will be granted by you, and this is more likely to be realized. When you say "Perhaps I will grant you," you may say it in a moment of pleasing the one you are speaking with; then something may reach you about him that changes your attitude, or you come to give him something and find nothing to give, and here the hope has not been realized.

But when you say: "Perhaps Allah will grant you," you are hoping for him from Allah, who is capable of all things and whom no changes affect. As for when Allah says of Himself: "Perhaps Allah will do," this is the strongest means of hope.

So we are before four means of hope: that you say "Perhaps so-and-so will grant you," or that you say "Perhaps I will grant you," or you say "Perhaps Allah will grant you," and He may answer me, or may not answer my supplication; but when the Truthful One says: "Perhaps I will do," this is the fourth kind of hope. And they said: hope from Allah is an obligation.

﴿Perhaps Allah will turn to him﴾: this is hope that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. As for the repentance of the servant, it is a matter that requires remorse for what has passed, return to the method of Allah, and resolve not to anger Allah in the future. As for the repentance of Allah, it includes all kinds of repentance: Allah's legislation of repentance is mercy toward the one who committed the sin, and mercy toward the people upon whom the conduct that necessitated repentance fell. If you repent, then the acceptance of repentance is a second mercy. For if Allah had not legislated repentance, everyone who committed a sin would spread it and society would be scorched by its evils; but when Allah legislates repentance, there is hope that the servant will return to Allah, that society will be freed from the possibility of his returning to sin, and he will be finished with causing calamities to others.

When Allah accepts repentance, it is said: "Allah turned toward so-and-so." So for Allah there is more than one repentance. Therefore, when you read His saying, the Truthful One: ﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent…﴾ (118) (al-Tawbah), that is: He legislated repentance for them so that they would repent; when they repent, He, glorified is He, accepts repentance. So repentance has three stages: legislation of repentance, then actual repentance, then acceptance of repentance. Repentance is a return from something, and for the servant it is a return from a sin; and for Allah, if the sin deserves that Allah punish with it, then when you repent, the Truthful One pardons and withdraws the punishment (6).

The Truthful One concludes the verse with: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, because forgiveness is difficult for the servant. If someone steals something from you, it harms you, and the desire to take revenge on him persistently besets you, for the harm follows you. But does anyone weary his Lord by disobedience? No, for if you have harmed someone, you have only harmed yourself, and you have not harmed Allah, glorified is He, because harm does not reach Him through your sin; rather the sin reaches you.

So when He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Forgiving﴾, He is forgiving toward you, and ﴿Merciful﴾ toward you. Calamities are of two kinds: one kind in which the person has a creditor, and another kind that befalls a person with no creditor. If a person falls ill, he has no creditor in the illness; but if a person steals, the thief is his creditor, and a calamity a person has with a creditor pushes the soul to react by returning punishment to him, whereas when the calamity is without a creditor, it is the one that is reckoned with Allah. It is said that the calamity without a creditor is the one that requires strength of faith, and the Truthful One says:

﴿But whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾ (43) (al-Shura)

Here He emphasizes it, because his creditor persists against him; at the moment he sees him he recalls what his creditor did to him, so there is an incitement to evil.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And be patient over what has befallen you; indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾ (17) (Luqman),

He does not emphasize it, for in this calamity who would be his creditor? And those who acknowledged their sins are a people who stayed behind without excuse; then they came and said: we have no excuse. They did not invent excuses, because we know that there were people who did not make excuses, and others who made excuses that were true, and others who made excuses that were false. They ﴿acknowledged their sins﴾, meaning: they declared that their excuses for the expedition were not genuine, and that they had no justification for staying behind from the campaign. Allah turned to these people first within their souls, while the Messenger of Allah was still on the expedition to Tabuk from which they had stayed behind.

Then the Messenger returned from the expedition and entered the mosque as was his custom when returning to Madinah, and the first act he would do after returning was to enter the mosque and pray two rak'ahs in it (8). He found some people who had tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, the columns, so he asked about these people. They said: these are a people who stayed behind and whose excuses were false, but they acknowledged their sins, and they have pledged to Allah not to release themselves until you are the one who releases them and is pleased with them. So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "By Allah, I swear I will not release them, nor will I excuse them, until I am commanded to release them; they turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims" (9). When Allah revealed this verse, the Messenger of Allah released them, and among them was Abu Lubabah.

For this reason, whoever goes to visit Madinah, God willing, will find a column called "the column of Abu Lubabah," for he was the first to tie himself to the pillar, and others imitated him. This shows you that when the matters of faith ferment within the believer's soul, he does not wait to be punished by Allah, but hastens to punish himself.

An example of this: the woman who committed adultery, and the man who committed adultery, and they both confessed to the Messenger of Allah so that he would stone them (10). This means that neither of them waited for Allah to punish them, but each went of his own accord. For this reason, when Sayyidina Umar came and nearly kicked the corpse of one of them, the Messenger said: "Leave her, O Umar, for she has repented a repentance that, if it were divided among the people of the earth, would suffice them" (11).

That Abu Lubabah tied himself to the pillar indicates that when the matter of faith ferments within the believer, he does not leave himself until Allah meets him with His punishment, but says: No, I will punish myself so that I may be saved from the punishment of Allah, for he was certain that there is a punishment in the Hereafter harsher than this punishment. When they acknowledged their sins and examined themselves, asking: What occupied us from the expedition and made us make excuses with falsehood? They found that during the expedition to Tabuk, which took place in the heat, when the Arabs enjoyed sitting in the shade and eating dates, they said: By Allah, wealth is what occupied us from the expedition and led us to commit this sin, and we must give it in charity; therefore we said: this was not the obligatory charity, but rather the charity of expiation.

These people said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: Take this wealth that occupied us from jihad. He did not accept it until a word from Allah came down, and the Truthful One revealed His saying:

﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them; indeed, your prayers are a comfort for them, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (103).

1 Their acknowledgment and repentance for staying behind from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in the expedition to Tabuk.
2 ʿAsā is a rigid verb indicating hope; when the verb is attributed to Allah the Exalted, its meaning is that He has promised that the hoped-for matter will certainly take effect. ʿAsā is among the verbs of hope and is used in several ways, the two most common being: first, that a apparent noun is mentioned after it; second, that a verbal noun (masdar muʾawwal) is mentioned after it.
3 If it conforms to the method of Allah, acceptance comes from Allah.
4 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3169): "This verse, although it was revealed concerning Bedouins, is general until the Day of Resurrection concerning anyone who has good deeds and bad deeds." Ibn Kathir said (2/385): "This verse, although it was revealed concerning specific people, is general to all sinners, those who mix and are defiled." The lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the particularity of the occasion of revelation.
5 Tāba: returned from sins; tāba ila Allah: returned to Him in obedience after disobedience; tāba Allah ʿalayhi: Allah enabled him to repent and accepted it from him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms—indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness﴾ (39) (al-Ma'idah).
6 Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali said in explaining the name of Allah (al-Tawwab): "He is the one who returns to facilitating repentance for His servants time and again, through what He shows them of His signs, and what He sends to them of His admonitions and warnings, and what He reveals to them of His frightening and cautioning, until when they become aware through His instruction of the dangers of sins, they feel fear through His intimidation, and return to repentance; then the bounty of Allah returns to them by acceptance." Al-Maqsad al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna, p. 123, Maktabat al-Qur'an edition.
7 From Abu Dharr, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the sacred hadith: "O My servants, you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me, and you will never reach My benefit so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, it would not increase that in My dominion anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man, it would not decrease from My dominion anything." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2577), Ahmad in his Musnad (5/154, 177), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2495), and likewise Ibn Majah (4257).
8 Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2769) within a long hadith from Ka'b ibn Malik concerning his repentance for staying behind from the expedition to Tabuk with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Ahmad related it in abridged form in his Musnad (3/455), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2773).
9 See the occasion of revelation of the verse in al-Qurtubi's tafsir (4/3168) and al-Wahidi's Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 148).
10 The man was Ma'iz ibn Malik al-Aslami; al-Bukhari related his story in his Sahih (6815) and Muslim (1691). In some of Muslim's chains, Ma'iz said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have wronged myself and committed adultery, and I want you to purify me." As for the woman, she was al-Ghamidiyyah; Muslim related her story (1695).
11 That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered the woman, and she was stoned; then he prayed over her. Umar said to him: "Will you pray over her, O Prophet of Allah, when she has committed adultery?" He said: "She has repented a repentance that, if it were divided among seventy people of Madinah, would suffice them. And have you found a repentance better than giving her soul for the sake of Allah, the Exalted?" Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1696) and Ahmad in his Musnad (4/440).

This is the voluntary charity, not the obligatory one, because if it were the obligatory charity it would not need a new command. Rather, it is the charity of expiation (kaffarah). The words ﴿from their wealth﴾ mean the wealth of those who confessed their sins. He attributed the wealth and its ownership to them, although all wealth belongs to Allah, in confirmation of His saying:

﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you...﴾ (33) (al-Nur).

Yet the Truth transfers it to His creatures by His bounty. Glorified is He: it is as if He said, "Spend something of the wealth which I have given you, and I will not take back what I have given you." For this reason, when a believer needs something from another believer, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan...﴾ (245) (al-Baqarah). He, glorified is He, is the giver of wealth, and He honours the gift He has given to the owner of the wealth.

As for His saying ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾, the scholars have observed that when wealth is attributed to its owner, this is a reassurance to him, so that he moves about in life with more than he needs, and something remains for him to own. Thereby a person is eager for the movement from which others benefit, even if unintentionally. The Truth thus makes clear to him: be assured that everything that exceeds your need will become your property. Wealth does not leave the ownership of its owner unless the owner is not competent to dispose of it (1), in confirmation of the saying of the Truth:

﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth...﴾ (5) (al-Nisa').

Because the foolish person (2) cannot validly own property, since through foolishness he may squander everything. So the Truth decrees: the wealth of the foolish person which he owns is not really his; it is yours. But until when? Then comes the Truth's saying:

﴿But if you perceive in them sound judgment, then deliver to them their property...﴾ (6) (al-Nisa').

That is: return to them their property when they return to sound judgment and become fit for ownership.

In this verse the Truth says: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow.﴾ Allah, glorified is He, is the owner of wealth, and He brings wealth by the means He has placed for mankind in the movement of life. He secures them in their sweat and secures them in what they own, so that no one renounces movement. For if each person took from his own movement only according to his own needs, and did not possess wealth, people would be stingy with effort. And if people are stingy with effort, only those capable of effort would benefit. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, willed that what exceeds people's needs should become their property, because the soul loves to possess, and possession is an instinct in the soul. The evidence is that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, Himself asked that wealth be taken, and made clear that He would multiply it for him. His multiplying it for him means that He develops in him the instinct of possession.

As for His saying ﴿Take from their wealth﴾, we note that the wealth is attributed to its owners, so long as there is no foolishness in their disposal or lack of sound judgment, such as when the heir of the wealth cannot dispose of it. So He, glorified is He, made clear to us: do not regard the wealth of the foolish person or the wealth of the minor as his own; rather, let the guardian (wasi) look after the wealth as if it were his own, and He warned the guardian: beware of transgressing in the ownership of this wealth, for He who made you its owner only made ownership for the sake of supervising the wealth, and until the minor reaches his maturity or the foolish person returns to his reason.

﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made for you a means of support...﴾ (5) (al-Nisa'). So beware, O guardian, of supposing that Allah has given you this wealth; rather, He has given you only the right to supervise it. Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿But if you perceive in them sound judgment, then deliver to them their property﴾, and He did not say, "deliver to them your property," for otherwise the matter would be difficult for people.

Here is an observation the scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, noted: when wealth contains a known right for the beggar (3) and the deprived, a person may not attribute all the wealth to himself, because the beggar and the deprived are partners in it. So the wealth belongs to its owner except for the right of the beggar and the deprived.

In another verse the Truth says: ﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right, for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (24-25) (al-Ma'arij). The "known right" is the obligatory zakat from a nisab of a specified amount. As for the second matter, it is also a right, but what makes it obligatory and determines it is the owner of the wealth upon himself, and it is voluntary. For this reason He did not say "a known right," as in surah al-Dhariyat:

{Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good. They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness, and in their wealth was a right for the beggar and the deprived} (15-19) (al-Dhariyat).

Here He mentioned the right and did not say it is known, because the owner of wealth falls within the station of ihsan (4), which is the station in which a person obligates himself to something beyond what Allah has prescribed, of the same kind as what Allah has prescribed. Allah, glorified is He, did not require a person to stand in prayer all night, or to remain asking forgiveness all night. Rather, the Muslim may pray the 'isha' and sleep, then rise for the dawn prayer. But if he finds energy in himself, he stands in prayer through the night, because he wants to enter the rank of ihsan.

Likewise the Muslim pays zakat, which is a known right. As for if the Muslim desires to enter the station of ihsan, he gives beyond the zakat. Allah has made this a right, but not a known one, so as to leave room for the generosity of the noble to exceed the known right. Thus, instead of two and a half percent, the one who enters the station of ihsan may give double that or more.

The scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, paused here and said: the Truth's saying ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ does not mean that the portion taken from the wealth is the right of the poor; rather, it is the wealth of the one who pays. Had Allah specified the right of the poor and separated it from the wealth of its owner, this would mean that if the wealth were destroyed the poor would have nothing. But because the wealth is the rich man's, the right of the poor is preserved in the liability of the owner of wealth, and this is better for the poor. For if the rich man did not pay the zakat at its time, and afterwards the wealth was destroyed, the rich man is liable for the right of the poor.

﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them﴾. The charity purifies them, because the sin they committed and confessed caused them to defile themselves with disobedience. And since they had defiled themselves with disobedience (5), they need to be purified by the wealth which had been the cause of their not going forth to the campaign.

Observe the feature of "the rhetorical expression" in the Qur'an. The Truth, glorified is He, says ﴿Take﴾, which is a command to the Prophet (ﷺ), and He says ﴿from their wealth a charity﴾, from the wealth of the wealthy. This charity will go to the needy. So here there are four elements: the one who takes is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the one from whom it is taken is the owner of the wealth, the one for whom it is taken is the needy poor person.

And since the command is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this command extends accordingly to whoever is entrusted with any of the affairs of the Muslims. One may say: but it is a charity, not zakat. We reply: since Allah is the one who commanded it as a purification, it has become obligatory, and the verse is explicit. It requires that, so long as there is a legitimate authority, the ruler is the one who takes from the people and gives to the poor, or to the channels of expenditure which Allah has legislated (6). For Allah does not want to humiliate the poor by having him stretch out his hand to take from his neighbours. But if he takes from the ruler, who is responsible for the poor, it will not be a disgrace. Also, the Truth, glorified is He, wants to protect the family of the poor from others knowing that a certain house gives them zakat, so that the children of the recipient suffer humiliation before the children of the giver, and the children of the giver live in a haughtiness for which there is no need. Thus, when the ruler is the one who gives, there will be no one who is superior or who is looked down upon.

But if there is no Islamic authority, and a person does not know where the wealth will go, then it becomes incumbent upon every person to observe the religious environment in which he pays zakat. In that case we have a giver, who is the owner of the wealth, and the giver's wealth goes to the poor.

Upon whom does the Truth's saying ﴿purify them and cause them to grow﴾ return? Superficial thinkers say: it purifies the one from whom we take the wealth and causes the wealth from which we take to grow. But whoever possesses depth of understanding says: since in this verse there are elements, it is necessary that the purification (1) and the growth return to them. It purifies and causes to grow the one who receives, and also purifies and causes to grow the one from whom it is taken, the owner of the wealth, and likewise purifies and causes to grow the wealth taken, and also purifies and causes to grow the one for whom it is taken, the poor, because purification means the removal of filth, and growth means increase.

Filth is an accidental condition upon the thing we wash and purify, and growth is something that returns to it so that it increases. Thus the charity purifies and causes to grow all the elements of the act. Purification has a meaning for the giver, and growth has a meaning for him as well. For if you take wealth from him, it may be that he has mixed into his wealth something doubtful, so the charity and the zakat purify this wealth.

As for how the owner of the wealth is made to grow: if you take from him while he is able, this means you reassure him that if he is in need, you will give to him. Thereby he knows that he does not live in society alone, and he does not fear that his wealth will be lost. He feels reassured at the moment you take from his wealth while he is able, so that you may give to the needy. It is as if you reassure him and say to him: if you were in need, you would not be lost. Thereby you cause his conscience and his trust to grow, and you also purify him from having doubt in his wealth. This is from the side of the owner of the wealth.

As for the side of the wealth itself, charity purifies the wealth, because doubtful matter may become mixed into the wealth, so zakat purifies it.

It may seem to you that when you take from the wealth it decreases, contrary to usury (riba) which increases wealth. For example, usury achieves an increase so that a hundred pounds becomes a hundred and ten, while for the one who pays zakat, a hundred pounds becomes ninety-seven and a half. The superficial person thinks that zakat diminishes wealth and usury increases it. But this is by human measures, not by the measures of the One who owns things. The zakat which you consider a loss causes growth, and usury which you consider growth actually diminishes. The Truth says:

﴿Allah destroys usury and causes charities to grow...﴾ (276) (al-Baqarah).

So there are human measures, and there are other measures with the Truth. What you see as a loss to you is with Allah an increase, and what you see as an increase to you is in reality a loss. How? Because people only look at the positive provision and think that this is provision; they do not recall that there is a provision called "the provision of subtraction." Positive provision may increase your income, for example from a hundred to a hundred and ten. But the provision of subtraction is represented in that you spend only seventy instead of a hundred, so thirty remains for you, in addition to its preventing you from the channels of evil. This is in terms of wealth.

And the Truth says:

﴿And whatever you give in usury to increase the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah. But what you give in zakat, seeking the countenance of Allah, those are the ones who receive multiplied reward﴾ (39) (al-Rum).

How can charity be a purification for the recipient when he has committed no sin that needs purification, but rather the giver gave to him because he is needy? We reply: when the recipient takes from the wealth of another, while he is unable to earn, he is purified of resentment toward the one who has blessing, because some of the wealth of the one who has blessing has reached him, so he does not resent him or envy him. If he sees good in him, he prays for him to increase, because some of that good returns to him.

The farmers in the countryside of Egypt give one another some of the milk of their livestock, or some of the good that comes from its milk, and when one of them passes by the people of the village they ask Allah to protect it. In this way the soul of the poor person is purified of resentment and envy.

This is concerning purification. What about purification (tazkiyah) and growth? When the poor person sees himself as poor, and sees that the community of faith takes care of him and does not leave him alone, and people of goodness hasten to his aid, his soul grows through reassurance, because he is in a community of faith. Thus the Truth's saying ﴿purify them and cause them to grow﴾ refers to all the elements in the verse.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And pray for them﴾, that is: invoke good upon them. For this reason, whenever a people brought the Prophet (ﷺ) any charity, he would say, "O Allah, bless them." So Abu A[...]

(1) This is what is known as ḥajr (legal restriction on property). Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir on ﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth﴾ (al-Nisa' 5): "From it is derived the ḥajr upon the foolish, and they are of several kinds. Sometimes the ḥajr is due to youth, for a child is deprived of legal capacity of expression. Sometimes it is due to insanity, sometimes due to bad disposal from deficiency of intellect or religion, and sometimes due to insolvency, which is when debts surround a man and his wealth is insufficient to repay them; if the creditors ask the judge to place him under ḥajr, he is placed under ḥajr." (1/452)

(2) The safih (foolish person) is one whose intellect is deficient and who disposes of property badly, according to the Truth's saying ﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth﴾ (al-Nisa' 5), that is, those who dispose of their property badly due to their ignorance or deficiency of intellect. The Truth also says ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?﴾ (130) (al-Baqarah), where it is taken to mean ignorance and levity.

(3) The known right is the prescribed zakat, and the unknown right is what is left to the choice of the soul in giving, in order to reach the station of ihsan according to its generosity with Allah.

(4) Ḥasuna (to be good) means to become good and beautiful. The Almighty said ﴿And excellent companions they are﴾ (69) (al-Nisa'), that is, they became good companions. "Aḥsan" is the comparative form, its feminine being "al-ḥusnā." The Truth said: {Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it} (18) (al-Zumar), and said: {And to each Allah has promised the best} (95) (al-Nisa'), that is, the rank which is the best of ranks. Ihsan is sincere generosity and pure giving. Ihsan to parents is honouring them, and it is the highest station of the servant's approach to Allah.

(5) That is, they made themselves a target of blame and reproach. Imam Malik in his Muwatta' (p. 825) related, from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, as a mursal report, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, the time has come for you to refrain from the limits of Allah. Whoever has committed any of these filthy things, let him conceal himself with the concealment of Allah, for whoever shows us his face, we will enforce upon him the Book of Allah."

(6) The channels of zakat have been specified by Allah in His saying: ﴿Charities are only for the poor and the needy, and those employed to collect them, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and for freeing captives, and for those in debt, and for the cause of Allah, and for the traveller, an obligation from Allah; and Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ (60) (al-Tawbah). The insights and inspirations of our respected shaykh have already passed in the explanation of this verse. For the ruler who applies the law of Allah, it is permissible to take from the wealth of the Muslims to establish the edifice of justice in society, in confirmation of the meaning of the verses.

(7) Ṭahura (to purify) means to be free of filth and dirt, sensibly and morally. The soul is purified when it is safe from moral afflictions and is free from hypocrisy, resentment and every vice. The Almighty said: ﴿And if you are in a state of impurity, then purify yourselves﴾ (6) (al-Ma'idah), which refers to physical matters. His saying ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ (103) (al-Tawbah) means that their hearts are cleansed from moral afflictions, and this concerns non-physical matters.

(8) Maḥaqahu (to destroy it) from the pattern of fataḥa means to diminish it, or annul it, or destroy it. The Almighty said: ﴿And Allah destroys the disbelievers﴾ (141) (Al 'Imran), that is, He destroys them. And He said ﴿Allah destroys usury﴾ (276) (al-Baqarah), that is, He diminishes it or destroys it, the opposite of what is done with charities.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 104:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful? (104)﴾

﴿Did they not know﴾ consists of three words: the interrogative hamzah, "lam," a particle of negation, and "ya'lam" (know), which is a verb. Does Allah here intend to negate knowledge from them, or to affirm knowledge for them? He, glory be to Him, has used the hamzah that they call "the hamzah of denunciatory interrogation" (hamzat al-istifham al-inkari), and denunciation is a negation; when a negation enters, it becomes an affirmation, meaning "let them know."

Why did He not present the matter as a command? We say: when the Truth presents it in the form of a question, He is confident that the answerer will answer only in this way, and instead of being a command from Allah, it becomes an acknowledgment from the listener.

﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance﴾: why did the Truth use the word ﴿huwa﴾ (He), when He could have said, "Did they not know that Allah accepts repentance," and the style would not have been disturbed?

I say: the Truth willed to bring the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), just as we say: "So-and-so is able to do such-and-such for you." This statement does not prevent someone else from being able to accomplish the same deed. But when you say: "So-and-so is the one who is able to accomplish such-and-such for you," this means that there is no one else. This is the pronoun of separation, which signifies exclusivity and restriction (al-ikhtiṣāṣ wal-qaṣr) and prevents sharing.

Therefore the Truth said: ﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance... (104)﴾ (repentance).

Was there any suspicion that anyone other than Allah accepts repentance? No, rather everyone knows that we repent to Allah, and we do not repent to the Messenger of Allah. When we survey the methods of the Qur'an, we find that the pronoun of separation or the pronoun of exclusivity is what prevents sharing in what follows it with others. It is clear in the story of our master Ibrahim (Abraham), when he said:

﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?" (70) They said, "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them." (71) He said, "Do they hear you when you call (on them)? (72) Or do they benefit you or harm you?" (73) They said, "Rather, we found our fathers doing so." (74) He said, "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, (75) you and your forefathers? (76) Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds (77)"﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

Our master Ibrahim did not say, "They are enemies," but gathered them all into one group and said: ﴿Indeed, they are an enemy to me﴾. And ﴿innahum﴾ (indeed they), as we know, is plural, then he says after it ﴿'aduww﴾ (enemy), which is singular, so our master Ibrahim treated them as if they were one thing. Some of the people of Ibrahim worshipped a single God, and another group worshipped idols and said they were partners of God. So the forms of worship among the people of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, took two kinds.

Since there were those who worshipped Allah along with partners, Ibrahim's statement might be interpreted as including Allah in the enmity; therefore our master Ibrahim made an exception and said ﴿Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning that Allah, glory be to Him, is not an enemy of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and that the enmity is restricted to the idols. But if his people worshipped gods other than Allah, that is, did not worship Allah at all, Ibrahim would not have made an exception.

The exception here is evidence that some of his people were those who said:

﴿We do not worship them except that they bring us nearer to Allah in position (3)﴾ (al-Zumar).

Thus our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, disavowed the partners, saying ﴿Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds﴾, and this is precise, calculated speech. He added:

﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me (78)﴾ (al-Shu'ara') and he did not say, "Who created me guides me," but left "created me" without "huwa" and specified Allah alone for guidance when He said ﴿fa-huwa yahdin﴾ (and it is He who guides me); because "huwa" comes only where there is a suspicion that you see a partner to Him, whereas in the matter of creation no one claims that he created anyone. Creation is not claimed, and therefore he did not say "Who He created me."

And the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who says: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah..." (87)﴾ (al-Zukhruf).

So there is no creator except Him, glory be to Him. Therefore, a matter that no one other than Allah claims does not take the pronoun. But a matter in which someone is claimed to share with Allah takes "huwa" to specify it as His alone, as in ﴿who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾. No one may insert his nose into this matter, because no one has claimed that he created anyone. The exclusive form here came in the domain of guidance by the method of the Truth, through laws from creation. It is possible for a human to say: "I set the laws that make mankind happy, benefit society, and eliminate its afflictions." We say: No, He who created us alone, glory be to Him, is the One who guides us by His laws.

Therefore, what is not claimed does not take "huwa," but what may be claimed takes "huwa." And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And He who feeds me and gives me drink (79)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

He also brought the pronoun of separation here, because a person may be satisfied by his father when he brings him food and drink, and so he may think the father is a partner with Allah. Therefore He brought ﴿huwa﴾. If you attribute every provision that your father brings to him, you would end up at what your father did not provide, because everything that has a cause among humans ends at what humans have no causes for. So everything is from Allah. Therefore our master Ibrahim said:

﴿And He who feeds me and gives me drink (79), and when I am ill, it is He who cures me (80)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

He also specified healing, so that no one would think the physician is the one who heals, forgetting that Allah alone is the Healer; the physician is only a treater. Therefore you find that we may take a person to a physician and he dies in the physician's hands. Hence a poet says about death:

If it sleeps (i.e., death) from you, what benefit is any medicine?
And if it does not sleep, then medicine is among its underlings.

The physician may give a patient medicine, and the patient dies because of it. Our master Ibrahim brought the restriction in healing to Allah, so that no one would think that healing lies in any hand other than the hand of Allah, glory be to Him. Then our master Ibrahim says:

﴿And He who causes me to die (81)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

He did not say "huwa yumītunī" (He causes me to die), because death is a matter that belongs to the Truth alone. Someone may say, "It should have said 'huwa yumītunī'," and we say: note that death is not the same as killing; death occurs without a defect in the structure, while killing occurs only with a defect in the structure. And the Truth adds on the tongue of our master Ibrahim:

﴿And He who causes me to die and then gives me life (81)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

Also He did not say "huwa yuḥyīnī" (He gives me life), because this matter is beyond any imagined partnership in it. He brought "huwa" in matters where a partnership might be suspected, and this is speech weighed in the balance: ﴿And He who I aspire will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense (82)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

He did not bring "huwa" here either, because forgiveness is owned by no one but Allah.

Thus every matter known not to be shared is brought without "huwa," and every matter that may be claimed is brought with "huwa."

Here the Truth says: ﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. The apparent form would be: "Did they not know that Allah accepts repentance *from* His servants," but He left "min" and brought "'an." Some say that particles substitute for one another, so "min" may stand in place of "'an." We say: No, because it is the speech of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, and no particle in it substitutes for another particle, since the meaning of repentance is that a sin has occurred and the wrongdoer has become liable to punishment. If Allah accepts the repentance, then He has passed over the punishment. Therefore the statement from the Truth came specified: ﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance﴾, meaning: passing over punishment by accepting repentance.

Here "'an" came in its proper meaning, because He, glory be to Him, is the One who accepted the repentance, and He is the One who passed over the punishment.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and takes charities﴾. It is true that Allah is the One who said to the Messenger: ﴿Take﴾, but the Messenger is only a conduit to the hand of Allah, and "yaʾkhudh" (takes) here means "yatakabbal" (accepts). Read the word of the Truth: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs (15), receiving what their Lord has given them (16)﴾ (al-Dhariyat).

That is, receiving from the One who gave them, Allah. An example of this is what is related about Lady Fatimah, when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered upon her and found her polishing a dirham, which is a coin of silver. Silver is among the metals that do not rust, and silver in its origin is soft, so they mix it with another metal that gives it some hardness; the metal that gives hardness is the one that oxidizes, so the silver rusts. Therefore our lady Fatimah was polishing the dirham. When the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, entered upon her, he asked: "What is this?" She said: "It is a dirham." He asked her why she was polishing the dirham. She said: "I thought I would give it in charity, and I know that charity, before it falls into the hand of the poor, falls into the hand of Allah, so I love that it be shining."

Our lady Fatimah did this because she knew that Allah alone is the One who takes the charity.

﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants, and takes charities, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?﴾ This whole verse is a negation of the suspicion that they might doubt, if they did such a thing with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and the Messenger of Allah took the charities, that their repentance had been accepted; rather, the One who accepts repentance is Allah, and the One who takes charities is Allah, for He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. Therefore after that the Truth's statement came:

﴿And say: "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do." (105)﴾

1 The acts that proceed only from Allah, glory be to Him, in which the creature has no part, are not brought with the pronoun of exclusivity, such as His saying: ﴿Who created me (78)﴾ (al-Shu'ara'). But if an act is claimed by some to be done by them, the Qur'anic style responds with the pronoun of exclusivity, because guidance is from Allah, and the servant has no part in it except acceptance and commitment.
2 In this He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And who forgives sins except Allah...﴾ (Al 'Imran: 135).
3 This agrees with what al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir (4/3176): "His saying, the Exalted, 'huwa' is an affirmation of the singularity of Allah, glory be to Him, in these matters. The realization of that is that if He had said, 'Indeed Allah accepts repentance,' it would not be excluded that the acceptance of the Messenger is an acceptance from Him; so the verse establishes that, which no prophet or angel reaches."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 9, verse 105:

So: they declared their repentance after acknowledging their sins, mixed a righteous deed with another evil one, tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, and said: "We will not release ourselves until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) releases us," and they said: "Take from our wealth a charity to purify us." All of this created a dividing line between a past they regret and a future they are now beginning, which has just been born. A new page has been opened, so will you walk in accordance with the requirements of this repentance or not?

And do not think that your affairs will be in secret only; rather, they will be in the open as well. As for your hidden affairs, Allah will know them; therefore He said: ﴿Allah will see﴾. As for the matters that require the acuteness (fitnah) of prophethood (a gloss: the discernment proper to the Prophet), the Messenger (ﷺ) will see them by his innate nature, with his light, in your conduct. As for the other apparent matters, ﴿the believers﴾ will see them.

We are here before three kinds of action: an action that all the believers see, so adhere to this method so that the believers may bear witness to you by what they see of your deeds. Beware of deceiving the believers, for the Messenger of Allah, by his acuteness, his illumination, his purity and his transparency, will recognize deception. As for if the matter is obscured from the believers and from the Messenger, then Allah is the One who knows.

﴿And say: Work﴾, meaning: work a new work that suits your acknowledgment of your sins, suits your declaration of repentance, suits the fact that you tied yourselves in the mosque, and suits the fact that you gave charity of your wealth: a work by which you resume your lives on a new page. And know that We will be watching your work. Allah watches it in what mankind does not know, which is the intentions; and the Messenger of Allah knows it in what accords with his illumination and radiance. And the believers know it in customary matters. This seeing by Allah, by the Messenger, and by the believers will have no value unless a reward follows it, reward or punishment; it is not merely seeing, but rather the one who sees has the power to reward or to punish. And "to Him you will certainly return." And if in this world you live within the means in which the disbeliever and the believer live, and in which the obedient and the disobedient live, then there is the realm of the unseen, which Allah alone possesses: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ (Ghafir).

So: the penitent will be treated well, as long as he has repented. Perhaps he sinned because of a heedlessness that befell him; he forgot the Last Day, so he needs a renewed reminder of faith.

Therefore He said: ﴿And say: Work, Allah will see your work, and His Messenger and the believers﴾.

His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿will see﴾ mentions the verb once, so the seeing is one, interlocked with itself: ﴿that He may see whether you are on the method or not﴾.

﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾. As for the realm of the unseen, Allah alone is its possessor. As for the realm of the witnessed, the Messenger will know things about you, and likewise the believers know things, and perhaps One who knows all. And He does not reward mere knowledge, but the intention of each person by what he did; and He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this day as a reckoner﴾ (al-Isra').

Therefore the Truth concludes this verse with His saying:

﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ And these who acknowledged their sins, tied themselves to the pillars, and gave charity of their wealth, and in whose case Allah gave His judgment by making the Messenger of Allah the one who releases their bonds from the pillars, and accepted their charities, are not alone: there are other people who did the same thing but did not tie themselves to the pillars of the mosque, nor acknowledged their sins. Therefore there comes His saying, the Truth:

﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah: either He punishes them or He turns to them in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.﴾ (106)

1 Because the Messenger has qualities befitting him: infallibility, trustworthiness, conveying (the message), and acuteness.

2 On the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "If one of you were to work inside a solid rock that has no door and no window, his work would come out to the people, whatever it may be." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/28), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (4/214), who declared it sound and al-Dhahabi agreed. It was also narrated by Ibn Hibban (1942 – Mawarid al-Dhaman). And in the hadith the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware the insight of the believer, for he sees by the light of Allah." It is narrated from five of the Companions, as far as I have examined, and all of them are not free from criticism. Among them is the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri in al-Tirmidhi's Sunan (3127), where he said: gharib (strange). In it is Mus'ab ibn Salam. The hadith has other routes and narrations.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 106:

The ones intended by this verse are the three whom the Qur'an singles out with special verses, in which it says:

﴿And [He has forgiven] the three who were left behind, until when the earth became narrow for them despite its vastness, and their souls became straitened for them, and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ (At-Tawbah)

These three are Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Marwan ibn al-Rabi'(1). They also stayed behind from the expedition to Tabuk, and they had no excuse at all for staying behind. Each of them owned his mount, and they had their wealth, and they had everything. One of them has related his own account(2), and he explained to us that he had no excuse: "In no day of my life was I more capable in terms of wealth and mount than I was in that expedition. I used to say, 'I will prepare tomorrow,' and I would not prepare, until the caravan departed. Then I said, 'I will catch up with them,' but I did not catch up with them."

These are the three about whom the statement came: ﴿And others [are] deferred to the command of Allah﴾. The word ﴿deferred﴾ (murjawn, or murji'un) means delayed (al-irja' [meaning postponement] is delay). That is, "the judgment concerning them had not yet appeared, because Allah wished to make a matter clear to the people, especially since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not established in the Islamic state a prison in which to isolate a criminal. This was for a wisdom: for you to take the criminal and isolate him from society and confine him in a place is permissible, but the punishment lies in leaving him free while society is imprisoned from him."

Thus the greatness of faith becomes manifest. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) issued a command that the people should boycott them: no one should speak to you, no one should ask about them, not even their relatives, and no one should mix with them in the market or in the mosque.

One of them would deliberately pray near the Prophet (ﷺ) and steal glances to see whether the Prophet was looking at him or not. Then he would go to his cousin's house and climb the wall and say to him, "Do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?" And he would reply, "Allah and His Messenger know best." Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) isolated society from them, but did not isolate them from society. Likewise he isolated them from their wives, which is a matter difficult to control. The Messenger (ﷺ) warned their wives not to draw near to them until Allah brings His command.

﴿And others [are] deferred to the command of Allah: either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness.﴾

For us, it is: either He will punish them or He will accept their repentance. But Allah alone, the Most High, knows the fate of each of them.

So the uncertainty is for us, because they are deferred to the command of Allah, and no judgment has been passed concerning them, neither to the Fire nor to Paradise, and no pardon has been decreed for them. As for their matter, it is known to Him, glorified is He: either He punishes or He turns to them. For every judgment from Allah has an appointed time in which it is born, and for every birth there is a wisdom. There are people whose judgment Allah hastened, and people whose judgment Allah delayed, in order to purify the situation with a purification of education, for themselves and for those who witness them.

This matter continued for more than fifty days, so that they might be disciplined with the discipline that the faithful community imposes on them. Allah did not will to make the judgment clear until this discipline was completed.

When these were disciplined, their discipline would be in the sight and hearing of all the people, so they would take an example from this discipline.

Had Allah hastened the judgment, the matter would have passed without disciplining those who made false excuses and others, so He said: ﴿And others [are] deferred to the command of Allah﴾. Since He, glorified is He, has judged here that they are postponed to the command of Allah, it is not for us to hasten their story until Allah brings about His command concerning them:

﴿And [He has forgiven] the three who were left behind... (118)﴾ (At-Tawbah). Allah wanted to relate to us another story of their circumstances, so He said:

﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as a station of preparation for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before. And they will surely swear, "We intended only good." And Allah testifies that indeed they are liars. (107)﴾

1. Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari was a well-known poet who witnessed the Pledge of al-'Aqabah, missed Badr, witnessed what came after it, then stayed behind at Tabuk. He died in the year 50 AH during the time of Mu'awiyah (al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah 5/309).
As for Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Ansari, he witnessed Badr and what came after it, died during the caliphate of Mu'awiyah, and it was he whose truthfulness became evident in his accusation of his wife of adultery (al-Isabah 6/289). As for Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-Ansari, he is a well-known companion who also fought at Badr (6/76).
2. This is Ka'b ibn Malik, who said: "I was never stronger or more well-off than when I stayed behind from him in that expedition. By Allah, I had never gathered two mounts before, until I gathered them in that expedition... The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out on that expedition when the fruits and shade were pleasant, and I was inclined toward it (i.e., I leaned toward it). So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prepared, and the Muslims with him, and I began to set out in the morning to prepare with them, but I would return without having accomplished anything, and I would say to myself, 'I am capable of that if I want.' This continued with me until the people became earnest... This continued with me until they hastened and the campaign passed me by..." A long hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (2769).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 9, verse 107 (part 1 of 2):

The Qur'an here addresses one of the states of the hypocrites (munafiqun)(١), and their states in relation to faith are many. The Truthful One, glory be to Him, has mentioned among them several things which He introduced with His saying: ﴿And among them﴾, ﴿And among them﴾, and ﴿They swear﴾, ﴿They swear﴾. For this reason the scholars call these "the sayings of repentance" (manahim al-tawbah), such as His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God...﴾ (9:75).
And the saying of the Truth: ﴿And among them are those who abuse the Prophet...﴾ (9:61).
And His saying: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial..."﴾ (9:49). And the Truth said of them also: ﴿They swear﴾, ﴿They swear﴾, ﴿They swear﴾, and they call these "the oath-sites of repentance" (mahalif al-tawbah)(٢). The Truth now relates another state of the hypocrites, of which He had given a parallel earlier. These hypocrites, as we have said, are in conflict in their faculties: a tongue-faculty that professes faith, and a heart-faculty that disbelieves. Combining contradictory faculties is difficult for the self and burdensome; it requires emotional effort, intellectual effort, and physical effort. When they are alone with their devils they say one thing; when they meet those who believe they say another. The Truth relates the first when they declare faith with their tongues, in His saying: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe..."﴾ (2:14). As for when they are alone with themselves, the Truth describes their condition: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you..."﴾ (2:14).
Thus the faculties of their tongues are restrained from saying what they wish when they are with the believers; but when they are with their own brethren they vent the ailment of their faculties and speak a different speech. This is a contradictory matter; therefore the Qur'an earlier described it: {And if they could find a refuge or caves or a place to enter, they would turn toward it while rushing headlong} (9:57). That is: if they found a secure place where the believers could not see them, they would vent themselves, revile the Prophet, revile the believers, and say what they wish. But they do not find this place; they wish they had found a refuge to flee to, or a cave to enter, so that they might vent themselves. Therefore: {they would turn toward it while rushing headlong}(٣), but they do not stop.
Here the Truthful One, glory be to Him, relates another story of their states, saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief...﴾ (9:107).
We know that the word "mosque" (masjid) in its general sense is a place of prostration, and in its specific sense is a place set aside for prostration and prayer alone. If you intend the general meaning, then the whole earth is a mosque(٤), and you may pray in any place and it becomes a mosque, not by the place but by the one who dwells in it(٥); after that you carry on the affairs of life in it. You may pray in a classroom, an office, a factory, a field, or any place where you pursue the means of life.
Thus the place where you pray becomes a mosque by the one who dwells in it. But there is another mosque set permanently for prayer, when a portion of a place is taken and it is said, "it has been reserved to be a mosque," so that no process of life is carried on in it except prayer, and this is a mosque by place. We know that the first mosque founded was the mosque of Quba', and those who built it were the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf. Then the hypocrites wished to vent themselves in the form of obedience, so they built a mosque for harm, which the Banu Ghanm ibn 'Awf built, and by this mosque they intended to rival the mosque of Quba'.
We know how harm occurs between rivals over something, as it happens now exactly, and you hear someone say: "Why did such-and-such neighbourhood build a mosque, and we did not build a mosque?"
Accordingly, every mosque that has this characteristic — the quality of rivalry to obtain reputation, or partisanship toward a faction, or ostentation — this is considered a mosque of harm, because all these matters divide the community of Muslims.
Someone might say: "Is this not a healthy phenomenon?" We say: No. We must know that it is a diseased phenomenon in faith, because when you see a mosque and there are not two complete rows in it, and then a few meters beyond it there is another mosque, and a third mosque a few meters after that, and then a fourth, all these are mosques of harm(٦).
So: "mosque" in its specific meaning is the place that is reserved until it becomes a mosque, in which nothing is practised other than being a mosque. Therefore we find that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he saw a man seeking his lost property in the mosque, said to him: "May God not return your lost property to you"(٧). Because when you enter the mosque you declare the intention of seclusion (i'tikaf), so as to be in the presence of your Lord, and you have outside the mosque enough time to speak about worldly matters.
So: these people wished to vent their hypocrisy under the appearance of one of the manifestations of obedience. They said: "We will build a mosque, and by this we will divide the community of Muslims: one group prays here and another group prays there. If we sit and pray in it, we will be free and speak as we wish; but when we go to pray in the other mosque, we sit there repressed, unable to speak. We want to vent ourselves."
They built the mosque, then asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to pray with them in the new mosque while he was setting out for the expedition to Tabuk. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, excused himself and explained to them: "We are in a condition that does not permit this, but if God wills, on our return from the expedition we will pray in it." After he returned from the expedition, they tried to hold him to his promise and ask him to fulfil his word; then Gabriel descended to him with the verses that explain the account of this mosque, and how it is a mosque of harm, because God knew their intention in it.
The meaning of "harm" (dirar) is from injury (mudarrah), and they intended to take their ease at all times and to keep away from being present with the believers in the mosque where the Messenger of God prays, and they wish to isolate some of them with others, and to speak as they wish in harming the Muslims and dividing the community of Muslims. Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and to cause division among the believers﴾.
So: everything that fragments the community of Muslims is a matter harmful to the interest of Islam, because Islam wishes to make people know that they are a united force, and that the affair of this force be clear. For this reason the Truth permitted the prayers to be performed in any place, but made it obligatory that we pray together on Friday in one place, so that Muslims may rejoice when they see themselves coming to the religion, and each of them meets the other. Therefore this mosque of harm is a means of dividing the Muslims.
Then He, glory be to Him, says:
﴿and in preparation for one who had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾. And "preparation" (irsad)(٨) is watchfulness; therefore it is said: "The people remained in such-and-such a place to lie in wait for so-and-so," meaning they were people awaiting his coming at a place in order to kill him; this is the watchfulness of hatred, not the watchfulness of love. Those who built this mosque set it up as a lookout, watching and waiting for a man who had a previous history of enmity toward the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him(٩), and he is the one who asked them to build this mosque: "Abu 'Amir the monk," whom the Messenger of God named "the wicked" (al-fasiq).
This Abu 'Amir was a man who had become a Christian in the Jahiliyyah, and the Jahiliyyah was not an environment of religions. For instance, a person who travelled to a place and heard of a religion would bring it to call people to this religion and to lead those who followed it; and Abu 'Amir was among those who had become Christian and who had settled in Medina. When the Messenger of God came to nullify all these things in Medina and his leadership was lost, he opposed the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to the point that someone said to him: "I have never seen a people fight you without your fighting with them." When Islam established itself in Medina he fled to Mecca, and when Mecca was conquered he fled to Ta'if; when the people of Ta'if believed, he found no homeland for himself and went to the Byzantines "in al-Sham." Then he wrote to the hypocrites: "Prepare a mosque; I will come to you from the king of the Byzantines, to attack Muhammad, fight him, and expel him from Medina"(١٠).
So: they built that mosque as harm, and disbelief, and division, and watchfulness — that is, lying in wait and expectation — for that monk who would go to al-Sham and come back with troops to war against God and His Messenger. And although they did this, they had the audacity to ask the Messenger of God to pray with them in it, with the aim of establishing this place as a mosque in which people would pray as long as the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, had prayed in it; and they thought this stratagem would succeed. But God, who guards His Prophet and guards his religion from the hypocrites, revealed to him the reality of the mosque.
The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, may overlook some of the hypocrites' conduct for a wisdom: they had adopted Islam in a form of companionship, and he did not expose them at first, lest it be said: "Muhammad fights his own companions"(١١). Therefore the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, knew what others did not know; so he wished to protect Islam from the tongue of one who would not know. But after the matter became clear, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, 'Amir ibn al-Sakan, and Wahshi, who had killed Hamzah, and Ma'n ibn 'Adi, to demolish this mosque, and to make in its place a dunghill (qumamah). Thus the hypocrites were exposed, and they hid their feelings within themselves.
When you see from your enemy an act that you dislike, your first step is to nullify the act for him; this is the first stage. If the act is repeated and he does not desist, you must put him in his proper place. The hypocrites intended by this mosque harm and injury to Islam, and they should have ceased such an act once the Truth had exposed them. But they did not cease, and they went on heedlessly in enmity toward Islam; therefore, just as you first rid yourself of the act, you must rid yourself of the doer. For this reason they became fearful that the deterrent would be directed at the doer, and the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The hypocrites are wary lest a surah be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say: "Mock, [but] indeed God will bring out that which you fear."﴾ (9:64).
We know that the suspicious person almost says: "Arrest me." By his conduct he points to himself, and the Qur'an in another surah says: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. They are as propped-up wood. They suppose every cry is against them...﴾ (63:4).
They behave in this way because suspicion fills their depths(١٢), and whenever one of them sees a believer walking toward a direction, he supposes he has come to discipline him with a beating or to kill him.
The Truth, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿and in preparation for one who had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾. The phrase ﴿before﴾ implies that they have precedents in warring against the Messenger of God with the purpose of harming him, peace and blessings be upon him; but the Truth, glory be to Him, always protects him, and no scheme or war by which they might harm him, peace and blessings be upon him, remained.
There are many examples of this matter. The Qur'an, when it relates to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, the states of the Jews and explains to him: ﴿and they kill the prophets without right...﴾ (2:61).
Does this statement not prompt in his mind the possibility that they might kill him? Indeed, since they had the audacity to kill the prophets, what would prevent them from killing him? But the Truth reassures him, rebukes them, and cuts off their hope, and the Truth's saying comes: ﴿Why then did you kill the prophets of God before...?﴾ (2:91).
His saying ﴿before﴾ here means that this will not happen now, since the situation has changed. Thus God reassured His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and in this way this idea was rendered futile, if they had considered it(١٣).
Likewise, when the Qur'an reveals their intention to do something that they have not yet done, and the Qur'an exposes them by announcing what is in their intention, and from their stupidity they do the exposed act, whereas if they had a little intelligence they would refrain from doing what the Qur'an has exposed them for.
This is seen in one of the occasions on which they swear. If there were among them a man of sound judgement possessing balanced thinking, he would say to them: "You will swear, [saying] ﴿We intended nothing but good﴾, so do not swear, lest the Muslims doubt the Qur'an." And from their stupidity also, they swore about a matter in which they had a choice whether to do it or not, as the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah which they had been facing?"...﴾ (2:142). They had not yet spoken, and the Truth revealed that in a Qur'an recited at every prayer, and...

³ "Jamaha al-faras": it ran off, not restrained by anything, or its rider was overcome so it ran as it wished. God, exalted, said: ﴿they would turn toward it while rushing headlong﴾ (9:57), that is, they would hurry out of fear toward any refuge, nothing turning them back, like unrestrained horses.
⁴ From Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I have been given five things that no one before me was given: every prophet was sent to his own people in particular, but I am sent to all the red and the black; spoils of war were made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me; the earth was made for me pure and a place of prostration, so whichever man is overtaken by prayer may pray wherever he is; I was supported with terror a month's journey ahead of me; and I was given intercession." Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (335) and Muslim (521).
⁵ "Makana" (makan, with the sense of firmness): he is "makin," meaning he is established and firm, stable in position. And "makkana lahu fi al-shay'" means he made him firm in the matter. God, exalted, said: ﴿Did We not establish for them a secure sanctuary?﴾ (28:57), that is, a firm sanctuary; and "amkanahu min 'aduwwihi" means he gave him power over his enemy and made him victorious over him. God, exalted, said: ﴿They had already betrayed God before, so He gave [you] power over them﴾ (8:71).
⁶ This agrees with what al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3180): "Our scholars said: it is not permissible to build a mosque beside a mosque, and it is obligatory to demolish it and prevent its construction, lest the people of the first mosque turn away and it remain empty, unless the quarter is large and its people cannot be accommodated by one mosque, in which case it may be built. Likewise they said: it is not appropriate for two or three congregational mosques to be built in one city, and the second must be prevented; and whoever prays Friday in it, his prayer is not valid." Linguistically, "darra yadurruhu mudarrah wa darran" is a reciprocal form between two: ﴿Let not a mother be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child﴾ (2:233). The establishment of a mosque like this harms the gathering of the Muslims and invites division.
