Related by al-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-yawm wa al-laylah (p. 73), al-Darimi (1/326), and al-Tirmidhi (1321), who said: hasan gharib.
⁸ "Arsada": he prepared and readied. God, exalted, said: ﴿and in preparation for one who had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾ (9:107), that is, a stronghold against the enemies of Islam who were and still are warring against it; so the mosque of harm was a refuge for whoever wished to plot against Islam.

٩ Ibn Hisham mentioned this in his *al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah* in the account of the Battle of Uhud (3/80): "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell into one of the pits that Abu 'Amir had dug for the Muslims, without them knowing. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib took the hand of the Messenger of Allah, and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah lifted him until he stood upright." See also Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* (2/387).

١٠ The story of this man's hypocrisy and enmity towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is mentioned in al-Wahidi's *Asbab al-Nuzul* (occasions of revelation) (p. 149), al-Qurtubi's *Tafsir* (4/3183), Ibn Kathir (2/387, 388), and Ibn Hisham's *Sirah* (3/80). He was the father of a noble Companion, Hanzalah, known as "the one washed by the angels." Hanzalah was martyred on the day of Uhud while in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah), so the angels washed him.

١١ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was keen that people should not say, "Muhammad kills his own companions." This is narrated in the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: Ibn Ubayy said, "By Allah, if we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it." This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and 'Umar stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Leave him, so that people do not say that Muhammad kills his companions." Related by al-Bukhari in his *Sahih* (4905) and Muslim in his *Sahih* (2584).

١٢ On this, the Lord of Might says concerning them: ﴿Their building which they have built will not cease to be a cause of doubt in their hearts...﴾ (al-Tawbah: 110). Ibn Kathir says in his commentary on it: "That is, a doubt because of their committing this shameful act, and it bequeathed hypocrisy to their hearts."

١٣ From 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ used to be guarded until this verse was revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people...﴾ (68) (al-Ma'idah). Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his head out of the tent and said to them: 'O people, go away, for Allah has protected me.'" Related by al-Tirmidhi in his *Sunan* (3046), who described it as gharib (strange/unusual). It is also related by Abu Nu'aym in *al-Hilyah* (6/206), and al-Hakim in his *Mustadrak* (2/313), who declared it sahih.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) says after that:

﴿Never stand you (O Messenger) in it. A mosque founded upon righteousness from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.﴾ (108)

Does His saying, the Truth, ﴿Never stand (lā taqum)(1) in it﴾ mean that the mosque should remain standing but no prayer be established in it? Is ﴿lā taqum fīhi abadan﴾ in the form of a prohibition, meaning "let him not pray in it"? Or is it a report from the Truth that you will never establish prayer in it, because it will have no existence?

His saying, glorified is He, means that this mosque must not have any existence. Then you find that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, will say: ﴿a mosque founded upon righteousness from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it﴾. So the matter is not about the building of the mosque, but about who enters the mosque and maintains it. Here there is a mosque, and there is another mosque. As for the first mosque (2), it was founded upon righteousness, and in it are people who love to purify themselves. As for the mosque of harm, it was built by hypocrites who love to be defiled, because they are the opposite of those who love to purify themselves.

The meaning of love (ḥubb) is the inclination of the nature toward a thing, by which the soul is expanded and becomes light to act upon it.

When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, Allah has praised you for purification (ṭuhūr), so what is this purification of yours?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we perform ablution for prayer and we wash from major impurity (janābah)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Is there anything besides that?"

At this point the people of Quba said: "No, except that when one of us comes out from the privy (ghā'iṭ), he loves to cleanse himself with water (yastanji bil-mā')" (3). Each of them would hold a stone and wipe the place of relieving himself, and then he would lighten his use of water, because water was scarce among them; then he would use water after the stones (4) to complete and perfect his cleanliness. They added: "And we do not spend the night in major impurity, and we do not persist in sin; if sin overtakes us, we hasten to repentance."

﴿They love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾. Here the love is mutual. Nothing is harder on the soul than love from one side only, and this is misery itself. The poet says: "You are the beloved, but I seek refuge in you / Lest I be a beloved who is not loved."

The misery of lovers is that love is from one side only; but when love is mutual from both sides, it is the summit of happiness. Likewise, when enmity is from both sides it reaches the summit of threat and estrangement. When enmity is from one side, it ends quickly; but when it is from both sides, it does not end but rather increases in blaze.

So when love is mutual, you find that the lover, whenever he sees love from his beloved, responds with love, so love grows and increases. This is not so unless the love of the hearts is in what does not change, which is "love for the sake of Allah" (al-ḥubb fī Allāh). If you see love between two people diminishing with the passage of time, know that it is love for other than Allah; and if you see love growing every day, know that it is love for the sake of Allah.

The Truth, glorified is He, says in the story of Pharaoh and Moses: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief...﴾ (28:8). They did not pick him up so that he would become an enemy to them; had this possibility come into the minds of Pharaoh's family, they would have killed him. Rather, they picked him up so that he would be a delight of the eye for them. So look how Allah brings about the deception of those who disbelieve in Him. The family of Pharaoh were the ones who raised Moses; for this reason Pharaoh said to him: ﴿Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed among us for years of your life?﴾ (26:18). But Moses, peace be upon him, did not flatter in the truth, because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who raised him; as for the upbringing of Pharaoh, it had no weight in the balance of the Truth. Enmity might have been light had it been from Moses alone, but Allah willed that enmity not be from Moses only, but from Pharaoh's side too. So He, glorified is He, says: { He will be taken by an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his...} (20:39).

And He, glorified is He, says in the sphere of mutual love: ﴿So Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him...﴾ (5:54).

So when they love Allah, He, glorified is He, responds to the greeting of love with increased love, and they in turn respond to the greeting of love from Him with increased love; and so increase follows increase until we reach the summit of love. But love with Allah has no end. When you read the Qur'an you find His saying, glorified and exalted is He: { Say: Praise belongs to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen...} (27:59).

And He, glorified is He, says also: ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be "Peace"...﴾ (33:44).

Here He did not bring the definite article "al-" (salām), because if it had come with it, He would have restricted peace to one aspect. When you say "I met the man," you have specified the man. But if you say "I met a man," the man may be this one or that one or other than them. When the noun comes indefinite it becomes general, whereas with the definite article it becomes specific.

When the Truth spoke of Yahya, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿And peace upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive﴾ (19:15).

Because He did not want to multiply peace. When Isa, peace be upon him, spoke of himself, he said: ﴿And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾ (19:33).

When a person meets you, he says to you "Peace be upon you (as-salāmu ʿalaykum)," and you reply "And upon you be peace (wa-ʿalaykumu as-salām)." Why? Because "Peace be upon you" means that peace from me is upon you and upon others, whereas your reply "And upon you be peace" means that you have specified this peace for him.

Here is the verse which is the subject of our reflections on greeting, where the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.﴾ This is because the one who loves to be pure always has become intimate with Allah's overflowing bounties upon him (7). As long as all his atoms are pure from both immaterial and material impurities, his receiving apparatus for Allah's overflowings is always fit to receive. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, sends His provisions at every moment, and His provisions to creation never end; and He describes Himself as al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting). So be reassured, for if you wish to sleep, then sleep, for your Lord is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep.

So faith has come not to weary us, as He describes Himself (8): ﴿Rather, both His hands are outspread; He spends as He wills...﴾ (5:64). That is, the creation is reassured that merely by their faith, Allah's provisions and His immaterial and material overflowings will come to them. So purify your receiving apparatus, so that there is no material impurity or immaterial impurity in it. Therefore, when you see a person who has overflowings from the Truth, know that the atoms of his body are built from what is lawful (9), and there is no immaterial filth nor material filth in him; all of this becomes clear in the features of his face, his words, and the goodness of his reception. And if he is dark-skinned, you will find that he captivates you and snatches your heart with his luminosity. You may find a person who is fair-skinned, yet there is no light in his face, because the overflowings of our Lord are not manifest upon him.

And how do the overflowings come? They come through the purification of the soul, because if a person lacks the Lord's overflowings, he must look into his receiving apparatus. Let me give an example with radio broadcasting: radio stations transmit, and whoever owns a sound receiving apparatus picks up the broadcast; but if the receiver is faulty, that does not mean the radio stations are not broadcasting their programs.

For this reason the Truth said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outspread...﴾ (5:64). So be ever keen to receive from your Lord's hand the provision that does not end. The noble hadith says:

"Indeed Allah extends His hand at night to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by day, and He extends His hand by day to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by night, until the sun rises from the west" (10).

Night may end for one person and begin for another, and likewise day; but the night is continuous and the day is continuous. His hands, glorified is He, are always outspread and never closed.

1 qāma yaqūmu: to rise upright without limping; it is used metaphorically for uprightness in conduct. Qāma bil-makān: to remain in a place in any state, like aqāma. Related by Ahmad (6/108, 133), Abu Dawud in his Sunan (40), al-Nasa'i (1/41, 42), and al-Daraqutni (1/54). So the people of Quba would add water after these three stones, stone after stone, out of their intense care for purity.
5 On this the Truth says: ﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said: "A delight of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son," while they did not perceive﴾ (28:9).
6 From Abu Hurayrah who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs; if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7405) and Muslim (2675).
7 Because they abstained from impurities both material and immaterial, and adorned themselves with purity and worship, so Allah manifested Himself upon them with His overflowing and light.
8 This is because the Jews described Allah, glorified is He, as miserly, not spending, and they said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained; their hands are chained and they are cursed for what they said...﴾ (5:64). The two Shaykhs, al-Bukhari and Muslim, related in their Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The right hand of Allah is not diminished by continuous spending by night and day. Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not decreased what is in His right hand, and His Throne is upon the water, and in His other hand is the scale; He raises and lowers." Related by al-Bukhari (7419) and Muslim (993).
9 From Abdullah ibn Amr that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, the likeness of the believer is like the bee which eats what is good and produces what is good." Related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/199).
10 Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2759) and Ahmad in his Musnad (4/395, 404), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.

Then He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Is one who founded his building upon piety from Allah and approval better, or one who founded his building on the edge of a crumbling cliff, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (9:109)

His saying ﴿Is one who﴾ is an interrogative, as if He is saying: How can you equate a mosque founded upon piety from the first day with a mosque that was taken for harm, for disbelief, for dividing the community of the Muslims, and as a station of observation for whoever fought Allah?

They are never equal. When the Truth presents this matter in the form of a question, He, glorified is He, is confident that His servant will answer in accordance with what Allah wills.

And His saying, the Truth: ﴿one who founded his building﴾. We find the word "bunyan" (building), which is a verbal noun; "banā" "bunyānan" is not applied to the built thing itself, so we say: "this bayān (exposition) is beautiful," or we say, for example: "the style of this bunyān (structure) is Pharaonic."

Thus, there is a difference between the process of building and the thing that results from this process. The word bunyān is a collective noun of a genus (ism al-jins al-jam‘i), because it is valid for it to be a plural, and its singular is "bunyānah," just as we say "rummān" (pomegranates), whose singular is "rummānah," and "ʿinab" (grapes), whose singular is "ʿinabah," and also "rūm" (Romans), whose singular is "rūmī," where the nisba ya' has entered upon the plural and made it singular. Thus one distinguishes between the one and the many, either by the yā' or by the tā'.

He, glorified is He, has ruled that they should not pray in the mosque of harm, and that they should pray in the other mosque, which is the mosque of Quba. Then He returns the matter to the believers, so that they may know that what Allah has ruled is what minds accept, and that their judgment agrees with the judgment of their Lord.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿or one who founded his building on the edge of a crumbling cliff, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell.﴾ Here there are three words: shafā, jurf, and hār. Shafā is derived from shafah (lip), and "shafā" is the edge and border of a thing. The inhabitants of seashores know that the seas have an undercutting beneath the earth: the water digs for itself a space under the ground and leaves a lip of earth; if a person walked upon it he would fall, because it is the edge that has no base and whose underside is undercut.

"Shafā jurf" means an edge that will collapse, because it is "hār," i.e., not firmly held together. The image is that the water undercuts the shore, producing a lip that has a surface but no base beneath it, and this is what is called "shafā jurf."

The Qur'an has said in another place:

{And remember the favor of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and you became, by His favor, brothers; and you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it...} (3:103)

It is the pit in the Fire, so what is its shape? It must be terrifying.

We know that when they dug wells to draw water, they would place stones in the wall of the well to prevent its collapse, because a well without a wall of stone may collapse through the fall of sand from its mouth. Likewise, the stones prevent any eroded part of the surface of the well from falling into it, and the eroded part is the crumbling edge (jurf hār). Thus was the mosque of harm: it collapses with those in it into the fire of Hell.

The Truth concludes the verse: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ They were wrongdoers through hypocrisy, so Allah did not guide them to good deeds, for Allah does not guide the wrongdoer.

He, glorified is He, says in more than one place in the Qur'an: {And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people} (5:108)

And He says: ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ (2:264).

And He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ (2:258).

Guidance, as we have known before, is of two kinds: the guidance of indication (hidāyat al-dalālah), which is for all creation, by which people are shown the path of good, and they may take it or not, for they are free; so Allah has a guidance that encompasses all, which is the guidance of indication. As for the guidance negated here, it is the guidance of assistance (hidāyat al-maʿūnah).

1 "ʿAlā shafā jurf": on the edge of a well-pit not built with stones. "Hār": crumbling and cracked, or collapsed. "Fa-nhār bihi": the building fell with its builder.
2 The interrogative comes here with the hamzah, which is used to request conception and assent, unlike hal, which is for assent only, while the interrogative particles are for conception only. (al-Itqān fī ʿUlūm al-Qurʾān by al-Suyūṭī, 2/141). The interrogative here is one meaning confirmation, that is, confirming that one who founded his building upon the piety of Allah is better than one who founded his building on the edge of a crumbling cliff.
3 "Assasa bunyānahu": established it upon a strong foundation and firm bases.
4 The collective genus noun: it is a word that has a singular sharing its form and meaning, but the singular is distinguished by adding the feminine tā' at its end or the nisba yā'. Al-Fayrūzābādī said in "Baṣā'ir dhawī al-tamyīz" (p. 277): "Al-bunyān is singular with no plural. Some said: it is a plural whose singular is 'bunyānah', on the pattern of 'nakhlah' and 'nakhl', and this kind of plural may be made masculine or feminine."

Then Allah says:

﴿The building which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts, unless their hearts are cut to pieces. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

The building they built is the mosque of harm (Masjid al-Dirar). They intended by it harm, disbelief and division against those who had waged war against Allah and His Messenger. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had promised them that he would pray in it, but the Truth revealed to him that they intended, by the Messenger's prayer in it, a pretext (dhari'a)(1) and to establish prayer in it as a means of deception.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the Battle of Tabuk, Allah revealed to him: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾ The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent some of his Companions(2) to demolish this mosque. He did not stop at demolition, but commanded that the site of the mosque be made a dunghill, indicating by this, (ﷺ), that the mosque in its first construction had a spiritual impurity, and when physical impurity is placed in it, it becomes purity in comparison with the spiritual impurity; thus it was, as it were, purified of spiritual impurity by physical impurity.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) teaches us that the matter is not one of physical impurities; rather, spiritual impurities are more heinous than physical impurities. A person may guard against physical impurities, but the impurities that penetrate (khamara) hearts, beliefs and emotions are what cause a person misery.

Here Allah says: ﴿The building which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts.﴾ After the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) demolished this building and its site became a place of filth, the matter of this building remained a cause of doubt among them, and they began to fear that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would inflict punishment upon them. They remained in doubt that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) might harm them, and this doubt will not leave their hearts except when those hearts are cut to pieces by death.

Doubt and suspicion have their seat in the heart, and the heart is the second organ in the race of life; the first organ in the race of life is the brain. As long as the cells of the brain are sound, life may return to a person, but in a sluggish way. As for the heart, when it stops, doctors try to restore its movement, either by opening the chest or by massaging the heart so that its pulse returns, and they may succeed as long as the brain cells are sound. The brain in a human being is the master of the whole body, and for this reason you find that Allah has protected the brain with the strength of the protection of the skull bones.

Likewise the spinal cords that control the will of the body: He, glory be to Him, has assured them the highest degree of protection from bones. In fossil excavations we see that skulls are the most durable thing, which indicates that to preserve the brain Allah has given it the strongest bones. As long as the brain, the master of the body, is sound, life may continue, and for this reason the whole body serves the one who manages the body and maintains its upkeep.

If a person is subjected to hunger, he eats from his fat; and if a person misses the time of his meal, when food is offered to him he says: "I have no desire to eat." This is nothing but a scientific expression of what has happened in the body: you have already eaten, so once the time of your meal has passed and you will not eat, your body takes what it needs from the stored fats within it. When the fat runs out, a person takes from his flesh, and when the flesh runs out, a person takes his nourishment from his bones, all so that the master, which is the "brain," may remain protected.

This is why, when the Qur'an presented the matter of Prophet Zakariya, it said in his words: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened(4)...﴾ (Maryam), meaning that the last store of sustenance had nearly come to an end. As for plants, they are the opposite of humans: the master of the plant is its lowest part, which is the root, and the plant strives to preserve its root. If food is withheld from the plant by withholding water, the leaves of the plant begin to wilt, because they give their vitality and water to the root; then you find the stem drying out, because it gives life to the root so that it may continue until a little water or a little nourishment comes, whereupon it returns strong.

The heart is the seat of beliefs and convictions, which are the things that arise from sensible perceptions and form in the fu'ad(5) so as to become convictions that do not float again to debate. As for the intellect, it discusses all matters, and as soon as it finishes being convinced of an idea, it settles in the heart.

Here Allah clarifies for us that this building's effect will remain in their hearts and will never leave them except by one thing: ﴿unless their hearts are cut to pieces.﴾ Hearts are not cut to pieces except by death, and it is as if the doubt arising from this building will continue to pursue them until they die.

Or: ﴿unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾ means: that they be cut to pieces through repentance, regret and grief.

This is a threat to them that their evil deeds do not come from outside; rather, their evil deeds come from their own selves. The presence of doubt in their souls means that it will not allow them to persist in corruption, because of their constant fear of punishment.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ His knowledge, glory be to Him, is comprehensive, so nothing is hidden from Him; His wisdom, glory be to Him, is that He places everything in its proper place.

1 Rayba: doubt and hypocrisy in their hearts.
2 Among them: Malik ibn al-Dukhshum and Ma'n ibn 'Adi. As for Malik, he witnessed Badr. As for Ma'n ibn 'Adi ibn al-Jadd, an ally of the Ansar, he witnessed the Battle of Uhud. (See al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba.)
4 Khamara al-qulub: mixed with them and blended into them.
5 The heart is the pump of blood in the arteries and veins of the body; this is the definition of the substance, while the fu'ad is the mind of the heart, the seat of beliefs arising from perception, in accordance with the words of the Exalted: {So that they have hearts with which they understand} (al-Hajj 46), and His words: {Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?} (Muhammad 24). The term "heart" is applied to the fu'ad, and the term "fu'ad" is applied to the heart; the two are interdependent. The heart reaches belief through perception as an affect; after the affect comes choice through discussing matters, then choice among alternatives, and it ends in conviction.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 111:

Then He, glorified be He, says:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who fulfills his covenant more than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great triumph.﴾ (9:111)

After the Truth spoke about those who stayed behind from the expedition, about those who offered false excuses, and about those whose judgment Allah deferred, and He wished to show, glorified be He, that their hesitation has no importance for Him, because Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has replaced them with better than them in faith and in Islam, beware lest you think that by refraining from the expedition they will harm Islam. No; for the Truth, glorified be He, grants victory

So the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased(1) from the believers their lives and their properties﴾:

The scholars say: how does Allah purchase from the believers their lives and their properties, when it is He who created the lives and He who bestowed the wealth? They said: but Allah's gift to them is not retracted, as evidence that the wealth is Allah's wealth; and when He gives it to a person as a result of his work, He makes clear to him that he is its owner, such that if a brother of yours in religion needs it, I borrow it from you; and He did not say, "I will reclaim it." Glorified be He, the One who says:

﴿Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him many times over? And Allah withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ (2:245)

The Truth has honored the gift to the human being, and has honored his sweat and his effort. As if He, glorified be He, when He granted mankind life, and granted them their lives, declared that they are truly their possession, yet He gave them to them. And when He wishes to take them from you, He does not say that He reclaims them; rather He purchases them from you for a price. Therefore the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed, the merchandise of Allah is precious, indeed the merchandise of Allah is precious, indeed the merchandise of Allah is Paradise," meaning: make its price high.

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties.﴾ The word ﴿purchased﴾ indicates that there is a deal, a process of buying and selling. And if this is Allah's possession, then Allah is the buyer and Allah is the seller, so this matter must have a symbolic dimension. This symbolism is observed in the guardian of an orphan or a foolish person: it may be valid for me to have a thing while I am the guardian of an orphan, so I buy this thing in my capacity, then I sell it in my other capacity; the single person is both the buyer and the seller(2). It is as if Allah gives us this example: "You, without the method of Allah, are foolish; so let Allah sell and let Allah buy."

And what is the price? The Truth specifies it: ﴿that they will have Paradise.﴾ This is the price that does not perish and does not decay; and your bliss in it is according to the capacities of Allah, which have no end. As for your bliss in your life, it is according to your own capacities in the means of Allah. Thus the price is precious.

When the Ansar came to the pledge of 'Aqaba to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha said: "Stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish."

He said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me as you protect yourselves, your wealth." They said: "What then will be ours if we do that?"

What did the Messenger of Allah say? Did he say, "You will conquer the palaces of Busra and Syria, and you will become kings, and the East and the West will open to you"?

He, peace and blessings be upon him, did not say anything of this; rather he said: "Paradise," because everything in this world is trivial in comparison with this price. And they said: "The profit of the sale, we will neither cancel nor seek cancellation"(3). And with the mere conclusion of the covenantal deal between the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Ansar(4), it was possible that one, two, or three would die before Islam reached its portion and its peak. It may be said: "So-and-so died without taking any of the material goods of life." But when he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Paradise," whoever dies enters it.

﴿That they will have Paradise﴾ is the price, and it is a promise of something that comes afterward, but it is a promise from One who possesses the ability to fulfill it; because what undermines people's promises to people is that you may promise something yet your life ends without fulfilling it, or your capacities fall short of execution.

So: the true promise is from the One who possesses and is able, the Living who does not die. Therefore in this verse:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise.﴾

And He says at its end: ﴿a promise binding upon Him in truth.﴾ "Promise" is a verbal noun; where is the verb? We understand: that Allah promised them Paradise, a promise from Him, glorified be He, and He is the One who possesses, and it is a true promise. And when the Qur'an brings a cosmic matter, the believer receives it as something that will certainly happen; and when its time comes and it occurs, it becomes a firm truth, just as He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they will be the victorious.﴾ (37:173)

This is a Qur'anic matter: it happened before and was established in the universe.

And what comes after Allah purchases from the believers their properties and their lives? Here the Truth specifies the task before them:

﴿They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed.﴾ "Qatala" is from the pattern "fa'ala"; "qatala" is other than "qatala" (the simple form). Killing is an act from one side, but "qatala" (the form with a long vowel) implies mutual action, like "shaaraka Zayd 'Amran" (Zayd made a partner of 'Amr). Every "fa'ala" and "tafa'ala" form clarifies to us sharing in the matter: each one of them is an agent, and each one of them is an object. Therefore you find in the usage of the Arabs what shows you that the aspect of agency predominates in one and the aspect of objecthood predominates in the other, but in reality each of them is an agent from one aspect and an object from the other aspect.

For example: a man who traveled in a desert where there are snakes and serpents, and the man did not provoke the snakes or the serpents during his journey, but avoided them; and a serpent, as long as you do not provoke it, does not secrete venom, because the venom of a serpent is secreted only in defense.

And when the serpent sees that you are going to confront it, it uses its venom. So if the man was walking and had the ability to avoid provoking the serpents, not the snakes, then he has "sallama" them (made peace with them).

And the poet says: "The ancient one has made peace with the snakes from him, and the viper and the great serpent."
The viper (al-af'wan) is the terrible serpent. We note that "al-af'wan" is in the accusative, and "al-hayyat" (the snakes) is in the nominative. So: "al-qadam" (the foot) is the object, "al-hayyat" (the snakes) is the subject, and he put "al-qadam" in the accusative; likewise "al-shujm" (the great one), because of the objecthood in the snakes; because if the snakes made peace with the foot, then the foot has made peace with them, as if he said: "The foot made peace with the snakes," then he made "al-af'wan" an appositive to them.

And here the Truth says:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers... in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight﴾ — so whoever fights, either he kills, or he is killed, or he kills and is killed. And in the reading of al-Hasan, he places the second before the first(7), and says: "fayuqtalun wa-yaqtulun" (they are killed and they kill); the matter is a transaction according to His saying: ﴿that they will have Paradise﴾, therefore He places their being killed first, and this is closer to the meaning of the transaction. Also, the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another(8); when the believers come on one side and the unbelievers on another side, the believers are a building, and the Truth is the One who says:

﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as if they were a compact structure.﴾ (61:4)

So if a group of the believers precedes others in being killed, it is as if all were killed. Therefore: when some of the believers are killed, we may read the saying of the Truth according to the reading of al-Hasan and say: "fayuqtalun wa-yaqtulun" (they are killed and they kill); or: when they entered the fighting, they placed in themselves that they would be killed, and did not prioritize the side of safety.

And we all know the story of the Companion who said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "Is there not between me and Paradise only that I meet these, so they kill me?" He said to him: "Yes." So the Companion took out a date that was in his mouth, and entered the fighting as if he were hastening toward Paradise(9).

﴿A promise binding upon Him in truth in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an﴾: this is an affirmation that they will have Paradise; it is a promise from the Truth in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an to those who enter battles in defense of faith.

Every religion in its time has believers who believe in it and enter battles in its defense. Therefore fighting in the way of Allah, in support of the religion and defending it, is not a matter restricted to Muslims; but it was not general among the messengers. The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, was the One who intervened to punish the people of disbelief, and the Messenger would convey, and if his people did not respond to him, Allah, glorified be He, would punish them. The Qur'an says:

﴿So of them We sent a storm of stones upon, and of them was he who was seized by the Blast, and of them We caused the earth to swallow, and of them We drowned...﴾ (29:40)(10)

The Qur'anic matter of fighting in the way of Allah did not come except when the Jews, after our master Musa, peace be upon him(11), asked to fight in the way of Allah: ﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Musa, when they said to a prophet of theirs: "Send for us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah..."﴾ (2:246).

So this is a promise from Allah in the Torah for those who believed in Musa, peace be upon him, and asked for fighting in the way of Allah; and likewise in the Gospel for those who believed in Isa, peace be upon him; and finally in the Qur'an for those who believed in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him(12).

Or: this promise is specific to the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, because it is the trusted community for defending the Word of Allah through human effort. Thus the promise in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an is a promise to the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him; and likewise the Gospel gave glad tidings of this promise to the Muslim community. The evidence for that is the saying of the Truth at the end of Surat al-Fath:

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves...﴾ (48:29).

So religion does not shape the religious person either to harshness or to mercy; rather it shapes him into a disposition suited to the situation of harshness so that he is harsh, and to the situation of mercy so that he is merciful. Had he been shaped only to harshness, he would have been harsh all the time, and had he been shaped only to mercy, he would have been merciful all the time; but Allah willed that He shape the believers to be forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. Therefore religion does not shape people to humiliation or to honor; rather it makes them humble toward the believers and honorable toward the disbelievers.

Thus the believer disciplines himself: he is harsh and merciful, honorable and humble. He is pliable to the method: when the method of Allah requires him to be harsh, he becomes harsh; when the method of Allah requires him to be merciful, he shows mercy; when Allah requires him to be humble toward his brothers in faith, he humbles himself; and when He requires him to be honorable toward the disbelievers, he becomes honorable.

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves...﴾ (48:29)

And the attributes of the believers continue in His saying: ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating...﴾ (48:29)

And in their bowing and prostrating they express the values of loyalty to Allah.

Then He describes them: ﴿seeking bounty from Allah and approval. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration...﴾ (48:29).

They seek nothing but the approval and bounty of Allah, and light shines from their faces(13), because they are people of values. He adds: ﴿That is their description in the Torah...﴾ (48:29), meaning: the Torah brought good tidings that Muhammad would come with a community possessing the faith-based and value-based qualities that are not found among the Jews, those whose materialism dominates and whose spirits are not elevated by religious values. If you look at the distorted Torah, you will not find in it anything about the Last Day; rather all of it is material matters.

As for the Gospel, Christianity brought monasticism, and material things in it are weak; therefore the Qur'an came as a comprehensive method by which life is organized: guarding values and a guarded material base. The world corrupts when values are covered over and recede, or when values exist without material strength to defend them, so the strong oppressor insists on overpowering the spiritual values with his material power, and the imbalance appears in the social structure.

So: we are in constant need of values guarded by material force, and material force guarded by values. Allah informed the people of Musa: "You do not possess moral values, and you take pride in material values; therefore the community of Muhammad will come possessing the values of spirit and material together; they bow, prostrate, and seek bounty from Allah and approval..."

1 Purchase (ishtira'): acquiring ownership through exchange and compensation. "Shara" (to sell) and "ishtara" (to buy) can both mean "to sell" and "to buy"; the buyer gives something and takes its equivalent. "Shara" meaning "sold" occurs in His saying: ﴿And they sold him for a meager price...﴾ (12:20), i.e., they sold him; and "ishtara" meaning "took the goods and paid the price" occurs in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise...﴾ (9:111).
2 This is permissible according to Imam Malik on condition that one does not favor oneself in buying from the orphan's property or in selling to oneself. See Fiqh al-Sunna by Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq (3/334).
3 At that time this verse was revealed. Al-Suyuti mentions this occasion of revelation in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 101, Dar al-Sha'b edition), attributing it to Ibn Jarir al-Tabari from the mursal narration of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi; similarly Ibn Kathir mentions it in his tafsir (2/391), and al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3193).
4 They were seventy-three men and two women from the Aws and Khazraj, among them: Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, and Sa'd ibn 'Ubada; and the two women were Nusayba bint Ka'b and Asma' bint 'Amr.
5 Al-Af'wan: the male of the vipers; the feminine is "af'a," which is the snake.
6 Al-shujja' al-shujma': the huge serpent.
7 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3194): "al-Nakha'i, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read with the object placed before the subject. The rest read with the subject placed before the object."
8 On the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of which strengthens another." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2446) and Muslim in his Sahih (2585), and the wording is Muslim's.
9 A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on the day of Uhud and said to him: "Tell me, if I am killed, where will I be?" He said: "In Paradise." So he threw the dates in his hand, then fought until he was killed. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4046) and Muslim in his Sahih (1899), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.
10 These are four kinds of punishment: "al-hasib" is a very cold, violently blowing wind that carries pebbles of the earth and throws them upon people and uproots them from the ground, with which Allah punished the people of "Ad; "al-sayha" (the cry) that seized the people of Thamud and destroyed them; "al-khasf" (the swallowing up) with which Allah punished Qarun; and "al-gharq" (drowning) by which Allah destroyed Pharaoh and his soldiers, and the disbelievers of the people of Nuh, peace be upon him.
11 This was about a thousand years after our master Musa. The prophet here whom the Children of Israel asked to send them a king to fight with him in the way of Allah is Shamʿun or Shamuʾil, as said by al-Suddi, Mujahid, and Wahb ibn Munabbih, and this is what Ibn Kathir preferred in his tafsir (1/300).
12 Al-Qurtubi (4/3194) said in explaining the verse: "This is information from Allah, exalted be He, that this was in these books, and that jihad and resisting enemies originates from the time of Musa, peace be upon him." And He, mighty and majestic, said on the tongue of our master Musa: ﴿O my people, enter the holy land which Allah has assigned to you, and do not turn back on your heels, lest you return as losers﴾ (5:21), until He said: ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight..."﴾ (5:24).
13 On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed good guidance and moderation are a part of twenty-five parts of prophethood." Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/296) and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4766). Some righteous people said: indeed a good deed has a light in the heart, and a radiance in the face, expansion in provision, and love in the hearts of people. See Ibn Kathir (4/204).
14 Islam combined the intellect of matter through planning with the intellect of spirit through refinement, and from here comes the harmony between the energy of the spirit, the energy of matter, and the energy of the mind; so the message of Islam is the intellect of values. Allah says: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein. Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them. Allah chooses for it whom He wills and guides to it whoever turns back [to Him]..."﴾ (42:13).

The Truth (Allah) then says:

﴿Those who turn in repentance, who worship, who praise, who travel (or fast), who bow, who prostrate, who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and who guard the limits set by Allah. And give good tidings to the believers.﴾ (112)

After the Truth has presented this bargain, who are those who accept it?(2) They are the penitents (al-tha'ibun). Repentance (al-tawbah) is the turning away from any falsehood toward truth.

And from what do these penitents turn?

We know that there is the innate faith (iman al-fitrah). We find this in the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this." Or lest you should say, "Our fathers associated partners with Allah before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ (Al-A'raf, 172–173)

Thus, faith is an innate matter, and disbelief is what comes upon it. We said before that disbelief is the first evidence of faith, because kufr (disbelief) is literally concealment (al-satr)(3). Whoever disbelieves in Allah, Allah forbid, is only concealing his existence, so it is as if his existence is the original state, and then disbelief arises and conceals it. Then someone comes who awakens in a person the feelings of certainty and faith, and the person returns to belief in Allah after removing the veil that has settled over the fitrah.

And "the penitents" (al-tha'ibun): among them are those who repent from disbelief that arose over the innate faith, and who take up the method of Allah in which they believe. From here arises worship (ibadah), which requires the existence of a worshipper and a worshipped, and worship means the worshipper's submission to the commands and prohibitions of the One worshipped.

"The penitents, the worshippers, the praisers": worship is entirely obedience, embodied in applying what the method brings of "do" and "do not do." The method may intervene slightly in your freedom, and you, through the strength of faith, consider this intervention in your freedom a blessing for which you must praise Allah. For if He left you to your own desires, as the guardian of a student leaves his son to his own desires, he fails. But the father who urges his son to study and forbids him from play and idleness, he must succeed.

Thus, the commands and prohibitions here are a blessing, for which we should praise our Lord, and everything Allah brings upon the believing servant the servant must accept as a blessing.

So those who repented from disbelief that arose over the innate faith are penitents who take the method of faith from the One worshipped, and thereby become worshippers of Allah, that is, executors of the commands and distancing themselves from the prohibitions. They know that the commands restrict the movement of the soul, and so do the prohibitions, but they believe his words, peace and blessings be upon him: "Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and Hellfire is surrounded by desires"(4).

When you know that worship, or your connection to it, is a burden on your soul, know that this is for your benefit and that you must praise Allah for it. In this way the believer enters the company of the praisers.

When you believe in Allah, Allah becomes present in your mind, so that your preoccupation with the blessing does not distract you from Him, glorified be He. Beware of being occupied with the blessing to the exclusion of the Blessor. Keep Allah always in your mind. The Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿No indeed! Man does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient.﴾ (Al-'Alaq, 6–7)

Therefore the believer always reflects on Allah and thanks the Giver for the blessing and its effects, such as comfort in a home for the children and in work.

And "the praisers" must also receive every decree of Allah upon them with contentment, because the one who decrees upon them, so long as He has not commanded them with what is not within their power, is Wise, and He, glorified be He, does not decree upon them except what is in their interest. And after the soul is content with what Wisdom has brought upon it. For this reason He, glorified be He, says:

﴿Fear Allah, and Allah teaches you...﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 282)

The Truth continues the attributes of those who accept the faith-bargain, saying: "the travelers" (al-sa'ihun). The meaning of "sa'ih" is one who leaves a place that is his home, where his house, his family, his children and his comfort with people are, and then travels (yasih) to a place where he has nothing at all, where he may be exposed to dangers. The believer does this only because nothing in the universe distracts him from the Creator. The Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿Say, "Travel through the earth and then observe...﴾ (Al-An'am, 11)

Thus, travel (al-siyahah) is comprehensive travel. Travel on the earth is of two kinds: travel of contemplation, to look into the dominion of the heavens and the earth and to derive from the signs of Allah what confirms his faith in his Lord; and travel of gain, by striking through the earth(5) seeking Allah's bounty.

So travel is either travel of contemplation or travel of gain. As for travel of gain, it is specific to those who strike through the earth, who are men.

As for travel of contemplation, it is something shared by men and women, as evidenced by the fact that Allah said this in describing women:

﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submitting, believing, obedient, penitent, worshipping, traveling...﴾ (Al-Tahrim, 5)

So "traveling" (sa'ihat) here is meant as travel of contemplation, or travel that takes place in the company of a husband who strikes through the earth.

It has also been said that travel (siyahah) was applied to fasting, because travel removes you from what you are used to: residence in a homeland, property and family, and fasting removes you from what you are used to: food, drink and desire(6).

So the common ground between men and women is travel of contemplation and the travel of fasting.

Then the Truth, glorified be He, says: "those who bow, those who prostrate," meaning those who establish the prayer. He mentioned only two aspects of the prayer, though prayer includes standing, sitting, bowing and prostration, because bowing and prostration are the two movements specific to prayer, whereas standing may occur outside prayer, and so too sitting. So the two distinctive features are bowing and prostration. And the Truth says: "O Mary, be obedient (uqnti)(7) to your Lord, prostrate, and bow with those who bow" (Al 'Imran, 43), meaning: pray with those who pray. Thus we find that bowing and prostration are the two movements that are specific to the movements of prayer.

Then He, glorified be He, says: "those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong." Enjoining right and forbidding wrong is a responsibility specific to the Muhammadan community, so that it may be the best community brought forth for humankind. The Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿You are the best community brought forth for humankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong...﴾ (Al 'Imran, 110)

So if you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, you must be distant from this wrong, for it is not reasonable to forbid something you yourself practice(8). Thus enjoining right and forbidding wrong is a righteousness or guidance that extends from the self to others, after the self has taken its own share of it.

Enjoining right and forbidding wrong requires that you know the right you enjoin and the wrong you forbid. Therefore you must be a people of specialization in knowing Allah and knowing the limits of Allah, in what is permitted and what is prohibited. As for anyone who comes and inserts himself into the matter, saying, "I enjoin right and I forbid wrong," we say to him: do not place religion and piety at a rank lower than the professions that people of thought and specialists must practice.

Then He, glorified be He, says: "those who guard the limits of Allah." "Limits" (hudud) is the plural of "hadd" (limit). In the Qur'an, limits come in two meanings. The first meaning is guarding the commands, and the Truth follows this with His words:

﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them...﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 229)

Every command in which this is said is a limit of Allah, so do not overstep this limit. The second meaning is keeping away from what is forbidden, so He does not say "do not transgress them," but rather, glorified be He, says:

﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them...﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 187)

The Truth, glorified be He, ends the verse with His words: "And give good tidings to the believers," meaning: give good news to those who follow this conduct, conforming to the certainty and faith they hold, not to those hypocrites who may pray or fast outwardly. The word "wa-bashshir" (give good tidings), "istabshara" (to rejoice), "al-bushra" (good news) and "al-bashir" (bearer of good news) are all from a root that indicates good news that brings expansion and joy to the soul, such that when you see a person's face, you find it bright, its cheerfulness overflowing with happiness.

After that, the Truth speaks of a matter that preoccupied the believers who had fathers upon disbelief. Among the rights of this fatherhood upon the sons is that they seek forgiveness for them, in hope that Allah will forgive them. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, wished to show us that the sanctity of Allah's limits and rights takes precedence over blood kinship and over the feeling of tenderness and mercy. The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, is more deserving that a person be dutiful to Him than to a disbelieving father. And the Truth, glorified be He, has made lineage in Islam itself (a matter of faith).

1 "The penitents": from polytheism, and they do not practice hypocrisy in Islam. "The worshippers": those who humble themselves out of fear of Allah and humility. "The praisers": those who praise Allah in every state, in ease and hardship. "The travelers": those who fast. "Those who bow, those who prostrate": those who pray. "Those who guard the limits of Allah": those who stop at His command (see Tafsir al-Tabari).

2 Our shaykh (the author) highlights here an important meaning in the interpretation of this verse. Only one who possesses these qualities will enter this pledge, but not as a condition, for it is established in the Sunnah that there were those who were martyred without ever having bowed to Allah a single bow, and likewise the Sunnah reports that the martyr is forgiven his sins with the first drop of blood. (Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/131), and its chain was graded good by al-Mundhiri in al-Targhib (2/194).) The commentators have differed about this verse: is it connected to the verse before it, or separate? If connected, its meaning is that only a few rare ones will enter this pledge. If separate, its meaning is that these are attributes of the believers closest to selling their souls and wealth in exchange for Paradise. See Tafsir al-Qurtubi (4/3197).

3 Disbelief (kufr) is of four types: disbelief of denial, by which one does not know Allah nor acknowledge Him; disbelief of rejection (juhud); disbelief of obstinacy (mu'anadah); and disbelief of hypocrisy (nifaq). Whoever meets his Lord with any of these, He will not forgive him... As for disbelief of denial, it is disbelief of the heart and tongue. As for disbelief of rejection, it is that the disbeliever acknowledges in his heart but does not affirm with his tongue, like the disbelief of Iblis and Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: "But when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it" (Al-Baqarah, 89). As for disbelief of obstinacy, it is that one knows Allah in his heart and affirms with his tongue, but refuses to submit to Him out of envy and rebellion, like the disbelief of Abu Jahl. As for disbelief of hypocrisy, it is affirmation with the tongue and disbelief in the heart. Ibn Manzur transmitted this in Lisan al-Arab (root: k-f-r).

4 Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/153, 254, 284), Muslim in his Sahih (2822), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2559), and al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/339), from Anas ibn Malik. Al-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim (17/171): "As for the hardships, they include striving in acts of worship, persistence in them, patience with their difficulties, such as suppressing anger, pardoning, forbearance, charity, kindness to the one who wrongs you, and patience against desires and the like. As for the desires surrounded by the Fire, the apparent meaning is the forbidden desires, such as wine, fornication, looking at a non-mahram woman, the beardless youth, use of musical instruments and the like. As for permissible desires, they are not included in this, but excessive indulgence in them is disliked, lest it lead to what is forbidden, or harden the heart, or distract from acts of obedience, or necessitate preoccupation with acquiring worldly things for spending on them, and the like."

5 Striking through the earth: traveling to seek provision and trade. He, glorified be He, says: "And others who strike through the earth seeking Allah's bounty" (Al-Muzzammil, 20).

6 The fasting person has been called "sa'ih" (traveler) because one who travels in worship travels without provision, but whenever he finds provision [he eats]; and the fasting person does not eat either, so by his resemblance to him he was named a traveler. Ibn Manzur transmitted this in Lisan al-Arab.

7 Qunut: performing obedience in humility and submission, together with acknowledging servitude to Allah.

8 From Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "A man will be brought and thrown into the Fire, and his entrails will spill out in it, and he will go round in it as a donkey goes round the millstone. The people of the Fire will gather around him and say, 'O so-and-so, did you not used to enjoin right and forbid wrong?' He will say, 'I used to enjoin right but I did not practice it, and I used to forbid wrong and I practiced it.'" Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3267) and Muslim with similar wording (2989). And the poet says:

Do not forbid a trait while you yourself practice its like;
Disgrace is great upon you if you do it.

God, the Exalted, says:

﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾

Before Allah, glorified is He, forbade the believers from seeking forgiveness for their hypocrite fathers, He began with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet﴾. If the Prophet is forbidden, then the believers have no right in this matter all the more so; for if Allah had willed to honour any of the fathers for the sake of anyone, He would have honoured the fathers of the Prophet, had they been non-believers.

The phrase ﴿mā kān﴾ (it is not [for]) differs from the phrase "mā yanbaghī" (it is not fitting). When you hear "mā yanbaghī laka an taf'ala dhālik" (it is not fitting for you to do that), this means you have the ability to do it, but it is not proper for you to do so. But when it is said "mā kāna laka an taf'ala" (it was not for you to do), it means that you are not qualified at all to do this.

An example: one says to a very poor man, "mā kāna laka an tashtariya fīdyū" (it was not for you to buy a video), because by virtue of his poverty he is not qualified to buy such a device. But when it is said to another, "mā yanbaghī laka an tashtariya fīdyū" (it is not fitting for you to buy a video), it means he has the ability to buy it, but the speaker sees a reason other than poverty that should prevent the purchase. So there is a difference between negating possibility and negating propriety.

Here the Exalted says: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives, after it has become clear to them.﴾ That is: it is not for the Prophet, nor for the believers, to seek forgiveness for those who died in polytheism and disbelief, even if they were close relatives. This is a matter that is not permissible. And so that none of the believers may argue that our master Abraham, peace be upon him, sought forgiveness for his father, the Exalted brought the gracious statement:

﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was compassionate and forbearing.﴾

Note 1: The phrase "mā kāna" comes in the Qur'an in two senses.
Negation: such as His saying, ﴿You could not have made grow its trees (20)﴾ (an-Naml), and His saying, ﴿It is not for a soul to die except by the permission of Allah (145)﴾ (Āl ʿImrān).
Prohibition: such as His saying, ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah (53)﴾ (al-Aḥzāb), and His saying, ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists (113)﴾ (at-Tawbah).

Note 2: Among what is reported regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse: when the death of Abu Ṭālib approached, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him and found with him Abu Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayya ibn al-Mughīra. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I can testify for you before Allah." Abu Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayya said: "O Abu Ṭālib, will you turn away from the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept presenting it to him and repeating that statement until Abu Ṭālib's last words to them were that he was upon the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and he refused to say: "There is no god but Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will surely seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from it." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire (113)﴾ (at-Tawbah). Reported by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (24).

Thus, our master Abraham (peace be upon him) promised his father what the Qur'an mentions: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He has ever been gracious to me﴾ (Maryam). ﴿Ḥafiyyā﴾ means that the Lord of Abraham loves him and will honour him in his seeking forgiveness for his father.(1)

﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾. Then the Exalted Truth presents the inspiring reason: Abraham possessed qualities of goodness in great abundance, to the degree that Allah, his Creator, says of him: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation…﴾ (An-Nahl 120). That is, the qualities of goodness in Abraham (peace be upon him) are not found gathered in one person, nor in two, nor in three. Rather, the qualities of goodness are distributed among all people. One has the quality of trustworthiness, another is adorned with truthfulness, a third is distinguished by nobility, and a fourth is gifted in knowledge. Thus, Allah always spreads the qualities of goodness among His creation so that there is equality of opportunity among humanity, in professions, crafts, genius and talents, and no person is found in whom all talents are complete, so as to become a gathering of all talents.

But the Truth willed to gather for our master Abraham (peace be upon him) many qualities of goodness, so He said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾. That is, in him (peace be upon him) are the qualities of goodness that are scattered through the nation. Then He gives us the reason that made our master Abraham a nation and a collector of the qualities of goodness in this form: when Allah gives him a command, he carries it out with ʿishq (the highest degree of love), not as a mere obligation that he wants to finish and throw off his back. Rather, he carries out the obligation with ʿishq. Read the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And [mention] when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them…﴾ (Al-Baqarah 124). That is, he carried them out completely. When he fulfilled them, Allah wanted to reward him, so He said:

﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people…﴾ (Al-Baqarah 124).

Thus he is, therefore, one who is made to follow, so that he may be a leader for the people, because he is a model. That is, he shares with people the fact that he is a human being, but he came with complete qualities of goodness, so he became an example for people, so that no one says: "He did good because he is an angel and has a nature other than the nature of humans." No, he is one of the humans. The Exalted Truth said:

﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people…﴾ (Al-Baqarah 124), meaning: an example and a model. An example and a model must be of the same kind, not of a different kind. Allah therefore does not make an angel an example for humans, lest someone say: "Can I do the same as his work?" For this reason, the Exalted and Glorified Truth, in presenting this matter, says: {And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"} (Al-Isra 94). When some people were astonished that our Lord had sent a human as a messenger, the Truth revealed this statement, and He, glorified is He, added: {Say, "If there were upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."} (Al-Isra 95).

So, since you are human, a messenger from among you must be sent to you, so that the example is realised. For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they are confusing [themselves]﴾ (Al-An'am 9).

Let us see how our master Abraham (peace be upon him) completed some obligations with ʿishq. Consider the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House…﴾ (Al-Baqarah 127).

The meaning of raising the foundations is bringing into existence the third dimension, which is height. The Sacred House has length, and this is the first dimension, and it has breadth, which is the second dimension, and by these two the area is determined. As for height, multiplying it by the other two dimensions gives us the volume. Our master Abraham (peace be upon him) established the third dimension, which makes the volume manifest. Some superficial people have said that our master Abraham (peace be upon him) built the Kaʿbah. No, he did not build the Kaʿbah; rather, he raised the foundations that make manifest the volume of the Kaʿbah. The evidence is that when he came, he and his wife Hagar, with the suckling infant Ishmael (peace be upon him), he said: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House…﴾ (Ibrahim 37).

This is proof that the House was known before Abraham (peace be upon him). Hagar and her child Ishmael settled there until he grew up and was able to raise the foundations together with his father. Therefore we say that there is a difference between "al-makān" (the place) and "al-makīn" (the structure). What Abraham did was establish "al-makīn," that is, the building itself, whereas the place (al-makān) was already known.

Let us suppose that a flood came upon the Kaʿbah and demolished it: towards what would we pray? Until we establish the structure. Therefore, this process of building is for the place, not for the structure.

And the Truth says about the Sacred House: ﴿In it are clear signs…﴾ (Al-Imran 97).

"Āyāt" (signs) is plural, and "bayyināt" (clear) is plural. And among the clear signs there came only "the station of Abraham": ﴿In it are clear signs: the station of Abraham…﴾ (Al-Imran 97). That is, "the station of Abraham" is the totality of the clear signs. Because Allah commanded him to raise the foundations, he had to search for means that would help him in raising them, for if he had raised them only as far as his arm could reach, he would not have reached the height of the Kaʿbah above the level that the two arms can reach. Therefore our master Abraham (peace be upon him) reflected and contemplated, and brought a stone to stand upon at the height of the Kaʿbah's walls. This is one of the indications that he carries out the obligation with ʿishq, and in the most perfect manner. For this reason the Truth said:

﴿In it are clear signs: the station of Abraham﴾. In this are clear signs that when a person is charged with a matter, he should not carry out the command merely to end the obligation by any means, but he must perform what he is charged with out of ʿishq, and try to increase it. Thus he performs the "farḍ" (obligation), and what exceeds the obligation is the "nāfilah" (supererogatory act).

And here we are, in the matter of seeking forgiveness: ﴿The request of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was compassionate and forbearing﴾ (At-Tawbah 114).

Here is a pause that clarifies for us the nature of our master Abraham (peace be upon him) as "awwāh" and "ḥalīm." The "awwāh" is one who often grieves and sighs over himself out of fear of Allah, and over people if he sees them in disobedience, speaking to himself about the punishment that will befall them. He occupies himself with the affair of others; this is his innate nature. He is "awwāh" because sighing is a kind of consolation that Allah places in some of His servants to comfort other servants of His.(4)

Therefore the poet says:
"And there must be a complaint from a man of honour,
who consoles you, or soothes you, or grieves with you."(5)
That is: if a human being is struck by a calamity, he complains to a man of honour, who either helps him face the problem or consoles him, so as to bear the calamity with him by sighing for him and sharing in his fatigue over his misfortune. This sighing is a sign of tenderness of compassion and the delicacy of mercy in the human soul.

So Abraham is "awwāh," and this is an innate trait in him that he displays with all people. What then of a relative of his? He must necessarily sigh much, especially if the matter concerns his father. Nevertheless, Allah willed to place Abraham's (peace be upon him) disposition of sighing in its correct place, but Allah made clear to him: beware of seeking forgiveness for your father, for you have no concern with him. The matter is not in the disposition, but in the Lord of the disposition who commanded that.

Here is an important issue that I wish to be clarified among the schools of knowledge and the scholars in the whole world, because it is a matter that causes many problems, and much is raised in it.

The Exalted Truth commanded Abraham (peace be upon him) not to seek forgiveness for his father, after it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah. Since Abraham's father has been described with this attribute, that he is an enemy of Allah, and Muhammad (ﷺ) is from the descendants of Abraham, then why does the Messenger say: "I am the best of the best of the best"?

If we understood the saying of the Truth, "Abraham is an enemy of Allah," this would contradict the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah. And since Abraham's father was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him, and the Truth said: Do not seek forgiveness. Therefore, in the lineage of the Prophet (ﷺ) there is one of the enemies of Allah, and this contradicts his saying (ﷺ): "The best of the best of the best; I have continually moved from the loins of the pure men to the wombs of the pure women."

For this reason we want to clarify this matter with the clarification of scholars, not the clarification of the mob. Let us ask: who is the father? The father is the one from whose lineage you come and who begot you, or the lineage of one from whose lineage you come. Thus there is a direct father, and his father is considered a father to you as well, all the way back to Adam. This is the meaning of the word "father" as we know it. But we find that the Qur'an has addressed it in a much deeper way than our traditional understanding, and the subject "Yūsuf, Yūsuf" was enriched by addressing this root; because the root "ab" (father) came twenty-eight times in this surah. For example, at the beginning of Surah Yusuf there is the saying of Yusuf (peace be upon him): ﴿When Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen eleven stars…"﴾ (Yusuf 4).

After that the surah states that Allah will choose Joseph and teach him the interpretation of events:

﴿And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of [dream] narrations and perfect His favour upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He perfected it upon your two fathers…﴾ (Yusuf 6).

The two fathers intended here are Abraham and Isaac (peace be upon them). Then the Truth said after that: ﴿When they said, "Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we…"﴾ (Yusuf 8).

Then came the saying of the Truth on the tongue of Joseph's brothers: ﴿But we are a group; indeed our father is in clear error﴾ (Yusuf 8). And in the same surah the Truth says of Joseph's brothers: ﴿Kill Joseph or throw him to some land that your father's face may be [turned] to you…﴾ (Yusuf 9).

Then Joseph's brothers pave the way to get rid of him, beginning with dialogue with the father: ﴿O our father, what is [wrong] with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph while we are indeed his advisers? Send him with us tomorrow to eat and play, and indeed we will be his guardians﴾ (Yusuf 11–12). And after they threw him into the depths of the well and returned to their father: ﴿And they came to their father at night, weeping﴾ (Yusuf 16).

This was the eighth mention of the word "father" in Surah Yusuf. Then comes the ninth: ﴿They said, "O our father, we went racing and left Joseph with our belongings…"﴾ (Yusuf 17).

Then the events continue until our master Joseph entered prison, and there he met two prisoners, who told him that they saw him as one of the good-doers, and that they had dreams they wanted him to interpret for them. He said to them: ﴿No food will come to you as provision except that I will inform you of its interpretation…﴾ (Yusuf 37).

He attributes that favour to the Exalted Truth, saying:

﴿That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers. And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob…﴾ (Yusuf 37–38).

Thus he mentioned the names of three of his fathers: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (peace be upon them).

Then Joseph went out of prison for trade and took charge of organising the economy of Egypt. His brothers came to trade, and he recognised them, and the Qur'an relates his meeting with them without them recognising him. He said:

﴿And when he had provided them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father…"﴾ (Yusuf 59).

He also said: ﴿They said, "We will seek to persuade his father about him…"﴾ (Yusuf 61).

Then they returned to their father, asking him to permit them to take their younger brother with them. Jacob (peace be upon him) permitted them to take him after they gave him a covenant from Allah that they would bring him back, unless they were encompassed by a matter beyond their control. They descended into Egypt and asked for provisions.

﴿So when he had provided them with their supplies, he placed the drinking cup in the pack of his brother. Then a caller called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves!" They said, turning toward them, "What is it that you have lost?" They said, "We have lost the king's measuring cup, and for whoever brings it is a camel's load, and I am its guarantor." They said, "By Allah, you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we were not thieves." They said, "Then what is its penalty if you are liars?" They said, "Its penalty is that he in whose bag it is found—he is its penalty…"﴾ (Yusuf 70–75).

They said: {Indeed, he has an elderly father, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers} (Yusuf 78).

Joseph said: ﴿[I seek] refuge in Allah from taking anyone except him in whose possession we found our property…﴾ (Yusuf 79).

Our master Joseph (peace be upon him) instructs them: ﴿Go back to your father and say, "O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew, and we were not guardians of the unseen."﴾ (Yusuf 81).

They return to their father, who rebukes them: ﴿Rather, your souls have enticed you to something…﴾ (Yusuf 83).

Then he instructs them to return once more, saying: {O my sons, go and search for Joseph and his brother.

1 Ḥafiyyā: extravagantly honouring and granting his need in a manner of kindness and gentleness.
