And how does Allah ask us to have harshness against them when He said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you... (159)﴾ (Al 'Imran)?

This negates harshness. I say: let us distinguish between two matters: the matter of harshness in making the proof strong, and the harshness that fighting requires. As for social life, eating together and gentle companionship, these require softness and gentleness.

His saying, the Truth: ﴿and let them find in you harshness﴾ indicates that harshness is not a permanent trait; rather it means that when the matter demands it, it must be present in you. Likewise we have said: Allah did not make the believer naturally inclined to harshness, nor to severity, nor to might; rather He said: ﴿Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves... (29)﴾ (al-Fath).

And He said: ﴿humble towards the believers, mighty towards the disbelievers... (54)﴾ (al-Ma'idah).

The Truth concludes the verse: ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾ Beware lest you understand that you face your enemies of the disbelievers with your numbers and equipment; numbers and equipment are required so that you enter the battle with some assurance. An example of this is one who travels through deserts (6) or barren wastelands (7) or a lonely road, where he may encounter highwaymen; he prepares by carrying a weapon, which gives him only some sense of security, and so it is with numbers and equipment.

As for victory, it comes from the divine support of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. And since Allah is with the righteous, and Allah has a companionship with the righteous, He will surely support them with His aid; for this reason the Truth here said: ﴿that Allah is with the righteous﴾, so that we pay attention that whoever enters the Truth is the one who will behave harshly towards the enemies, and may behave with harshness out of desire for spoils, entering upon the disbeliever with cruelty; and this disbeliever's heart may be ready for faith, so he says: "I have embraced Islam and submitted." But whoever enters upon him will be impressed by the mount of this disbeliever and regard it as spoil (8). Therefore the warning comes in His saying: ﴿that Allah is with the righteous﴾. If he submits and surrenders, then take him captive, and beware of harming him or taking his equipment as spoil; for you did not go out to fight for the sake of booty, or to gain standing in your society as a reward, but you fight when fighting is required, and you conduct yourself with the believing character fitting for one of the righteous towards Allah, and you fight so that the word of Allah is the highest (9), and here is Allah's companionship with you: ﴿that Allah is with the righteous (123)﴾.

So, harshness does not mean that it has become a trait within you; rather your enemy finds harshness in you if the matter requires harshness. If the matter does not require harshness, then gentleness and tranquil conduct must be present in your nature.

For this reason they say: the man, entirely a man, is one who has courage in war and gentleness in peace, and the best of you is one who is fierce in the army and gentle at home, a boy in the house. He does not bring his harshness toward the enemy into the home, to the wife and children, because that would be placing energy in the wrong place.

Thus we understand His saying, the Truth:

﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous (123)﴾ (al-Tawbah). That is: be harsh in your war as fits the situation, because war requires severity and firmness; but beware of using these matters for your own benefit; rather use them for Allah, so that you ensure you are in the companionship of Allah (10).

1 The group of teaching and learning is what is expressed today as moral orientation, and moral orientation is the foundation of faith-based launch; this is what Allah, glorified is He, wants for His call.
2 The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts...? (41)﴾ (al-Ra'd). Ibn 'Abbas said in its interpretation: "Do they not see that We open the land for Muhammad (ﷺ) after land?" This is the preferable interpretation of this verse: his victory of Islam over polytheism, town after town. Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/25).
3 Al-Farra' said: the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and Banu Asad is "ghilzah" with a kasra on the ghayn, and the dialect of Banu Tamim is "ghulzah" with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Zajjaj said: there are three dialects: ghilzah, ghulzah, ghilzah. See Lisan al-'Arab, root (gh l ẓ).
4 Yastanim al-mu'min: that is, the believer is caught off guard, his sleep or his lack of attention to his weapon is exploited. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿The disbelievers wish that you would neglect your weapons and your belongings, so they could come down upon you in one attack... (102)﴾ (al-Nisa'). So neglect of weapons and belongings during fighting is the opportunity the disbelievers long for, to attack the believers in one assault, and take them at once.
5 The origin of ribat is the tethering of horses, which are tied in confrontation with enemies at the frontiers and borders with the enemy, so it carries the sense of lying in wait for the enemy and caution against his treachery. Among what has been reported regarding the excellence of ribat in the way of Allah: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better than the world and what is in it; the place of one of your whips in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it; and a journey or a morning's going forth that a servant makes in the way of Allah is better than the world and what is in it." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2892), Ahmad in his Musnad (5/339), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1664), from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi. The word ribat is also used in meanings such as His saying: ﴿And We strengthened their hearts (14)﴾ (al-Kahf), that is, We made their hearts and resolve firm in faith; they were the people of the Cave.
6 Mafawiz: plural of mafazah, the deadly desert; it is called so because whoever enters it, leaves it and crosses it succeeds (fāza). Ibn Shumayl said: a mafazah is one in which there is no water.
7 Muqfirah: empty of pasture and people.
8 Al-mati-yyah: the camel or she-camel on whose back one rides, that is, mounts. Plural: matayá.
9 From Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: a bedouin man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man fights for booty, a man fights to be mentioned, and a man fights to be seen in his place; who is in the way of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is highest, he is in the way of Allah." In another narration: "...is the highest, then he is in the way of Allah." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (123) and Muslim (1904).
10 From Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Raiding is of two kinds. As for one who seeks the face of Allah, obeys the imam, spends the noble wealth, aids his partner, and avoids corruption, then his sleep and his wakefulness are all rewarded. As for one who raids for pride, showing off, and reputation, and disobeys the imam and spreads corruption on earth, he returns with only the bare minimum." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/234), Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2512), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/49).

And after that He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And when a surah is sent down, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.﴾ (124)

His saying, the Truth: ﴿And when it is sent down﴾ means: when it is revealed. We know that there is "nazala," "anzala," and "nazzala." "Anzala" is for causing to descend (transitive). The Qur'an descended from the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) to the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya). Then the Truth sent it down by stages (nujum) [1]. So "tanzil" means the successive descent of the parts of the Qur'an. The Qur'an was sent down in its entirety, and then, after that, the Truth caused it to descend, and Jibril, peace be upon him, brought it down upon our master Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

This verse brings together the Truth's sending down of the Qur'an from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then the descent of Jibril, peace be upon him, with the Qur'an upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And with truth We sent it down, and with truth it descended... (105)﴾ (al-Isra')

In another verse He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down (193)﴾ (al-Shu'ara').

Here the Truth says: ﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾. A surah is a portion of the Qur'an marked off by a particular designation, or for example: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ and after its end comes another surah beginning with His saying, the Truth: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, and it is derived from "sur," which defines a place [2]. Does the Truth's saying here mean the descent of a complete surah of the Qur'an or the descent of part of the Qur'an? The intended meaning is the descent of part of the Qur'an.

The verse continues: ﴿Among them are those who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ What is meant by this are the hypocrites who turned back from faith. We know that the Qur'an is truth, that it is from Allah, and that it has an enthralling force and an illuminating effect on the purity of the soul. The disbelievers had heard it before and testified to it [3]; as for the believers, when they heard it, it captivated them.

This is because of readiness to receive it, since in all events the matter is not from the agent alone, but from the agent and the one who receives the action — and to Allah belongs the highest similitude. For example, you bring a hammer and strike a piece of iron, and it splits and its surface increases; but if you strike with the hammer a piece of steel that is harder than the hammer, it will not be affected.

Thus, striking is one thing, and the receptivity to being struck is another. So the agent must have a receiver, and what is required of the receiver is that it receive the thing without enmity toward it arising from its heart. If anyone wishes to hear the Qur'an, he must remove from his heart what is opposed to the Qur'an, place the Qur'an and its opposite outside his heart, and listen to this and that; whatever penetrates his heart after this, let him accept it. But if he receives the Qur'an with the hatred of the Qur'an that is in his heart, he will not be affected by it, just as some hypocrites confronted the Qur'an and said: "We were not affected by it."

The reason for this is that there is what is called the container (al-hayyiz), and the non-intermingling within the container. The heart is a container that cannot hold a thing and its opposite. So do not fill your heart with your hatred of religion and then say: "I have heard the Qur'an, and it has not affected me." Here we say to you: remove from your heart what is opposed to the Qur'an, and also place the Qur'an outside your heart, then look at the two so you see what your heart is at ease with. But if you are filled against the Qur'an and then say that the Qur'an has not affected you, this does not mean that you have not noticed the difference between the agent and the receiver, nor that you have not noticed what is called the container and the extent of its capacity to contain.

A bottle with a narrow mouth does not receive water inside it if you plunge it into water, because the narrowness of the mouth does not help the air inside it to exit, nor does it help the water to enter; for the water will not enter unless the air exits. Therefore the mouth of the bottle must be wide, allowing the air to exit and the water to enter, and then you will see the bubbles of air rising above the mouth. If this is so with sensible things, then what of immaterial matters, which are like sensible ones?

Thus: remove from your heart whatever contradicts the truth, leave falsehood and truth outside, then receive the two. In such a state you can only receive the truth. The Truth, glory be to Him, describes those who persist in disbelief: ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts... (93)﴾ (al-Tawba).

That is: what is outside these hearts does not enter them, and what is within them does not exit.

Thus: since the Truth has sealed their hearts, these hearts will not open to faith and will remain holding to disbelief. If among these disbelievers or hypocrites there is one who hears the Qur'an but its clarity does not captivate him, that is because of their inability to look at the meanings and values it contains [5]; for when a person hears the Qur'an and his soul is pure, with nothing in it to disturb the attraction and clarity of the Qur'an that affects him, his soul is at rest with it.

For this reason, when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, heard the Qur'an — and before that he had been severe against Islam — he went to his sister to verify the matter of her Islam, and when blood flowed from her during her emotional attachment to it, then he read the Qur'an and it settled in his heart [6].

Thus: you must first remove what is in your mind in order to receive the Qur'an. So when a surah is sent down, the believer receives it with purity [7]. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, some of them say: ﴿Which of you has had his faith increased by this?﴾ The verse gives the sense that we are before two groups: one that reads and one that listens. We understand from the context of the verse that the one who asks such a question directs it to two groups: one of them weak in faith, or recent converts, or hypocrites — these are the ones who have not removed disbelief, or part of it, from their hearts, and the receptivity of some of them to faith has not yet been confirmed. Of them the Truth said:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you until, when they go out from your presence, they say to those who have been given knowledge, "What did he just say?"... (16)﴾ (Muhammad)

And He says: ﴿And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them... (44)﴾ (Fussilat).

Thus: the agent is one thing, and the receiver is another. They heard the Qur'an, as evidenced by the Truth's saying: ﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾, and the context of the verse suggests that there is a whisper among some of them: ﴿Which of you has had his faith increased by this?﴾ This whispering comes in the tone of one who mocks, and the one who whispers means that his hearing of the Qur'an has added nothing to him and taken nothing away, and he whispers to a hypocrite like himself, or to one weak in faith. ﴿Which of you has had his faith increased by this?﴾ Then Allah answers the psychological matter and teaches us that He, glory be to Him, has divided people into two divisions: a division that is disbelieving or hypocritical, for which the Qur'an increases disbelief [9]; and the believing division, whose receiving of the Qur'an increases their faith [10].

Thus: the agent is one thing and the receiver is different. The scholars stood before this verse with a difference of opinion among them: ﴿And when a surah is sent down, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ Some of them said: faith increases and decreases; others said: faith neither decreases nor increases. A battle of the theologians (ahl al-kalam) arose, and a battle among intelligent people does not spread unless the direction of understanding in the matter they dispute is separate: some of them turn their thought in one direction, and others turn their thought in another direction [11].

As for those who said that faith neither increases nor decreases: at the moment faith shines in the heart, it settles in it — namely faith in Allah, that there is no god but Allah and no worshipped one besides Him, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah who conveys from Him; this faith neither increases nor decreases. The example is the saying of Imam 'Ali, may Allah honor his face: "Were the veil lifted from me, I would not increase in certainty."

As for the scholars who said that faith increases and decreases, they meant by this the application of the requirements of faith from the verses, for every verse requires of one who affirms it that he be a believer in Allah first, and then implement the requirements of the verse.

All Muslims believe in Allah, but in the particulars of application you find one who applies twenty particulars and another who applies thirty; as for the root of faith with which a person accepts the obligation, which is monotheism (tawhid), it neither increases nor decreases. As for these hypocrites, when they said: ﴿Which of you has had his faith increased by this?﴾ — did they discuss that secretly or say it openly? They must have said it secretly, and the Truth, glory be to Him, exposed them. It would have sufficed for them to know that Allah informs the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of everything they conceal; but they were addicted to contentiousness [12], so they said: ﴿Which of you has had his faith increased by this?﴾

The Truth, glory be to Him, responds:

﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.﴾ "Yastabshir" means: joy fills his face, so you see the brightness, the happiness, the expansion — all of which are signs of rejoicing. One who rejoices at a verse of the verses of the Truth is one who understands from the verse something new; joy enters his soul; therefore he is at ease with the descent of new faith-based obligations, so that his reward may grow and increase; whereas one who is otherwise dislikes that a new ruling from Allah should descend.

This is the meaning of "yastabshir."

As for the others, the Truth, glory be to Him, says of them:

﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added to them filth upon their filth, and they died while they were disbelievers (125).﴾

[1] According to the circumstances of the events.
[2] In the technical definition, a surah is a Qur'anic composition containing verses with an opening and a closing, the least of which is three verses. Every surah is a miracle and a sign of Allah the Exalted. Some surahs are long and some short; yet surahs such as al-Kawthar, which has three verses, possess the same inimitability as al-Baqarah. See the detailed proof in al-Zarkashi's al-Burhan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an (1/263, 265).
[3] Among these is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, whom the disbelievers tried to get to describe the Qur'an as soothsaying, confused madness, poetry, or the speech of a magician. He said: "By Allah, it has sweetness, its root is fruitful, and its branch is laden with fruit; nothing you say would be taken as anything other than falsehood." Sirat al-Nabi by Ibn Hisham (1/270).
[4] In fulfilment of His saying: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts? (24)﴾ (Muhammad). The heart is locked by Allah, and without His speech they did not reflect.
[5] Among what Ibn Ishaq narrates in the Prophetic biography: some of the disbelievers of Quraysh went out one night to listen secretly to the Qur'an from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he prayed in his house. They stayed up listening to him, each unaware of the others, until dawn broke and they departed; the road gathered them and they reproached one another, then pledged not to repeat that, yet they returned to listening to the Qur'an several times. One of them, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, asked Abu Sufyan: "Tell me, O Abu Hanzala, your opinion about what you heard from Muhammad?" He said: "O Abu Tha'laba, by Allah, I heard things I recognize and understand what is meant by them, and I heard things whose meaning I did not grasp." Al-Akhnas, wishing to turn the question to Abu Jahl, responded to him: "What did you hear? We and the Banu 'Abd Manaf competed for honor: they fed, and we fed; they gave, and we gave; until when we were level on the knees, like two racehorses, they said: 'Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven; so when will we attain such a thing? By Allah, we will never believe in him." (See Ibn Hisham's Sirah 1/315-346).
[6] The story of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab's conversion is related by Ibn Hisham in the Prophetic biography (1/343, 346), quoting Ibn Ishaq.
[7] On this He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Allah has sent down the best discourse, a Book consistent and repeating; the skins shiver of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills... (23)﴾ (al-Zumar).
[8] Waqr: heaviness in hearing; it is said it is deafness.
[9] As in His saying that follows: ﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added to them filth upon their filth, and they died while they were disbelievers (125)﴾ (al-Tawba).
[10] In fulfilment of His saying: ﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely (2)﴾ (al-Anfal).
[11] Those who said faith neither increases nor decreases looked at the linguistic meaning of faith, namely assent and acknowledgment, which does not admit of decrease. The others looked at faith as assent of the heart, utterance of the tongue, and action of the limbs. Action of the limbs increases and develops the meanings of faith in the servant's heart if it is in obedience; but if it is in disobedience, it diminishes it, meaning it weakens its firmness in the heart. See the detailed treatment in books of kalam and creed.
[12] Contentiousness (lajaja): dispute and quarrelling without right. Lisan al-'Arab, root l-j-j.

Ar-Rijs (filth) is that which is loathsome, and filth may be physical (ḥissī) or moral (maʿnawī). Carrion, for example, is physically filthy, because it has died with its blood still in it. Blood, as we know, has two courses: one course for blood before it is recycled, and another course for blood after it is recycled. Blood before it is recycled passes through the lungs and the kidneys, which purify it of the harmful substances that reach it as a result of the reactions of the body's various organs. After it has been purified through the two lungs and the kidneys, it becomes good blood.

So when an animal dies, its good blood and its bad blood both remain in it. That is why we slaughter an animal before eating it, and let out its blood, the good along with the bad, so that the bad blood does not infect us with diseases. For this reason carrion is considered filth. Wine is also physical impurity. And there is moral filth, which is why the Truth (al-Haqq) said: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it...﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 90).

So there is physical filth and moral filth. The term rijs is also applied to disbelief, and at times it is applied to the whispers and insinuations of Satan.

On this the Truth says:

﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him, and sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby and remove from you the defilement of Satan...﴾ (al-Anfal: 11).

And here the Truth says: ﴿As for those in whose hearts is disease, it has added to them defilement upon their defilement﴾, and because they disbelieve in Allah and His signs, this increases them in defilement over their defilement, and their disbelief becomes compounded. Thus we find good news for the believers, while for the disbelievers there is warning, because their disbelief increases, and they die upon that disbelief.

(1) Ar-rijs: filth and stench, physical and moral. It is applied to what is abhorrent in the Sharia. Rijs and rijz have one meaning. Rijs and rijz are also applied to punishment, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said, "Already there has fallen upon you from your Lord defilement and wrath"﴾ (al-A'raf: 71), and His saying: ﴿So He increased them in defilement over their defilement﴾ (al-Tawbah: 125), meaning moral and psychological filth; and His saying: ﴿But when the punishment (ar-rijz) fell upon them﴾ (al-A'raf: 134), meaning the punishment.

(2) Al-Ansab: everything worshipped besides Allah, such as the idols and images that the disbelievers used to set up around the Ka'bah, worshipping them and slaughtering at them. As for al-Azlam: they are arrows without feathers, on some of which is written "Do" and on others "Do not." If a man wanted to travel or to marry, he would go to the custodian of the Ka'bah, who would say: "Draw for me an arrow." If it came out "Do," he would do it; if it was "Do not," he would not do it. See: Lisan al-'Arab, entry (n-ṣ-b).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 126:

And the Almighty says after that:

﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year, yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed?﴾ (9:126)

His saying, the Truth: ﴿Do they not see?﴾ means: let the hypocrites take as a witness their history with Islam, and let them know that they are tested every year, once by calamities and once by disgrace. We find that the Messenger of Allah, when he sees them, brings some of them out from among the rows and says to them: "Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite" (1). Then, after months, the situation recurs. Here the Truth, glory be to Him, reminds them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sifts them once or twice every year.

The origin of fitnah (trial, a test that separates the sound from the unsound) is that it is an examination and a test. It is not blameworthy in itself, but it is blamed for the outcome that results from it. Thus any examination is not blameworthy, but what is blameworthy is that a person fails the examination. Therefore, affliction or fitnah (2) is not blameworthy in itself; what is blameworthy is that the result comes out contrary to what one desires. They are tested when they see the victory of the Muslims despite their hypocrisy and their plotting against the Muslims. They should have known that they will not be able to obstruct the course of Islam, because it is victorious by Allah. They should have taken heed and repented so that they might attain the good of Islam, for its good extends despite their noses (in spite of them), and the loss will not fall upon Islam, but the loss falls upon those who disbelieve in it.

We know that Islam began among the weak until the strong came to it, and that is the sunnah of Allah in the universe. Indeed, we find that at the beginning of the mission the Prophet (ﷺ) was required to believe that he was a messenger. Just as you say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," the Prophet (ﷺ) too was to say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." And the Almighty, glory be to His majesty, the Most Generous Creator, first bore witness to Himself, as evidenced by His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He... (3:18)﴾ (Al 'Imran).

So the first witness to the true divinity is Allah Himself, and He bore witness to Himself. The meaning of the mention of His witnessing to Himself for us is that we should believe that He, glory be to Him, exercises His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah) and the absoluteness of His power by the word "Be" (kun), and that He knows that His creatures respond with certainty. He had to teach us that He first believed that He is the First, and that He is the true God, such that when any being is commanded a command of subjugation, that command must come to pass, and He, glory be to Him, does not hesitate to command. Therefore He said to us: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He﴾, a witness of the Essence to the Essence. The angels bore witness by direct vision (shahadat al-mashhad), and those of knowledge bore witness by inference (shahadat al-istidlal). And when Muhammad (ﷺ) bears witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, he believes that he is a messenger. Had he not believed in his mission, he would have hesitated to convey the message to us. After the Prophet (ﷺ) believed that he was a messenger from Allah, the command came to him from the Truth:

﴿And warn your closest kinsmen (26:214)﴾ (Al-Shu'ara').

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to call to Islam and to convey the verses of the Truth until the verses of defending the religion of Allah came, and the Truth said:

﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you... (9:123)﴾ (Al-Tawbah).

So, in the beginning, he had to believe that he was a messenger, and to convey the call to Quraysh and to the whole of the Arabian Peninsula. His call then passed from the Peninsula to Syria, and the message extended to Syria by announcement, even if it had not yet extended in fact; until his followers from among the Companions came and spread Islam throughout every corner of the earth. This is why there was symbolism in the sending of letters: a letter to so-and-so and a letter to so-and-so (3), so that the world would learn that the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) to faith and Islam is an outward-reaching call, because it differed from the calls of the messengers, peace be upon them, for every messenger used to know that the limits of his call were his own people (4).

As for Muhammad (ﷺ), his mission had stages: he believed in his own self first, then he called his closest kin, then Quraysh, then he conveyed to the Arabs, then to Syria, and the call extended by letters to all the kings of the world. The community of Muhammad (ﷺ) became entrusted with carrying the call and spreading it to any place, and with it is its proof, which is the Qur'an.

Allah willed that the Messenger of Allah be the seal of the messengers, and sent him with a religion that prevails over civilizations, even though he (ﷺ) was from an unlettered people who knew nothing (5); so that it would not be said of Islam that it was merely a civilizational leap, and there came to them a method that overcame the civilizations contemporary with it: Persia and Byzantium at one and the same time.

So the matter was a tribal matter, in which one of their own ruled them in this manner, without experience with social systems, and they knew nothing before Islam. Rather, they were a nomadic people (6) with no concern for political and economic systems. Each man among them carried his saddle and his tent and a few tools to sustain him in life, and every group settled in any place where grass appeared and water was found. After the flocks and herds had eaten the grass, the Arab would move with his group to another place, after one of them had looked at the sky to know the course of the clouds and where the rain would fall. Then these people would spread out with the call afterwards; for if they had belonged to a homeland, a house or a place, travel would have been difficult for them, but they were practiced in wandering the earth.

The verse under discussion reveals the weakness of faith in some, and the hypocrisy in others. The Truth says: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year, yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed?﴾ That is: it was necessary for them to repent or take a lesson, and to know that their standing against Islam has not and will not veil Islam, and that they will be crushed and lost. So why does not each of them remember himself and see his own interest in faith?

1. On the authority of Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us a sermon, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "Indeed among you are hypocrites, so whoever I name, let him stand." Then he said: "Stand up, so-and-so; stand up, so-and-so; stand up, so-and-so," until he named thirty-six men... Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/273) and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (6/286). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/112): "In it is 'Iyad ibn 'Iyad from his father, and I have not seen anyone who has biographed the two of them."

2. The word fitnah has many meanings in the language, all revolving around testing and putting to trial after trial, so that the good is distinguished from the bad. Its origin is taken from the fitnah of silver and gold, i.e., when you melt them with fire to know the inferior from the superior, in confirmation of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial (21:35)﴾ (Al-Anbiya').

3. The Messenger of Allah sent letters to the kings of the earth around the Hijaz, such as the Caesar of Byzantium, the Khosrow of Persia, the Muqawqis of Egypt and others, calling them to Islam with a group of his Companions, and he directed each of them to a direction, and said to them: "Indeed Allah has sent me as a mercy and for all mankind, so convey from me, may Allah have mercy upon you." Cited by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (4/607) from Ibn Ishaq.

4. This is among what was specific to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). On the authority of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that none before me was given. Every prophet was sent to his own people specifically, but I have been sent to every red and black (person). Spoils of war were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me. The earth was made for me a pure place of prostration and a mosque, so whichever man the prayer overtakes may pray wherever he is. I was aided with terror (cast into hearts) at a distance of a month's march, and I was given intercession." Agreed upon: related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (335) and Muslim (521).

5. The Lord of Might said concerning this: ﴿He it is who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they had been in manifest error (62:2)﴾ (Al-Jumu'ah).

6. A man became a bedouin (tabaddā): he dwelt in the desert. The desert was called badiyah because of its being apparent and exposed. See Lisan al-'Arab (b-d-w).

And when a surah is sent down, some of them look at one another, [asking], "Does anyone see you?" Then they turn away. God has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not comprehend. (9:127)

And before this, the Truth said:

"And when a surah is sent down, some of them say, 'Which of you has had his faith increased by this?' ..." (9:124) (Al-Tawbah)

That is: these hypocrites feel constricted and besieged, and they fear to speak, because they are present among the Muslims. Yet they do not find a means to express their disbelief, so one of them winks with his eye or gestures with his hand. Earlier, when they asked, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?", that question concerned the obligations; but the matter we are now considering contains no new obligations.

They wanted to say something, but they could not speak with their mouths, so they spoke with their eyes and glances. It is as if the glance itself was in this statement: "Does anyone see you?" You may see this in one who listens to a preacher's sermon, yet sees things that displease him, so you find him expressing his dissatisfaction through the movements of his face.

So there is a glance and there is speech, and they may ask: "Does anyone see you?" It is like your saying: "Do I have any wealth?", meaning that you do not possess at the outset anything that could be called wealth. The noble statement is certainly more eloquent than saying: "Does anyone see you?"

His saying, "Does anyone see you?", is evidence that they fear someone will catch them. Afterwards you find them slipping out of the circle of listening to the Qur'an or to the Messenger, because they cannot bear to continue listening, since the logic of the Truth bridles falsehood. Each of them is unable to believe in the truth and unable to declare disbelief, so they withdraw, and each one departs. Therefore we find that some of them had said earlier: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it" (41:26) (Fussilat).

They said that because the disbeliever or hypocrite may at some moment be heedless of falsehood, and faith then slips into his heart, just as the believer may at some moment be heedless of the Truth, but he seeks God's forgiveness for it.

When the hypocrite or disbeliever experiences a moment of heedlessness toward his disbelief or hypocrisy, the onslaught of faith comes upon him and he fears it, so he says to those like him: "It is better that we tell those with us: do not listen to this Qur'an." Why? So that it does not encounter a period of heedlessness from hypocrisy; for if it encounters a period of heedlessness from hypocrisy, faith may enter the heart. That is why they said: "Do not listen to this Qur'an." The matter did not stop there; they asked their followers to make noise during it, that is, to confuse it: "And make noise during it, that perhaps you will overcome" (41:26).

So they have no victory at all except by not listening to the Qur'an or by creating confusion when it is recited, so that the Qur'an does not penetrate the hearts. (2)

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says of these hypocrites:

"And when a surah is sent down, some of them look at one another, [asking], 'Does anyone see you?'" They said that because, as hypocrites, they had previously professed Islam, and they claimed to be forward in applying the rulings of faith. They insisted on standing in the first row during prayer, in order to ward off the accusation of hypocrisy from themselves, as the proverb says: "The suspect nearly says, 'Take me.'" Looking at one another, they asked: "Does anyone see you?" Then they departed, because they could not bear to sit with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or with the believers. The Truth concludes the verse:

"God has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not comprehend." This is the result of their psychological inclination toward hypocrisy, and God assists them in it. Since they do not recognize the value of faith, let them go far from it. The Truth turned them away only by their own choice, lest anyone say: "God is the turner of hearts, so what is their fault?" No; they turned away by the choice God created in them, so God turned their hearts, why? Because they are "a people who do not comprehend," that is: they do not understand. (3)

Understanding (fahm) is the first stage of the human self, and there is a difference between fahm and 'ilm (knowledge). Fahm means that you possess the capacity to grasp the essential nature of things by a faculty within you; but 'ilm means that you do not understand by your own essence, rather someone else understands and teaches you. You may learn a particular matter not from yourself but from a teacher. Whoever does not understand must accept instruction, but these people did not understand even when they were taught, and they insisted on refusing knowledge.

After this comes the conclusion of Surah al-Tawbah: "A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a treaty" (9:1).

The conditions of the disbelievers and hypocrites have been mentioned, along with the arduous obligations of jihad, and the Truth wished to conclude the surah by highlighting these previously mentioned hardships. He explains to us: beware of deserting the Messenger or angering him; for even if he brings you a message containing matters burdensome to you, take these burdensome matters as coming from a beloved to you, not from an enemy.

For example, if you see an enemy strike your son and wound him, the impact is severe upon you, because it comes from an enemy. But if you take your son to the doctor and the doctor decides to perform surgery on the boy, you accept that to remove a danger from your son. Thus there is a difference between an enemy's wounding of your son and a doctor's wounding of him, even though the pain may be the same.

So do not reject the burdensome matters that come upon you; but first recognize who imposed these hardships upon you. If it is your Lord, then your Lord is merciful to you. If it is the Messenger, then take the Messenger's commands and apply them, for they come from a beloved who wants good for you.

(1) Al-laghw fihi: al-lughu fihi, meaning speak loudly, with confused, mixed, tumultuous and clamorous speech, so that no one understands anything from it, and the hearts of their followers remain veiled from accepting God's guidance.
(2) This has been the practice of the polytheists and disbelievers toward every revelation that comes from heaven, like the people of Noah, of whom He said: "And indeed, every time I have called them that You may forgive them, they have put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and been arrogant with extreme arrogance" (71:7).
(3) The Exalted has given an example of this: "So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate, and God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people" (61:5), concerning the people of Moses.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 128:

And here the Truth says:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer; he is anxious over you; for the believers he is full of kindness and mercy.﴾ (9:128)

We notice here that the Truth has attributed [the coming] to the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and did not say: "I have sent you a Messenger." All of us know that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not come of his own accord, and did not claim this noble matter for himself. But the charge of faith indicates that he was created with what qualifies him for prophethood (1), and as soon as revelation descended upon him he possessed a self-generated drive to discharge the mission, and he did not need anyone to push him to discharge it. Therefore, the Truth, glorified is He, wished to establish for the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, that his coming was self-generated, but this self-generated coming was not from Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, at the beginning; rather he is a Messenger from Allah. So the Truth, glorified is He, here used the word "jā'a" (came).

The word "Messenger" indicates that he is not from himself, and the word "came" indicates that the charge of faith made his very self an act, so he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, loves striving for the sake of the mission, and loves struggle to realize this mission.

Therefore: do not look at what the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has brought you with the view you hold toward burdensome matters that tire you, but look at from whom it has come. If it is from the original source in the sending of messengers, then the Lord is merciful: He created you from nothing, and He continues His blessings upon you even while you disobey Him. You disobey Him, and yet Allah, glorified is He, loves the one who covers over you (2), so do not doubt and do not let yourself be doubted. You must take the obligations as coming from a beloved, and do not say: "They are a hardship." For you — and to Allah is the highest likeness — ask your son to study his lessons, and review them with him, forcing him at times against his will, and you may hold his hands so the doctor can give him an injection of the medicine that Allah made a cause of healing.

Therefore, do not take circumstances by their incidental effects upon you, but take them by their incidental effects from the One who decreed and ordained them, and He is the Truth, glorified and exalted:

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, meaning: the Truth, glorified is He, did not bring a stranger to you, but brought one of you, capable of communicating with you. The Truth's words ﴿from among yourselves﴾ have multiple meanings. Sometimes its meaning is "from your kind," just as He said about Eve: ﴿And created from it its mate...﴾ (4:1), meaning: He created Eve from the same essence as the human Adam. So let no one say: "How did Allah send us a human as a messenger?" For the Truth willed that the Messenger be from among mankind, out of mercy toward people. That is why he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, emphasized his humanness many times and in many places (3), and the Qur'an says:

﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ (17:94).

Therefore, the humanness of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, is not to be taken as a charge against Allah, but is taken as coming from Allah, because He sent one of the same kind so that he would be able to communicate with humans, and the emulation of him would be easy. That is why He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Say: "If there were in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ (17:95).

And the Truth's words ﴿from among yourselves﴾ mean: from the kind of the Arabs; He did not bring him from the Romans or the Persians, but chose for you the one who knows your natures best. Or the meaning of ﴿from among yourselves﴾ is: from the same tribe to which you belong, the people of Quraysh.

Or ﴿from among yourselves﴾ means that you know his history and know that he is fit to bear the trust of heaven to earth, just as you bear your trusts from earth to earth; and because this is his conduct, he is capable of bearing the trust of heaven to earth. You called him "the Truthful, the Trustworthy, the Faithful," and these were all preliminaries that suggested the necessity of believing in him as a Messenger from Allah. And if the chain of his deeds among you aroused your pride, then his coming as a Messenger raises your remembrance and elevates your standing. You are the people of Quraysh and Makkah, and you have sovereignty over the Sacred House, and Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to increase the scope of your sovereignty. If you were the masters of the House before his mission, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, then after his mission you will become the masters of the world.

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned﴾ (43:44).

So he is a prophet for all the world, and from the Arabs, and from Quraysh, and it was fitting that they rejoice in his mission and support it, but Allah did not will that. For Quraysh was a tribe that had become accustomed to sovereignty over the Arabs, and this made the Arabs take account of them, and all the tribes of the Arabian Peninsula feared them, and they had enormous awe; because all the Arabs are obliged to make pilgrimage to the Ka'bah, and during the pilgrimage all the tribes are in the land of Quraysh. Therefore the tribes used to protect the caravans of Quraysh, and no tribe ever confronted Quraysh at all; their caravans went out and came back, south and north, and no tribe could stand against Quraysh or attack them.

All this standing and this awe Quraysh gained from its service to the Sacred House of Allah. Therefore the Truth willed that Abraha could not destroy the House, so that sovereignty would remain with Quraysh; for had the Sacred House been destroyed, the pilgrimage would have shifted to Yemen, as Abraha wished, and from where would sovereignty have come to Quraysh? That is why the Truth said of Abraha and his people: ﴿And made them like eaten straw﴾ (105:5).

And He followed it with His words: ﴿For the accustomed security of Quraysh (1), their accustomed security in the caravans of winter and summer (2)﴾ (106:1-2). And since the Truth, glorified is He, willed this, in the next verse He says: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House (3), who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear (4)﴾ (106:3-4).

And the Truth, glorified is He, willed to send Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, as a Messenger who would first call the chieftains, and the tribe possessing awe and standing, so that the call of faith would be in the ears of the lords of the Peninsula whom all tribes feared, so it could not be said: "Muhammad preyed upon a few weak people and announced his call among them." No, his call came to the ears of the chieftains and the masters, and it mocked their dreams; and when they rejected his call, he migrated; then permission to fight them came. Support for Islam did not come from the masters; rather, the weak believed in him first, and then he migrated to Madinah, so that support would come from there.

For if support had come from the masters, they would have said: "Support for Islam came from a people accustomed to sovereignty," and no one among them would have appeared saying that he was a Messenger; they wanted to use him to dominate not only the Arabian Peninsula but the whole world, so the partisanship for Muhammad would be what created faith in Muhammad. But Allah wanted support to come from the weak, so that everyone would understand that faith in Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, is the cause of partisanship for Muhammad.

Thus we understand the meaning of ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger﴾: that is, a sent one from Allah, and ﴿from among yourselves﴾ with all that the stages of the self imply; and he is one who conveys from Allah, so he did not bring anything from himself, but the entire message he brought is from his Lord; and the Lord, by your own acknowledgment, is the One who created for you what you benefit from in the heavens and the earth.

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: Allah...﴾ (43:87).

And He says: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: Allah...﴾ (31:25).

Therefore, the created being is the human vicegerent, and what Allah created in the universe He created for your service, all of you, and you acknowledge that. So if the Lord has preceded you with these blessings, and the Messenger who came to you from Him came with what makes you happy, and you received his goodness before he brought you the obligations, and you received his blessing before you were addressed by Him, then the One who sent His Messenger with the obligations and the method for you must have appointed one who is trusted over you. He, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not come to you as a model in action, so do not be surprised. But the stupidity of those who disbelieve in Allah led them to want the Messenger to be an angel, so the Truth said:

﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?" Say: "If there were in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ (17:94-95). That is: if you want an angel, then the angel has a form you do not see, and we must make him an angel in the form of a human so that he may address you. So is the problem one of appearance and form? Moreover, angels by their creation: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ (66:6).

So if the angel Messenger said to you: "I am a model for you in righteous deeds," would the model be valid? Surely some of us would say: No, the model will not benefit, because you are an angel disposed to good, you have no appetite of the belly and no appetite of the private parts; so your example to us is not valid.

Therefore, from His mercy toward you, glorified is He, He made for you a Messenger from among yourselves, from your own tribe, from the Arabs, not from Persia or Rome, and he addresses you in your language; for you are the first ears to receive the call, so the Messenger must come in your tongue. Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to you with familiarity and intimacy, because he is from Quraysh, which has branches throughout the Peninsula and kinship and familiarity with all the Arabs. A third intimacy is that he is human, and the Truth, glorified is He, brought him as one individual among individuals, judged to be truthful and trustworthy before he conveyed to you his message from Allah.

Therefore, when the Messenger brings you an obligation that may be difficult for you, keep all these things in mind, so you may answer yourselves: he is a human and not an angel; he is from the Arabs and not from non-Arabs; he is from your own tribe in which he grew up among you; he is one whose conduct you know before he conveyed anything from Allah, for he did not lie to people about human matters, so would he lie to people about the right of Allah?

And 'Abdullah ibn Qusayt recited this verse: ﴿from among yourselves﴾, meaning: by human measure, he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, is the one most capable among you and the best of you (5). Therefore, when the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, brought the call from Allah, did our lady Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, await his bringing her a miracle? Did Abu Bakr await that he bring him a miracle? No, neither of them waited, because each of them took the miracle from the standpoint of his past history.

When he said to Khadijah: "It comes to me, it comes to me, it comes to me," she was mature in constitution, thought and intellect, and we know from what she said why Allah chose for him to marry her when he was twenty-five years old and she was forty, although it is customary for a person to love marrying someone younger than himself.

But the matter was not a marriage in the known sense; it was a marriage for a mission higher than what we know, for in the period of this marriage there would be the transitional phase between ordinary humanity and the humanity that receives from heaven, and this is a period that needs a mother's heart and a mother's vessel that embraces him and pats him.

Had he been a young girl and he had said to her what the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to Khadijah, she would have doubted his mental powers; but the wise Khadijah examined the matter by purely rational examination. When he said to her: "I fear that what comes to me is a jinn companion (6)," she said to him: "You join the ties of kinship, you earn for the destitute, you help in the calamities of truth, and by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you."

Therefore, from the antecedents of his life before the mission she took what indicates his truthfulness after the mission.

Likewise Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, when they said to him: "Your companion claims that he is a Messenger," he said: "Did he say it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "He is a Messenger from Allah, for he has not lied throughout his life" (8).

After that the Truth says: ﴿It grieves him that you suffer﴾. The word ﴿'azīz﴾ means: that which no one can attain or reach, and a "precious" thing is one of rare existence. You might say to a person: "You may become a minister," and he remains silent out of hope; but if you say to him: "You will become prime minister," he says: "This is a difficult matter and somewhat great for me."

Therefore, "'izza" comes from the impossibility of something, either because of its power, or in the sense of rare, or because it is impossible. And "'azīz" is the matter that is hard for people to attain, so it is said: "It is hard for me to reach the peak of the mountain." ﴿It grieves him﴾ means: it is hard for him that he should cause you hardship by a ruling; his heart is merciful toward you, and he does not bring you rulings so that they may burden you, but the rulings descend from Allah for your benefit; he himself is grieved

(1) Because his nature is the great character, and he was trained by the discipline of his Lord, and he lived moved by faith in lofty sublimity, and in deed by thinking of Allah, and in the self by tranquility toward Him, and in the body by movement for Him, and in the heart by monotheism and love; so his coming was self-generated, in the company of Allah. The Truth says: ﴿And indeed you are of a great character (4)﴾ (68:4).

(2) This is one of the rights of a Muslim over his brother, and it is a matter that Allah loves from His servant. On the authority of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim; he does not wrong him nor abandon him, and whoever is in need of his brother, Allah is in his need; whoever relieves a Muslim of a distress, Allah relieves him of a distress of the distresses of the Day of Resurrection; and whoever covers a Muslim, Allah will cover him on the Day of Resurrection." Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari (2442) and Muslim (258). It should be understood here that the covering intended is not silence about the wickedness of one who persists in sin, but covering a sin that a person committed and that has passed.

(3) The Mighty and Majestic says: {Say: "I am only a human like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God..."} (41:6). The Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, emphasized this matter very much, among them:
On the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, heard a dispute at the door of his chamber, so he went out to them and said: "I am only a human; the litigant comes to me, and perhaps one of you is more eloquent than another, so I judge that he is truthful and give him a ruling accordingly. Whoever I give by ruling the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of Fire, so let him take it or leave it." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2458) and Muslim (1713).
And on the authority of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: "I am only a human, and I have stipulated with my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that whichever Muslim I revile or curse, that it be for him a purification and a reward." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2602) and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/391, 400).

(4) "Like eaten straw" has two meanings: one, that He made the companions of the Elephant like leaves from which the grain has been taken, and the grain is gone; the other, that He meant He made them like the leaves of plants that animals have eaten and then excreted. Both are in the Arabic language (root: '-ṣ-f).

(5) Therefore Allah singled him out with sensory and moral qualities that make him, among the creatures of Allah, the most honored before Allah. The Truth says: {O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner (45), and as one calling to Allah by His permission and as an illuminating lamp (46)} (33:45-46).

(6) Ri'y min al-jinn: a companion whom a person has become accustomed to from seeing him often. It may also be from "ra'y" (opinion), meaning one who has an opinion of his own. See Lisan al-'Arab (root: r-'-y).

(7) When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, after Gabriel came to him in the cave of Hira, returned to Lady Khadijah with his shoulder-muscles trembling, and said: "Wrap me up, wrap me up," so they wrapped him until the fright left him. Then he said to Khadijah: "O Khadijah, what is wrong with me?" and told her the news. He said: "I have feared for myself." She said to him: "No! Rejoice, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. By Allah, you join the ties of kinship, you speak the truth, you bear the burdens of others, you earn for the destitute, you host the guest, and you help in the calamities of truth." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3) and Muslim (160), from 'A'ishah. Bawadiruh: the flesh between the shoulder and the neck, an indication of intense terror. Zammilūnī: cover me. Tahmil al-kall: that is, he spends on the weak, the orphan, and one unable to spend. Tuqri al-dayf: that is, you are generous and bountiful, you feed the guest. Nawā'ib al-haqq: events of good and evil.

(8) On the authority of Abu al-Darda', that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said about Abu Bakr: "Will you leave my companion for me?" (twice). "I said: 'O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all,' and you said: 'You lie,' but Abu Bakr said: 'You speak the truth.'" Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3661, 4640) and Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Sunnah (2/576).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 9, verse 129:

The Truth (al-Haqq) did not tell His Messenger: "If they turn away, then say: Allah is sufficient for me" (1). No, rather He commanded him to proclaim it to all people, so that they would hear it. Perhaps in your proclaiming it there is something that draws their attention to the truth, because if you say it, you will not say it except with a store of faith in it. And if any one of them does something against you, then Allah will punish him.

When you proclaim "Allah is sufficient for me" after they have denied you, the events that will come after your proclaiming "Allah is sufficient for me" will confirm that your sufficiency is in its proper place, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness. You say, "The support of so-and-so is sufficient for me," because you trust in the power of this person. But power in life is changeable. When you say "Allah is sufficient for me," there is no god but Him, glory be to Him, and no other god opposes Him in this or in anything else.

Say: "Allah is sufficient for me," with the support of "There is no god but He." "There is no god" is negation, and "but He" is affirmation. So in this saying, "There is no god but He," there is logical negation with removal, and logical affirmation with positive assertion. Here is the negation of any divinity for other than Allah, and the exception from that is Allah. May Allah have mercy on our shaykh Abd al-Rahman Azzam, when he translated from Muhammad Iqbal (2), the great Pakistani poet, and said:

"Tawhid is only affirmation and negation;
In them for the self are resolve and vigor."

Affirmation is in "but He," and negation is in "there is no god." In both of them is for the self resolve and vigor. That is, they are for the self the two poles of electricity. So negate divinity from other than Allah, and affirm it for Allah.

People, as we know, are of three categories: one category denies that there is any god for the universe absolutely, and they are the atheists (al-mulhidun). A second category says: there is Allah whom the Muslims affirm as one, but there are partners who benefit us with Allah. A third category affirms the oneness of Allah.

When we say "There is no god but He," we have affirmed divinity for Allah, and we have affirmed that He has no partner, and we have affirmed that there is no god other than Him, glory be to Him, who says:

"So if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust." (Qur'an 9:129)

This is a natural matter, and it can be known through calculation; therefore He brought "hasbi" (sufficient for me) from "hisab" (calculation). Calculate it, and you will find nothing but Allah. Since Allah is your sufficiency and there is no god but He, He extends His protection over you and His support for you. It is reasonable for you to place yourself in the hands of your Messenger, who conveyed to you the complete message from Allah, and to put your trust in Him, glory be to Him.

Since He, glory be to Him, is your sufficiency and there is no god but He, the obligation requires you to remain in His company, glory be to Him. The company of Allah has two stages: the first is by taking the means which He has provided to His creation, and the company of your absolute faith that if the means fail you, you turn to the Causer of causes, who exists and is the Lord of existence.

Consider, for example, people who need water, because it is a necessity for life. They go to the well and do not find water despite the existence of the well, because the water comes from the depths of the earth, and no longer seeps into it. Why? Because the store of rainwater that used to come from the mountain peaks and seep beneath the earth has been exhausted. Therefore we need a supply from the rains of the sky, so that they flow into the channels beneath the earth and the water returns to the well.

And if the wells around us dry up, do we despair? No, because our Lord has made clear to us: "Raise your hands to your Lord" (3). So, if we have exhausted the means, we ask the Causer. And so, if a person exhausts the means of Allah extended to him, and turns to Allah, He will respond to him.

Indeed, the hand of Allah is extended to us with the means, and it is not right for a person to neglect them and not take them, and say, "I am reliant upon Allah." Rather, a person must first take the means and exhaust them, and after that say, "There is no refuge for me except You, glory be to You." And if you wish, recite the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: "Is He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him...?" (27:62)

The distressed one (al-mudtarr) is the one who has exhausted his means and has nothing but Allah. But if a person says, "I supplicate to Allah night and day, and glorify Him, and recite Surat Ya-Sin for example, and Allah does not answer my supplication," we say to such a speaker: You are not supplicating out of necessity, and you have not taken the means. Take the means which Allah has created first, then supplicate afterward. Do not supplicate except when the means have been exhausted, so that the Causer responds to you. In this way you will not be tempted by the means. When the means are withheld, you turn to Allah. And if the means were all given, they would tempt a person by the means, and the Truth, glory be to Him, says: "No! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient" (96:6-7). Therefore we find that the Truth always makes clear that all the means are in His hand. We see a man who plows, sows, irrigates and tends, then the crop approaches ripeness, and after that a scorching wave comes and kills it, or a flood descends and sweeps it away. So: take the means, and keep the Causer always in mind, and here your reliance upon Allah is valid.

Many people err in understanding the word "tawakkul" (reliance upon Allah), and I say: tawakkul means that you first take the means of Allah which He created in His cosmos. If the means are scarce and do not reach a result, then turn to Allah, in confirmation of His saying: "Is He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him?"

We sometimes supplicate without necessity and neglect the means, and the example is found in our lives when a son says to his mother, "Pray for me that I succeed," and the unlettered mother answers with a simple phrase: "Supplication is aided by a little study," and by that she directs her son to the necessity of taking the means.

So: the meaning of tawakkul is that you benefit from the means which the hand of Allah has extended to you. If you have exhausted them, beware of despairing, because you have a Lord, and He, glory be to Him, is a mighty support to which you return.

Another example: if you are walking in the street with one pound, for instance, and then it falls from you or is stolen, and you do not possess in the house or in the bank a single piastre, here you grieve. But if there are ten pounds in the house, the proportion of anger and grief will be small; and if there are ten pounds in the house and a hundred pounds in the bank, you will not grieve or be angry at the loss of the one pound.

Thus you trust in the equivalent instead of the equivalent; so will you not trust in the Giver of this equivalent, in place of the equivalent?

So tawakkul is that the limbs work and the hearts rely (5). The lazy are those who want tawakkul to be for the limbs and not for the hearts.

It would have been possible for the Truth to change the style in the verse and say: "In Him I have trusted," instead of "In Him I have put my trust." But if you grasp the understanding of His saying, you will find that when a person says, "I have relied upon You," he may add, "and upon so-and-so, and upon so-and-so." But your saying, "In Him I have put my trust," cannot be followed by any conjunction, and in it is the exaltation of Allah, and no one else is relied upon by the Truth, just as you say in al-Fatiha: "You alone do we worship" (1:5), meaning: we do not worship other than You, so you have restricted worship to Him, glory be to Him.

Your reliance upon Allah has a foundation, because He is your Lord and the Lord of the cosmos that received you, and your power does not reach Him. You, on earth, plow it, sow it, and irrigate it, then you take from the bounty of Allah to you. He is your Lord and the Lord of the cosmos that received you, and this cosmos has become subjected to you, while you were not capable of subjecting the cosmos.

It is true that you may subjugate a beast, tie it, ride it, and load it with manure for example, and all of that is subjected to you and within your power, and this is from the grace of Allah upon you. His grace increases, and you see creatures subjected to you which are not within your power: the sun is subjected to you, rising every day with warmth and heat, and likewise the moon, and the clouds, and all these creatures are not within your power to control, yet Allah has subjected them for your service.

Your Lord, and the Lord of the cosmos that received you, subjected to you what is not in your hand, and He, glory be to Him, is the Lord of the dominion (malakut) who manages all of that, while you do not see Him, and He is the One who manages all these things. So do not look only at the appearances of bounty, but look at the causes of bounty within the appearances of bounty, and do not turn to any appearance except to know what lies behind that appearance. What lies behind any appearance is much.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: "He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne" (9:129). Yes, He is the Lord of the cosmos that received you and subjected to you what is in your hand and what is not in your hand, and what is behind the observable things of the world of the dominion, so that He manages everything with perfect power, and everything in the cosmos belongs to Allah. To Him, glory be to Him, belongs the Mighty Throne. So what is the Throne? We know at first glance that the Throne is the roof (6). We build a single-story building and make a roof for it, to shelter you from the glare of the sun and the rain, and if the ground is soft the buildings sink, and we build roofs so that they protect the walls from the factors of erosion.

The saying of Allah, glory be to Him, "the Mighty Throne," means: the affair being firmly established, in which every power is included. Therefore He, glory be to Him, expressed the kingship, for example, in the kingdom of Sheba through the tongue of the hoopoe, when he said: "I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a mighty throne" (27:23).

The throne, then, is a symbol of control. In our life, and to Allah is the highest likeness, we find that whoever takes the kingdom from one who was before him begins by cleansing the surrounding pockets and seeks out supporters, to reorder the kingdom in the way he sees fit for himself, until affairs are settled for him, and then sits thereafter upon the throne.

So: sitting on the throne means the affair is finally settled for the supreme Owner.

And He, glory be to Him, says: "Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise..." (40:7).

Whenever you hear the word "throne," take it as a symbol of the settling of the affair for Allah, and that everything has entered the sphere of His power, and in the sphere of His power, and in the sphere of "Be" (kun), just as the affair settles for a sensible king, who does not sit on the throne or rest until worldly affairs are settled. This is what we see in worldly affairs; how much more, then, the settling of all the cosmos from eternity belongs to Allah, glory be to Him and exalted?

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: "Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne..." (7:54).

That is, the affairs have been settled for Him. Thus we find that the word "throne" occurs in worldly thrones and in the Throne of Allah, glory be to Him. Worldly thrones symbolize the settling of the affair for whoever sits upon them, while the Throne, for Allah, is a symbol of the settling of the affair of the whole cosmos for Him, glory be to Him, so that nothing disturbs Him and nothing leaves His dominion.

The whole cosmos, with everything in it, is settled by the word "Be" and created by it, and subject to the authority of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted.

Here the Truth says: "And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne," and the Throne is not described as mighty except that in people's minds are the thrones of kings which we see in our lives, just as the hoopoe said about the queen of Sheba: "And she has a mighty throne (27:23)," that is, by human measures.

As for His saying here, "And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (9:129)," it is by the measures of the Lord of humanity. It is the throne of the Mighty Creator, glory be to Him, and it is beyond human conception; therefore we understand it within the frame of "There is nothing like unto Him" (42:11).

1 Al-hasb: a noun meaning sufficient. "Hasbi Allah" means: Allah suffices me.
2 Muhammad Iqbal, a poet and Islamic thinker who struggled with his pen and his soul in the path of Islam and the liberation of his country. He has literary and poetic works inclined toward Islam, which are studied in scholarly institutions. He was of Pakistani origin, Islamic homeland, of universal thought. He was translated in Egypt by Dr. Abd al-Rahman Azzam and al-Sawi Shu'lan.
3 Raise your hands in supplication and humility, on condition of responsiveness to it and faith in it, and you will find the answer together with right guidance.
4 Among the etiquette of supplication is that the supplicant should not be impatient for Allah's response to his supplication, lest he grow weary and abandon supplication. Rather, he should realize that Allah wants what is best for His servant. A servant may supplicate for what he thinks is good for him, but the All-Knowing of the unseen knows it is evil for him. On this the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "A servant's supplication continues to be answered so long as he does not supplicate for sin or the severing of ties of kinship, and so long as he does not become hasty." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is haste?" He said: "He says: I have supplicated, and I have supplicated, and I have not seen that it is answered for me, so he becomes weary at that point and abandons supplication." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (2735), the third narration of the hadith.
5 He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a extent" (65:3).
6 The Throne: the kingdom; "the kingdom was established upon his throne" means: he ruled. Among its meanings also is the couch of kingship, as in His saying: "And she has a mighty throne (27:23)." Also from it is the roof of a house, and it may be applied to the house itself. All these meanings indicate the settling and stability of the affair. See Lisan al-Arab (root: '-r-sh).
7 Worldly thrones indicate the settling of the affair for whoever rules upon them, while the Throne of Allah indicates the affair of the cosmos belonging to Allah, glory be to Him.
8 The thrones of human kings are limited in place and time, while the Throne of Allah, glory be to Him, has no limits, for He is the Owner of the dominion (malakut).
